Imagine a customer named **Tariq** wants to pay **`250.000 LYD`** to **Al-Madina Clinic** for a medical checkup. There are **4 players** in this story: 1. **The Merchant (Al-Madina Clinic):** Uses our **Merchant Portal** to create a digital bill called a **Payment Link** for `250.000 LYD`. 2. **The Payer (Tariq):** Clicks the link on his phone, opening our **Checkout Page**. 3. **Our Platform (The Payment Gateway):** Shows Tariq the available payment methods (**Rails** like Sadad, Edfali, Moamalat Card, LYPay), locks the link so nobody else can pay the same bill at the same time, talks to the bank, and records the accounting entry. 4. **The Upstream Gateway / Bank Switch (e.g., Almadar Sadad or Moamalat National Switch):** The external institution that actually holds Tariq's money and verifies his SMS OTP or card PIN. #### Lesson M1-L2: Wallets, Applications, Payment Links & The Single-Use Slot Lock Before a Merchant can create a Payment Link, they set up two building blocks inside their account: - **A Wallet (`wallets`):** The digital account where the merchant's money accumulates on our platform. Each wallet has a single currency (default `LYD`) and is tied 1-to-1 to a **`MERCHANT_WALLET` General Ledger Account**. - **An Application (`applications`):** Represents one sales channel of the merchant (for example, *"Clinic Website"*, *"WhatsApp Billing Desk"*, or *"Main Reception POS"*). - **Hard Rule:** Every Application is connected to **exactly one Wallet** (`assigned_wallet_id`). Why? So there is never any confusion about which wallet receives the money when a link is paid! When a customer opens a **Single-Use Payment Link (`use_count = 1`)** and clicks "Pay with Sadad", what stops them from opening the same link on a second phone and paying the same invoice twice? - **The Atomic Slot Reservation (`active_locked_count`):** The instant Tariq clicks "Pay", our database locks the link row and sets `active_locked_count = 1`. - Our database enforces the formula: **`confirmed_count + active_locked_count <= use_count`**. - While Tariq's attempt is in progress (`active_locked_count = 1`), anyone else opening that single-use link sees *"A payment is currently in progress for this link"*. - The lock is released **only** if Tariq's attempt ends in `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, or `EXPIRED`. If Tariq's attempt becomes **`UNKNOWN`** (because the bank timed out), the lock stays **HELD** so Tariq cannot accidentally pay twice while we verify with the bank! #### Lesson M1-L3: Why We Never Trust the Customer's Browser (Zero-Trust Checkout) In web browsers, customers (or attackers) can change anything on their screen: - They can modify the URL bar after a redirect to say `?status=success&amount=250.000`. - They can open the browser's Developer Console (`F12`) and trigger a JavaScript callback like `Lightbox.completeCallback()`. - They can try to send `"amount": 0.01` in an API request body. **How our platform defeats all three attacks automatically:** 1. **Checkout Never Accepts Amounts from the Browser:** The `/initiate` and `/confirm` APIs do not even have an `amount` field! `core-back` reads the amount strictly from `payment_links.amount` in the database. 2. **Return URLs and Browser Callbacks Are "Doorbells", Not Proof:** When a browser hits `/return/:token` or `/client-event`, our server transitions the attempt to `VERIFYING` and makes a secure, server-to-server **`VERIFY` (Inquiry)** call directly to the bank's server. Money is posted **only** when the bank's server confirms all **5 Trusted Success Facts** (Status = Success, Our Reference Matches, Settled Amount Matches, Currency Matches, Environment Matches). #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 1 (`LAB-01`): The Payment & Tamper-Detection Tracer - **What the Student Sees in the Lab UI:** An interactive 4-column visual simulation showing `[Payer's Browser] -> [checkout-back] -> [core-back + Database] -> [Bank Switch]`. - **Step 1 Task:** The student clicks **"Start 250.000 LYD Payment"**, observes `active_locked_count` change from `0` to `1`, and must answer what happens when a second browser tab tries to initiate on the same link (*Correct action: Block second tab with `SLOT_RESERVATION_FAILED`*). - **Step 2 Task (Attack Simulation):** The simulated payer intercepts the browser redirect and changes the URL to `/return/tok_123?status=PAID&amount=250.000` without paying at the bank. Not every edit requires a second person. If a merchant fixes a typo in their store's display trade name, making them wait for a Checker would slow down support. However, if someone changes a merchant's **payout bank IBAN**, **commission rate**, **risk tier**, or **application wallet binding**, a single mistake or malicious insider action could misdirect funds. Therefore, our platform divides every field into two classes: 1. **Descriptive Fields (Direct Edit + Logged in `detail_change_logs`):** - Merchant `trade_name`, display logo, POS terminal name/location, application `name` and `business_use_description`. - Takes effect immediately, and writes an unchangeable before/after row in `detail_change_logs` so Support can always see who changed what and when. 2. **Sensitive Fields (Strictly Governed by Maker-Checker `approval_requests`):** - **Merchant:** `legal_name`, `tax_id`, `registration_no`, `business_category`, `payout_bank_details_json`, `risk_tier`, `kyb_status`, `commission_receivable_ceiling`, `negative_balance_ceiling`. - **Application:** `assigned_wallet_id`, `rail_whitelist`, `redirect_domain_allowlist`. - **Platform & Money:** All `adjustments` (refunds, chargebacks, manual credits/debits), `commission_profiles`, `velocity_rules`, `aml_rules`, `aml_cases` resolutions, `regulatory_reports`, `gateway_versions` promotions to `LIVE`, and admin `users` authority changes. #### Lesson M2-L2: Optimistic Concurrency (`base_version`) & Stale Approvals What happens if Maker 1 proposes changing a Merchant's `risk_tier` when the Merchant record is at `version = 4` (`base_version = 4`), and before a Checker reviews it, another approved request updates the Merchant to `version = 5`? - When the Checker clicks **Approve** on Maker 1's request, `ApprovalService` compares `base_version (4)` against the Merchant's current version (`5`). - Because they no longer match, the system **refuses to overwrite the newer record** and returns the request to `DRAFT` (`BASE_VERSION_MISMATCH`) so the Maker can review the updated record first! #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 2 (`LAB-02`): The Checker Approval Desk Simulator - **What the Student Sees:** A simulated `/approvals` queue containing **4 pending requests** with full JSON-Patch diffs and attached evidence documents. If someone changes a flow step URL to an unlisted external domain, the engine refuses to attach any secrets from `credential_sets`! 4. **The Unmapped Money-Step Rule:** In `StatusRule`, if a `MOVES_MONEY` step receives a response that matches **none** of your status rules, the engine transitions the attempt to **`UNKNOWN`** (never `FAILED`). #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 5 (`LAB-05`): Build & Verify a Two-Step OTP Rail + Moamalat Hex-HMAC Profile - **What the Student Does in the Lab:** 1. Two days later, the merchant voluntarily refunded **`40.0000 LYD`** to the customer (`PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`). A week later, the customer's bank sends a `100.0000 LYD` **Chargeback (`DISPUTE_OPENED`)** webhook for that same payment! - If our system blindly drafted a `100.0000 LYD` chargeback adjustment, the merchant would lose `40 + 100 = 140 LYD` on a `100 LYD` sale! - **How Our Platform Protects the Merchant (Edge Case 126):** When the dispute arrives, our engine locks the attempt (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), sums all `EXECUTED` and `EXECUTING` refunds (`40.0000 LYD`), and automatically caps the drafted `CHARGEBACK` adjustment to the unrefunded remainder (**`60.0000 LYD`**). If the payment was already 100% refunded, it records the dispute with `NO_CHARGEBACK_DRAFTED` and drafts `0.0000 LYD`! #### Lesson M8-L2: The 12 Go-Live Gates (`GoLiveGateValidator`) Neither `activateGatewayVersion` (promoting a draft to `LIVE`) nor `rollbackGatewayVersion` (rolling back to a previous version) can execute unless **all 12 Go-Live Gates** pass against persisted `GatewayVersionEvidence`: 1. **Gate 1:** Four-Eyes Maker-Checker Approval (`checker_user_id != maker_user_id`). 2. **Gate 2:** All 15 Automated Sandbox Scenarios Passed Green. 3. **Gate 3:** Amount Pipeline Contract Test Passed (proving `amount_scale`, `amount_precision`, and `amount_rounding` on wire values). 4. **Gate 4:** Reference Format Contract Test Passed (proving charset and max-length rules). 5. **Gate 5:** Cryptographic Signature Contract Test Passed against captured partner vectors. 6. **Gate 6:** Channel Verification Strength Enforced (`must_inquire = true` on all weak/hint channels). 7. **Gate 7:** Named Rollback Version (`rollback_version_id`) Configured. 8. **Gate 8:** Route Limits, Commission Profile, and Statement Parser Preview Verified. 9. **Gate 9:** Evidence Level `VERIFIED` (or signed executive `risk_acceptance_note` for `HIGH_RISK` gateways; What Is a Wallet (`Wallets` -> `/wallets`)? A **Wallet** is your digital safe inside our platform where money from your customers accumulates in real time (`LYD`). - Can my company have more than one Wallet? **Yes!** For example, if you run a clinic with two branches (*Tripoli Branch* and *Benghazi Branch*), you can create two separate Wallets so each branch's revenue and monthly accounting statements are kept completely separate. - **How is my Wallet balance calculated?** Your Wallet balance is not just a simple counter; it is calculated directly from our **Double-Entry Financial Ledger**. An **Application** represents one sales channel where your customers pay you—for example: - *"Main Online Store Website"* - *"WhatsApp & Instagram Customer Billing"* - *"Downtown Showroom POS Counter"* #### 3. Why Must Every Application Connect to Exactly One Wallet? When you create an Application, you select **one Assigned Wallet (`assigned_wallet_id`)**. - This ensures there is **zero confusion** about where money goes: every Payment Link created under *"Downtown Showroom POS Counter"* automatically deposits its money into the exact Wallet assigned to that Application. - Multiple Applications can share the same Wallet if you want all your sales channels to pool into one balance. #### 4. | What to Tell the Customer | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **`SUCCEEDED` (Green)** | The bank confirmed the payment and the money is credited to your Wallet. | **YES — Deliver immediately.** | *"Thank you, your payment is confirmed!"* | | **`AWAITING_CUSTOMER`** | The system sent the SMS code or displayed the QR/Redirect, and is still waiting for the customer to finish. | **NO — Wait.** | *"Please enter the SMS code or approve the notification in your wallet app before the timer ends."* | | **`VERIFYING` / `UNKNOWN` (Amber)** | The customer submitted their confirmation, and our server is currently verifying the final receipt with the bank switch (or waiting for a slow bank response). | **WAIT until it turns `SUCCEEDED`.** | *"Our system is confirming your payment with the bank right now. **Please do not pay a second time**—your payment reference is saved and will update automatically."* | | **`FAILED` / `EXPIRED` / `CANCELLED` (Red/Grey)** | No money was taken (wrong OTP 3 times, insufficient funds, customer limit exceeded, or timer ran out). | **NO — Not paid.** | *"The payment did not go through and you were not charged. Click **Request Cash-Out**, select your Wallet, and enter the LYD amount you want wired to your verified corporate bank account. - Your request moves through 4 transparent stages: - `PENDING` (Submitted by you) -> `PROCESSING` (Being wired by our Finance team to the exact bank IBAN snapshotted when you clicked request) -> `COMPLETE` (Wire sent) -> `SUBTRACTED` (Finalized on your ledger statement). 2. **Downloading Hash-Verified Monthly Statements (`/wallets`):** - At the end of every month, you can download your official **Monthly Wallet Statement** (`CSV` or `PDF`), showing: - **Opening Balance** (which always equals the exact Closing Balance of the previous month), - **Every Confirmed Payment** (Gross Amount, Platform Commission, Net Credited), - **Refunds & Dispute Adjustments**, - **Cash-Out Payouts**, and - **Closing Balance**, sealed with a cryptographic SHA-256 content hash for your auditors. --- ### CHAPTER M-08: Responding to Customer Disputes & Refunds (`/disputes` & `/payments`) **Who this is for:** Business Owners & Customer Support 1. **What Happens When a Customer Opens a Dispute (Chargeback)?** - If a customer claims to their bank that they did not receive their order or did not authorize a card payment, the bank notifies us and a **Dispute (`disputes`)** opens in `/disputes` with a strict **Evidence Deadline (`evidence_due_at`)**. - You will receive an immediate email and in-app notification (`DISPUTE_OPENED`). - While the dispute is open, the disputed amount is temporarily held in reserve (`CHARGEBACK_RESERVE`). 2. **How to Win a Legitimate Dispute:** - Open `/disputes` **before `evidence_due_at`**, click **Upload Evidence**, and attach proof that you delivered the goods or services (signed delivery receipt, customer invoice, shipping log, or service record). - If the bank decides the dispute in your favor (**`WON`**), the full net amount is immediately released back into your Wallet! 3. **What if a Chargeback Happens After You Already Cashed Out Your Wallet?** - If a chargeback or refund is approved when your Wallet balance is low (and within your approved `negative_balance_ceiling`), your Wallet balance will temporarily show a negative number (e.g., `-45.000 LYD` owed to the platform). You do not need to send a separate wire: your next incoming customer payments will automatically pay down that negative balance until your Wallet is positive again! --- ### CHAPTER M-09: Using Your Own Gateway Credentials (`MERCHANT_DIRECT` Mode — `/credentials`) **Who this is for:** Enterprise Merchants with Their Own Direct Aggregator/Bank Contracts By default, your payments use **our platform's master bank connections (`PLATFORM_CLEARING`)**, and we wire your money via Cash-Outs. However, if your company already has its own direct merchant contract with an aggregator or switch that supports merchant-owned credentials (such as **DPay**), you can plug your own keys into **Credentials (`/credentials`)**: 1. **Write-Only Security:** When you enter your API keys/secrets and click **Save & Verify**, our server encrypts them inside our hardware-backed `Vault` and runs a live **`CREDENTIAL_CHECK`** test call. Once saved, no human being (not even you or our staff) can ever read the secret back—it can only be replaced. 2. **How Money & Commission Work in `MERCHANT_DIRECT` Mode:** - Because the gateway is using **your own account**, when a customer pays `100.000 LYD`, the gateway sends that `100.000 LYD` **directly to your company's bank account**! - Therefore, our platform **does not credit your Merchant Wallet** for `MERCHANT_DIRECT` payments. Instead, open **Team (`/team`)** and invite each staff member with only the permissions they need: - **`MERCHANT_CASHIER`:** Can only operate assigned in-store POS screens (`/pos`). Customer clicks "Checkout (150.000 LYD)" on Your Website │ ▼ 2. Your Backend Server calls: POST https://merchant./api/v1/external/links (Using your secret `pg_live_...` Bearer Token + Amount: "150.000") │ ▼ 3. Our Platform returns: { "key": "lnk_01J...", "checkoutUrl": "https://pay./pay/lnk_01J..." } │ ▼ 4. Your Website sends the Customer to `checkoutUrl` (where they pay with Sadad, Edfali, Moamalat, LYPay, etc.) │ ▼ 5. When the Customer finishes, Your Backend Server verifies the truth by calling: GET https://merchant./api/v1/external/links/lnk_01J... (or GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference) — and ONLY marks the order paid when `state === "COMPLETED"` / `status === "SUCCEEDED"`! ``` --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-02: Authentication (`pg_live_` Bearer Tokens) & IP CIDR Allowlists (`/developers/tokens`) #### 1. Creating Your API Access Token 1. In the Merchant Portal, open **Developers -> API Tokens (`/developers/tokens`)** and click **Create Token**. 2. Select the **Application** this token will belong to, and select the minimum required **Scopes** (`links:create`, `links:read`, `links:cancel`, `payments:read`). 3. Copy your token immediately (it starts with **`pg_live_`** followed by 32 random base64url bytes). - **Why can't I view the token again later?** For your security, our database never stores your plaintext token—it stores only a one-way `SHA-256` hash (`token_hash`) and the last 4 characters (`last_four`). If you lose the token, revoke it and create a new one. 4. **NEVER put a `pg_live_` token inside frontend browser JavaScript, a React/Vue bundle, or a mobile APK!** `pg_live_` tokens must only be called from your own backend server. #### 2. Locking Your Token to Your Server's IP Address (`ip_whitelist_enabled`) To make a stolen token useless to an attacker, enable **IP Whitelist (`ip_whitelist_enabled = true`)** and add your backend server's static public IP in CIDR notation: - Single server IP example: `203.0.113.45/32` - Subnet example: `203.0.113.0/24` If any request arrives with your token from an IP address outside your CIDR list, our edge and core guards reject it immediately with `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-03: Money Precision Rules & Redirect Allowlists (Avoid These 3 Common Mistakes) 1. **Always Send Amounts as Decimal Strings (Never Floats!):** - Libyan Dinars have **3 decimal places (Dirhams)**, and our ledger uses `DECIMAL(18,4)`. - Always pass amounts as strings like `"150.000"` or `"76.255"`, **never** JavaScript floats like `150.00000000000003`. 2. **`redirectUrl` Rules:** - A custom `redirectUrl` is permitted **only on Single-Use links** (`infiniteUse: false, useCount: 1`). - The hostname of `redirectUrl` (e.g., `https://shop.yourcompany.ly/orders/4092/return`) **must** be pre-registered in your Application's `redirect_domain_allowlist` in `/applications`, otherwise link creation will fail with `400 REDIRECT_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`. 3. **Never Trust the Browser Return Alone:** - When the customer's browser lands back on your `redirectUrl`, treat that page load only as a trigger for your backend server to call `GET /api/v1/external/links/:key` (or `GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference`). Only fulfill the order when our API returns `state: "COMPLETED"` and the attempt `status: "SUCCEEDED"`. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-04: Complete Endpoint Reference (`/api/v1/external/*`) #### Endpoint 1: Create a Payment Link — `POST /api/v1/external/links` - **Required Header:** `Authorization: Bearer pg_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` - **Request Body Schema:** ```json { "applicationId": "0192d4a0-7c10-7000-8000-000000000001", "amount": "150.000", "currency": "LYD", "feeBearer": "MERCHANT_ABSORBS", "infiniteUse": false, "useCount": 1, "redirectUrl": "https://shop.yourcompany.ly/checkout/return?orderId=ORD-9012", "railWhitelist": null, "expiresAt": "2026-11-01T18:00:00.000Z" } ``` - Returns the current link `state` (`PENDING | COMPLETED | EXPIRED | CANCELLED`), slot counters (`confirmedCount`, `activeLockedCount`), and the array of attempts with their `reference`, `status`, `railCode`, `requestedAmount`, `surchargeAmount`, `totalChargedAmount`, `platformCommissionAmount`, `netMerchantAmount`, and `terminalAt`. #### Endpoint 3: Get Single Payment Attempt by Reference — `GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference` - Looks up a specific attempt by its unique platform reference (`reference`) and returns its authoritative status and settlement breakdown. #### Endpoint 4: Cancel an Unpaid Payment Link — `POST /api/v1/external/links/:key/cancel` - Cancels a `PENDING` link as long as no attempt is currently past the point of no return. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-05: Copy-Pasteable Production Code Templates (Interactive Code Generator) The interactive widget in `/guide/developers` pre-fills your selected `applicationId` and generates ready-to-run code in 4 languages: #### 1. PHP (Laravel / Guzzle) ```php acceptJson() ->post(config('services.payment_gateway.base_url') .  # STANDALONE FAKE PAYMENT RAILS EMULATOR & CHAOS TESTING PORTAL — MASTER ARCHITECTURE & TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION
 
 **Target Repository:** `selmotamed-ctrl/payment-gateway-monolith`  
 **Service Workspace Directories:** `fake-rails-back` · `fake-rails-front` · `deploy` · `core-back`  
 **Runtime & Stack Conventions:** Bun (`^1.4.1`) + Express 5 (`^5.2.1`) + Zod 4 (`^4.5.4`) + `bun:sqlite` (zero-dependency isolated persistence) · Vue 3 (`^3.5.22`) TSX/JSX + Vuetify 3 (`^3.10.7`) + `kt-dc` + Vite (`rolldown-vite`)
 
 ## Executive Summary & Architectural Vision
 
 Testing a zero-code, multi-rail payment gateway platform across 20 heterogeneous Libyan and international payment switches (each with distinct collection modes, cryptographic signature schemes, amount scales, asynchronous webhook shapes, and T+N statement formats) cannot rely solely on unit mocks or unstable partner sandboxes. Partner sandboxes frequently suffer from strict hourly rate limits, unannounced downtime, inability to deterministically trigger edge cases (such as `MOVES_MONEY` socket resets, conflicting webhook vs. inquiry states, or T+N fee variances), and lack of visibility into what the upstream switch actually received.
 
 This specification designs a **Standalone Fake Payment Rails Emulator & Chaos Testing Service** (`fake-rails-back` + `fake-rails-front`) that acts as a complete, self-contained external payment ecosystem:
 
 1. **Zero Shared Database with the Payment Gateway (`100% Out-of-Process Isolation`):**
-   - `fake-rails-back` has zero access to `core-back`'s MySQL/MariaDB database and shares no memory with `core-back`. It persists its own transactions, webhook delivery queues, and chaos rules in an isolated embedded SQLite WAL database (`bun:sqlite` at `shared/data/fake-rails.sqlite`).
+   - `fake-rails-back` has zero access to `core-back`'s PostgreSQL 18 database and shares no memory with `core-back`. It persists its own transactions, webhook delivery queues, and chaos rules in an isolated embedded SQLite WAL database (`bun:sqlite` at `shared/data/fake-rails.sqlite`).
    - To `core-back`, the Fake Rails Service is indistinguishable from 20 real external bank switches and aggregators over HTTPS.
 2. **All 9 Collection Modes, All 10 Flow Phases, and All 20 Gateway Profiles:**
    - Emulates every collection mode (`OTP_PULL`, `REDIRECT`, `EMBEDDED`, `PUSH_APPROVAL`, `QR_DISPLAY`, `PAY_CODE`, `DEEP_LINK`, `MANUAL`, `HYBRID`) and every lifecycle phase (`CREDENTIAL_CHECK`, `PRE_INITIATE`, `INITIATE`, `SUBMIT`, `VERIFY`, `CANCEL`, `REFUND`, `VOID`, `CAPTURE`, `SETTLEMENT_FETCH`), plus interactive Hosted Checkout pages (`REDIRECT`) and drop-in JavaScript widget scripts (`EMBEDDED` Moamalat Lightbox & MPGS Hosted Session).
 3. **Production-Deployable via the Multi-Host Deployment Engine (`deploy/`):**
    - Integrates into `deploy/deploy.env` and `deploy/deploy.ts` as an optional 6th logical host role (`FAKE_RAILS_HOST`, colocated or dedicated) gated by explicit safety flags (`FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="true"` and `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION="true"`), with configurable ports, TLS modes, PM2 process management, Nginx reverse-proxy templates, and UFW firewall rules.
    - Automatically relaxes `core-back`'s SSRF private-IP guard **only** for the explicitly allowlisted Fake Rails host/IP when `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS="true"` is set, preserving full SSRF protection against all other private/loopback addresses.
 4. **Single-User Tester Portal & Live Chaos Matrix (`fake-rails-front`):**
    - Protected by a single tester credential pair (`FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER` and `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`) injected directly from `deploy.env`.
    - Streams incoming requests, outbound responses, and webhook deliveries in real time over Server-Sent Events (SSE).
    - Provides per-rail and per-phase **probabilistic failure sliders (0%–100%)** and **deterministic scenario overrides** so testers can configure any rail to fail at a given percentage chance with specific failure modes (`TIMEOUT_HANG`, `SOCKET_RESET`, `HTTP_500`, `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `WRONG_OTP`, `AMOUNT_MISMATCH`, `DUPLICATE_WEBHOOK`, `FORGED_SIGNATURE`, `CONFLICTING_INQUIRY`), manually approve/reject pending `PUSH_APPROVAL` / `QR_DISPLAY` / `PAY_CODE` payments, and generate downloadable CSV/XLSX/JSON settlement statements.

 ### 2.2 Startup & Deployment Safety Gates (`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` & `fake-rails-back/lib/env/index.ts`)
 
 Both the deployment orchestrator (`deploy/deploy.ts`) and the service startup (`fake-rails-back/lib/env/index.ts`) enforce three non-negotiable rules:
 
 1. **Explicit Production Opt-In Gate:**
    - If `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED === "true"` and `NODE_ENV === "production"`, startup immediately checks `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION === "true"`. If false or omitted, `configSchema.ts` and `fake-rails-back` abort with exit code `1` (`FAKE_RAILS_PRODUCTION_GUARD_BLOCKED: Set FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION="true" to run Fake Rails in production mode`).
 2. **Non-Empty Single-User Portal Credentials Gate:**
    - When `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED === "true"`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER` (min 4 chars) and `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (min 12 chars, never default/empty) are strictly validated by Zod 4 before any SSH connection or process startup.
 3. **Port Collision & Firewall Isolation Gate:**
    - `configSchema.ts` verifies that `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT` (`4104`) and `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` (`8444`) do not collide with `CORE_PORT` (`4000`), `ADMIN_BACK_PORT` (`4101`), `MERCHANT_BACK_PORT` (`4102`), `CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT` (`4103`), `ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT` (`8443`), or public `80`/`443`.
    - `firewallConfigurator.ts` opens `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` (`8444`) to `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` (plus `CORE_PRIVATE_IP` and `CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP`), while keeping `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT` (`4104`) bound strictly to `127.0.0.1`.
 
 ### 2.3 Scoped SSRF & TLS Allowlist in `core-back` for Fake Rails
 
 In `core-back`, Safeguard 10 (`StepExecutor.ts` custom DNS hook) blocks outbound calls to private/loopback IP ranges (`10.0.0.0/8`, `192.168.0.0/16`, `127.0.0.0/8`) to prevent SSRF. When `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="true"` is deployed on a LAN IP (e.g., `https://10.10.0.20:8444`) or `127.0.0.1:8444`:
 
 - `deploy/deploy.ts` writes `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS="true"` and `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS="fakerails.internal,10.10.0.20,127.0.0.1"` into `core-back`'s `shared/.env`, and trusts the generated `fake-rails-ca.crt` (or `internal-ca.crt` used to sign the Fake Rails Nginx TLS certificate) in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.
 - `core-back/engine/flow/StepExecutor.ts` checks: if `env.ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS === true` and the target hostname/IP is **both** in `env.FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` **and** in the gateway version's `gateway_environments.allowed_hosts`, the private-IP rejection is bypassed for that exact host:port. All other private/loopback/metadata IPs (`169.254.169.254`, database ports, internal admin ports) remain strictly blocked.
 
 ### 2.4 Extension to the 12-Step Deployment Pipeline (`deploy/deploy.ts`)
 
 When `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="true"` (or `./deploy/deploy.sh --only=fake-rails`), the orchestrator executes:
 - **Step 2b (Local SPA Build):** Builds `fake-rails-front` via Vite (`bun run build`) alongside `admin-front`, `merchant-front`, and `checkout-front`.
 - **Step 3b (Certificate Minting):** Mints `fake-rails.crt` / `fake-rails.key` signed by the deployment CA with `SAN = DNS:${FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN}, IP:${FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP}, IP:127.0.0.1` so `core-back` verifies HTTPS TLS 1.3 cleanly without disabling TLS verification.
 - **Step 6b (Deploy `fake-rails-back` & `fake-rails-front` to `FAKE_RAILS_HOST`):**
   - Rsyncs `fake-rails-back/` and `fake-rails-front/dist/` to `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/releases/<TS>/`.
   - Creates `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/shared/data/` (for persistent `fake-rails.sqlite`) and `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/shared/.env` (`chmod 600`) containing `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL=https://${CHECKOUT_DOMAIN}/api/v1/inbound`, and deterministic signing secrets matching `seedFakeRails.ts`.
   - Switches `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/current` symlink, starts PM2 process `pg-fake-rails-back`, renders `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/pg-fake-rails.conf` on `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT`, runs `nginx -t`, and reloads Nginx.
   - If `SEED_FAKE_RAILS_BLUEPRINTS="true"`, runs `bun run seed-fake-rails` on `CORE_HOST` so all 20 gateway configurations in `core-back` have their `base_urls` and `script_urls` pointed to `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and their `ConfirmationChannel` path tokens synced with `fake-rails-back`.
 
 ## 3. Single-User Authentication Architecture (Configured via `deploy.env`)
 
 Per the specification, the Fake Rails Portal has **one user** whose username and password are provided in `deploy.env`.
 
 ### 3.1 Authentication Flow (`fake-rails-back/api/portal/auth.ts`)
 
 1. **Zero Database User Table Required:**
    - On startup, `fake-rails-back/lib/env/index.ts` reads `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and `FAKE_RAILS_JWT_SECRET` from `.env` (populated by `deploy.ts` from `deploy.env`).
    - Startup derives a SHA-256 digest of both credentials in memory for constant-time comparison via `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
 2. **Login Endpoint (`POST /portal-api/auth/login`):**
    - Validates `{ username, password }` using Zod 4.
    - Enforces a sliding-window brute-force rate limiter (max 10 failed attempts per IP per 15 minutes).
    - Compares `username` and `password` against the `deploy.env` credentials using `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
    - On match, issues a signed HS256 JWT (`exp: 12h`, `sub: env.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER`, `role: "FAKE_RAILS_TESTER"`) and returns `{ token, user: { username: env.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER, allowInProduction: env.FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION } }`.
 3. **Portal Guard Middleware (`portalAuthGuard.ts`):**
    - Protects all `/portal-api/*` endpoints (except `/portal-api/auth/login` and `/portal-api/internal/bulk-seed`, which requires the `X-Fake-Rails-Seeder-Token: ${FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN}` header).

 1. **Interactive Hosted Checkout Page (`/hosted/redirect/:sessionId`):**
    - When a customer in `checkout-front` selects a `REDIRECT` rail (e.g., T-LYNC, MyPay, DPay Hosted, MPGS 3DS2), `checkout-front` redirects the browser to `https://<FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN>:8444/hosted/redirect/:sessionId`.

    - If **Interactive Tester Mode** is active, the page displays the gateway's branded checkout simulator with 6 one-click buttons for the tester:
      - **1. Approve & Redirect Normally** (fires valid signed webhook + redirects to `return_url`),

      - **4. Close Tab / Abandon — Fire Webhook 30s Later** (tests Edge Case 1 & async webhook settlement),

      - **6. Customer Cancel** (redirects to `cancel_url`).
 2. **Drop-In Embedded Widget Simulator (`/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js` & `/hosted/widget-frame`):**
    - `core-back` seeds the Moamalat Lightbox `WidgetDefinition.script_urls` to `https://<FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN>:8444/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js` (with its matching SHA-384 SRI hash and CSP origin).
    - When `checkout-front` loads the script and calls `window.Lightbox.Checkout.configure({ MID, TID, AmountTrxn, MerchantReference, TrxDateTime, SecureHash, completeCallback, errorCallback, cancelCallback })`, the script verifies the server-computed `SecureHash` against `fake-rails-back` and mounts an interactive Lightbox modal overlay with one-click buttons: **Complete Card Payment**, **Spoof Browser `completeCallback` Without Server Payment (Tests T-06 / Edge Case 21)**, **Trigger Card Decline**, and **Cancel**.
 
 ## 5. Probabilistic Chaos & Failure Injection Engine
 
 A core requirement is configuring whether a given rail is going to fail or succeed with a **given percentage chance**, alongside fine-grained control over *how* it fails at each lifecycle phase.
 
 ### 5.1 Chaos Configuration Data Model (`fake_rail_scenarios` in SQLite)
 
 Each of the 20 rails has a persisted configuration row in `fake-rails-back` (editable live from the Tester Portal with zero restart):
 
 ```ts
 export interface RailChaosScenarioConfig {
   railCode: string;                       // e.g. "edfali", "sadad", "moamalat", "lypay", "tlync", "neompay"
   enabled: boolean;                       // If false, returns HTTP 503 Connection Refused (simulates full outage / RB-01)
   overallFailureChancePercent: number;    // 0 to 100 (e.g. 25 means 25% of transactions on this rail will fail)
 
   // Phase-specific failure distribution (when the PRNG rolls a failure, which phase & error mode is chosen)
   phaseBreakdown: {
     initiateFailWeight: number;           // Weight for failing during INITIATE (before point_of_no_return -> tests Route Failover)
     submitFailWeight: number;             // Weight for failing during SUBMIT / CONFIRM (MOVES_MONEY -> tests UNKNOWN & Lockout)
     verifyFailWeight: number;             // Weight for failing during VERIFY / INQUIRE
     webhookFailWeight: number;            // Weight for webhook delivery anomalies
     refundFailWeight: number;             // Weight for failing during REFUND / VOID (tests Adjustment EXECUTING state)
   };
 
   // Weighted distribution of failure modes when a failure is triggered
   failureModeWeights: {
     TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: number; // Explicit 200/400 decline -> FAILED
     LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CUSTOMER_CEILING: number;     // Customer ceiling hit -> FAILED (must NOT trip circuit breaker)
     WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE: number;                 // Mistyped OTP -> stays AWAITING_CUSTOMER (otp_attempts + 1)
     HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT: number;              // 500 Internal Server Error -> UNKNOWN on money step, trips breaker on initiate
     TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL: number;         // Sleeps 20,000ms so core-back AbortController times out -> UNKNOWN
     SOCKET_RESET_MID_STREAM: number;             // Destroys TCP socket after receiving body -> UNKNOWN
     MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY: number;      // Returns 200 OK with broken/changed JSON schema -> UNKNOWN (Edge Case 57)
     RATE_LIMIT_HTTP_429: number;                 // Returns 429 Too Many Requests
     AMOUNT_ROUNDING_MISMATCH: number;            // Settles +/- 0.050 LYD or 2-decimal rounded amount -> tests mismatch_policy
     CONFLICTING_WEBHOOK_VS_INQUIRY: number;      // Webhook says PAID, Inquiry says FAILED -> P1 CONFLICT (Edge Case 20)
   };
 
   // Latency & Async Confirmation Timing
   latencyMs: { min: number; max: number };       // Artificial network latency range (e.g. 50ms - 400ms)
   autoApproveAsyncAfterSec: number | null;       // For PUSH_APPROVAL / QR_DISPLAY: auto-confirm after N sec (null = wait for manual click in Portal)
   webhookBehavior: {
     delaySeconds: number;                        // Delay before sending webhook (set > session TTL to test Late Success Recovery)
     duplicateCount: number;                      // Send 1 (normal) or 2..5 identical webhooks (tests dedupe_key)
     outOfOrderPendingAfterPaid: boolean;         // Send PAID webhook followed 2s later by PENDING (tests forward-only rule)
     corruptSignatureChancePercent: number;       // 0 to 100% chance of sending an invalid HMAC signature (tests RB-02)
   };
 }
 ```
 
 ### 5.2 Deterministic Magic Inputs + Probabilistic PRNG Evaluation (`ChaosEvaluator.ts`)
 
 Every incoming request to `/rails/:gatewayCode/*` passes through `ChaosEvaluator.evaluate(req, railConfig)`:
 
 1. **Priority 1 — Deterministic Magic Test Inputs (100% Reproducible Contract & 15-Scenario Suite):**
    - Before rolling the percentage dice, `ChaosEvaluator` checks if the request contains a deterministic magic phone number, OTP, or amount suffix (used by `core-back`'s 15-scenario sandbox runner and automated tests):
      - OTP `000000` or `0000` -> Always returns `WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE`.
      - OTP `999999` or Phone ending in `9901` -> Always returns `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`.
      - Phone ending in `9902` -> Always returns `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
      - Phone ending in `9905` or OTP `500500` -> Always returns `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` on `SUBMIT` (`MOVES_MONEY`).
      - Phone ending in `9906` or OTP `408408` -> Always hangs for `20,000ms` (`TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL`).
      - Phone ending in `9907` -> Always returns `200 OK` with `{ unexpected_schema: true }` (`MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY`).
 2. **Priority 2 — Per-Transaction Override from the Tester Portal:**
    - If the tester clicked **"Force Next Outcome"** on an active transaction in the Portal (while the customer is on the OTP, QR, Push, or Redirect screen), that explicit outcome wins.
 3. **Priority 3 — Configured Percentage Chance (`overallFailureChancePercent`):**
    - For normal traffic, when a transaction first hits `INITIATE` (or `PRE_INITIATE`), `ChaosEvaluator` draws `roll = Math.random() * 100`.
    - If `roll < railConfig.overallFailureChancePercent`, the transaction is assigned a failure fate (`assignedFailPhase` and `assignedFailureMode`) sampled from `phaseBreakdown` and `failureModeWeights` and stored on its `fake_transactions` row in SQLite.
    - Pinning the roll at transaction creation ensures coherent multi-step behavior: for example, if the roll decides this transaction will fail at `SUBMIT` with `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL`, `INITIATE` succeeds normally (sending the OTP), and when `SUBMIT` arrives, it hangs as scheduled.

 You are implementing a safety-critical training and reference system for people who will move real money.  # PART I — PRODUCT DESIGN
 
 ## I-1. Why this is being rebuilt
 
 The current guide is a searchable list of ten short "books" plus three simulators. It reads like a feature tour. It assumes the reader already knows what a gateway, a ledger, an OTP, a webhook or AML is. A new employee cannot learn the platform from it, and nothing in it stops a tired operator from clicking the wrong button.
 
 The new Guide has three jobs, in this order of importance:
 
 1. **Prevent human error at the moment of action.** Every screen has a "?" drawer; every risky action shows a checklist before it executes.
 2. **Teach from zero.** Anyone who can read can understand the whole system, A to Z, with no prior knowledge. Every unfamiliar word is explained where it first appears and again in the glossary.
 3. **Be the reference during incidents.** Calm, step-by-step runbooks, a symptom-to-action playbook and a plain-language catalog of the 140 edge cases.
 
 ## I-2. Audience
 
 | Audience | What they need | How the guide serves them |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | Brand-new employee, any role, no background | Vocabulary, the big picture, safety rules | Book 0 → Book 1 → Book 2, glossary tooltips everywhere |
 | `OPERATOR`, `SUPPORT` | Daily queues, reading statuses, what to do about `UNKNOWN` | Books 3, 5, 7, 10 |
 | `FINANCE` | Ledger, settlement, cash-outs, refunds, disputes | Books 4, 7, 8 |
 | `COMPLIANCE`, `MLRO` | AML program, cases, reporting, confidentiality | Books 4, 5, 9 |
 | `GATEWAY_ADMIN`, `SECURITY_ADMIN` | Gateways, rails, routes, credentials, deployment, security | Books 4, 6, 11, 12 |
 | Management | One place to see the rules everybody is held to | Book 0 (Golden Rules), Book 4, Book 13 |
 
 All seven admin roles can open every article. Roles only change **recommendation** ("Recommended for you") and the reading path. The guide contains **no live data, no real thresholds, no real names, no secrets**; it explains rules, not records, so it is safe for everyone to read.
 
 ## I-3. Writing principles (already applied to PART III; use them to judge any future edit)
 
 1. **Zero assumed knowledge.** Define every term at first use, in a short parenthesis or sentence. Never write "obviously", "simply", "just".
 2. **Say who, where, what, why, and what if I get it wrong.** Instructions name the role, the exact screen, the exact button, the reason, and the recovery.
 3. **Short sentences, concrete numbers.** Use real examples (100 LYD, 3% commission) rather than abstractions.
 4. **One meaning per word.** The same concept is always called the same thing (see glossary). UI labels appear in **bold** exactly as on screen.
 5. **Honest about gaps.** If a feature exists in the design but has no screen yet, the article says so (`ui=NOT_YET` banner) and names who performs it today.
 6. **Safety first, in plain voice.** Warnings use the `warning` / `danger` callouts and explain the consequence, not just the rule.
 7. **No secrets, no live data, no external links.** The platform's admin side is LAN-only; the guide never links outside it.
 8. **Versioned.** Every build carries `contentVersion`; reading progress records the version read so a major change can request a re-read.
 
 ## I-4. Scope
 
 **In scope:** the Admin Guide (`/guide/**`), global command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K), contextual "?" drawer on every admin screen, safeguard checklists on risky actions, five simulators, glossary with auto-linking, symptom playbook, 140-case catalog, reading paths, read-tracking, English content (Arabic-ready).
 
 **Out of scope:** Merchant Guide, Checkout Help, any change to payment, ledger or engine behaviour, server-side search, analytics, external links, AI/LLM features.
 
 **Arabic:** the platform is Arabic-first (RTL). This file ships **English content in full** plus an Arabic term table (the `ar=` attribute in the glossary) so translation is consistent. The loader must support `articles.ar.json` and show English with a visible "Arabic version pending" chip until it exists (§II-8). Do **not** machine-translate; translation is a separate human-reviewed work package.

 ## II-2. Content format and the extractor
 
 ### II-2.1 Block syntax (everything in PART III uses exactly this)
 
 All content blocks begin with a line that starts with `@@` and end with `@@end` (except one-line `@@term` and `@@term`-style lines). **Attributes** are `key=value` or `key="value with spaces"`. Parsing rule for attributes: regex `([a-zA-Z_][\w-]*)=("([^"\\]|\\.)*"|[^\s]+)`.
 
 | Block | Opening line | Body | Closed by |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | Book | `@@book id=2 title="..." audience="..." summary="..."` | none | (single line) |
 | Article | `@@article id=b02-03 book=2 order=3 title="..." roles=ALL minutes=6 ui=AVAILABLE related=b07-01,b08-02` | Markdown | `@@end` |
 | Term | `@@term slug=ledger term="Ledger" aliases="books;general ledger" ar="دفتر الأستاذ" related=double-entry :: Short definition.` | none | (single line) |
 | Card | `@@card id=sg-approve-adjustment title="..." screen=Approvals risk=HIGH irreversible=true` | Markdown with 4 fixed bold headings (§II-7) | `@@end` |
 | Situation | `@@situation id=s-unknown-attempt title="..." screens=OperatorCases cases=5,8,20 articles=b07-03` | Markdown | `@@end` |
 | Path | `@@path role=OPERATOR title="..." :: b00-01,b00-03,...` (`role` is a staff role or `ALL` for the new-employee path) | none | (single line) |
 | Data | `@@data id=ledger-events` | one fenced ```json block | `@@end` |
 | Map | `@@map id=context-map` | one fenced ```json block | `@@end` |
 | FAQ | `@@faq id=q-001 article=b07-03` | first line `Q: ...` then answer text | `@@end` |
 
 Lines outside blocks (headings such as `### BOOK 4`, blank lines) are ignored. Inside `@@data` and `@@map` only the single fenced `json` block is read. `roles` is `ALL` or a comma list from `GATEWAY_ADMIN,SECURITY_ADMIN,FINANCE,OPERATOR,COMPLIANCE,MLRO,SUPPORT`. `ui` is `AVAILABLE`, `PARTIAL` or `NOT_YET`. IDs are lowercase `[a-z0-9-]`.
 
 ### II-2.2 Markdown dialect inside article bodies
 
 * CommonMark + tables (via `markdown-it`, `html:false`, `linkify:false`, `typographer:false`).
 * **Callout containers** (implemented by you as a small `markdown-it` core/block rule, no extra package): a line `:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::warning`, `:::danger`, `:::example`, `:::do`, `:::dont`, optionally followed by a title (`:::warning Never do this`), content lines, closing line `:::`. Render as `<aside class="callout callout-{type}" role="note">` with an icon and a visible type label (Note / Tip / Warning / Danger / Example / Do / Don't) — meaning must not rely on color alone.
 * **Widget placeholder:** a line `{{widget:ledger-explorer}}` (allowed ids: `transform-sandbox`, `crypto-lab`, `ledger-explorer`, `visible-rails`, `attempt-states`). Replaced by the component.
 * **Article link:** `[[a:b07-03]]` → link to the article using its title; `[[a:b07-03|custom text]]` → custom text. **Card link:** `[[c:sg-approve-adjustment]]`. **Situation link:** `[[s:s-unknown-attempt]]`. **Glossary link:** `[[g:ledger]]` (explicit; auto-linking also exists, §II-4).
 * Fenced code blocks tagged ` ```diagram ` render monospace, `dir="ltr"`, horizontally scrollable; they are used for text diagrams.
 * Headings inside articles start at `###` (the page supplies the `##` title). Every heading gets a stable id = slug of its text, de-duplicated with `-2`, `-3`.
 * Tables are wrapped in an `overflow-x:auto` container. No raw HTML, no images, no external links (an `http(s)://` link in content fails the content test).
 
 ### II-2.3 `scripts/extract-guide-content.ts` — required behaviour
 
 Run with `bun run content:guide`. Steps:
 
 1. Locate the design file: `design/guide_system_design_and_content.md` (relative to repo root, found via `../design/` from `admin-front`). If absent: print an error and exit 1.
 2. Read the file as UTF-8, normalise `\r\n` to `\n`. **Only parse content between the two marker lines `<!-- CONTENT:BEGIN -->` and `<!-- CONTENT:END -->` (each marker is a whole line by itself; mentions of them inside other text are not markers)** (markers exist in PART III).
 3. Parse blocks line by line with the grammar above. Unknown `@@` keywords, duplicate ids, a missing `@@end`, or an unparsable JSON fence → exit 1 with file line number.
 4. Validate cross-references: every `related`, `[[a:]]`, `[[c:]]`, `[[s:]]`, `[[g:]]`, `articles=`, `article=`, path entry and context-map id must exist.
 5. Emit into `src/content/guide/generated/`: `books.json`, `articles.en.json` (array of `{id, book, order, title, roles, minutes, ui, related, body, headings[], plainText}`), `glossary.en.json`, `cards.en.json` (with parsed `checklist: string[]` from lines beginning `- [ ] `), `playbook.en.json`, `paths.json`, `faq.en.json`, `data.json` (`{ [id]: parsedJson }`), `context-map.json`, `meta.json` (`{contentVersion, generatedAt, counts, sourceSha256}`). `contentVersion` is the value of the `<!-- CONTENT_VERSION: x.y.z -->` marker (initially `1.0.0`).
 6. Also generate `error-codes.en.json` from article `b13-01`: for every table row whose first cell is a single backticked token, emit `{code, where, meaning, action}` (the four cells, markdown stripped). Then generate `edge-cases.en.json` by parsing the 140-row tables of Section 13 of the repository file matched by glob `design/payment-gateway-refined-design-v4*.md` (the file in the repo is named `payment-gateway-refined-design-v4.1.md`). Row format: `| **N** | scenario | resolution | severity |`; group headings are `### **Group X: Name (Cases a–b)**`. Strip markdown bold and backslash escapes (`\_`, `\#`, `\\+`, `\\-`). Output `{n, group, groupName, scenario, resolution, severity}`; must yield exactly **140** rows or exit 1.
 7. Generated files are **committed**. A unit test (§II-10) re-runs the extractor in a temp dir and asserts byte equality with the committed output, so a design edit without regeneration fails CI.

 ## II-3. Loading, routing, layout
 
 * Content JSON is loaded with dynamic `import()` so it is not in the main bundle. Total gzip size of all generated JSON must stay below 400 KB (test asserts).
 * Routes are added to the explicit `createRouter` table in `src/router/index.ts` (the project does not use file-based routing for admin). Names: `AdminGuide`, `AdminGuideBook`, `AdminGuideArticle`, `AdminGuideGlossary`, `AdminGuideTools`, `AdminGuidePlaybook`, `AdminGuideCards`, `AdminGuideEdgeCases`. They need **no** authority (`routesAuthorities` entry `[]`), because every admin must be able to read the guide.
 * Layout of an article page (desktop ≥ 1280px): left = book outline (collapsible), centre = article (max width 820px, line-height 1.7, base font 16px), right = "On this page" TOC. Below 960px: single column, TOC becomes a collapsible panel at the top. The page must work in RTL and LTR (use logical CSS properties: `margin-inline-start`, etc.). Text diagrams stay LTR.
 * Every article page shows: breadcrumb (Guide › Book › Article), reading time (`minutes`), "Recommended for" role chips, `UiStatusBanner` when `ui` is not `AVAILABLE`, content version + "Report a problem" (copies `article id + contentVersion + screen URL` to clipboard; no network), `ReadToggle` ("Mark as read", also auto-marks when the reader has scrolled to the end and spent ≥ 25% of `minutes` on the page), previous/next, and "Related" list.
 
 ## II-4. Glossary auto-linking and popovers
 
 * Build a matcher from every term's `term` and `aliases` (case-insensitive, whole word, longest match first; Arabic and Latin boundaries handled with Unicode-aware lookarounds).
 * When rendering an article body, wrap the **first occurrence per article** of each term in `<button class="gl-term" data-slug="...">`. Do **not** wrap inside headings, code, links, table header cells, callout titles, or the term's own glossary page.
 * Click/Enter/Space opens a popover (`role="dialog"`, focus-trapped, Esc closes): term, `short` definition, Arabic term (if any), "Open in glossary", related terms. It never navigates away by itself. Hover alone must not be the only way to read the definition (touch/keyboard users).
 
 ## II-5. Search and command palette
 
 * Index with `minisearch`: fields `title` (boost 5), `headings` (3), `aliases` (4), `plainText` (1); options `prefix:true`, `fuzzy:0.2`, `combineWith:"AND"` falling back to `"OR"` if zero results. Document types: `article`, `term`, `card`, `situation`, `edge-case`, `faq`, `error-code` (the codes in article b13-01).
 * Normalise **both** index text and query: lowercase; strip Arabic diacritics and tatweel; unify alef variants (أ إ آ → ا), ya/alef-maqsura (ى → ي), ta-marbuta (ة → ه); convert Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII (reuse `src/utils/arabic.ts`). Underscores in codes are searchable with or without (`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `limit exceeded`).
 * Results are grouped by type with the type name visible; max 8 per type; keyboard: ↑ ↓ Enter, Esc closes, Tab moves between groups. Empty query shows "Recent" (last 8 opened, stored in `localStorage` key `pg.guide.recent`, wrapped in try/catch) and the five most-read **Golden Rule** articles.
 * The index is built lazily on first palette open (target < 150 ms for the full corpus; test measures the build and fails above 1000 ms on CI).
 * Palette is global: mounted in `layouts/default.tsx`; shortcut Ctrl+K / Cmd+K; also a magnifier button in the app bar for touch users. It must not open while the user is typing in an input unless they press the shortcut explicitly.

 ### II-13.3 `ledger-explorer` (T-accounts)
 
 Data: the 16 events in `@@data id=ledger-events` (§III-F.1). Inputs: link amount `A` (default `100`), commission rate `rate` percent (default `3`), gateway fee `fee` (default `0.8`), provider fee `provFee` (default `1`), surcharge `sur` (default = commission when the event says so), wallet start balance (event 15 only, default `40`). Derived: `comm = round4(A × rate / 100)` (ROUND_HALF_UP). Amount expressions are `IDENT ((+|-) IDENT)*` over the variable names (`A, comm, fee, provFee, sur, net, var, hold, walletStart`); evaluate with a tiny tokenizer + `Decimal`, **no eval**. Show each journal entry as two columns (Debit | Credit) per GL account, with totals and a green **Balanced** / red **NOT BALANCED** badge (Σdebit == Σcredit to 4 decimals), plus a running check of the system-wide equation using the account classes in the data file. Include an "Explain" sentence per line (`why` field). Each event contains one or more `entries` (separately balanced journal entries, for example confirmation then release); show each, then the cumulative equation after the whole event. `derived` formulas are evaluated in order; `sur` defaults to the computed `comm`; `showBalance` (event E15) adds one extra displayed line. Default-value expectation: every event balances; the equation holds after each event starting from zero balances. Vector: event `E02` with defaults must produce debits `GATEWAY_CLEARING 100.0000`, `GATEWAY_FEE_EXPENSE 0.8000`; credits `MERCHANT_WALLET 97.0000`, `PLATFORM_INCOME 3.0000`, `GATEWAY_FEE_ACCRUAL 0.8000`; totals `100.8000` each.
 
 ### II-13.4 `visible-rails` and `attempt-states`
 
 * `visible-rails`: implements the 9-predicate resolution from the data block `visible-rails` (§III-F.2). The user changes link amount, currency, the application's rail whitelist, time of day, and each sample route's status/health/limits. For each rail the tool shows **Visible** or **Hidden because:** followed by the first failing predicate in plain language. Vectors in the data block (`vectors` array) must pass.
 * `attempt-states`: implements the teaching transition table in `@@data id=attempt-transitions`. The user clicks events (e.g., "Customer enters wrong OTP", "Gateway times out on confirm"; an event with `to:"SAME"` leaves the state unchanged and only shows its note); the tool shows the new state, whether the link slot is still reserved, whether money was posted, and what a human should do. States not reachable by an event are disabled. The tool states: "Teaching model — the real engine in `core-back` is authoritative."

 @@article id=b00-01 book=0 order=1 title="Welcome: what this system is and why this guide exists" roles=ALL minutes=2 ui=AVAILABLE related=b00-02,b00-03,b02-01
 ### In one sentence
 This platform lets shops and businesses in Libya accept payments from many different payment methods through one single system, and keeps exact, auditable records of every dinar that moves.
 
 ### What the platform does
 A customer wants to pay a shop. The customer might use a mobile wallet, a bank app, a card, or a code sent by SMS. Each of those is run by a different company with different technical rules. The platform sits in the middle: the shop connects once to us, and we connect to all the others. The customer sees a simple payment page. Behind it, our system talks to the right payment company, waits for a trustworthy answer, and then writes the money movement into our books.
 
 ### Why a guide this long?
 Because the work is serious. The people reading this may be new to payments, to accounting, to compliance or to software. A wrong click can pay the wrong person, release held money, or tell a suspect that we are investigating them. This guide exists so that **nobody has to guess**.
 
 ### What you will find
 * **Books 1–2** explain the world from zero: payments, computers, trust, money records, compliance, and the parts of our platform.
 * **Books 3–5** teach you how to work in the Back Office, how approvals work, and how merchants are handled.
 * **Books 6–9** go deep: gateways, payments, the ledger (our accounting books), and anti-money-laundering.
 * **Books 10–12** are for emergencies, security and hosting.
 * **Book 13** is a reference: tables, codes, a symptom playbook and quick answers.
 
 :::tip How to start
 If today is your first day, read Book 0 and Book 1 in order. They take about two hours and make everything else easier. Then follow the reading path for your role (button on the guide home page).
 :::

 @@article id=b00-03 book=0 order=3 title="The Ten Golden Rules" roles=ALL minutes=3 ui=AVAILABLE related=b04-01,b07-03,b09-08,b11-03
 Every rule here exists because someone, somewhere, lost money or trust by breaking it. Read them until you can say them without looking.
 
 1. **Never share your password, your one-time codes, or your session.** Not with your manager, not with IT, not with "support". Nobody legitimate will ever ask.
 2. **Never approve something you cannot explain in one sentence.** If you do not understand what the request will change, reject it with a reason or ask the person who made it.
 3. **Never approve your own work, and never help someone get around the two-person rule.** The system blocks the same account from approving its own request. Asking a colleague to click "Approve" without reading is the same offence.
 4. **Amounts come only from the system.** Never take an amount from a customer's message, screenshot, phone call or email. The platform reads the amount from the payment link in its own database.
 5. **A page saying "Paid" proves nothing.** Customers' screens, return links and browser messages can be faked. Only a payment that our server has verified with the payment company counts. Never tell a customer "your payment is confirmed" from a screenshot.
 6. **`UNKNOWN` means we do not know. Never guess.** Do not mark it failed because it is old. Do not ask the customer to pay again. Do not re-send an OTP. Use **Inquire**, then follow Book 7.
 7. **Never reveal or hint that an anti-money-laundering review exists.** Not to a merchant, not to a customer, not to a colleague who has no need to know. This is called *tipping-off* and it can be a crime.
 8. **Never paste secrets anywhere.** API keys, tokens, passwords, certificate keys, card numbers, OTPs do not belong in chat, email, tickets, screenshots or this guide.
 9. **Always write a real reason.** "ok" or "as discussed" is not a reason. A good reason says what you checked and why you decided (Book 4, article on reasons).
 10. **When unsure, stop and escalate.** Being slow is acceptable. Being wrong with other people's money is not. Never "fix" books by editing numbers; corrections are new, approved entries.
 
 :::danger Rules 1, 6 and 7 are the most common serious breaches
 If you remember nothing else: do not share credentials, do not guess on `UNKNOWN`, do not tip off.
 :::
 @@end
