 # pg-backup-daemon
 
 The backup and point-in-time-recovery control plane for the PostgreSQL 18 storage tier. The daemon
 wraps WAL-G or Barman, keeps a backup/drill catalog, exposes an mTLS HTTP API, and runs the
 scratch-restore + ledger-invariant drill.
 
 - Runtime: Bun + TypeScript.
 - Default listener: `127.0.0.1:4090` (`/health` is the liveness probe).
-- Configuration: environment variables validated by `src/config.ts`; see
-  `backup.env.example`.
+- Configuration: environment variables validated by `src/config.ts`. In a
+  deployment the entire daemon environment is generated automatically by
+  `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts` from `deploy/deploy.env`;
+  `backup.env.example` is the local/troubleshooting reference, not a manual
+  production step.
 - Storage targets: primary S3/MinIO/R2 (WAL-G or Barman Cloud) and an optional secondary remote
   SSH/S3 target.
 - Drills restore the core into `BACKUP_SCRATCH_DIR`/`BACKUP_SCRATCH_PORT` and the dedicated audit
   database into `BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_DIR`/`BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_PORT`, then check double-entry zero
   drift, sharded balance parity and the audit hash chain.
 - The in-process scheduler owns the full/delta/drill cron. Policy changes made through
   `PUT /v1/policy` take effect without a restart. Set `SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` only when an
   external `/etc/cron.d/pg-backup` drives the trigger script instead.
 
 ## Commands
 
 ```bash
 bun install
 bun run start       # bun run src/index.ts
 bun run typecheck   # bunx --bun tsc --noEmit
 bun test
 ```
 
 ## HTTP API
 
 The daemon serves these routes after the mTLS listener starts:
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `GET` | `/health` | Liveness and the active engine mode. |
 | `GET` | `/v1/overview` | Engine mode, WAL health, storage targets, schedule/policy, recent backups and drills. |
 | `POST` | `/v1/backups/trigger` | Queue a backup; body `{ "target": "all" \| "postgres_core" \| "audit_db" \| "redis", "kind": "full" \| "delta" }`. |
 | `PUT` | `/v1/policy` | Update the full/delta/drill cron, retention days and alert lag. |
 | `GET` | `/v1/runs` | Recent backup runs (`?limit=`). |
 | `POST` | `/v1/drills/run` | Queue a restore + invariant drill. |
 | `GET` | `/v1/drills` | Recent drill reports (`?limit=`). |
 
 `core-back` reaches these routes through `BACKUP_DAEMON_URL` (an `https://` URL) and proxies the
 administrator surface as `/api/v1/admin/system/backups/*`.
 
 ## Configuration
 
 All keys below are read from the process environment. `src/config.ts` is the source of truth.
 
 ### Engine and encryption
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `BACKUP_ENGINE_MODE` | yes | — | `wal-g` or `barman`. |
 | `BACKUP_COMPRESSION` | no | `zstd` | `zstd`, `lz4`, `lzma`, `brotli` or `none`. |
 | `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX` | yes | — | Hex key, at least 16 bytes (32 hex characters), even length. Used for encryption and drill-report signing. |
 | `BACKUP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP` | no | `false` | Allow a plain-HTTP listener instead of mTLS (development only). |
 | `BACKUP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` | no | `1800000` | Timeout for a WAL-G/Barman/pg command (30 minutes). |
 
 ### Primary S3 target and optional secondary vault
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT` | yes | — | S3/MinIO/R2 endpoint URL. |
 | `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_BUCKET` | yes | — | Primary bucket/prefix (for example `s3://payment-gateway-backups/prod`). |
 | `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ACCESS_KEY` | no | empty | S3 access key; must be supplied together with the secret key. |
 | `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_SECRET_KEY` | no | empty | S3 secret key; must be supplied together with the access key. |
 | `BACKUP_CORE_S3_PREFIX` | no | `<bucket>/postgres_core` | WAL-G prefix for the core database. |
 | `BACKUP_AUDIT_S3_PREFIX` | no | `<bucket>/audit_db` | WAL-G prefix for the audit database. |
 | `BACKUP_SECONDARY_SSH_TARGET` | no | empty | Optional secondary vault (`user@host:/path`). |
 
 ### Schedule, retention and alerts
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `BACKUP_FULL_CRON` | no | `0 2 * * 0` | Five-field full-backup cron. |
 | `BACKUP_DELTA_CRON` | no | `0 2 * * 1-6` | Five-field delta-backup cron. |
 | `BACKUP_DRILL_CRON` | no | `0 4 * * 0` | Five-field restore/invariant drill cron. |
 | `BACKUP_RETENTION_FULL_COUNT` | no | `8` | Full backups retained. |
 | `BACKUP_RETENTION_WAL_DAYS` | no | `14` | WAL archive retention in days. |
 | `BACKUP_ALERT_LAG_SECONDS` | no | `300` | WAL archive lag that marks the daemon unhealthy. |
 | `SCHEDULER_ENABLED` | no | `true` | Run the in-process full/delta/drill scheduler. |
 | `SCHEDULER_TICK_MS` | no | `30000` | Scheduler evaluation cadence. |
 
 ### Listener and mTLS
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `BACKUP_DAEMON_PORT` | no | `4090` | Control-plane listener port. |
 | `BACKUP_DAEMON_BIND_HOST` | no | `127.0.0.1` | Listener bind address. |
 | `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_PATH` | no | — | Server certificate path; must be supplied with the key. |
 | `BACKUP_DAEMON_KEY_PATH` | no | — | Server private key path; must be supplied with the certificate. |
 | `BACKUP_DAEMON_CA_CERT_PATH` | no | — | Client CA path; requires the certificate and key as well. |
 
 By default the listener requires a certificate/key pair and refuses to start without one. Set
 `BACKUP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true` only for local tests/development to serve plain HTTP. Provide all
 three mTLS keys for the production control plane.
 
 ### PostgreSQL 18 connection and paths
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `PG_PRIMARY_HOST` | no | `127.0.0.1` | PostgreSQL primary host. |
 | `PG_PRIMARY_PORT` | no | `5432` | PostgreSQL primary port. |
 | `PG_PRIMARY_USER` | no | `postgres` | Backup/restore role. |
 | `PG_PRIMARY_PASSWORD` | no | empty | Backup/restore role password. |
 | `PG_PRIMARY_DB_NAME` | no | `payment_gateway_prod` | Core database name. |
 | `PG_AUDIT_DB_NAME` | no | `pg_audit_db` | Audit database name. |
 | `PG_REPLICA_NODES` | no | empty | Comma-separated replica identifiers/hosts used by the engine. |
 | `PG_DATA_DIR` | no | `/var/lib/postgresql/18/main` | Primary data directory. |
 | `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` | no | — | Optional audit database data directory. |
 | `PG_BIN_DIR` | no | `/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin` | PostgreSQL 18 binaries (`pg_ctl`, `initdb`, `psql`, …). |
 | `WALG_BIN` | no | `wal-g` | WAL-G binary. |
 | `BARMAN_BIN` | no | `barman` | Barman binary. |
 | `BARMAN_CLOUD_BIN` | no | `barman-cloud-backup` | Barman Cloud binary. |
 | `BARMAN_SERVER` | no | — | Optional Barman server name for the core database. |
 | `BARMAN_AUDIT_SERVER` | no | `PG_AUDIT_DB_NAME` | Barman server name for the audit database. |
 | `PGPASSFILE` | no | — | Libpq password file used by Barman for the replication role. |
 | `BACKUP_CATALOG_PATH` | no | `/var/lib/pg-backup/catalog.json` | Backup/drill catalog file. |
 | `BACKUP_SCRATCH_DIR` | no | `/var/lib/pg-backup/scratch` | Core restore target for drills. |
 | `BACKUP_SCRATCH_PORT` | no | `55432` | Core scratch PostgreSQL port. |
 | `BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_DIR` | no | `<scratch>/audit` | Audit restore target for drills. |
 | `BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_PORT` | no | `55433` | Audit scratch PostgreSQL port. |
 
 ### Redis snapshot support
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Meaning |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `REDIS_URL` | no | — | Redis URL when the `redis` backup target is used. |
 | `REDIS_CLI_BIN` | no | `redis-cli` | Redis CLI binary. |
 
 ## Deployment note
 
 `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts` writes the daemon environment file
-`/etc/pg-backup/backup.env`. Keep its key names aligned with `src/config.ts`; in particular the
+`/etc/pg-backup/backup.env` from `deploy/deploy.env`, then `deploy/deploy.ts` syncs

 #

 # one host can carry several roles (development/staging) or every tier can be
 # distributed across dedicated hosts (production). A compute tier scales from
 # one node to N nodes by adding comma-separated entries to its *_NODES array.
 #
 # Multi-node format (all *_NODES arrays, PG_PRIMARY_NODE, PG_REPLICA_NODES,
 # REDIS_NODES, AUDIT_DB_NODE, LOG_DB_NODE and BACKUP_NODE):

  * The multi-host deployment configuration.
  *
  * `deploy/deploy.env` is parsed by this schema. Everything is validated before
  * a single SSH connection is opened: a typo in an IP address must fail on the
  * operator's machine, not halfway through a production deploy.
  */
 
 const ipv4 = z
   .string()
   .trim()
   .regex(/^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/, "must be an IPv4 address")
   .refine((value) => value.split(".").every((octet) => Number(octet) >= 0 && Number(octet) <= 255), "octet out of range");
 
 const cidrList = z
   .string()
   .trim()
   .min(1)
   .refine((value) => {
     return value.split(",").every((entry) => {
       const [address, bits] = entry.trim().split("/");
       if (!address || bits === undefined) return false;
       const isV4 = /^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/.test(address);
       const isV6 = /^[0-9a-fA-F:]+$/.test(address);
       const width = Number(bits);
       if (!Number.isInteger(width)) return false;
       return isV4 ? width >= 0 && width <= 32 : isV6 && width >= 0 && width <= 128;
     });
   }, "must be a comma separated list of CIDRs (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.0.0/16)");

 /**
  * One entry of a horizontal node array:
  *
  *   nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
  *
  * `sshHost` is the address the orchestrator connects to (it may be public),
  * `privateIp` is the LAN address the node advertises to its peers (it is the
  * address written into TLS SANs and firewall allowlists), and `servicePort` is
  * the port the application/storage daemon listens on.
  */
 export interface NodeSpec {
   nodeId: string;
   sshHost: string;
   sshPort: number;
   privateIp: string;
   servicePort: number;
 }
 
 const NODE_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$/;
 const IPV4 = /^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/;
 
 const validateIpv4 = (value: string, label: string): void => {
   if (!IPV4.test(value) || value.split(".").some((octet) => Number(octet) < 0 || Number(octet) > 255)) {
     throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' must be an IPv4 address`);
   }
 };
 
 const parsePort = (value: string, label: string): number => {
   if (!/^\d+$/.test(value)) throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' must be a port number`);
   const port = Number(value);
   if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' is out of range`);
   return port;
 };
 
 /**
  * Parses a comma separated horizontal node list and rejects malformed entries,
  * duplicate node ids and duplicate private IPs *within the same list*.
  */
 export const parseNodeList = (value: string | undefined | null): NodeSpec[] => {
   if (!value || value.trim().length === 0) return [];
   const nodes: NodeSpec[] = [];
   const ids = new Set<string>();
   const ips = new Set<string>();
   for (const rawEntry of value.split(",")) {
     const entry = rawEntry.trim();
     if (entry.length === 0) continue;
     const at = entry.indexOf("@");
     if (at <= 0 || at === entry.length - 1) {
       throw new Error(`node '${entry}' must use nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`);
     }
     const nodeId = entry.slice(0, at).trim();
     const parts = entry.slice(at + 1).split(":");
     if (parts.length !== 4) {
       throw new Error(`node '${entry}' must have exactly sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort after '@'`);
     }
     const [sshHostRaw, sshPortRaw, privateIpRaw, servicePortRaw] = parts as [string, string, string, string];
     const sshHost = sshHostRaw.trim();
     const privateIp = privateIpRaw.trim();
     if (!NODE_ID.test(nodeId)) throw new Error(`node id '${nodeId}' is invalid`);
     validateIpv4(sshHost, `node '${nodeId}' sshHost`);
     validateIpv4(privateIp, `node '${nodeId}' privateIp`);
     const sshPort = parsePort(sshPortRaw.trim(), `node '${nodeId}' sshPort`);
     const servicePort = parsePort(servicePortRaw.trim(), `node '${nodeId}' servicePort`);
     if (ids.has(nodeId)) throw new Error(`duplicate node id '${nodeId}'`);
     if (ips.has(privateIp)) throw new Error(`duplicate private IP '${privateIp}' in node list`);
     ids.add(nodeId);
     ips.add(privateIp);
     nodes.push({ nodeId, sshHost, sshPort, privateIp, servicePort });
   }
   return nodes;
 };

 export type DeployConfig = z.infer<typeof base>;
 
 /** True when any PostgreSQL 18 storage field is configured. */
 export const pgStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
   config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH
   || config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE.trim().length > 0
   || config.PG_REPLICA_NODES.trim().length > 0
   || config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length > 0;
 
 export const redisStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
   config.REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || parseNodeList(config.REDIS_NODES).length > 0;
 
 export const auditDbConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
   config.AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.AUDIT_DB_NODE.trim().length > 0;
 
 export const logDbConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
   config.LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.LOG_DB_NODE.trim().length > 0;
 
 export const backupStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
   config.BACKUP_ENABLED || config.BACKUP_NODE.trim().length > 0;
 
 /**
  * The core upstream URLs every edge service receives. The helper is the single
  * source of truth: an explicit CORE_BACK_URLS wins, otherwise the core node
  * array, otherwise the legacy single-host fields.
  */
 export const edgeCoreUrls = (config: DeployConfig): string[] => {
   if (config.CORE_BACK_URLS && config.CORE_BACK_URLS.trim().length > 0) {
     return config.CORE_BACK_URLS.split(",").map((entry) => entry.trim()).filter((entry) => entry.length > 0);
   }
   const coreNodes = parseNodeList(config.CORE_NODES);
   if (coreNodes.length > 0) {
     return coreNodes.map((node) => `https://${node.privateIp}:${node.servicePort}`);
   }
   if (config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP) {
     return [`https://${config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP}:${config.CORE_PORT}`];
   }
   return [];
 };
 
 /** The effective relational database (legacy DB_* or the PG 18 settings). */
 export const effectiveDatabase = (config: DeployConfig): {
   engine: DeployConfig["DB_ENGINE"];
   host: string | null;
   port: number;
   name: string;
   user: string;
   password: string;
   url: string | null;
   privateIp: string | null;
   managedViaSsh: boolean;
 } => {
   const primary = parseNodeList(config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE)[0] ?? null;
   const pg = pgStorageConfigured(config);
   // When the PostgreSQL 18 storage tier is configured its credentials are
   // authoritative; the legacy DB_* block is only a compatibility path for an
   // externally managed database.
   const name = pg ? config.PG_DB_NAME : (config.DB_NAME ?? config.PG_DB_NAME);
   const user = pg ? config.PG_DB_USER : (config.DB_USER ?? config.PG_DB_USER);
   const password = pg ? config.PG_DB_PASSWORD : (config.DB_PASSWORD ?? config.PG_DB_PASSWORD);
   const host = primary?.privateIp ?? config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? null;
   const port = primary?.servicePort ?? config.DB_PORT;
   const derivedPort = config.PGBOUNCER_ENABLED ? config.PGBOUNCER_PORT : port;
   const url = pg && host
     ? `postgresql://${encodeURIComponent(user)}:${encodeURIComponent(password)}@${host}:${derivedPort}/${name}`
     : (config.DATABASE_URL ?? null);
   return {
     engine: config.DB_ENGINE,
     host,
     port,
     name,
     user,
     password,
     url,
     privateIp: pg ? (primary?.privateIp ?? config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? null) : (config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? primary?.privateIp ?? null),
     managedViaSsh: config.DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH,
   };
 };
 
 /**
  * Cross-field rules. A value can be valid in isolation and still make the
  * topology impossible (the database URL not matching the engine, a certbot
  * domain with no certificate path, a database host with no SSH target, …).
  */
 export const validateDeployConfig = (config: DeployConfig): string[] => {
   const problems: string[] = [];
   const pgConfigured = pgStorageConfigured(config);
 
   if (pgConfigured && config.DB_ENGINE !== "postgresql") {
     problems.push("DB_ENGINE must be 'postgresql' when PostgreSQL 18 storage fields are configured");
   }
   const replicaNodes = (() => {
     try {
       return parseNodeList(config.PG_REPLICA_NODES);
     } catch (error) {
       problems.push(`PG_REPLICA_NODES: ${(error as Error).message}`);
       return [];
     }
   })();
   const primaryNodes = (() => {
     try {
       return parseNodeList(config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE);
     } catch (error) {
       problems.push(`PG_PRIMARY_NODE: ${(error as Error).message}`);
       return [];
     }
   })();
   if (primaryNodes.length > 1) problems.push("PG_PRIMARY_NODE must describe exactly one primary");
   if (replicaNodes.length > 0 && primaryNodes.length === 0) {
     problems.push("PG_REPLICA_NODES requires PG_PRIMARY_NODE");
   }
   if (config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH) {
     if (primaryNodes.length === 0) problems.push("PG_PRIMARY_NODE is required when PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.PG_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("PG_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length === 0) problems.push("PG_DB_PASSWORD is required when PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
   }
   if (pgConfigured && config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length > 0 && config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length < 8) {
     problems.push("PG_DB_PASSWORD must be at least 8 characters");
   }
   if (config.PGBOUNCER_ENABLED && !pgConfigured) {
     problems.push("PGBOUNCER_ENABLED requires the PostgreSQL 18 storage fields");
   }
 
   if (config.DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH && !pgConfigured) {
     if (!config.DB_SSH_HOST) problems.push("DB_SSH_HOST is required when DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.DB_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("DB_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.DB_PRIVATE_IP) problems.push("DB_PRIVATE_IP is required when DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
   }
 
   if (!pgConfigured) {
     if (!config.DB_NAME) problems.push("DB_NAME is required");
     if (!config.DB_USER) problems.push("DB_USER is required");
     if (!config.DB_PASSWORD) problems.push("DB_PASSWORD is required");
     if (!config.DATABASE_URL) problems.push("DATABASE_URL is required");
   }
   if (config.DATABASE_URL) {
     const enginePrefix = "postgresql://";
     if (!config.DATABASE_URL.startsWith(enginePrefix)) {
       problems.push(`DATABASE_URL must start with ${enginePrefix} (DB_ENGINE=${config.DB_ENGINE})`);
     }
     if (config.DB_PRIVATE_IP && !config.DATABASE_URL.includes(config.DB_PRIVATE_IP)) {
       problems.push("DATABASE_URL should point at DB_PRIVATE_IP");
     }
   }
   // A single-box installation legitimately co-locates the database with the
   // core (the database binds to 127.0.0.1 and is never exposed); on separate
   // nodes the operator points DATABASE_URL at the database host's private IP.
 
   // --- Horizontal compute node arrays -------------------------------------
   const tiers = [
     { name: "CORE_NODES", value: config.CORE_NODES, legacy: [["CORE_SSH_HOST", config.CORE_SSH_HOST], ["CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["CORE_PRIVATE_IP", config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP]] },
     { name: "ADMIN_NODES", value: config.ADMIN_NODES, legacy: [["ADMIN_SSH_HOST", config.ADMIN_SSH_HOST], ["ADMIN_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.ADMIN_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["ADMIN_PRIVATE_IP", config.ADMIN_PRIVATE_IP]] },
     { name: "MERCHANT_NODES", value: config.MERCHANT_NODES, legacy: [["MERCHANT_SSH_HOST", config.MERCHANT_SSH_HOST], ["MERCHANT_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.MERCHANT_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["MERCHANT_PRIVATE_IP", config.MERCHANT_PRIVATE_IP]] },
     { name: "CHECKOUT_NODES", value: config.CHECKOUT_NODES, legacy: [["CHECKOUT_SSH_HOST", config.CHECKOUT_SSH_HOST], ["CHECKOUT_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.CHECKOUT_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP", config.CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP]] },
   ];
   for (const [name, value, keyPath] of [
     ["CORE_NODES", config.CORE_NODES, config.CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH],
     ["ADMIN_NODES", config.ADMIN_NODES, config.ADMIN_SSH_KEY_PATH],
     ["MERCHANT_NODES", config.MERCHANT_NODES, config.MERCHANT_SSH_KEY_PATH],
     ["CHECKOUT_NODES", config.CHECKOUT_NODES, config.CHECKOUT_SSH_KEY_PATH],
   ] as const) {
     if (value.trim().length > 0 && !keyPath) {
       problems.push(`${name} requires the matching *_SSH_KEY_PATH`);
     }
   }
   const parsedTiers = new Map<string, NodeSpec[]>();
   for (const tier of tiers) {
     if (tier.value.trim().length === 0) {
       for (const [field, value] of tier.legacy) {
         if (!value) problems.push(`${field} is required when ${tier.name} is empty`);
       }
       parsedTiers.set(tier.name, []);
       continue;
     }
     try {
       parsedTiers.set(tier.name, parseNodeList(tier.value));
     } catch (error) {
       problems.push(`${tier.name}: ${(error as Error).message}`);
       parsedTiers.set(tier.name, []);
     }
   }
 
   // --- Storage node arrays / single nodes ---------------------------------
   const storageNodes: Array<{ label: string; nodes: NodeSpec[] }> = [];
   for (const [label, value] of [
     ["PG_PRIMARY_NODE", config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE],
     ["PG_REPLICA_NODES", config.PG_REPLICA_NODES],
     ["REDIS_NODES", config.REDIS_NODES],
     ["AUDIT_DB_NODE", config.AUDIT_DB_NODE],
     ["LOG_DB_NODE", config.LOG_DB_NODE],
     ["BACKUP_NODE", config.BACKUP_NODE],
   ] as const) {
     storageNodes.push({ label, nodes: label === "PG_PRIMARY_NODE" ? primaryNodes : label === "PG_REPLICA_NODES" ? replicaNodes : (() => {
       try {
         return parseNodeList(value);
       } catch (error) {
         problems.push(`${label}: ${(error as Error).message}`);
         return [];
       }
     })() });
   }
   if (config.REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH) {
     const redisNodes = storageNodes.find((entry) => entry.label === "REDIS_NODES")?.nodes ?? [];
     if (redisNodes.length === 0) problems.push("REDIS_NODES is required when REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.REDIS_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("REDIS_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.REDIS_PASSWORD) problems.push("REDIS_PASSWORD is required when REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
   }
   if (config.AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH) {
     if (!config.AUDIT_DB_NODE) problems.push("AUDIT_DB_NODE is required when AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.AUDIT_DB_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("AUDIT_DB_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.AUDIT_DB_PASSWORD) problems.push("AUDIT_DB_PASSWORD is required when AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
   }
   if (config.LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH) {
     if (!config.LOG_DB_NODE) problems.push("LOG_DB_NODE is required when LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.LOG_DB_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("LOG_DB_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
     if (!config.LOG_DB_PASSWORD) problems.push("LOG_DB_PASSWORD is required when LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
   }
   if (config.BACKUP_ENABLED) {
     if (!config.BACKUP_NODE) problems.push("BACKUP_NODE is required when BACKUP_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.BACKUP_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("BACKUP_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when BACKUP_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_BUCKET) problems.push("BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_BUCKET is required when BACKUP_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX) problems.push("BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX is required when BACKUP_ENABLED=true");
     const endpointIsHttpUrl = (() => {
       try {
         const endpoint = new URL(config.BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT);
         return (endpoint.protocol === "http:" || endpoint.protocol === "https:") && endpoint.hostname.length > 0;
       } catch {
         return false;
       }
     })();
     if (!endpointIsHttpUrl) {
       problems.push("BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT must be an absolute http(s) URL when BACKUP_ENABLED=true");
     }
     const backupNodes = (() => {
       try {
         return parseNodeList(config.BACKUP_NODE);
       } catch {
         return [];
       }
     })();
     const auditNodes = (() => {
       try {
         return parseNodeList(config.AUDIT_DB_NODE);
       } catch {
         return [];
       }
     })();
     const backupIp = backupNodes[0]?.privateIp;
     const primaryIp = primaryNodes[0]?.privateIp;
     if (config.BACKUP_ENGINE_MODE === "wal-g") {
       if (backupIp && primaryIp && backupIp !== primaryIp) {
         problems.push("BACKUP_NODE private IP must equal PG_PRIMARY_NODE private IP when BACKUP_ENGINE_MODE=wal-g (WAL-G reads the local data directory)");
       }
       const auditIp = auditNodes[0]?.privateIp;
       if (backupIp && auditIp && auditIp !== backupIp && config.PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR.trim().length === 0) {
         problems.push("PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR is required when the audit database is on a different host from the WAL-G backup node");
       }
     }
   }
   // Node ids are unique across the whole plan; private IPs are unique within a
   // tier (co-locating different tiers on one box remains supported).
   const allNodes = [...parsedTiers.values(), ...storageNodes.map((entry) => entry.nodes)].flat();
   const duplicateIds = new Set<string>();
   const seenIds = new Set<string>();
   for (const node of allNodes) {
     if (seenIds.has(node.nodeId)) duplicateIds.add(node.nodeId);
     seenIds.add(node.nodeId);
   }
   for (const id of duplicateIds) problems.push(`node id '${id}' is used more than once across the node lists`);
 
   const pgIps = [...primaryNodes, ...replicaNodes].map((node) => node.privateIp);
   const duplicatePgIps = new Set<string>();
   const seenPgIps = new Set<string>();
   for (const ip of pgIps) {
     if (seenPgIps.has(ip)) duplicatePgIps.add(ip);
     seenPgIps.add(ip);
   }
   for (const ip of duplicatePgIps) problems.push(`PostgreSQL primary/replica private IP '${ip}' is used more than once`);
 
   // The same SSH endpoint cannot host two compute roles on the same port.
   const endpointPorts = new Map<string, Map<number, string>>();
   for (const [label, nodes] of parsedTiers) {
     for (const node of nodes) {
       const endpoint = `${node.sshHost}:${node.sshPort}`;
       const ports = endpointPorts.get(endpoint) ?? new Map<number, string>();
       const owner = ports.get(node.servicePort);
       if (owner && owner !== `${label}:${node.nodeId}`) {
         problems.push(`port ${node.servicePort} on ${endpoint} is requested by both ${owner} and ${label}:${node.nodeId}`);
       }
       ports.set(node.servicePort, `${label}:${node.nodeId}`);
       endpointPorts.set(endpoint, ports);
     }
   }
   // A storage listener may share 5432 with another PostgreSQL-family role on
   // the same host (co-located primary/audit/log), but never a compute listener.
   const storagePortClaims: Array<{ label: string; node: NodeSpec; port: number; family: "postgres" | "redis" | "backup" | "pgbouncer" }> = [];
   for (const entry of storageNodes) {
     const family = entry.label.startsWith("PG_") ? "postgres" as const : entry.label === "REDIS_NODES" ? "redis" as const : entry.label === "AUDIT_DB_NODE" || entry.label === "LOG_DB_NODE" ? "postgres" as const : "backup" as const;
     for (const node of entry.nodes) storagePortClaims.push({ label: entry.label, node, port: node.servicePort, family });
   }
   for (const node of primaryNodes) storagePortClaims.push({ label: "PGBOUNCER_PORT", node, port: config.PGBOUNCER_PORT, family: "pgbouncer" });
   if (config.PGBOUNCER_ENABLED) {
     for (const node of replicaNodes) storagePortClaims.push({ label: "PGBOUNCER_PORT", node, port: config.PGBOUNCER_PORT, family: "pgbouncer" });
   }
   const storageEndpointPorts = new Map<string, Array<{ label: string; family: string; port: number }>>();
   for (const claim of storagePortClaims) {
     const endpoint = `${claim.node.sshHost}:${claim.node.sshPort}`;
     const computeOwner = endpointPorts.get(endpoint)?.get(claim.port);
     if (computeOwner) {
       problems.push(`storage port ${claim.port} on ${endpoint} collides with compute listener ${computeOwner}`);
     }
     const claims = storageEndpointPorts.get(endpoint) ?? [];
     const clash = claims.find((other) => other.port === claim.port && other.family !== claim.family);
     if (clash) {
       problems.push(`storage port ${claim.port} on ${endpoint} is claimed by both ${clash.label} and ${claim.label}`);
     }
     claims.push({ label: claim.label, family: claim.family, port: claim.port });
     storageEndpointPorts.set(endpoint, claims);
   }
 
   for (const [role, enabled, mode, cert, key] of [
     ["MERCHANT", config.MERCHANT_SSL, config.MERCHANT_SSL_MODE, config.MERCHANT_SSL_CERT_PATH, config.MERCHANT_SSL_KEY_PATH],
     ["CHECKOUT", config.CHECKOUT_SSL, config.CHECKOUT_SSL_MODE, config.CHECKOUT_SSL_CERT_PATH, config.CHECKOUT_SSL_KEY_PATH],
   ] as const) {
     if (enabled && mode === "custom" && (!cert || !key)) {
       problems.push(`${role}_SSL_MODE=custom requires ${role}_SSL_CERT_PATH and ${role}_SSL_KEY_PATH`);
     }
   }
 
   // Distinct listeners within a portal. The two public portals may share
   // 80/443 because they are told apart by server_name.
   for (const [role, httpPort, httpsPort, lanPort, lanEnabled] of [
     ["MERCHANT", config.MERCHANT_HTTP_PORT, config.MERCHANT_HTTPS_PORT, config.MERCHANT_LAN_PORT, config.MERCHANT_LAN_PORT > 0],
     ["CHECKOUT", config.CHECKOUT_HTTP_PORT, config.CHECKOUT_HTTPS_PORT, config.CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT, config.CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT > 0],
   ] as const) {
     const ports: Array<[string, number]> = [
       [`${role}_HTTP_PORT`, httpPort],
       [`${role}_HTTPS_PORT`, httpsPort],
       ...(lanEnabled ? [[`${role}_LAN_PORT`, lanPort] as [string, number]] : []),
     ];
     for (let i = 0; i < ports.length; i += 1) {
       for (let j = i + 1; j < ports.length; j += 1) {
         if (ports[i]![1] === ports[j]![1]) {
           problems.push(`${ports[i]![0]} and ${ports[j]![0]} must differ (two listeners on the same port)`);
         }
       }
     }
     if (httpPort === config.ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT && lanEnabled) {
       problems.push(`${role}_HTTP_PORT must differ from ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT`);
     }
   }
 
   const lanPorts = [
     ["MERCHANT_LAN_PORT", config.MERCHANT_LAN_PORT],
     ["CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT", config.CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT],
     ["ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT", config.ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT],
   ].filter(([, port]) => Number(port) > 0);
   for (let i = 0; i < lanPorts.length; i += 1) {
     for (let j = i + 1; j < lanPorts.length; j += 1) {
       if (lanPorts[i]![1] === lanPorts[j]![1]) {
         problems.push(`${lanPorts[i]![0]} and ${lanPorts[j]![0]} must differ (two listeners on the same port)`);
       }
     }
   }
   if (config.MERCHANT_DOMAIN === config.CHECKOUT_DOMAIN) {
     problems.push("MERCHANT_DOMAIN and CHECKOUT_DOMAIN must differ (two public vhosts on the edge host)");
   }
 
   if (config.CORE_PORT === config.ADMIN_BACK_PORT
     || config.CORE_PORT === config.MERCHANT_BACK_PORT
     || config.CORE_PORT === config.CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT) {
     problems.push("CORE_PORT must differ from the edge backend ports");
   }
 
   // --- Fake Rails tier -----------------------------------------------------
   if (config.FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED) {
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_SSH_HOST) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_SSH_HOST is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_JWT_SECRET) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_JWT_SECRET is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN) problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN is required when FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (config.DEPLOY_ENV === "production" && !config.FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION) {
       problems.push(
         'FAKE_RAILS_PRODUCTION_GUARD_BLOCKED: Set FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION="true" to run Fake Rails in production mode',
       );
     }
     if (config.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD && config.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD.length < 12) {
       problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD must be at least 12 characters");
     }
     if (config.FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT === config.FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT) {
       problems.push("FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT and FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT must differ");
     }
     const reserved = [
       ["CORE_PORT", config.CORE_PORT],
       ["ADMIN_BACK_PORT", config.ADMIN_BACK_PORT],
       ["MERCHANT_BACK_PORT", config.MERCHANT_BACK_PORT],
       ["CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT", config.CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT],
       ["ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT", config.ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT],
     ] as Array<[string, number]>;
     for (const [name, port] of reserved) {
       if (config.FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT === port) problems.push(`FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT must differ from ${name}`);
       if (config.FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT === port) problems.push(`FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT must differ from ${name}`);
     }
     for (const port of [80, 443]) {
       if (config.FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT === port) {
         problems.push(`FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT must not be the public ${port}`);
       }
     }
   }
 
   if (config.RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED) {
     if (!config.IS_TEST_SERVER) problems.push("RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED requires IS_TEST_SERVER=true");
     if (!config.FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED) problems.push("RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED requires FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true");
     if (config.DEPLOY_ENV === "production" && !config.FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION) {
       problems.push("RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED requires FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true in production");
     }
   }
 
   return problems;
 };
 
 /** A tiny dotenv parser that understands `KEY=value`, `KEY="value with spaces"` and `#` comments. */
 export const parseDeployEnv = (source: string): Record<string, string> => {
   const values: Record<string, string> = {};
   for (const rawLine of source.split(/\r?\n/)) {
     const line = rawLine.trim();
     if (line.length === 0 || line.startsWith("#")) {
       continue;
     }
     const eq = line.indexOf("=");
     if (eq <= 0) {
       continue;
     }
     const key = line.slice(0, eq).trim();
     let value = line.slice(eq + 1).trim();
     // A quoted value ends at its closing quote; anything after it (an inline
     // comment such as `# "auto" | "fresh"`) is not part of the value. This
     // also preserves a `#` that is legitimately inside the quotes.
     if (value.startsWith('"') || value.startsWith("'")) {
       const quote = value[0]!;
       const end = value.indexOf(quote, 1);
       value = end > 0 ? value.slice(1, end) : value.slice(1);
     } else {
       const hash = value.indexOf(" #");
       if (hash >= 0) {
         value = value.slice(0, hash).trim();
       }
     }
     values[key] = value;
   }
   return values;
 };
 
 export interface ConfigLoadResult {
   ok: boolean;
   config?: DeployConfig;
   problems: string[];
 }
 
 /** Parses and validates a `deploy.env` source. */
 export const loadDeployConfig = (source: string): ConfigLoadResult => {
   const env = parseDeployEnv(source);
   const parsed = base.safeParse(env);
   if (!parsed.success) {
     return {
       ok: false,
       problems: parsed.error.issues.map((issue) => `${issue.path.join(".") || "(root)"}: ${issue.message}`),
     };
   }
   const problems = validateDeployConfig(parsed.data);
   if (problems.length > 0) {
     return { ok: false, problems };
   }
   return { ok: true, config: parsed.data, problems: [] };
 };
 
 export const deployConfigSchema = base;

You were partly right: the daemon env was already generated and deployed, but several daemon settings were hard-coded in the provisioner, and the separate `backup.env.example` made it look manual. That separation is now removed as a deployment concern.

## Investigation findings

- `deploy.ts` already synced `deploy/backup-daemon` to `/opt/pg-backup-daemon` and enabled the systemd unit when `BACKUP_ENABLED=true`.
- `backupEngineProvisioner.ts` already wrote `/etc/pg-backup/backup.env` from `deploy.env`.
- But these were hard-coded instead of coming from `deploy.env`: cert directory, catalog path, `.pgpass`, scratch paths/ports, command timeout, scheduler tick, binary paths, insecure-HTTP flag.
- Custom cert directories would have broken cert upload, daemon health checks, the trigger script and systemd `ReadWritePaths`.
- `deploy/backup-daemon/backup.env.example` was documented like a manual production step.

- `backupDaemonEnv()` generates every daemon setting from `deploy.env`.
- Custom cert dirs flow through certificate upload, daemon env, health checks and the trigger script.
- `ReadWritePaths` is generated from the configured catalog, scratch, cert and `.pgpass` paths.
- `deploy.ts` remains the single orchestration path: provision env/unit, sync daemon source, install dependencies, enable/restart systemd.

parts.text:
Need plan for centralized project-design. Need inspect design docs content structure/headings to map to parts. Also actual code surface and features not in docs. We need deeply investigate. We can use parallel explore agents to analyze groups of design docs and code surfaces. Need gather facts to plan file structure and content. Since plan mode, we can delegate read-only exploration. Let's launch multiple explore agents in parallel:
1. Core design docs (final v5, refined v4.1, Dynamic v2, opencode tracker) vs core-back actual features.
2. Performance/storage/backup/scaling/deep search/synthetic seeder docs vs actual.
3. UI/guides/academy docs vs actual frontends.
4. Deploy docs + fake rails + voucher + smart AI docs vs actual.
5. Agent instruction/harness files across repo and how to add persistent instructions.

We need be careful agent outputs concise but comprehensive. They can read many files. Let's launch 4-5 explore agents in parallel with specific prompts.
I’m splitting the audit across design domains and implementation surfaces so the plan covers every project part, not just the database work.

## 3. Blocking / High-Severity Gaps

### P0 — Deployment and drill correctness

1. **PostgreSQL remote TLS/auth mismatch**
   - `pgHbaSnippet` grants remote application and replication only through `hostssl`:
     `deploy/provisioners/postgres18Provisioner.ts:117-128`.
   - Replica `pg_hba.conf` only allows primary and backup IPs, not core IPs:
     `deploy/provisioners/postgres18Provisioner.ts:258-268`.
   - Core DSNs are built as plain `postgresql://...` with no `sslmode`, and `buildPostgresPoolConfig` never sets `ssl`:
     `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts:479-500`; `core-back/lib/db/connectionConfig.ts:1-31`.
   - The provisioner does not set `ssl = on`, `ssl_cert_file`, or `ssl_key_file` in `postgresConfigSnippet`:
     `deploy/provisioners/postgres18Provisioner.ts:85-103`.
   - PgBouncer is configured `server_tls_sslmode = require`:
     `deploy/provisioners/postgres18Provisioner.ts:170-184`.
   - Impact: core→PG, core→replica, core→audit/log, and PgBouncer→PG can fail unless the distro’s default PostgreSQL SSL is enabled and the client negotiates it. With the default `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED="false"`, direct core-to-replica reads also fail because replicas do not accept core IPs. `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts:311` defaults PgBouncer off.

2. **Backup daemon certificate ownership**
   - Deploy writes backup certificates with `sudo: true`; cert files become root-owned (`0644`) and the private key root-owned (`0600`):
     `deploy/deploy.ts:119-141`.
   - The daemon systemd unit runs as `User=pgbackup`:
     `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts:231-261`.
   - `provisionBackupEngine` creates the cert directory as `pgbackup` but does not recursively change existing cert files:
     `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts:400-405`.
   - The daemon reads `BACKUP_DAEMON_KEY_PATH` at startup:
     `deploy/backup-daemon/src/server.ts:387-412`.
   - Impact: the daemon cannot read its private key and either fails to start or cannot serve mTLS, which makes admin backup/drill operations and health verification fail.

3. **Restore drill connects to the audit scratch DB with the wrong role**
   - `buildPsqlCommand` always uses `config.PG_PRIMARY_USER`:
     `deploy/backup-daemon/src/backupEngine.ts:279-305`.
   - `RestoreDrillRunner` uses it for both core and audit scratch databases:
     `deploy/backup-daemon/src/restoreDrillRunner.ts:308-322`, `437-478`.
   - The audit DB provisioner creates `AUDIT_DB_USER` (`pg_audit_writer`) as a distinct role:
     `deploy/provisioners/auditAndLogDbProvisioner.ts:243-251`.
   - Impact: the audit hash-chain check in the restore drill can fail solely because the core application role does not exist in the restored audit cluster.

4. **Balance-parity drill compares incompatible identifiers**
   - `CheckpointService` stores `lastCheckpointId` as the latest **`journal_entries.id`**:
     `core-back/engine/ledger/CheckpointService.ts:52-71`.
   - The restore drill compares **`journal_lines.id::text > last_checkpoint_id`**:
     `deploy/backup-daemon/src/restoreDrillRunner.ts:66-71`.
   - The seeder stores `lastCheckpointId` as a synthetic `checkpoint-YYYY-MM` string:
     `core-back/prisma/syntheticSeeder/generators/05_ledgerAndCheckpoints.ts:113-137`.
   - Impact: Check 2 (“Sharded Balance Parity”) is semantically unreliable and can report false mismatches or mask real ones. The production live-balance code correctly uses `checkpointAt`, but the drill uses `last_checkpoint_id`.

5. **`target="all"` backup can fail on a normal deployment**
   - `WalGEngine.triggerBackup("all")` always requests `postgres_core`, `audit_db`, and optionally `redis`:
     `deploy/backup-daemon/src/backupEngine.ts:736-739`.
   - It throws if `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` is absent:
     `deploy/backup-daemon/src/backupEngine.ts:741-749`.
   - Deploy validation only requires `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` when the audit host differs from the WAL-G backup host:
     `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts:756-772`.
   - The default deploy environment leaves `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR=""`:
     `deploy/deploy.env.example:168-172`.
   - Impact: a default WAL-G backup with `target="all"` fails unless operators explicitly add `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR`, even when audit is co-located; if no audit DB is configured, the daemon still attempts the audit target.

6. **Barman audit replication-slot mismatch**
   - Barman config names the audit server slot `barman_audit`:
     `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts:221-228`.
   - `barmanStreamingSql()` always creates a slot named `barman`:
     `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts:362-367`.
   - It is applied to both primary and audit hosts at `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts:537-546`.
   - Impact: Barman streaming archiving for the audit server can fail because the configured slot does not exist.

## 4. Area-by-Area Findings

### 4.1 PostgreSQL 18 schema, indexes, partitioning

Implemented:
- Baseline migration creates 75 Prisma models and the storage tables (`gl_account_shards`, `outbox_events`, `audit_outbox`, `backup_catalog_runs`, `backup_restore_drills`) at `core-back/prisma/migrations/20261103000000_postgres18_init/migration.sql:1687-1770`.
- `journal_lines` is monthly range-partitioned with a DEFAULT partition and maintenance function.
- Partial indexes for worker claims, BRIN indexes, covering index on `payment_attempts`, and several trigram GIN indexes exist.

Gaps / drift:
- The design’s “exact storage migration” DDL is split across the baseline, `20261103120000`, and `20261103180000`; the storage migration itself does not create `gl_account_shards`, `outbox_events`, `audit_outbox`, backup catalog tables, or `pg_stat_statements`.
- `schema.prisma` does not represent the partial/BRIN indexes:
  - `OutboxEvent` `@@index([id])` and `@@index([createdAt])` have no `WHERE processed_at IS NULL` / BRIN representation (`core-back/prisma/schema.prisma:2677-2690`).
  - `AuditOutbox` index has no partial predicate (`schema.prisma:2692-2711`).
  - `JournalLine` declares generic indexes, while hardening creates named covering/BRIN indexes with different names (`schema.prisma:1139-1157`; `20261103180000_storage_hardening/migration.sql:112-120`).
  - Trigram GIN indexes exist only in SQL, not in Prisma schema (`20261103180000_storage_hardening/migration.sql:145-248`).
- Business tables use `TIMESTAMP(3)` rather than `TIMESTAMPTZ` in the baseline (`20261103000000_postgres18_init/migration.sql:528-537`; `core-back/prisma/schema.prisma:1924-1970`). The design’s DDL uses `TIMESTAMPTZ`.
- UUIDs are generated by Prisma `@default(uuid(7))` / the custom client UUIDv7 helper, not PostgreSQL `uuidv7()` column defaults. The design’s `audit_outbox.id UUID DEFAULT uuidv7()` is not present in the migration.
- The design says `journal_lines` covering index uses `(gl_account_id, id) INCLUDE (...)`; actual hardening uses `(gl_account_id, created_at) INCLUDE (direction, amount)` because the partition key must participate (`20261103180000_storage_hardening/migration.sql:115-117`). This is a reasonable partition-driven change but is not documented.
- Partition creation in the hardening migration covers 2023-01 through 2028-12 and then `ensure_journal_line_partitions(18)` from the current month; the DEFAULT partition is present. The design does not describe the DEFAULT partition or the 2028 ceiling.

### 4.2 `gl_account_shards`

Implemented:
- 16 shards for non-wallet system accounts and 1 shard for `MERCHANT_WALLET`; FNV-1a deterministic shard selection. `shardBalances.ts:1-32`; `seedGlAccounts.ts:96-127`.
- Ledger lines project into shards in the same transaction through `ledgerShardWriter.ts:8-31`.
- Balance reads use `SUM(current_balance)` and natural-sign normalization. `shardBalances.ts:51-97`.
- UoW exposes `lockGlAccountShardsSorted()` with deterministic ordering and `FOR UPDATE`. `uowAdapter.ts:52-97`.

Gaps:
- `lockGlAccountShardsSorted()` has no production call site. The shard writer uses UPSERT arithmetic, not the sorted lock path. The design’s “acquire sorted row locks before posting” is therefore implemented as an unused capability.
- `ensureAccountShards()` is exported but not called by wallet creation or wallet listing. Merchant wallets created by the application receive a shard row only when a posting first occurs. `ledgerShardWriter.ts:34-51`; `api/internal/merchant.ts:1336-1355`.
- Shard selection uses `line.refId` rather than the attempt ID:
  - `ledgerShardWriter.ts:16` calls `shardIdForAttempt(line.refId, ...)`.
  - Refund/chargeback IDs are synthetic (`${attempt.id}-refund`, `${attempt.id}-chargeback`) in the seeder and adjustment flows, so shards do not always map to the original attempt’s shard.
- The seeder creates synthetic wallets without explicit `gl_account_shards` rows; only postings create shard rows. The restore drill’s sharded-balance parity can therefore depend on posting history rather than a complete shard layout.

### 4.3 Outbox, audit outbox, and read models

Implemented:
- UoW flushes pending outbox and audit-outbox rows inside the same transaction (`uowAdapter.ts:102-137`).
- `OutboxRelayWorker` claims rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and marks `processed_at` (`outboxWorkers.ts:211-246`).
- `AuditShipperWorker` claims unshipped audit rows, appends to the audit DB, and marks `shipped_at` (`outboxWorkers.ts:334-383`).
- Read-model projection for `attempt.transitioned` updates `rm_merchant_daily_stats` and `rm_route_daily_volumes` (`outboxWorkers.ts:68-132`).
- Worker runtime starts both shippers when storage is configured (`engine/workers/productionRuntime.ts:310-328`).

Gaps:
- Only `attempt.transitioned` has a real handler. `ledger.entry_posted`, `merchant.updated`, `kyb.document_uploaded`, `reconciliation.completed`, and `config.invalidated` are all no-ops (`outboxWorkers.ts:149-157`). The design’s ledger-driven wallet/read-model projection is not implemented.
- There is no `rm_wallet_statements` model. The design names it, but schema has only `RmMerchantDailyStat` and `RmRouteDailyVolume` (`schema.prisma:2757-2784`).
- The two read models are maintained but not read by dashboards. Admin `/stats/overview` still aggregates `payment_attempt` on the primary (`api/internal/admin.ts:763-860`). Merchant `/stats/overview` also reads the primary (`api/internal/merchant.ts:2427-2475`).
- Processed `outbox_events` rows are never purged. The design’s BRIN index exists, but no retention job deletes processed rows.
- `audit_outbox` rows are marked `shipped_at`, not deleted, despite the design saying the shipper deletes them (`outboxWorkers.ts:338-383`; design line 773-774). There is no retention/purge for `audit_outbox`.
- `RetentionWorker` covers `notifications`, `inbound_events`, `attempt_step_logs`, `audit_log`, and `detail_change_logs`, but not `outbox_events` or `audit_outbox` (`engine/workers/RetentionWorker.ts:240-276`).
- `writeAudit` only writes `audit_outbox` when `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` is set (`writeAudit.ts:55-78`). The UoW, in contrast, always flushes pending audit outbox rows. This is inconsistent for deployments that enable the audit outbox later.
- Audit metadata is usually sparse: most `writeAudit` call sites pass only actor/action/entity and omit `actorEmail`, `merchantId`, `requestId`, `clientIp`, and `userAgent`. The audit DB columns therefore stay mostly null, which weakens audit deep search by request ID/email.
- `writeAudit` accepts those extra fields but passes them straight into `auditLog.create`, and the `AuditLog` model has no such columns (`schema.prisma:2251-2270`). A caller using the documented optional fields can trigger an unknown-argument Prisma error.
- `AuditShipperWorker` selects a batch in a short transaction, releases the locks, then appends. It is idempotent on source ID, but concurrent shippers can duplicate work; there is no held claim until the `shipped_at` update.

### 4.4 Replica routing, LSN, and read scaling

Implemented:
- `PostgresReplicaReadStore` supports primary, replica, round-robin, max lag, LSN candidates, `maxWaitMs`, timeouts, and primary fallback (`readStoreAdapter.ts:21-192`).
- LSN comparison is robust and tested (`lsn.ts:1-34`).
- `createStorageEngine` starts the LSN monitor and creates replica clients from `DATABASE_REPLICA_URLS` (`storageEngine/index.ts:56-98`).
- UoW captures commit LSN and the runtime stores it per attempt (`uowAdapter.ts:139-172`; `platform.ts:182-197`).

Gaps:
- Replica reads are used only in:
  - `POST /internal/admin/search` (`api/internal/admin.ts:687-703`).
  - Merchant `/wallets`, `/links`, `/payments` list endpoints (`api/internal/merchant.ts:1323`, `1661`, `1744`).
- Admin lists, dashboards, exports, recent activity, audit summary, finance/profitability, and merchant stats still read the primary. The design’s “all dashboards, lists, exports, and deep search on replicas” is not met.
- `listQuery.ts` is offset pagination (`skip: (page - 1) * pageSize`), not keyset pagination as the design requires (`core-back/lib/listQuery.ts:216-220`). This remains a major scalability issue at 50M–500M rows.
- The edge clients expose `minLsn` / `consistencyLsn` and a `consistencyHeader`, but there are no call sites that take a core response header and send it on the next read:
  - `admin-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts:376-399`; same in merchant/checkout.
  - `x-pg-min-lsn` is set by checkout (`api/internal/checkout.ts:1166`, `1371-1375`) and read by admin search/merchant lists, but the edge BFFs do not automatically propagate it end-to-end.
- The outer fallback can re-run a whole search on the primary after a replica timeout: `readThroughReplicaOrPrimary` calls `readStore.execute` with a timeout, and `execute` itself already falls back to the primary. If one search provider stalls, the entire search may be executed twice (`storageEngine/index.ts:249-268`; `readStoreAdapter.ts:165-192`).
- No sustained replica lag/failover or 1,000+ TPS test exists; this is explicitly still open in `design/opencode_technical_delivery_design.md:1164`.

### 4.5 Redis cache, velocity, and invalidation

Implemented:
- L1 memory cache, Redis L2 adapter, single-flight loaders, TTLs, prefix deletion, and `getOrLoad` (`redisCacheAndVelocityAdapter.ts:42-141`, `168-280`).
- Atomic Lua sliding-window velocity script with `EVALSHA` and `EVAL` fallback (`redisCacheAndVelocityAdapter.ts:17-40`, `282-336`).
- `AttemptGuardPipeline` calls `storage.cache.incrWindowCounter` for velocity rules (`AttemptGuardPipeline.ts:1205-1235`).
- Redis-backed invalidation bus is configured at startup (`core-back/index.ts:191-245`; `lib/invalidationBus/index.ts`).
- Redis provisioner sets private bind, `requirepass`, `save 3600 1`, maxmemory, and UFW rules (`deploy/provisioners/redisProvisioner.ts:19-81`).

Gaps:
- The L1+L2 “config cache” is not used. `getOrLoad` has no production call sites; only velocity and storage health probes use the cache (`storageEngine/index.ts:159-166`).
- The invalidation bus is separate from `CachePort`; cache `del` is not subscribed to credential/gateway/config invalidation events. Cross-node invalidation does not flush the cache adapter.
- `RedisCacheAdapter.del` uses Redis `KEYS` (blocking, O(N)) rather than `SCAN` (`redisCacheAndVelocityAdapter.ts:269-280`).
- `RedisCacheAdapter.set` ignores `options.l1TtlMs` and always uses `ttlSec` for L1 (`redisCacheAndVelocityAdapter.ts:252-267`).
- The constructor eagerly creates `scriptShaPromise`; an unreachable Redis can create a rejected promise before any caller catches it (`redisCacheAndVelocityAdapter.ts:176-180`).
- The admin BFF search rate limiter is an in-memory `Map` (`admin-back/api/protected/search.ts:19-60`), so horizontally scaled admin nodes each get their own 120 req/min bucket instead of a shared Redis limiter.
- No Redis cache/invalidation benchmark exists.

### 4.6 Dedicated audit and log databases

Implemented:
- Audit DB DDL with `audit_records`, entity/actor/BRIN/trigram indexes, immutability trigger, and least-privilege writer grants (`deploy/provisioners/auditAndLogDbProvisioner.ts:10-65`, `111-136`).
- Log DB DDL with partitioned `attempt_step_logs` and `http_access_logs`, BRIN indexes, and `ensure_log_partitions()` retention function (`auditAndLogDbProvisioner.ts:67-107`, `158-233`).
- Buffered `DedicatedPostgresLogSink` with 250ms flush, bounded buffers, step-log preservation, access-log drop, remembered logs, and query fallback (`auditAndLogAdapters.ts:333-523`).
- Audit hash chain uses deterministic stable JSON and a serialized advisory lock (`auditAndLogAdapters.ts:42-55`, `105-202`).
- Audit query, count, lookup, and chain verification are implemented (`auditAndLogAdapters.ts:204-330`).

Gaps:
- `gateway_wire_logs` is named in the design but does not exist in DDL, schema, or adapters.
- No disk spool under pressure; step logs drop oldest and access logs drop new. The design says “drop or spool.”
- Access-log `dbQueries` and `dbDurationMs` are always `0` (`lib/requestLogger/index.ts:185-200`). The log schema supports them, but no instrumentation populates them.
- Audit query uses offset pagination from the API, not the cursor fields exposed by the port (`AuditQueryParams` has cursor fields, but `auditStoreParamsFromRequest` always supplies `offset`; `api/internal/admin.ts:15587-15614`).
- Audit search does not filter on `requestId`; `buildFilters` covers entity/actor/role/action/search text, but not request ID (`auditAndLogAdapters.ts:204-247`).
- Log partitions have no DEFAULT partition; if the maintenance cron lapses, inserts outside the six-month window fail.
- Audit/log DB DDL is deployment-only. There are no Prisma migrations for `pg_audit_db` / `pg_logs_db`; local development must use test helpers or manual provisioning.
- `AuditShipperWorker` marks `shipped_at`; it never removes shipped rows, so the audit outbox grows indefinitely.
- `RetentionWorker` purges the legacy primary `audit_log` but not the dedicated audit DB; that is probably intentional, but no dedicated-retention story is documented.

### 4.7 Backup daemon, WAL-G, Barman, and restore drills

Implemented:
- Target-aware full/delta backups for core, audit, Redis; WAL-G and Barman engines.
- WAL-G S3 encryption/compression environment, backup verification, optional rclone/rsync mirror, prune, list, recover.
- Barman check/backup/list/recover plus Barman Cloud backup.
- mTLS server, catalog, scheduler, policy API, target health checks, WAL lag query, and restore drill runner.
- Backup policy maker-checker through core approval execution.
- Admin backup UI with WAL lag, target health, backup history, restore drill cards, trigger, drill, and policy editing.

Gaps:
- **No size/start/end LSN is returned by backup execution.**
  - WAL-G parses `startLsn` from stdout but discards it (`backupEngine.ts:701-702`).
  - `WalGEngine.triggerBackup` returns only `storageTargets` (`:757`).
  - Barman returns only `primary-s3` (`:818`).
  - Scheduler and catalog therefore persist `sizeBytes`, `startLsn`, `endLsn` as undefined (`scheduler.ts:219-227`; `server.ts:275-283`).
- **WAL archive lag health query is incorrect.**
  - `last_archived_wal` is a WAL filename, but it is passed directly to `pg_wal_lsn_diff()` as if it were an LSN (`backupEngine.ts:235-239`).
  - Expect the query to fail or report zero lag; health falls back to the replica LSN values.
- **WAL-G retention does not honor `BACKUP_RETENTION_WAL_DAYS`.**
  - `buildWalGPruneCommand` only runs `wal-g delete retain FULL <fullCount> --confirm` (`backupEngine.ts:222-230`); no WAL retention/cleanup.
- **Secondary target is not continuously updated.**
  - WAL-G `archive_command` writes only to the primary prefix (`deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts:164-171`).
  - `buildWalGMirrorCommand` runs only after a base backup (`backupEngine.ts:693-699`); WAL archives are mirrored only when the next base backup runs.
- **Barman path has no mirror and no encryption.**
  - `triggerBarmanTarget` runs check, backup, and Barman Cloud backup, then returns `["primary-s3"]` (`backupEngine.ts:806-819`).
  - No secondary-target mirror, no encryption flags for Barman Cloud.
- **Audit target health is incomplete.**
  - WAL-G health checks only the core S3 prefix (`backupEngine.ts:711-733`); no audit S3 prefix check.
  - WAL archive status checks only the core primary; no audit host archive lag.
- **Redis backup is not hourly.**
  - Scheduler has only `full`, `delta`, and `drill` jobs (`scheduler.ts:8`, `119-160`).
  - Redis is included only when a full/delta/all target triggers `triggerBackup` (`backupEngine.ts:736-738`, `856-858`). The design’s hourly `BGSAVE` schedule is missing.
- **Scheduler timezone differs from design.**
  - Cron is explicitly evaluated in UTC (`cron.ts:13-14`), while the design says weekly Sunday 03:00 `Africa/Tripoli` (design line 1159).
  - Defaults are `0 4 * * 0` (`config.ts:58`), not 03:00 Tripoli.
- **Fallback cron restore script is much weaker than the daemon drill.**
  - `scratchRestoreVerifierScript` restores core only and verifies only double-entry drift (`backupEngineProvisioner.ts:288-317`).
  - It does not restore audit DB, verify sharded balance parity, or verify the hash chain.
- **Backup daemon mTLS TLS version**
  - Daemon uses `Bun.serve` TLS options without an explicit minimum version (`server.ts:404-410`); the core backup client requires TLS 1.3 (`backupControlClient.ts:128-136`).
- **Policy/catalog behavior**
  - Catalog sync happens only when `/overview` is called (`api/internal/backups.ts:221-248`); if no one opens the page, core’s local catalog can remain stale after a daemon crash.
  - `PUT /v1/policy` on the daemon trusts the caller; maker-checker exists only in core’s `PUT /internal/admin/system/backups/policy` and generic approval path.

### 4.8 Deep Search: 20 groups, registry, BFF, frontend

Implemented:
- Exact 20 built-in providers and registration order 10..200 (`globalSearch.ts:1604-1647`); test asserts 20 unique providers (`test/globalSearch.test.ts:180-186`).
- Authority prefilter before fetching; unauthorized groups omitted (`globalSearch.ts:1727-1741`).
- Per-provider `Promise.allSettled`, partial flag, slow-search warning, no raw query logging (`globalSearch.ts:1743-1813`).
- Smart parser, Libyan phone variants, SHA/email/ID detection, `type:`/`status:`/`merchant:` scoping, deterministic scoring, dedupe, sanitization (`search/engine.ts:80-137`, `146-196`, `254-300`, `333-389`).
- Server POST-only route with `no-store` (`api/internal/admin.ts:684-707`).
- BFF POST proxy, strict schema, 120 req/min hashed-token limiter (`admin-back/api/protected/search.ts:8-80`).
- Frontend 20 targets, palette, session cache, abort/sequence guard, recents-only query strings, pure VNode highlighting, and one-shot `useOpenQuery` (`admin-front/src/components/search/*`, `composables/useOpenQuery.ts`).

Gaps and drift:
- `supportsTokenKind` exists in the plugin interface and execution filter but no built-in provider implements it (`search/engine.ts:315`; `globalSearch.ts:1734-1739`). Expensive groups therefore run for every token shape.
- `payment_attempt` searches `idempotencyKey` but does not select it or include it in match signals, so it cannot receive exact/prefix ranking even when matched (`globalSearch.ts:239-286`).
- Several design-matrix fields do not exist in the schema:
  - Merchant `legalNameEn` / `legalNameAr`: schema stores single `legalName` / `tradeName` (`schema.prisma:827-847`).
  - Join request `applicationReference`: absent (`schema.prisma:2291-2317`).
  - Cashout `cashoutReference`, `bankTransferRef`: absent (`schema.prisma:1277-1296`).
  - AML case `caseNumber`: absent; provider uses rule/trigger (`schema.prisma:1213-1245`).
  - AML report `reportReference`: absent; provider uses `submissionRef` (`schema.prisma:2545-2571`).
  - User `fullName` / `userType`: absent (`schema.prisma:890-915`).
  - Gateway `nameEn` / `nameAr`: absent; single `name` (`schema.prisma:1339-1369`).
  - Audit `requestId` search: absent from audit query filters (`auditAndLogAdapters.ts:204-247`).
- `audit_log` provider with the dedicated store searches action/entity/actor only; it does not match request ID (`globalSearch.ts:1545-1557`).
- The storage design mentions “pg_trgm + Full-Text Deep Search”; actual implementation has trigram GIN indexes but no `tsvector` / `to_tsquery` full-text search anywhere.
- The deep-search design explicitly says **“No Database Migration in v1”** (`deep_search_plugin_architecture_plan.md:38`), but `20261103180000_storage_hardening/migration.sql:145-248` adds many trigram indexes for search. The docs are now internally inconsistent.
- Frontend target plugins do not declare per-plugin `routesAuthorities` / `routesRoles` as the design specifies; access is resolved centrally through `FrontendAccessContext` and route maps (`admin-front/src/components/search/targets.ts:12-31`, `:392-447`). Functionally similar, architecturally different.
- The design says `useOpenQuery` is wired across “13+ drawer/dialog pages”; actual usage is 12 pages (`grep -rl useOpenQuery admin-front/src/pages`). Several record types use direct route params instead.
- Security predicate drift:
  - `hasAuthority` does not support the design’s `admin:*` wildcard; only `*` (`core-back/lib/auth/confidentialAccess.ts:14-25`).
  - `hasConfidentialAmlAccess` grants `COMPLIANCE` and `MLRO` unconditionally, while the design requires an explicit AML/compliance authority (`confidentialAccess.ts:33-45`).
  - `hasMerchantSensitiveAccess` omits the design’s `merchant:sensitive`, `kyb:read`, and `finance:read` alternatives (`confidentialAccess.ts:48-62`).
- Search BFF rate limiting is per-process and in-memory, not shared across horizontally scaled admin nodes.
- No search query-plan benchmark against 50M rows and no 20-group performance gate.

### 4.9 Synthetic operational data seeder

Implemented:
- Deterministic xoshiro128** PRNG and Libyan data catalogue (`prng.ts`, `libyanDataCatalog.ts`).
- Chronological timeline with adoption curve, weekly rhythm, Ramadan/Eid, and salary multipliers (`timelineClock.ts`).
- Nine generators, including extra `09_operatorCasesGenerator.ts`.
- Two-phase bulk writer with topological ordering and 2,500-row chunks (`sync/bulkDataWriter.ts`).
- Fake Rails bulk sync to `POST /portal-api/internal/bulk-seed` with seeder token (`sync/fakeRailsBulkSyncClient.ts`).
- KYB document content encryption via `Vault`, owner identity documents, revalidation requests, and review scheduling (`sync/enrichKybDocuments.ts`).
- Seed-run completion registry keyed by seed key (`seedRunRegistry.ts`).
- In-memory and post-seed audit (`verify/postSeedAudit.ts`).

Gaps and drift:
- **Profile volume fields are largely unused.**
  - `joinRequests`, `kybDocuments`, `beneficialOwners`, `users`, `wallets`, `applications`, `amlCases` are never read from `config.volumes`.
  - Actual generation is derived: one join request per merchant, 4–7 KYB docs per merchant, 1–4 owners per merchant, 1–3 applications per merchant, random merchant users, one wallet per merchant, AML cases from screenings.
  - Standard profile therefore does not produce the documented 310 join requests, 1,650 KYB docs, 580 owners, 380 wallets, 520 applications, or 420 AML cases (`synthetic_operational_data_seeder_architecture.md:113-127`; `config.ts:47-67`).
- **Model coverage differs.**
  - Design says “all 66 Prisma models” (seeder doc line 11); actual schema contains **75 models** (`grep -c '^model ' core-back/prisma/schema.prisma` = 75).
  - Bulk writer covers roughly 50 model steps (`bulkDataWriter.ts:22-75`); it does not write `Gateway`, `Rail`, `RailRoute`, `CryptoProfile`, `Flow`, `FlowStep`, `StepParameter`, `StepOutput`, `StatusRule`, `ErrorMap`, `PollPolicy`, `WidgetDefinition`, `RedirectDefinition`, `ManualInstruction`, `BackgroundJob`, `GatewayInquirySchedule`, `GlAccountShard`, `OutboxEvent`, `AuditOutbox`, `BackupCatalogRun`, `BackupRestoreDrill`, or `Rm*`.
- **“All 15 journal templates” is false.**
  - Seeder uses direct `postLedger` only for `PAYMENT_ATTEMPT` and `ADJUSTMENT` refs (`generators/05_ledgerAndCheckpoints.ts:41-91`; `07_disputesCashoutsAdjustments.ts:171-181`).
  - No settlement sweep, fee variance, AML hold/release/void, cashout, commission netting, internal, suspense, or chargeback-won templates are exercised. Design line 25 and line 175 claim all 15.
- **Exact “middle-of-operation” counts are not implemented.**
  - Attempt weights at `04_linksAndAttemptsGenerator.ts:5-20` produce about 4.5% in-flight states, not the documented ~3.5%/450 rows; `UNKNOWN` is ~0.8% (~950 in STANDARD), not 35 active UNKNOWN.
  - Late-success recovery is a random 20% of EXPIRED, not 8 cases.
  - `INFECTED` KYB documents are random ~2%, not exactly 2.
  - Operator-case approvals always use `MARK_FAILED` or `CLOSE_CASE`; `MARK_SUCCEEDED` is never emitted (`09_operatorCasesGenerator.ts:29-34`).
  - Regulatory reports can be `SUBMITTED`/`ACKNOWLEDGED` while `submissionRef` and `submittedAt` remain null (`08_amlAndGovernanceQueues.ts:93-113`).
- **Ledger/AML/cashout entity linkage is incomplete.**
  - `Adjustment.journalEntryId` remains null; `CashoutRequest.adjustmentId` remains null; `AmlCase.holdJournalEntryId` remains null.
  - No cashout ledger entry, AML hold/release entry, settlement sweep, or fee-variance entry is generated.
  - Disputes and adjustments are generated, but their `journalEntryId` links are not populated.
- **Checkpoint identity is invalid for the drill.**
  - Seeder writes `lastCheckpointId = checkpoint-YYYY-MM` (`05_ledgerAndCheckpoints.ts:113-137`), while `BALANCE_PARITY_QUERY` compares it to `journal_lines.id::text` (`restoreDrillRunner.ts:66-71`).
  - This makes seeded databases especially likely to fail the drill’s Check 2 for reasons unrelated to real ledger drift.
- **Sensitive payloads are not actually encrypted.**
  - `BeneficialOwner.nationalIdCiphertext` is plain base64 (`02_merchantCohortGenerator.ts:303-312`).
  - `PaymentAttempt.contextCiphertext` is plain base64 (`04_linksAndAttemptsGenerator.ts:219`), so a seeded attempt that reaches a code path decrypting context may fail.
  - `RegulatoryReport.payloadCiphertext` is plain base64 (`08_amlAndGovernanceQueues.ts:107`), and notification address ciphertext is plain base64.
- **Platform synthetic users have an incompatible authority shape.**
  - Seeder writes nested objects like `{ gateway: ["read", "write"] }` (`01_adminAndStaffGenerator.ts:9-16`).
  - Core login only accepts array authorities or an object whose values are exactly `true` (`api/internal/admin.ts:616-620`). Nested arrays are dropped, so synthetic platform users log in with no effective authorities.
- **Safety gate is weaker than the prose design.**
  - The design prose lists a database `platform_settings.server.environment_mode === "TEST_SANDBOX"` gate; actual code has no such check (`SeederSafetyGate.ts:35-85`).
  - The handshake checks HTTP success but not the returned `ok` / `ready` fields (`SeederSafetyGate.ts:87-107`).
- **Timeline and date semantics differ.**
  - Design fixes `T_START = 2023-05-01` and `T_NOW = 2026-10-30`; actual timeline is relative to the runtime `new Date()` (`timelineClock.ts:17-22`).
  - Documented Tripoli business hours are stored as UTC hours (`timelineClock.ts:70-77`; `04_linksAndAttemptsGenerator.ts:73-74`), so local temporal patterns shift by two hours.
  - No four historical outage epochs are modeled; route health is randomized per route (`03_gatewayLifecycleGenerator.ts:209-233`).
- **Gateway state history is much narrower than documented.**
  - Only versions 2/3 are created, with version 4 pending for the first two gateways (`03_gatewayLifecycleGenerator.ts:22-38`). No `ROLLED_BACK`, `DRAFT`, `SUSPENDED`, `RETIRED`, v1 history, high-risk gateways, or gateway-level status changes are produced.
- **Post-seed audit is not a full database invariant check.**
  - `postSeedAudit` reruns the in-memory audit and only counts DB `payment_attempt`, `journal_entry`, and `payment_link` rows (`verify/postSeedAudit.ts:222-235`).
  - It does not verify DB FK integrity, DB ledger drift, shard balance parity, audit chain, or all model populations.
- **Deployment env bug**
  - Deploy passes `SYNTHETIC_SEED_YEARS_SPAN` (`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts:309-315`), but the seeder reads `SYNTHETIC_YEARS_SPAN` (`syntheticSeeder/config.ts:103`). The deploy span setting is ignored.
  - Deploy default profile is `COMPACT` (`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts:425`), while the seeder and design default to `STANDARD`.
  - `RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED` validation requires test server/Fake Rails but does not require `FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN` or a reachable Fake Rails host beyond the runtime handshake.
- **Fake Rails synchronization batches are split**
  - Transactions and events are sent in separate POST batches (`fakeRailsBulkSyncClient.ts:103-132`), not a single combined 5,000-record batch as the design describes. This is functionally workable but does not match the documented pipeline.

### 4.10 Benchmarks and performance gates

Implemented:
- `write-path-benchmark.test.ts` has two live-PostgreSQL tests:
  - 300 `writeAudit` writes under 10 seconds.
  - 16-shard balance read p95 under 25ms.
- `scripts/run-benchmarks.sh` runs those plus the storage-engine suite and backup control-plane tests.

Gaps:
- No 1,000+ TPS sustained write or replica failover benchmark.
- No read-your-own-writes load benchmark.
- No deep-search benchmark against 50M rows or all 20 groups.
- No synthetic seeder STRESS benchmark or deep-search index benchmark.
- No restore drill duration/RPO benchmark.
- The benchmark script comment says it exercises partitioned journal writes, `gl_account_shards`, `outbox_events`, `audit_outbox`, and Redis Lua (`scripts/run-benchmarks.sh:5-8`), but the performance test file only covers audit writes and shard reads; Redis/partition/outbox performance is covered only by ordinary tests, not benchmarked.
- The design’s Milestone 7 benchmark gates remain unfulfilled (`storage_driver_postgres18_backup_and_scaling_architecture.md:1419`), and the delivery tracker explicitly lists the sustained-load test as remaining work (`design/opencode_technical_delivery_design.md:1164`).

---

## 5. Documentation Drift

### Docs claim more than code does

| Document claim | Actual code |
| :--- | :--- |

| Hourly Redis `BGSAVE` (storage doc line 1155) | No Redis schedule; Redis is backed up only as part of a full/delta/all trigger. |

| Exact migration `20261103120000...` includes shard/outbox/audit tables (storage doc lines 858-1018) | Those tables are in the baseline; the storage migration contains indexes only. |

The compliance gate checks:
- exports,
- no unlayered universal padding/margin reset,
- no row tint production,
- `TableRowActions` presence,
- no raw `VDialog`, `VChip`, `VCard` in route pages,

- `SectionFields` and v2 container/table classes.

- XLSX export: `useTableXlsx` exports the rendered rows through the shared XLSX pipeline; page-level `SummaryExportCard`/`FormChecklist` exports use backend summary/export endpoints.

## 4. Missing / Partial / Aspirational Features

### 4.1 Voucher System — entirely missing

- Provider CRUD, auth methods, meta, query stack, reorder, dry-run.
- Provider extraction, API listing, fixed products, catalog tree, assets, services, forms.
- Access tokens, hashed tokens, per-token IP allow-lists.
- Catalog resolution, ranking, best-price selection, fallback rules.
- Voucher purchase, idempotency, expected-price, UNKNOWN handling.
- Public voucher API and admin voucher API.
- Voucher UI, tests and assets.
- Smart AI voucher kit, transcript, simulator, materializer, admin wizard.

### 4.2 Fake Rails — major gaps

- No full 9-mode / 10-phase implementation.
- No per-gateway protocol fidelity: JSON/form/multipart/XML differences, auth headers, signature verification, phone/birth-year/card validation and error-code maps are largely generic.
- No Auto-Pilot / automatic redirect completion.
- `autoApproveAsyncAfterSec` is dead configuration.
- No Fake Rails inbound signature verification.
- Core seed covers 13 gateways, not 20.
- `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay` route-name mismatches break LYPay and EvoPay protocol routes.
- Statement route list uses `ly_pay`/`evopay`, not `cbl_lypay`/`evo_pay`.
- No out-of-box credential binding for core callback verification.
- Webhook default path has an extra `/webhook` segment.
- Checkout embedded widget allow-list and CSP do not allow the Fake Rails host.
- Fake Rails SSL mode `certbot`/`custom` is not honored; deploy always uses the generated `fake-rails.crt`.
- `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is not validated against `FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN`/allowed hosts.
- Fake Rails `status`/inquiry behavior and statement generation are generic, not per-provider fidelity.

### 4.3 Deploy

- No actual PostgreSQL/Redis mTLS provisioning despite cert generation.
- No `pg_dump`/`psql` client installation on the core host for pre-migration backup; only `nginx/rsync/ufw/curl/nodejs`.
- PM2 templates are dead code.
- No true zero-downtime single-node edge deployment: `pm2 delete` + `pm2 start`.
- Multi-node co-located services share the same release directory/timestamp and Nginx site name; node-specific release identity is not preserved.
- Rolling batch health checks only `/health`; edge→core mTLS is only checked in the final step.
- `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL` uses HTTP and a private IP rather than the documented checkout domain HTTPS.
- Backup daemon certificate ownership is not corrected for the `pgbackup` user.
- Storage cert distribution is broader than the design’s per-role least privilege on co-located hosts.
- PKI always generates Fake Rails and backup-daemon leaves even when those tiers are disabled.
- No automatic certificate-expiry remediation beyond deploy-time inspection.
- `SshRunner.writeRemoteFile` can corrupt files if sudo is `NOPASSWD` because the password line is still sent on stdin.
- `preMigrationBackup()` embeds the password in a shell command; SQL passwords are interpolated directly in provisioners.
- `pgHbaSnippet` trusts `hostssl` but no server SSL configuration is written.
- Barman-mode backup health checks call WAL-G (`buildWalGVerifyBucketCommand`) even though WAL-G is not installed in Barman mode.
- Backup daemon `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR` is written before the `pgbackup` user ownership is established.

### 4.4 Edge

- No shared mTLS LB module; three duplicated 761-line files.
- Edge authority guard parses unsigned JWT claims; core remains authoritative, but local route gating can be bypassed.
- No edge-side per-route rate limiting for all public streams beyond existing middleware.
- `probeEdgeToCore` uses the host’s core cert directory for co-located hosts; this works only because core deployment writes all host-role certs into the core release.
- No explicit edge-to-core retry budget for non-idempotent POSTs; the design’s passive failover is limited to safe requests.

### 4.5 Guides / Help Systems

- Design claims 10 books; implementation has 12.
- Design claims 13-state attempt lifecycle; actual `AttemptStatus` has 14.
- Design claims per-rail help for all 20 gateways; `seedGuides.ts` has 14.
- Admin UI edits `instructions_ar`/`instructions_en`, but there is no admin API/UI to edit `help_guide_json`; per-rail structured walkthroughs are seed-only.
- Checkout help center is implemented and data-driven; it is a strong match.

### 4.6 Testing

- Suite 09 directory absent.
- Suite 07 has 2 of 5 planned files.
- Suite 06 missing concurrent refunds/cash-outs.
- Suite 08 missing the 140-case expanded matrix.
- Suite 10 is geometry-only, mocked, and covers no dialogs, filters, steppers, guide simulators, support-config toggle or admin/merchant create flows.
- Suite 11 live journeys are skipped by default.
- DB suites skip when PostgreSQL is unavailable; the test runner does not provision the database.
- `run-exhaustive-suite.sh` T-EX-09 runs `test/storage-engine` / `test/backup-admin`, not the design’s `test/exhaustive/09-storage-backup`.
- `run-exhaustive-suite.sh` T-EX-09b is UI; T-EX-10 is seeder; numbering no longer matches the plan.
- `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts` contains a default password and hardcoded deployment IP.
- Suite 04 uses scripted engine collaborators, not live Fake Rails.
- Suite 05 RBAC/mTLS tests use fake requests/sockets; list-filter tests use one generic `ListSpec`, not 27 real routes.
- The repository’s last-run artifact (`tests/test-results/.last-run.json`) says passed, but it cannot evidence the claimed exhaustive coverage because the default UI suite is mocked.
