+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part documents the edge-to-core transport used by `admin-back`, `merchant-back` and `checkout-back`. It owns the mTLS agent, the `CORE_BACK_URLS` node pool, node selection, passive failure detection, retries, request identity headers, the `x-pg-min-lsn` consistency hint, path/channel confinement, core error mapping and the SSE stream proxy.
+
+It does not own authorization or business validation. `core-back` remains authoritative for token verification, authorities, maker-checker, amount resolution, idempotency and channel-bound client-certificate checks. The client only guarantees that a request reaches an allowed core channel over an authenticated TLS 1.3 connection.
+
+The implementation exists as three near-identical copies:
+
+- `admin-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts`
+- `merchant-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts`
+- `checkout-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts`
+
+Each copy is 761 lines and differs only in `CORE_SERVICE_NAME` and `CORE_CHANNEL_PREFIX`. There is no workspace package, no generated shared module and no single build artifact for the pool.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The historical design requires every edge request to cross a private LAN boundary over mutual TLS 1.3. The edge authenticates with a dedicated client certificate whose CN names the service, and `core-back` binds each internal namespace to that CN. Edge services never receive `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` or another host's client key.
+
+When `core-back` scales horizontally, each edge receives `CORE_BACK_URLS`. The intended behavior is:
+
+- persistent keep-alive connections to every core node;
+- least-in-flight selection with round-robin tie-breaking;
+- passive removal of a failed node, a cooldown, and a half-open probe after the cooldown;
+- retry of idempotent requests on a different node;
+- propagation of `x-pg-min-lsn` so LSN-aware reads can wait for a replica that has replayed the caller's write;
+- no loss of the edge's identity headers (`x-request-id`, `x-real-client-ip`, `x-client-user-agent`, `x-edge-service`).
+
+The design describes this as enabling rolling core restarts without dropping edge traffic. The implementation provides that only for requests that can be retried and only while at least one other eligible node exists; it does not make an individual single-node core restart seamless.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Agent and TLS material
+
+`createCoreAgent()` in each copy builds one `https.Agent` per configured node:
+
+- client certificate from `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH`;
+- client private key from `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`;
+- CA from `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH`;
+- `minVersion` and `maxVersion` fixed to `TLSv1.3`;
+- `rejectUnauthorized: true`;
+- keep-alive enabled with 30-second keep-alive delay and `maxSockets: 64`;
+- the agent-level timeout is `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`.
+
+Material is loaded synchronously with `fs.readFileSync` when the agent is created. A missing file becomes `MTLS_MATERIAL_UNAVAILABLE` (HTTP 500) rather than a process crash. Because the agent is cached, replacing certificate files on disk does not affect a running process until the pool is rebuilt. The pool is rebuilt when the configured URL signature changes or when `resetCoreAgent()`/`resetCorePool()` is called by tests.
+
+### 3.2 Pool lifecycle and selection
+
+`ensureNodes()` parses `CORE_BACK_URLS` or falls back to `CORE_BACK_URL`. `parseCoreBackUrls()`:
+
+- splits on commas;
+- rejects empty entries;
+- requires absolute `https:` URLs;
+- de-duplicates by normalized `URL.toString()`;
+- preserves the original trimmed strings for requests.
+
+Each node state tracks `url`, `agent`, `healthy`, `inFlight`, `failures`, `lastFailureAt` and `cooldownUntil`.
+
+`eligiblePool(excluded)` implements the cooldown/half-open state:
+
+1. If any excluded node is unhealthy, has zero in-flight requests and its cooldown has elapsed, return only those half-open nodes. This lets one request probe recovery before the node rejoins the general pool.
+2. Otherwise return every healthy, non-excluded node.
+3. If neither set is non-empty the request fails with `503 CORE_UNAVAILABLE`.
+
+`selectNode()` picks the minimum in-flight count and uses a monotonic round-robin cursor to break ties. The cursor advances on every selection and is reduced modulo the tied set size. A node selected for an attempt is added to the request-local `attempted` set, so a retry never targets the same URL within one logical call.
+
+### 3.3 Failure marking and retries
+
+`markNodeFailure()` sets `healthy=false`, increments `failures`, records `lastFailureAt` and sets `cooldownUntil = now + CORE_FAILURE_COOLDOWN_MS` (5 seconds). `markNodeHealthy()` clears all failure state.
+
+Retry eligibility is controlled by `retryAttemptsFor()`:
+
+- idempotent methods default to retrying: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`;
+- `POST` and `PATCH` do not retry by default;
+- `retryIdempotent: true` forces retries; `retryIfUnavailable: true` allows a non-idempotent call to retry;
+- `maxAttempts` defaults to 2 and is floored to at least 1; there is no upper cap.
+
+`request()` marks a node failed and retries when the node returns HTTP `502` or `503`, or when the request throws a connection/TLS error. Any other status, including other `5xx` responses, marks the node healthy and is returned to the caller. If every attempt ends in a `502`/`503`, the last response body is returned rather than converted to a local error. If every node has already been attempted and no eligible node remains, the call fails with `CORE_UNAVAILABLE`.
+
+`mapCoreTransportError()` maps transport failures to stable edge errors:
+
+| Transport condition | Edge error |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `ETIMEDOUT`, `ESOCKETTIMEDOUT` | `504 CORE_TIMEOUT` |
+| `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `EHOSTUNREACH` | `502 CORE_UNREACHABLE` |
+| `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN` | `502 CORE_DNS_FAILURE` |
+| TLS error codes | `502 CORE_TLS_ERROR` |
+| other failures | `502 CORE_CONNECTION_ERROR` |
+
+### 3.4 Headers and consistency
+
+`buildCoreHeaders()` emits:
+
+- `x-request-id`: the resolved edge request id;
+- `x-real-client-ip`: the client IP resolved from the trusted proxy;
+- `x-client-user-agent`: the caller's user agent, possibly empty;
+- `x-edge-service`: `admin-back`, `merchant-back` or `checkout-back`;
+- `accept: application/json`;
+- `content-type: application/json` when a JSON body exists, or the supplied raw content type;
+- `authorization` when present;
+- every caller-supplied header, lowercased;
+- `x-pg-min-lsn` when `minLsn` or `consistencyLsn` is non-empty.
+
+`consistencyHeader(lsn)` is a helper that returns the same header or an empty object. The client does not generate an LSN. Callers must obtain one from a write response or another trusted source. `x-pg-min-lsn` is passed through to `core-back`, where `lib/storageEngine` converts it into an `atLeastLsn` read constraint with a 250 ms wait.
+
+### 3.5 Path and channel confinement
+
+`assertCorePath()` rejects:
+
+- empty paths and non-rooted paths;
+- protocol-relative paths (`//...`), embedded `://` and backslashes;
+- invalid percent escaping;
+- decoded `.` or `..` segments;
+- any path outside the service's channel prefix.
+
+The prefixes are:
+
+| Service | Prefix |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `admin-back` | `/internal/admin` |
+| `merchant-back` | `/internal/merchant` |
+| `checkout-back` | `/internal/checkout` |
+
+`resolveCoreUrlAgainst()` pins the result to the configured base origin and appends the path to the base pathname. `resolveCoreUrl()` exposes the same behavior for callers and tests. This is a client-side guard only; `core-back` independently enforces the certificate CN with `requireEdgeIdentity()` in `core-back/api/middleware/mtlsGuard.ts`.
+
+### 3.6 SSE streams and fallback behavior
+
+`openCoreStream()` is the streaming counterpart of `request()`:
+
+- sets `accept: text/event-stream` and `cache-control: no-cache`;
+- uses the same node selection, retry count, cooldown and attempted-node set;
+- increments `inFlight` until the stream ends, closes or errors;
+- if a node answers `502`/`503` and another attempt is possible, drains that response into a buffer, records it as `lastStream`, and tries the next node;
+- if retries are exhausted, returns `lastStream` or maps the transport error.
+
+`proxyCoreStream()` converts a non-2xx upstream into the normal core HTTP error, then copies the stream to the express response with `cache-control: no-cache, no-transform`, `connection: keep-alive` and `x-accel-buffering: no`. On client disconnect it aborts the upstream request.
+
+There is no true fallback to polling at the edge. Checkout and POS SSE are implemented by the core endpoint polling PostgreSQL on a timer; an established edge stream that breaks is ended, not resumed. The buffered `lastStream` fallback only preserves a failed handshake response body for retry purposes.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- Every core URL must be an absolute `https:` URL. Plain HTTP is not accepted by the edge configuration schema.
+- TLS 1.3 is the only accepted protocol version.
+- The client cert CN must match the channel; the client path guard prevents accidental cross-channel calls, and `core-back` prevents forged ones.
+- A call never retries against the same URL twice.
+- A default retry only applies to idempotent methods.
+- A `502`/`503` from any node is interpreted as node unavailability even if generated by application code.
+- Request identity headers and `authorization` are forwarded verbatim; the edge does not mint or re-sign tokens.
+- The pool does not load-balance SSE streams after establishment; selection happens once per stream open.
+- LSN hints are propagated, not validated. A malformed value is passed to core, where the storage layer decides how to handle it.
+- The client never receives or uses `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY`, or another service's certificate.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+### Environment
+
+| Key | Required | Used by | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `CORE_BACK_URL` | yes | all BFFs | First core URL and fallback when `CORE_BACK_URLS` is unset. |
+| `CORE_BACK_URLS` | no | all BFFs | Comma-separated core pool. |
+| `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH` | yes | all BFFs | Client certificate. |
+| `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH` | yes | all BFFs | Client private key. |
+| `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH` | yes | all BFFs | Internal CA certificate. |
+| `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | no | all BFFs | Per-request and agent timeout. Defaults: admin 60000, merchant/checkout 30000. |
+| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | no | all BFFs | Peers whose forwarded IP headers are trusted. |
+| `POS_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` | no | merchant | Stream timeout passed by the POS SSE route (default 900000). |
+
+### Deployment surface
+
+`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` derives `CORE_BACK_URLS` as `https://<core-private-ip>:<service-port>,...` by default. An explicit `CORE_BACK_URLS` in `deploy.env` wins. `deploy/deploy.ts` writes the URL list and `CORE_BACK_URL` (first URL) into every edge `.env`.
+
+The deploy engine installs only the CA and the edge's own client certificate on an edge host. Certificate paths in the generated `.env` are relative (`shared/certs/...`) and are expanded to the release directory by `absoluteEnv()`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- When adding a core node, add it to `CORE_NODES` or set `CORE_BACK_URLS`; re-deploy the edge tiers so their process environment changes. The pool itself would notice a changed environment only if the process configuration changes, which requires a restart in a deployed environment.
+- When rotating certificates, restart or redeploy the edge processes. Replacing files in place is not sufficient for a running pool.
+- Check `/health` on the edge only for process liveness; it does not probe core. Use `deploy/lib/healthVerifier.ts` or a manual mTLS request to check the upstream.
+- Use `x-request-id` to correlate an edge failure with core logs. The edge maps core envelopes and preserves `code`, `message`, `details` and `reference`.
+- To debug node selection, inspect `CORE_BACK_URLS` in the generated `.env`, the edge logs and the core health endpoint. There are no exported pool metrics or a status endpoint.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Per-node keep-alive TLS 1.3 agents with client certificates and CA verification.
+- Least-in-flight selection with round-robin tie-breaking.
+- Passive failure marking with a 5-second cooldown.
+- Half-open selection: one zero-in-flight request probes an unhealthy node after cooldown.
+- Idempotent retries and explicit non-idempotent retry opt-in.
+- `x-pg-min-lsn` propagation and header helper.
+- Channel path confinement and URL origin pinning.
+- Core envelope and transport error mapping.
+- SSE stream proxying with pre-establishment retry and buffering of failed handshake responses.
+
+### Partial
+
+- The "shared" client is a copy-paste implementation. Behavior is consistent today, but a change must be applied three times.
+- Certificate rotation requires a restart; there is no file watcher or hot reload.
+- The SSE fallback preserves a failed response but does not resume an interrupted stream.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No circuit-breaker metrics, pool introspection, or administrative pool status endpoint.
+- No request hedging or per-attempt deadline separate from the overall timeout.
+- No automatic retry for `POST`/`PATCH` unless a caller opts in.
+- No jitter on cooldown or randomized selection.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- Treating every upstream `502`/`503` as a node failure can evict a healthy core node that legitimately returned a gateway-style `502`/`503`.
+- A half-open node is preferred over healthy nodes while any half-open candidate exists. With several recovering nodes this can concentrate probe traffic rather than spread it.
+- `maxAttempts` can exceed the number of nodes; the attempted set then stops the loop early.
+- A pool with an empty URL list throws `CORE_UNAVAILABLE`; there is no startup-time rejection of an empty `CORE_BACK_URLS` beyond the fallback to `CORE_BACK_URL`.
+- The stream path does not retry after response headers are delivered; a mid-stream core restart is visible to the browser.
+
+### Code gap versus documentation
+
+The historical design describes zero-downtime rolling core restarts. The client enables retry-based continuity for idempotent one-shot calls and for stream establishment, but it does not guarantee zero downtime for non-idempotent calls, established SSE streams, or a single core node. This document records the as-built behavior.
+

+## Checkout Edge BFF
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+`checkout-back` is the public checkout and inbound-webhook edge. It serves anonymous payers and external payment gateways:
+
+- payer link resolution and attempt lifecycle under `/api/v1/pay/*`;
+- the checkout status SSE stream;
+- browser return handling under `/api/v1/return/*`;
+- raw inbound gateway webhooks under `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`.
+
+It owns edge schema validation, the zero-monetary-field assertion, raw webhook capture, header allowlisting, environment translation, client IP propagation, rate limiting, redirect construction and mTLS forwarding to `/internal/checkout/*`. It owns no database, no session, no money resolution and no gateway signature verification.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The checkout edge is deliberately read/execute-only. A payer can select a rail and submit form data, but can never create a link, change a link or supply an amount or currency. `core-back` resolves money from `payment_links` by `linkKey`.
+
+Inbound webhooks are treated as untrusted. The design calls for capturing the raw bytes and headers, forwarding them unchanged to the core inbox, and returning the gateway's configured ack quickly. The core verifies the signature, IP allowlist and replay window. The design's blueprint says the inbox returns the ack in under 10 ms; the as-built core performs verification inline before acking.
+
+The return URL is an untrusted browser hint. Core inspects the attempt, triggers an inquiry where appropriate, and the edge redirects the browser to the checkout status page.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Process and mount order
+
+`checkout-back/index.ts`:
+
+- disables `x-powered-by`;
+- sets `trust proxy` to false;
+- enables CORS with any origin and no credentials;
+- installs request logging;
+- serves unauthenticated `GET /health`;
+- mounts `/api/v1/inbound` with `inboundRouter` **before** the JSON body parser, so the inbound router can install its own raw parser;
+- then installs JSON and URL-encoded parsers (`MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`);
+- mounts `/api/v1` with the pay and return routers;
+- adds the shared 404 and error handlers.
+
+The listener binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`). The deploy engine writes `127.0.0.1`; Nginx is the public listener.
+
+### 3.2 Middleware and guards
+
+| Layer | Behavior |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `payLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), on the pay router. |
+| `returnLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, on the return router. |
+| `inboundLimiter` | 60-second window, `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 600), on the inbound router. |
+| Raw parser | `express.raw({ type: () => true, limit: MAX_INBOUND_BODY_BYTES })`, applied to every inbound request. |
+| `assertNoMonetaryFields` | Recursively rejects forbidden monetary keys (amount, currency, total, fee, commission, price, net/gross/debit/credit amounts, and close variants) with `400 AMOUNT_NOT_ACCEPTED`. Applied to initiate, confirm, resend, cancel and client-event. |
+| Schema validation | Zod schemas for link keys, attempt ids, rail codes, sub-modes, form data, OTPs, evidence, idempotency keys and client events. |
+| Header allowlist | Inbound forwards only `content-type`, `user-agent`, `content-length`, `x-signature`, `x-gateway-signature`, `x-hub-signature-256`, `x-moomalat-signature`, `x-timestamp` and `x-nonce`. |
+| Environment translation | `sandbox`, `test`, `uat` map to core `SANDBOX`; `live`, `production` map to `LIVE`; anything else is rejected. |
+
+There is no edge authentication. Anonymous payers and external gateways are the intended callers. The link key, attempt id/token, OTP and idempotency key are the edge-visible capabilities; core validates each against database state.
+
+### 3.3 Forwarding behavior
+
+Payer routes call `callCore()` directly with a method, path, body and context. They do not use a generic forwarder. The context includes the request id, resolved client IP, user agent and no bearer token.
+
+`GET /pay/:linkKey` resolves public link data. `POST /initiate` validates the rail code, optional sub-mode, form data and idempotency key, then forwards. `GET /logs/:attemptId` returns public attempt state. `POST /confirm`, `/resend`, `/cancel` and `/client-event` validate their schemas and forward.
+
+`GET /pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` calls `proxyCoreStream()` with a 10-minute timeout. The core endpoint itself polls PostgreSQL every 2 seconds, emits an SSE `status` event when the status changes, and ends on a terminal status or after the deadline. The edge retries a failed stream handshake on another core node but cannot resume an established stream.
+
+Inbound `ANY /inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`:
+
+1. Validates the gateway identifier, environment and path token shape.
+2. Reads the raw `Buffer` and the original `content-type`.
+3. Translates the environment.
+4. Calls `callCoreRaw()` with method, raw bytes, content type, allowlisted headers, request id, client IP and a 10-second timeout.
+5. Relays the core status code, content type and body.
+
+The edge does not parse the webhook body, compute a signature, or decide whether the event is genuine. Core stores the event, resolves the channel and attempt, performs synchronous verification, updates the event and then returns the channel ack status/body. If core returns an error, the edge relays it; no local ack is fabricated.
+
+Browser return `GET|POST /return/:attemptToken`:
+
+- validates the attempt token;
+- calls core with the query for GET or `{ hint: "browser_return" }` for POST;
+- builds `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` + `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH` with `attempt_token` and an optional `reference`;
+- redirects with 302.
+
+### 3.4 Route map
+
+| Method | Edge path | Core path |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| GET | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey` | `GET /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey` |
+| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/initiate` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/initiate` |
+| GET | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId` | `GET /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId` |
+| GET | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` | SSE proxy of `GET /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` |
+| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/confirm` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/confirm` |
+| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/resend` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/resend` |
+| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/cancel` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/cancel` |
+| POST | `/api/v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/client-event` | `POST /internal/checkout/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/client-event` |
+| ANY | `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken` | `ANY /internal/checkout/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken` (raw bytes) |
+| GET, POST | `/api/v1/return/:attemptToken` | `GET, POST /internal/checkout/return/:attemptToken` |
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- No payer schema accepts `amount`, `currency` or any normalized monetary field. The recursive assertion rejects nested occurrences before forwarding.
+- The payer can submit only the link key, rail code, sub-mode, form data, idempotency key, OTP and untrusted client event hints.
+- The edge never resolves money, fees or currency; core reads the authoritative link.
+- Inbound bodies are forwarded byte for byte. The edge must not normalize JSON or re-encode forms.
+- Only the allowlisted inbound headers cross the boundary. `authorization`, `cookie` and arbitrary `x-*` headers are dropped.
+- Core is the only place where gateway signatures, replay windows, IP allowlists and channel/environment bindings are verified.
+- Client event aliases (`COMPLETE_CALLBACK`, `ERROR_CALLBACK`, widget aliases) are normalized to `completeCallback`, `errorCallback`, `widgetEvent` and `returnHint`.
+- The return redirect destination comes only from configured `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` and `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH`, not from client input.
+- SSE responses must disable buffering; Nginx sets `proxy_buffering off` for the status route.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+### Environment
+
+| Key | Default | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `NODE_ENV` | `development` | Runtime mode. |
+| `PORT` | `4103` | Backend listener port. |
+| `BIND_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind address; deploy overrides to `127.0.0.1`. |
+| `CORE_BACK_URL` | required | First core node, absolute HTTPS. |
+| `CORE_BACK_URLS` | optional | Core pool. |
+| `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH`, `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`, `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH` | required | Edge mTLS material. |
+| `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | Default core timeout (inbound explicitly uses 10 seconds). |
+| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | loopback plus RFC1918 ranges | Trusted forwarded-IP peers. |
+| `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES` | `1048576` | JSON limit. |
+| `MAX_INBOUND_BODY_BYTES` | `3145728` | Raw webhook limit. |
+| `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:5103` | Redirect base. |
+| `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH` | `/pay/status` | Redirect path. |
+| `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `120`, `60000` | Pay and return limiters. |
+| `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `INBOUND_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` | `600`, `60000` | Inbound limiter. |
+
+### Deployment surface
+
+`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` writes `BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1`, `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL=https://<CHECKOUT_DOMAIN>` and `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH=/pay/status`. The checkout Nginx vhost proxies `/api/` to `127.0.0.1:4103`, disables buffering for the SSE route, and applies `client_max_body_size` sized for the inbound raw limit. The edge `.env` contains no database or KMS secret.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+```bash
+cd checkout-back
+bun install
+bun run start
+bun run dev
+bun test
+bun run typecheck
+```
+
+- Public reachability is through `https://pay.<domain>/api`; port 4103 stays loopback-only.
+- To test a webhook locally, send the exact gateway bytes and signature headers to the inbound route. The edge preserves bytes and the allowlisted headers; the core verification result determines the processing outcome.
+- A gateway retry is expected after a non-2xx edge/core response. Dedupe is by `channel.id + SHA-256(rawBody)` in core; the edge does not dedupe.
+- For SSE problems, check Nginx buffering, the core 10-minute deadline and the 2-second poll interval. The edge does not send keepalive comments of its own.
+- For a redirect loop, verify `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` and `CHECKOUT_FRONT_STATUS_PATH`.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Public pay, return, SSE and inbound route surface.
+- Zero-monetary-field assertion with nested scanning.
+- Raw inbound capture with byte preservation and strict header allowlist.
+- Environment and client-event vocabulary translation.
+- Core pool, retries, LSN propagation and channel confinement.
+- Rate limits per route family.
+- Browser redirect to the configured checkout status page.
+
+### Partial
+
+- Inbound webhooks are processed synchronously. The design describes a queue-and-fast-ack inbox; the code stores the event, runs verification inline, updates the event and only then ack's.
+- SSE is a core-side database poller, not a transition-bus subscription.
+- The edge's stream retry covers handshake failure only.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- Asynchronous webhook verification with a fast ack.
+- Stream resume/replay, `Last-Event-ID` support or a polling fallback.
+- Edge-side operational or diagnostic routes.
+- Signature pre-validation at the edge (intentionally left to core).
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- The 10-second inbound timeout can return `504 CORE_TIMEOUT` while core continues writing the event and processing it. The gateway may retry; core dedupe should suppress duplicate effects, but the observable response is ambiguous.
+- Synchronous verification puts crypto, IP lookup and replay checks on the webhook request path, so a slow verification consumes the gateway's timeout budget and an inbound worker.
+- If the core ack status or body is misconfigured, the edge faithfully relays it; there is no fallback ack.
+- The return handler issues a 302 after core responds. A core error is surfaced as an error response, not a redirect with an error state.
+- `CHECKOUT_FRONT_BASE_URL` accepts HTTP or HTTPS in the edge schema. In production it should be HTTPS.
+- The default `BIND_HOST` is `0.0.0.0`; only the deploy engine's override to loopback prevents direct exposure.
+

+
+After initiate, the page opens an `EventSource` for the checkout attempt status route through `checkout-back`.

+- `onmessage` parses `payload.attempt ?? payload`, applies the snapshot, updates the client action/reference/status and moves to `RECEIPT`, `ERROR` or `CONFIRMING` as appropriate.
+- `onerror` closes the stream and sets it to null. The page does **not** reconnect, back off or fall back to polling, so a dropped stream can leave the payer on `CONFIRMING` until a reload.
+- Unmount closes the stream and clears the countdown.
+- The stream is display-only. Server attempt state remains authoritative.

+
+On `SUCCEEDED`, the page enters `RECEIPT`, closes the stream and shows the payment complete badge, the server `totalAmount`, the reference and an optional "Return To Merchant" button.

+

+3. **Per-rail guide** prerequisites, steps and troubleshooting.

+When the admin disables support, `supportConfig` becomes `null`. The contact block, working hours and FAQ hide. The following remain available:

+- State guidance and attempt status.
+- Payment reference and copy action.

+## 8. UI system and conventions
+
+- Checkout uses the shared `--pg-*` token sheet and self-hosted Plus Jakarta Sans/Cairo/JetBrains Mono fonts. Vuetify defaults are flat cards, 36 px no-transform buttons, outlined compact fields, ripple off and RTL-aware locale.
+- The payer layout is intentionally not the admin/merchant shell. `layouts/checkout.tsx` renders one `<main class="pg-checkout">`; the page adds a max-width 560 px column centered on desktop and top-aligned on small screens.
+- The page composes a focused subset of primitives: `SurfaceCard`, `DescriptionList`, `MoneyDisplay`, `MonoRef`, `StatusBadge`, `EmptyState`, `SlideOverDrawer`, `MetaPill` and `FormField`.
+- There is no table/export workflow on the payer surface. Shared table/XLSX packages exist in the workspace, but checkout does not expose spreadsheet export.
+- Do not add page-local hard-coded palettes. Use the tokens, semantic status tones and shared primitives.

+## 9. i18n and RTL
+
+- Locales are Arabic (`ar`) and English (`en`). Arabic is the default: `locale-name` is treated as English only when stored as exactly `en`; otherwise the app starts in Arabic.
+- The locale is stored in `localStorage`, applied to `<html lang>`/`dir` (`rtl` for Arabic, `ltr` for English) and passed to Vuetify's locale adapter.

+
+- The deploy engine builds `checkout-front` with `bun run build` and syncs `dist` to the checkout host.
+- Nginx serves the SPA with history fallback and proxies `/api/` to `checkout-back`. The checkout host is public-facing with deploy-managed TLS (`certbot`, `custom` or `self_signed`).
+- The production SPA uses same-origin `/api`; `VITE_API_URL` is a development convenience only.
+- There is no `runtime-config.js` and no deploy-generated SPA flag for checkout-front. Checkout support visibility is controlled by the admin-managed platform setting, not an environment variable.
+- `checkout-back` exposes `/pay`, `/return` and `/inbound`, proxies the payer status stream and calls `core-back` over mTLS. The browser never receives core credentials.
+
+## 11. Testing and troubleshooting
+
+### Recommended checks
+
+```bash
+bun run type-check
+bun run lint
+bun run build
+```

+Browser/unit coverage comes from the `tests/` workspace:

+- `checkout/pay.spec.ts` for the payer surface and no horizontal overflow.
+- `checkout/a11y.spec.ts` for accessibility basics.
+- `exhaustive/exhaustive-checkout-surface.spec.ts` across viewports/locales/themes.
+- `unit/checkout-redirect.test.ts` for empty allowlists, scheme rejection, exact/subdomain matching and wildcard behavior.
+- `e2e-live/live.spec.ts` when the live stack is available.
+
+### Common problems
+
+| Symptom | Check |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Link will not load | Confirm the link key, link status/expiry and `checkout-back` availability. A load error is not the router 404 page. |
+| 404 recovery button loops | Known bug: the button targets the non-existent `Dashboard` route. Navigate directly to a valid `/pay/:linkKey`. |
+| Amount or currency mismatch | The server resolves both from the link. The SPA never sends them; investigate the link record/backend, not browser code. |
+| No return button after success | The link must have a redirect URL and a non-empty allowlist containing the exact host or a parent domain. An empty allowlist denies all. |
+| Redirect is blocked | The action URL host is not allowlisted, or the scheme is not a real HTTP(S) host. Do not bypass the host check. |
+| Payer stays on "Confirming" | The SSE stream may have dropped; the SPA does not reconnect or poll. Reload and check the server attempt status/reference. |
+| OTP form rejects input | Confirm OTP length/attempt limits and that Arabic digits are normalized; the SPA does not reveal whether the subscriber exists. |
+| Embedded widget fails to load | The provider host must be in the fixed allowlist. A new provider requires a code change; SRI hash selection is a known risk when multiple scripts are present. |
+| Help contact/FAQ disappeared | The admin disabled checkout support or hid the relevant contact flags. State guidance, reference, rail guide and banner remain. |
+| Rail instructions are missing | The selected rail has no `helpGuide`, or the link summary did not project one. Per-rail content is seed/code-managed; there is no admin editor. |
+| Payer shows "do not pay again" | `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN` is not a failure. Wait, refresh/check support with the reference and do not initiate a second payment. |

+## Checkout Payer Flow
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the public payer experience in `checkout-front`:
+
+- The `/pay/:linkKey` page and its phase machine.
+- Rail selection, field rendering, validation and client-action renderers.
+- Attempt initiation, confirmation, resend, cancellation and client-event forwarding.
+- SSE status consumption, amount breakdown, receipt and return-to-merchant behavior.
+- The checkout 404 surface.
+
+It does not own `checkout-back`, the core attempt engine, gateway protocols, or the checkout help content. It also does not claim that browser return/callback signals are trusted; the core only trusts server-verified channels.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The checkout is deliberately narrow and zero-trust:
+
+1. **The server owns the amount.** The SPA never sends `amount` or `currency` on initiate/confirm; `core-back` resolves both from the payment link.
+2. **The payer sees one focused column.** The layout is centered on desktop and top-aligned on small screens.
+3. **Rail selection is catalog-driven.** Visible rails, names, collection modes and fields come from the link summary.
+4. **The rail's client action determines the next screen.** OTP form, redirect, embedded widget, QR/code, or push/transfer.
+5. **The payer does not judge success.** Browser redirects and widget callbacks are hints; the authoritative status arrives through the server/SSE and core verification.
+6. **Money is displayed as decimal strings.** The page never computes totals with floating point.
+7. **Return is opt-in and allowlisted.** The return-to-merchant button appears only after success and only for an allowlisted redirect host.
+8. **A failed link is a clear dead end.** The page shows a friendly unavailable/failed state rather than a raw error.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Route and layout
+
+- `/pay/:linkKey` (`Pay`) renders `pages/pay/[linkKey]/index.tsx`.
+- `/` (`Home`) redirects to `NotFound`.
+- `/:pathMatch(.*)*` (`NotFound`) renders the token-styled 404 page.
+- `layouts/checkout.tsx` is a single `<main class="pg-checkout">` with an optional title.
+- The page adds a max-width 560 px column with the merchant name, help button, language toggle, summary card, phase content and footer.
+
+### 3.2 Phase machine
+
+`type Phase = "SUMMARY" | "FORM" | "ACTION" | "CONFIRMING" | "RECEIPT" | "ERROR"`.
+
+| Phase | Entered when | What renders |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `SUMMARY` | Initial ref value | Declared but not used as a visible state; loading and load errors are separate. |
+| `FORM` | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` succeeds | Rail cards, per-rail banner, rail fields, "Pay Now". |
+| `ACTION` | Initiate returns a client action | Countdown, renderer for the action kind. |
+| `CONFIRMING` | Snapshot status is `VERIFYING`, `UNKNOWN` or `AUTHORIZING` | Spinner, status badge, reference, cancel. |
+| `RECEIPT` | Snapshot status is `SUCCEEDED` | Payment complete, amount, reference, optional return button. |
+| `ERROR` | Load failure, cancelled attempt, or terminal failure status (`FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `BLOCKED`) | Failure message, status, "Try Another Method". |
+
+Loading and `loadError` are rendered outside the phase switch. A load error shows "This Payment Link Is No Longer Available" and "Cannot process this payment" in a card; it is not the router 404 page.
+
+### 3.3 Summary and amount breakdown
+
+`GET v1/pay/:linkKey` returns a `PayLinkSummary`:
+
+- `linkKey`, `merchantTradeName`, optional logo/description.
+- `amount`, `currency`.
+- `feeBearerMode` (`MERCHANT_ABSORBS`, `PAYER_SURCHARGE`, `SPLIT`).
+- `baseAmount`, `feeAmount`, `totalAmount`, `merchantAmount`.
+- Optional `splitPercent`.
+- `visibleRails`, optional `expiresAt`, `status`, `redirectUrl`, `allowlistedRedirectHosts`.
+- Optional `supportConfig`.
+
+The breakdown always shows the base amount and amount charged. It inserts a service-fee row only when the fee bearer is not `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`; for `SPLIT` the row label includes the split percentage. The amount charged is `totalAmount`.
+
+`visibleRails` is computed by the backend's visible-rails resolver (merchant status, application/rail whitelist, route health/limits, credential state, amount/currency, and related predicates). The SPA does not recompute visibility.
+
+### 3.4 Rail selection and fields
+
+`RailCards`:
+
+- Shows each visible rail's localized name and collection-mode pill.
+- Uses a collection-mode icon.
+- Selects the first rail by default after summary load.
+- Resets form values and errors when the payer switches rails.
+
+`RailFieldForm`:
+
+- Renders every field in `rail.fields`.
+- `select` uses a `VSelect`; all other input types use `VTextField`.
+- PAN-sensitive fields render as password inputs.
+- Labels/placeholders fall back between Arabic and English.
+- Inputs use `autocomplete="off"`.
+
+`zReady.ts` normalizes and validates:
+
+- Arabic digits are normalized to ASCII.
+- `phone` uses local `09` normalization.
+- `numeric`/`otp` strip non-digit characters (numeric allows a decimal point in normalization, then validates digits with optional decimals).
+- `wallet_id` expects `NP-` plus 12 digits.
+- `otp` expects 4-8 digits.
+- Required/min/max/regex rules from the rail field descriptor are applied.
+
+The page validates with `schema.safeParse(normalized)` and maps the first issue per field into `formErrors`.
+
+### 3.5 Initiate
+
+`POST v1/pay/:linkKey/initiate` sends:
+
+```json
+{
+  "railCode": "<selected rail>",
+  "formData": { "<field>": "<normalized value>" },
+  "idempotencyKey": "chk-<time>-<random>"
+}
+```
+
+The client generates a fresh idempotency key per initiate/confirm attempt. The response is `InitiateResponse` with `attemptId`, `reference`, `status` and `clientAction`. The page stores the attempt, opens the SSE stream, starts a countdown if the action has `expires_at`, and sets phase `ACTION`.
+
+A client-supplied `amount` or `currency` is outside this contract and is rejected by `checkout-back`/`core-back`.
+
+### 3.6 Client-action renderers
+
+| Action kind | Renderer | Behavior |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `SHOW_OTP_FORM` | `OtpFormRenderer` | OTP input, attempt counter, resend, verify/pay; Enter submits. |
+| `HTTP_REDIRECT` | `RedirectRenderer` | Auto-redirects on mount; GET query or POST form; blocks non-allowlisted hosts; manual retry button. |
+| `RENDER_EMBEDDED` | `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` | Loads allowlisted HTTPS scripts with SRI/crossOrigin, listens for postMessage callbacks, optional iframe sandbox, removes scripts on unmount. |
+| `SHOW_QR_OR_CODE` | `QrOrCodeRenderer` | Renders QR data URL, optional pay code, bilingual instructions, deep link, expiry. |
+| `SHOW_PUSH_OR_TRANSFER` | `PushOrTransferRenderer` | Shows destination/reference/wallet hint, instructions, optional proof upload, expiry. |
+
+`OtpFormRenderer` limits the OTP to the action length and normalizes Arabic digits. `RedirectRenderer` requires a non-empty allowlist; a wildcard accepts any real host but `javascript:`/`data:` URLs still fail host parsing. `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` uses a fixed allowlist of Moamalat, MPGS test, Evo, and Numo hosts and an origin check for incoming messages.
+
+### 3.7 Confirm, resend, cancel
+
+- `confirmOtp` posts `{ otp, idempotencyKey }` to `POST .../confirm`, applies the returned snapshot, and moves to `CONFIRMING` for `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN`.
+- `resendOtp` posts to `POST .../resend` and shows a notice; it does not reset the attempt.
+- `cancelAttempt` posts to `POST .../cancel`, closes the stream and moves to `ERROR`.
+- `sendClientEvent` posts to `POST .../client-event` with `{ event, payload }`.
+
+Client events are canonicalized through a local alias map:
+
+- `ready`/`widget_ready`/`widget_ready_event` → `widgetEvent`.
+- `closed`/`widget_closed` → `widgetEvent`.
+- `complete`/`completed`/`complete_callback` → `completeCallback`.
+- `error`/`error_callback`/`cancel`/`cancelled`/`cancel_callback` → `errorCallback`.
+- `return`/`return_hint` → `returnHint`.
+
+These events are hints. The core must still verify the payment through a trusted channel.
+
+### 3.8 SSE status stream
+
+After initiate, the page creates:
+
+```text
+new EventSource("v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status")
+```
+
+- `onmessage` parses `payload.attempt ?? payload`, applies the snapshot, updates client action/reference/status, and changes the phase for success, terminal failure, or confirming states.
+- `onerror` closes the stream and sets it to null; the page does not reconnect or start polling.
+- `onBeforeUnmount` closes the stream and clears the countdown.
+
+`checkout-back` exposes the status route as an SSE proxy and `tests/e2e/checkout`/`tests/e2e-live` expect `text/event-stream`. The historical performance note that core SSE polls the database rather than subscribing to a transition bus is recorded in the edge/core parts; the SPA only knows the SSE contract.
+
+The page also starts a one-second countdown from the client action's `expires_at`; it does not itself expire or cancel the server attempt.
+
+### 3.9 Receipt and return
+
+When the snapshot status becomes `SUCCEEDED`:
+
+- Phase becomes `RECEIPT`.
+- The stream closes.
+- The page shows "Payment Receipt", a success badge, the total amount and the reference.
+
+A "Return To Merchant" button appears only when `summary.redirectUrl` exists **and** `isAllowedRedirect(redirectUrl, allowlistedRedirectHosts)` is true. The allowlist must be non-empty; matching is exact host or subdomain. The button performs `window.location.assign`.
+
+There is no automatic return redirect on success. The payer may remain on the receipt.
+
+### 3.10 Error and unavailable states
+
+- A load error shows "This Payment Link Is No Longer Available" and "Cannot process this payment".
+- A terminal attempt status (`FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `BLOCKED`) moves to `ERROR` with the status badge and a "Try Another Method" button that returns to `FORM`.
+- An `UNKNOWN`/`VERIFYING`/`AUTHORIZING` status moves to `CONFIRMING` and tells the payer not to pay again (the detailed guidance is in the help drawer).
+
+### 3.11 404 bug
+
+`checkout-front/src/pages/public/not-found/index.tsx` renders a 404 card with a button:
+
+```text
+<RouterLink to={{ name: "Dashboard" }}>
+```
+
+The checkout router has no `Dashboard` route. The link therefore resolves to the catch-all `NotFound` again. The intended recovery target is unclear because checkout has no home page; `/` itself redirects to `NotFound`. This is a real recovery bug, not a styling issue.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **No client amount/currency.** Initiate and confirm payloads must not include `amount` or `currency`; the server rejects them.
+2. **Idempotency keys are required for initiate/confirm.** The client generates one per action.
+3. **The event/action contract is canonical.** Renderers consume the five `ClientAction` kinds; widget events are translated to canonical event names before posting.
+4. **Browser hints are not trust.** Return URLs, redirects and widget callbacks never mark an attempt successful in the SPA.
+5. **Redirect hosts must be allowlisted.** Empty allowlists deny all; `javascript:`/`data:` schemes are rejected.
+6. **The SSE stream is display-only.** The server attempt state remains authoritative.
+7. **Money is displayed, not calculated, as decimal strings.** The summary provides base/fee/total; the SPA does not sum floats.
+8. **The receipt amount is the server total.** The page does not recompute it from the base amount.
+9. **Return is opt-in.** Only an allowlisted `redirectUrl` produces a return button.
+10. **Checkout is unauthenticated.** There is no payer account or session authority.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Operation | Endpoint |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Load link summary | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` |
+| Initiate attempt | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/initiate` |
+| Attempt logs | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId` |
+| Status stream | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` (SSE) |
+| Confirm OTP | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/confirm` |
+| Resend OTP | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/resend` |
+| Cancel | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/cancel` |
+| Client event | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/client-event` |
+
+Environment: `VITE_API_URL` (edge base), `VITE_SEND_NOT_FOUND_TRANSLATIONS`, `VITE_MY_TAILSCALE`. The SPA talks only to `checkout-back` under `/api`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Debug a stuck payer: check the attempt status badge and reference; `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN` means "do not pay again", not "failed".
+- Debug a missing return button: confirm the link has a redirect URL and the host is in the application allowlist.
+- Debug a redirect: inspect `HTTP_REDIRECT` action URL/method/form fields and the allowlist; the page does not bypass the host check.
+- Debug an OTP: confirm the OTP length, attempt count and resend state; the SPA does not reveal whether the subscriber exists.
+- Debug the status stream: confirm the SSE endpoint returns `text/event-stream` and the attempt id matches; the SPA does not poll after an SSE error.
+- Debug a 404: do not use the recovery button until the route target is fixed; navigate manually to a valid `/pay/:linkKey`.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Summary load, amount breakdown, rail cards and rail-field validation.
+- Initiate, OTP confirm/resend, cancel and client-event forwarding.
+- Five client-action renderers with redirect/script allowlists.
+- SSE status consumption and phase transitions.
+- Receipt with server total and allowlisted return.
+- Terminal/unavailable/error states.
+- RTL/Arabic labels and responsive single-column layout.
+
+### Partial
+
+- `SUMMARY` is a declared but unused visible phase.
+- SSE has no reconnect/backoff or polling fallback.
+- Embedded widgets depend on a hard-coded host allowlist; a new provider requires a code change.
+- The 404 surface exists but has a broken recovery link.
+- `PushOrTransferRenderer` has an `onCancel` prop with no rendered cancel control.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No dedicated checkout home/status lookup page.
+- No payer-initiated receipt download/email.
+- No reconnect/resume UX after a dropped SSE stream.
+- No client-side handling for a late success after the page shows `ERROR` beyond a manual reload.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **404 recovery bug:** the catch-all button targets a non-existent `Dashboard` route.
+- **Status-stream risk:** if SSE drops, the page stops updating until reload; the payer may see `CONFIRMING` indefinitely.
+- **SRI risk:** `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` selects an SRI hash by the host allowlist index rather than the script URL index, so multiple scripts can receive the wrong hash.
+- **Cancel gap:** push/transfer actions show no cancel control even though the renderer receives a callback.
+- **Trust risk:** operators must not treat browser callbacks as proof; only the server-verified status is authoritative.
+- **Documentation risk:** the checkout is not a general payment status portal; it is a single-link payer surface.
+

+## Checkout Help Center
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the payer-facing help center in `checkout-front`:
+
+- The per-rail instructions banner on the payment form.
+- The "Help & Support" slide-over drawer on the payer page.
+- The `supportConfig` projection from the admin-managed platform setting.
+- The per-rail `helpGuide` projection from the rail record.
+- The state-aware guidance for in-flight, unknown, failed, expired and cancelled attempts.
+- The actual hide behavior when the admin disables support.
+
+It does not own the admin support settings page, merchant guide, admin guide, or the checkout phase machine. It documents the separation between the platform support configuration and the per-rail guides, and it records the gaps in the current authoring and visibility model.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The checkout help center is data-driven rather than hard-coded:
+
+1. **The payer never needs a second request for help.** Support details and per-rail walkthroughs travel with the payment-link summary.
+2. **Help is contextual to the selected rail.** The banner and guide section explain the exact steps, prerequisites and troubleshooting for the rail the payer is using.
+3. **Help is state-aware.** A `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN`/`FAILED`/`EXPIRED`/`CANCELLED` attempt gets a clear "do not pay again" or "safe to retry" message.
+4. **Support is centrally controlled.** The admin edits one platform setting for support channels, working hours and FAQ; the change applies to all checkout links.
+5. **The merchant contact is optional and separate.** The platform can show its own support channels, the merchant's contact details, both, or neither.
+6. **Per-rail guides are content, not code.** The rail record carries bilingual steps/prerequisites/troubleshooting so operators can tune guidance per payment method.
+7. **The payer can always copy the reference.** The drawer exposes the payment reference for support conversations.
+8. **Disabling support should not break the payment flow.** It hides the contact block, not the payment or the attempt-state guidance.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 The two data sources
+
+| Data | Source | Projection |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| Platform support config | `platform_settings` key `checkout.support_config` | `buildCheckoutSupportConfig` in `core-back/api/internal/checkout.ts` |
+| Per-rail guide | `rails.help_guide_json` (seeded by `core-back/prisma/seedGuides.ts`) | Passed through `visibleRails[].helpGuide` in `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` |
+
+The checkout page receives both in `PayLinkSummary.supportConfig` and `RailDescriptor.helpGuide`.
+
+### 3.2 Support config shape
+
+```text
+SupportConfig {
+  enabled: boolean
+  working_hours_ar: string | null
+  working_hours_en: string | null
+  platform: { phone, whatsapp, email } | null
+  merchant: { phone, email, tradeName } | null
+  faq_items: Array<{ q_ar, a_ar, q_en, a_en }>
+  channels: string[]
+}
+```
+
+Projection rules in `buildCheckoutSupportConfig`:
+
+- If the setting is absent, not an object, or `enabled !== true`, return `null`.
+- If `show_platform_contact` is not false, include the platform phone/WhatsApp/email.
+- If `show_merchant_contact` is not false, include the merchant phone/email/trade name from the loaded link.
+- Pass through `working_hours_ar`/`working_hours_en`, FAQ items (all four fields, null-coalesced) and a flat `channels` list derived from non-empty platform channels.
+- The projection deliberately excludes the setting's other fields; only the support-facing shape leaks.
+
+The admin form defaults both `show_*` values to true and saves the `checkout.support_config` setting as a new immutable platform-setting version. The core handler writes `CHECKOUT_SUPPORT_UPDATED` and `CHECKOUT_SUPPORT_EDIT_CHECKLIST` audits. The admin page's live preview is not the actual drawer.
+
+### 3.3 Per-rail help guide shape
+
+```text
+RailHelpGuide {
+  steps_ar: string[]
+  steps_en: string[]
+  prerequisites_ar: string[]
+  prerequisites_en: string[]
+  troubleshooting_ar: Array<{ q_ar, a_ar }>
+  troubleshooting_en: Array<{ q_en, a_en }>
+}
+```
+
+`core-back/prisma/seedGuides.ts` defines `RAIL_HELP_GUIDES` for 14 seeded rails: `edfali`, `sadad`, `moamalat_card`, `cbl_lypay`, `lypay`, `mypay`, `tlync`, `mobicash`, `onepay`, `yussor`, `sahara`, `mpgs`, `evo_pay`, `neompay_wallet` (the comment above the map says 13, but the actual object has 14 keys). A rail without a guide returns `helpGuide: null`; the banner hides and the drawer omits the rail-guide section.
+
+The admin portal has no rail-guide editor. Rails are seeded/updated from code and the admin Rails page manages rail catalog fields, not `helpGuideJson` content.
+
+### 3.4 Per-rail banner
+
+`checkout-front/src/components/help/PerRailInstructionsBanner.tsx` renders when `selectedRail.helpGuide` exists:
+
+- A region titled "How to pay with <rail>".
+- An expand/collapse button (default expanded).
+- A help button that opens the drawer.
+- Prerequisite pills (localized with fallback).
+- Numbered step rows.
+- Localized last-resort behavior: Arabic uses Arabic when present, otherwise English; English uses English when present, otherwise Arabic.
+
+The banner is independent of `supportConfig.enabled`. Disabling support does not hide it.
+
+### 3.5 State-aware drawer
+
+`checkout-front/src/components/help/CheckoutHelpDrawer.tsx` is a `SlideOverDrawer` (width 440) titled "Help & Support". It composes:
+
+1. **State guidance** for the current attempt status.
+2. **Payment reference** with a copy action when a reference exists.
+3. **Per-rail guide** from the selected rail's `helpGuide`.
+4. **FAQ** from `supportConfig.faq_items`.
+5. **Contact support** from `supportConfig.platform` and `supportConfig.merchant`.
+
+State guidance:
+
+| Status | Tone | Message summary |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `VERIFYING` | info | The platform is verifying; do not pay again; status updates automatically. |
+| `UNKNOWN` | warning | Could not confirm yet; do not pay again; wait/refresh; contact support with the reference. |
+| `FAILED` | error | Attempt did not complete; try another method; if charged, contact support with the reference. |
+| `EXPIRED` | warning | Payment window expired; do not use the old reference; start a new payment. |
+| `CANCELLED` | warning | Payment was cancelled; if charged, contact support with the reference; otherwise start again. |
+| Other | none | No state block. |
+
+The drawer always shows the reference block when a reference exists, regardless of support configuration. The rail-guide section shows prerequisites, numbered steps and troubleshooting when a guide is present. The FAQ section renders only when there are complete localized FAQ items. The contact section renders only when `supportConfig.enabled` is true.
+
+Contact behavior:
+
+- Platform WhatsApp builds `https://wa.me/<digits>?text=<encoded help message>`.
+- Platform phone uses `tel:` with whitespace removed.
+- Platform email uses `mailto:` with a localized subject and a body containing the link key and reference.
+- Merchant name/phone/email render when the merchant contact is present.
+- If support is enabled but no channel and no working hours exist, the drawer shows "No contact details are available right now."
+- The help message includes the link key and reference (or `N/A`).
+
+The drawer does not close/reset the payment form. It is opened by the header help button and by the banner's help button.
+
+### 3.6 Actual hide behavior
+
+This is the important distinction between design intent and code:
+
+- When `checkout.support_config.enabled` is false, `buildCheckoutSupportConfig` returns `null`.
+- The drawer's `support` computed value is null, so:
+  - **Contact support hides.**
+  - **FAQ hides** (the FAQ is derived from `supportConfig`).
+  - **Working hours hide** (inside the contact block).
+- The following remain visible/usable:
+  - The header "Help & Support" button and the drawer itself.
+  - State guidance for the current attempt.
+  - The payment reference and copy action.
+  - The per-rail guide section (from `rail.helpGuide`).
+  - The per-rail banner.
+- Therefore the admin warning "Disabling this hides the Contact Us block on every checkout page" is accurate for the contact/FAQ block, but it does not remove the entire help center. The setting is a support-channel switch, not a global help kill switch.
+
+### 3.7 Localization and fallback
+
+- `currentLocale` comes from the checkout locale adapter (`ar` or `en`).
+- Rail display names fall back between Arabic and English.
+- Guide steps/prerequisites/troubleshooting use the selected language first, then the other language.
+- FAQ questions/answers are filtered to complete localized pairs.
+- Working hours fall back between languages.
+- The drawer's section titles are bilingual inline.
+
+### 3.8 Separation from admin/merchant help
+
+- Admin contextual help uses `GUIDE_ROUTE_HELP` and the 12-book guide; it does not read `supportConfig`.
+- Merchant contextual help uses M/D chapters; it does not read `supportConfig`.
+- Checkout help uses `supportConfig` and `helpGuide`; it does not read admin/merchant guide content.
+- The admin `/settings/checkout-help` page is the only authoring surface for the platform support config.
+- Per-rail content is seeded from core code and has no admin authoring surface.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **Help data travels with the payment-link summary.** No second help request is required.
+2. **`enabled: false` returns `null` supportConfig.** The drawer must tolerate null and still render state/reference/rail help.
+3. **Only enabled support exposes platform/merchant contacts and FAQ.** The projection enforces this; the UI does not re-enable hidden data.
+4. **Merchant contact is link-derived.** It uses the loaded merchant's contact fields, not a merchant-supplied free-form block.
+5. **Per-rail guides are bilingual arrays.** Missing entries fall back to the other language.
+6. **The drawer never changes payment state.** It only displays status/reference and opens external contact links.
+7. **The banner is independent of support enabled.** It is driven by `rail.helpGuide`.
+8. **The reference copy is a UI convenience.** It does not prove payment.
+9. **No secrets are shown.** Support details are business contact data; payment secrets/OTP/PAN are never placed in the drawer.
+10. **The admin setting is versioned.** A change creates a new `checkout.support_config` version.
+

+### Implemented

+The daemon wraps WAL-G or Barman and supports full/delta backups of the core database, the dedicated audit database and optional Redis snapshots. Restore drills verify double-entry zero drift, sharded balance parity and the audit hash chain. The in-process scheduler evaluates five-field cron expressions in UTC. Policy changes require maker-checker; trigger and drill are direct `security:write` actions.
+
+Known deployment caveat: core reads `BACKUP_DAEMON_CA_CERT_PATH`, `BACKUP_DAEMON_CLIENT_CERT_PATH` and `BACKUP_DAEMON_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`, while the daemon reads `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_PATH`, `BACKUP_DAEMON_KEY_PATH` and `BACKUP_DAEMON_CA_CERT_PATH`. Verify the provisioned material in staging before relying on the control plane.

+| Dependency | Required | Failure behavior |

+## 6. Configuration reference
+
+`lib/env/index.ts` defines a strict Zod schema. Only schema keys are read from `process.env`; unrelated variables are ignored. Booleans accept `true`/`1`/`yes` and `false`/`0`/`no`. Invalid non-test configuration prints the failing key names and exits with code 1. In `NODE_ENV=test`, the loader prints one warning and returns a local test fallback, which is why tests can load without real secrets but still need a reachable database for database-backed suites.

+## 8. Migrations and seeding
+
+### 8.1 Schema workflow
+
+```bash
+bun run migrate-dev       # development: create + patch + apply a migration
+bun run migrate-deploy    # production: apply committed migrations
+bun run migrate-generate  # after schema changes, before typecheck/start
+bun run prisma:validate
+```
+
+`migrate-dev` wraps Prisma: it runs `prisma migrate dev --create-only --name init`, removes the generated `DROP TABLE "schema_versions"` statement, appends the schema-version table DDL and an upsert to version 8, then runs `migrate deploy`. Review the patched SQL before committing a migration. The patch is string-based.
+
+`migrate-reset` is destructive; it drops and recreates the database. There are no down migrations. A partial restore that stops before the storage-hardening migration leaves schema version 7; seeders refuse to run, while the HTTP server can still boot because it does not check the version.
+
+The `journal_lines` parent and its monthly partitions are created by the hardening migration. Keep the deploy partition cron or run `SELECT ensure_journal_line_partitions(18)` on the primary. The default partition is a safety net, not a substitute for maintenance.
+
+### 8.2 Baseline seed
+
+`bun run db-seed` is idempotent by lookup for most rows and covers:
+
+- Platform settings `OD-1` through `OD-11` plus join-request, onboarding and KYB settings.
+- System GL accounts.
+- Gateway/rail/route/flow blueprints and related definitions.
+- Platform credential sets.
+- Bilingual notification templates.
+- CBL large-transaction and suspicious-activity reporting rules.
+- Checkout support configuration and per-rail help guides.
+
+The baseline seed does not activate administrators; use `create-admin`.
+
+### 8.3 Fake Rails bridge
+
+`bun run seed-fake-rails` rewrites gateway environment base URLs and allowed hosts to the emulator, updates widget definitions to the emulator SDK and derives inbound verification secrets from the shared seeder token. Do not run it in an environment that must call real gateways.
+
+`FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and `FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN` must be set. Core can reach the emulator only when `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS=true`, the host is in `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, and the same host is in the gateway version's `allowed_hosts`.
+
+### 8.4 Synthetic history seeder
+
+`bun run seed-synthetic-history` builds a deterministic multi-year operation history for a designated test server. Its five-layer safety gate requires:
+
+1. `IS_TEST_SERVER=true`.
+2. `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true` and `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`.
+3. `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true` when `NODE_ENV=production`.
+4. A non-empty `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` that covers every configured gateway host.
+5. A live Fake Rails seeder handshake with `FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN`.
+
+It also requires a completed baseline seed and Fake Rails bridge. Profiles are `COMPACT`, `STANDARD` and `STRESS` via `SYNTHETIC_SEED_PROFILE`; `SYNTHETIC_SEED_KEY` identifies a completed run and seeds the PRNG; `SYNTHETIC_YEARS_SPAN` overrides the profile span. A completed key is skipped. The bulk writer is not transactional, so an interrupted run can leave partial rows; recreate the database for a clean rebuild. The seeder refuses to proceed on a non-zero ledger audit or an unbalanced entry.
+
+The safety gate does not inspect the database host. Never point `IS_TEST_SERVER=true` at production data.

+| Symptom | Likely cause | Action |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |

+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part describes the process boundary and the foundation layer of `core-back`: the Express application, the global middleware order, raw-body handling, the error envelope, the Prisma client and storage-engine ownership, the schema-version check, the TLS listener and the channel routers.
+
+It is the entry point for reading the rest of `01-core-back/**`. It does not document every route (`01-api-surface.md`) or the rail engine internals (`02-engine.md`), but it defines the request lifecycle those parts assume.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The historical design makes `core-back` the only trusted service:
+
+- It owns the database (`prisma/`), the database credentials, the KMS master key, the ledger and the outbound gateway engine.
+- It listens only on the private LAN with mTLS 1.3 and client-certificate verification.
+- It serves three internal namespaces, each bound to one edge certificate common name.
+- It re-validates every request: the bearer token, the user/merchant state, the authority, the payload schema, the link/attempt state and the money invariants.
+- It keeps the raw bytes for webhook/upload routes so signatures and document sniffing work.
+- It returns a stable error envelope with a request reference.
+- It owns a storage engine with explicit ports rather than ad-hoc database access.
+
+The design also expects a startup schema gate and a health/readiness contract. The actual code implements most of the boundary and middleware, but the schema gate is seed-time only and health is queue-only (see `00-platform/04-observability.md`).
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Process boundary
+
+`core-back/index.ts` is the entry point. When run as the main module, or when `NODE_ENV !== "test"`, it calls `start()`. Tests usually import `createApp()` and `createHttpsServer()` instead of running the full process.
+
+`start()`:
+
+1. Asserts that the durable background-job queue is drainable.
+2. Optionally configures Redis invalidation.
+3. Creates the HTTPS server (which creates the Express app and reads the TLS material).
+4. Creates the storage-engine singleton.
+5. Wires the platform runtime and access-log sink to the storage engine.
+6. Starts the production worker runtime when workers are enabled.
+7. Listens on `HOST:PORT`.
+8. Installs `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` handlers.
+
+The process is a single Bun process that owns the API and the workers. There is no separate worker process in the current tree; horizontal scaling runs multiple complete core processes and relies on database claim semantics.
+
+### 3.2 Express application
+
+`createApp(options)` builds one Express 5 app:
+
+```ts
+const app = express();
+app.disable("x-powered-by");
+app.set("trust proxy", env.TRUST_PROXY);
+app.use(requestIdMiddleware);
+app.use(requestLoggerMiddleware);
+app.use(rawBodyMiddleware);
+app.use(express.json({ limit: "1mb" }));
+app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true, limit: "1mb" }));
+app.get("/health", ...);
+app.use("/internal", internalRouter);
+app.use("/api", apiRouter);
+app.use(errorHandler);
+```
+
+`CreateAppOptions` allows tests to inject a `db` for the queue health probe and a `now` clock. Production uses the `client` proxy.
+
+The app does not mount Helmet, a CORS middleware, compression, a body-size guard beyond the parsers, a CSRF guard or a request timeout middleware. Those concerns are either not needed for the internal mTLS service or handled at the edge/reverse proxy.
+
+### 3.3 Route mounting
+
+`core-back/api/index.ts` builds:
+
+```ts
+const router = express.Router();
+router.use("/public", publicRouter);
+export const internalRouter = express.Router();
+internalRouter.use("/admin", requireEdgeIdentity("admin-back"), adminInternalRouter);
+internalRouter.use("/merchant", requireEdgeIdentity("merchant-back"), merchantInternalRouter);
+internalRouter.use("/checkout", requireEdgeIdentity("checkout-back"), checkoutInternalRouter);
+export const apiRouter = router;
+```
+
+`publicRouter` is an Express router with a 15-request/hour limiter and no route. It is mounted at `/api/public`; a request to any `/api/public/*` path reaches the terminal 404 handler after the limiter.
+
+`api/internal/index.ts` only re-exports the three channel routers; the live mounting, and therefore the certificate binding, is in `api/index.ts`.
+
+### 3.4 Authentication and authority middleware
+
+The internal routers apply authentication themselves:
+
+- Admin: `router.use(requireAuthentication)` after the channel health route; `requireAuthorities` on business handlers where declared (some authenticated dashboard/options routes have no specific authority).
+- Merchant: `router.use(requireAuthentication)` after the merchant health and public auth routes; onboarding and business routes require a bearer.
+- Checkout: no bearer authentication; link key/attempt token is the payer capability.
+
+`authDoubleCheck.ts` also exports `principalOf`, `requireAuthorities`, `requireMerchantScope`, `fingerprint`, `parseAuthorities`, `ipAllowed` and the principal types. The admin and merchant routers use different subsets; see `00-platform/02-security-and-mtls.md` and `01-api-surface.md`.
+
+### 3.5 Raw body handling
+
+`rawBodyMiddleware` must run before `express.json` because the JSON parser would consume and destroy the exact bytes used for signatures and document sniffing.
+
+It matches:
+
+- `RAW_BODY_PATHS`: `/internal/checkout/inbound`, `/internal/merchant/onboarding/kyb-documents`, `/internal/admin/reconciliation/upload`.
+- `RAW_BODY_PATTERNS`: `/internal/admin/join-requests/:id/kyb-documents`.
+
+The collector is `express.raw({ type: () => true, limit: "25mb" })`. Matching is exact or prefix-based for the paths and regex-based for the join-request document route. Every other path continues to the JSON/urlencoded parsers.
+
+The checkout webhook handler reads `Buffer.isBuffer(request.body) ? request.body : Buffer.alloc(0)`, so a mis-mounted parser would silently produce an empty body rather than a crash. The upload handlers enforce a declared MIME and magic-byte check in the route layer.
+
+### 3.6 Error envelope
+
+`core-back/lib/error/index.ts` defines `ApiError` and `toErrorEnvelope`:
+
+```ts
+{
+  code: string,
+  message: string,
+  reference?: string,
+  details?: unknown
+}
+```
+
+- An `ApiError` keeps its status, code, message, details and optional reference.
+- A non-`ApiError` becomes `{ code: "SERVER_ERROR", message: "Internal server error", ...(reference ? { reference } : {}) }`.
+- A `SyntaxError` from a body parser gets HTTP 400, but the envelope is still the generic `SERVER_ERROR` because `toErrorEnvelope` only special-cases `ApiError`.
+- The error handler logs only non-`ApiError` messages, prefixed with `[requestId]`.
+- If response headers are already sent, the handler returns without writing.
+
+`parseOrThrow(schema, data)` throws `ApiError(400, "INVALID_BODY", "Invalid request data", issues)` with `path`, `code` and `message` per Zod issue.
+
+### 3.7 Request IDs and logging
+
+`requestIdMiddleware` validates an incoming `x-request-id` against `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$`; an invalid or absent value becomes a UUID. The value is stored on `request.requestId` and returned as the `x-request-id` response header.
+
+`requestLoggerMiddleware` is mounted immediately after the request-id middleware. It creates a console logger, records request-scoped messages, and on response finish writes an access record to the configured `LogSinkPort`. The console logger uses its own short id, which is not the request id; see `00-platform/04-observability.md`.
+
+### 3.8 Database client ownership
+
+`core-back/prisma/client/base.ts` creates Prisma clients with `@prisma/adapter-pg`:
+
+```ts
+new PrismaClient({
+  adapter: new PrismaPg(buildPostgresPoolConfig(databaseUrl)),
+  log: [],
+});
+```
+
+`core-back/prisma/client/index.ts` wraps the base client in a Proxy so routes can import `client` without connecting at module load. `ensureSchemaVersion()` connects, reads `schema_versions` row `id = 1`, and requires version 8.
+
+The storage engine creates its own primary client from `DATABASE_URL` (and replica clients from `DATABASE_REPLICA_URLS`). It is the owner of the `UnitOfWork`, `ReadStore`, cache, audit and log ports. The runtime `PlatformRuntime` uses the database client for metadata reads and the storage engine for transactional writes when a storage engine is present.
+
+The schema version is checked by the seeders, not by `createApp` or `start`. A database with schema version 7 can boot the API; the first incompatible query fails. This is a material gap for rollout safety.
+
+### 3.9 Storage engine ownership
+
+`getStorageEngine()` lazily builds a singleton:
+
+- `PostgresUnitOfWorkAdapter` with the primary client.
+- `PostgresReplicaReadStore` with the replica set and the lag monitor.
+- `RedisCacheAdapter` or `MemoryCacheAdapter`.
+- `DedicatedAuditDatabaseDriver` when `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL` is set.
+- `DedicatedPostgresLogSink` over `LOG_DATABASE_URL` when set.
+
+`shutdownStorageEngine()` stops the LSN monitor, closes the log sink, closes the cache and disconnects the primary, replicas, audit pool and log pool. The engine is process-global; there is no per-request storage instance.
+
+### 3.10 TLS server boundary
+
+`createHttpsServer()` creates the Express app and a plain HTTP server, then a TLS server with the server key/cert/CA, `requestCert: true`, `rejectUnauthorized: true` and `minVersion: "TLSv1.3"`. It bridges `secureConnection` sockets into the HTTP server. A missing certificate file aborts startup with a clear error.
+
+The channel guard is not the TLS handshake alone: `requireEdgeIdentity` inspects the peer certificate CN after the handshake and rejects the wrong channel with `403 FORBIDDEN_SERVICE_IDENTITY`.
+
+### 3.11 Request lifecycle summary
+
+```text
+TCP + TLS 1.3 handshake (client cert required)
+-> secureConnection -> http.Server -> Express app
+-> requestIdMiddleware
+-> requestLoggerMiddleware
+-> rawBodyMiddleware (only opaque paths)
+-> express.json / express.urlencoded
+-> GET /health or /internal/:channel/* or /api/public/*
+-> requireEdgeIdentity(channel CN)
+-> channel router: auth (admin/merchant) -> Zod parse -> business handler -> DB/storage/engine
+-> response -> access log on finish
+-> terminal error handler on throw
+```
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **Core is not a public HTTP service.** It must be reachable only over the private LAN with mTLS.
+2. **The channel CN is the first authorization decision.** No internal business route runs before `requireEdgeIdentity`.
+3. **Raw bytes precede JSON parsing** for webhook and upload paths.
+4. **Every response carries a request id.** The request id is either the validated client value or a UUID.
+5. **Business errors use the envelope.** A thrown `ApiError` maps to its status/code/message/details.
+6. **Unexpected errors do not leak internals.** The response is `SERVER_ERROR` with `Internal server error` and a reference.
+7. **The database client is lazy and process-global.** Module import does not connect.
+8. **The storage engine is the transactional owner.** Routes should not open ad-hoc long transactions when a storage port exists.
+9. **Schema version 8 is required.** The seeders enforce it; the API currently does not at boot.
+10. **The TLS server requires a client certificate.** There is no optional-client-cert mode in production startup.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+### 5.1 Foundation code paths
+
+| Concern | Code |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| App, health, TLS, startup | `core-back/index.ts` |
+| Channel mounting | `core-back/api/index.ts`, `core-back/api/internal/index.ts` |

+
+### 5.2 Foundation env keys
+
+- `PORT`, `HOST`, `NODE_ENV`, `TRUST_PROXY`.
+- `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH`, `MTLS_SERVER_CERT_PATH`, `MTLS_SERVER_KEY_PATH`.
+- `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_REPLICA_URLS`, `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL`, `LOG_DATABASE_URL`.
+- `REDIS_URL`, `REDIS_NODES`.
+- `WORKER_ENABLED`, `WORKER_BACKGROUND_JOBS_ENABLED` for the boot guard.
+- `KMS_MASTER_KEY` for session derivation and vault.
+
+### 5.3 Foundation routes
+
+- `GET /health` (core queue health).
+- `GET /internal/admin/health`, `GET /internal/merchant/health`, `GET /internal/checkout/health`.
+- All business routes under the three internal routers.
+- `/api/public` mount with no routes.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+### 6.1 Boot order for a developer
+
+1. Generate certs.
+2. Set `DATABASE_URL`.
+3. Apply migrations.
+4. Seed (this also checks schema version 8).
+5. `bun run start`.
+6. Probe `/health` over mTLS with a client cert.
+
+### 6.2 Test harness
+
+Tests import `createApp({ db, now })` and use a fake queue database. `createHttpsServer()` is used where the TLS layer itself is under test. `test/setup.ts` sets a test `LOG_LEVEL` even though the logger does not consume it.
+
+### 6.3 Add a foundation concern
+
+- Request id: keep the regex; do not accept arbitrary header values.
+- Raw body: add the path to `RAW_BODY_PATHS` or a pattern, and mount the middleware before JSON.
+- Error shape: use `ApiError` and `parseOrThrow`; do not return ad-hoc error bodies.
+- Auth: add the guard at the router or handler, and repeat business validation in core.
+- Storage: add a port/adaptor rather than a raw pool in a route.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Express 5 app with a deterministic middleware order.
+- Three channel routers with certificate CN binding.
+- Raw-body preservation for webhook/KYB/reconciliation uploads.
+- Stable error envelope and request id.
+- Lazy Prisma client with `@prisma/adapter-pg`.
+- Storage-engine singleton and shutdown.
+- TLS 1.3 server with required client certificates.
+- Queue-drainability boot guard.
+
+### Partial
+
+- **Schema version.** `ensureSchemaVersion` exists and is tested through seeders, but the API does not call it.
+- **Error semantics.** A malformed JSON body returns 400 with `SERVER_ERROR`, which is less precise than a dedicated `INVALID_JSON` code.
+- **Request logging.** Console and access logs do not share an id; access logs have no actor or query timing.
+- **Public router.** `/api/public` has a limiter but no endpoints.
+- **Process supervision.** Workers start before `listen`; a listen failure does not stop them.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+

+### Known bugs / risks

+## Core API Surface
