+- `describeDatabase` is `describe` when reachable and `describe.skip` otherwise; `describeRedis` does the same for Redis.
+- `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts` probes `EXHAUSTIVE_DATABASE_URL` / `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and exports `databaseIsReachable`; several exhaustive files use `databaseIsReachable ? describe : describe.skip`.
+- `core-back/test/e2e/postgres-payment.test.ts` uses `test.skipIf(!reachable)` for live payment tests and a few PostgreSQL-invariant tests.
+- `core-back/test/storage-engine/*.test.ts` also registers a placeholder `test.skip(... requires the live database)` so the skip is visible.
+
+Redis-dependent suites:
+
+- `core-back/test/storage-engine/cache-velocity.test.ts` skips the live `RedisCacheAdapter` suite without Redis; the memory adapter tests still run.
+- `core-back/test/storage-engine/performance/storage-performance.test.ts` skips the live Redis velocity benchmark without Redis.
+
+Without PostgreSQL 18, the schema, ledger, storage-engine integration, backup-admin route and exhaustive DB suites do not prove anything; they skip. Without Redis, the live Lua/velocity path is unproven. The default `bun test` exit code can still be zero because skipped tests are not failures.
+
+Playwright:
+
+- `tests/playwright.config.ts` starts the admin, merchant and checkout preview servers and runs `tests/e2e/{admin,merchant,checkout}` with mocked APIs.
+- `tests/playwright.exhaustive.config.ts` starts four preview servers (admin, merchant, checkout, fake-rails) and runs the exhaustive UI specs. It does not start core, the BFFs or Fake Rails; the specs rely on route mocking for API data.
+- `tests/playwright.live.config.ts` targets the deployed single-node box over LAN with self-signed TLS and runs `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts`.
+- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/full-platform-lifecycle-journeys.spec.ts` is skipped unless `E2E_LIVE=1`. The exhaustive runner prints a skip message when the variable is absent.
+
+Deploy and daemon tests are unit-level. The backup daemon suite uses fake command runners and fake file systems; it does not require PostgreSQL, WAL-G, Barman, S3 or a real backup. The deploy suite tests planners/provisioners/config and does not deploy a real multi-host cluster.
+
+### 3.3 Exhaustive runner
+
+`scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` is the master runner:
+
+- forces `--parallel=1` for database suites;
+- runs core exhaustive groups 01 through 08, then edge BFF tests, then deploy tests;
+- runs `core-back/test/storage-engine` and `test/backup-admin` plus `deploy/backup-daemon` as `T-EX-09`;
+- runs the frontend-facing Vitest unit tests in `tests/` and the exhaustive Playwright config as `T-EX-09b`;
+- runs `test/exhaustive/10-seeder-and-deploy`;
+- runs the cross-service journey only when `E2E_LIVE=1`;
+- runs the full core regression last;
+- optionally runs `scripts/deploy-localhost.sh` with `--deploy`.
+
+The runner does not preflight PostgreSQL, Redis, browsers or the live stack. It inherits the skip behavior above. A green run therefore means "nothing that ran failed"; it does not mean every suite executed.
+
+### 3.4 Performance suites
+
+`scripts/run-benchmarks.sh`:
+
+- requires `DATABASE_URL`, `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` or `STORAGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, exiting with code 2 otherwise;
+- runs `bun test test/storage-engine/performance` (or a `BENCHMARK_FILTER`);
+- runs the full `test/storage-engine` regression;
+- runs `test/backup-admin`;
+- prints p50/p95 values; it does not store results or compare against a baseline.
+
+`core-back/test/storage-engine/performance/storage-performance.test.ts` contains:
+
+| Test | Assertion |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `compareLsn` 1,000,000 ops | median < 1,000 ms |
+| `uuidv7` 100,000 ids | median < 2,000 ms |
+| `stableJson` 10,000 rows | median < 2,000 ms |
+| memory velocity 10,000 evaluations | median < 2,000 ms |
+| read-store routing 100,000 selections | median < 1,000 ms |
+| 500 sequential UoWs with outbox + audit | < 10,000 ms |
+| 50 concurrent UoWs | p95 < 500 ms |
+| 1,000-event outbox drain | < 5,000 ms |
+| 16 shard rows load | < 50 ms and no sequential scan |
+| 1,000-row audit hash chain append + verify | < 5,000 ms |
+| 1,000 live Redis velocity evaluations | < 3,000 ms (skips without Redis) |
+
+`core-back/test/storage-engine/performance/write-path-benchmark.test.ts` adds:
+
+| Test | Assertion |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| 300 `writeAudit` calls (`audit_log` + `audit_outbox`) | < 10,000 ms |
+| shard balance reads for a 16-shard account | p95 < 25 ms |
+
+These are regression ceilings, not capacity benchmarks. They are generous enough for developer hardware and do not model 50M-500M records, 1,000+ sustained TPS, mixed read/write workloads, multi-node contention or p99 latency.
+
+### 3.5 Missing benchmark classes
+
+The design's target scale is 50M-500M financial records, 1,000+ TPS sustained writes and sub-5 ms reads. The repository has no executable proof of any of these:
+
+- no sustained TPS benchmark, load generator or latency percentile beyond p95 in two tests;
+- no test database at production scale; the performance tests use a small migrated test database;
+- no deep-search benchmark (20 providers, broad query, realistic candidate set, p95, partial rate);
+- no restore-drill benchmark (backup fetch + WAL replay + three checks under time);
+- no replication lag/read-after-write benchmark with real replicas;
+- no multi-node core/worker contention benchmark;
+- no audit/log DB throughput benchmark under buffering pressure;
+- no Redis outage/failover benchmark.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- A test that requires PostgreSQL 18 or Redis must skip explicitly when the service is absent. It must not silently pass a mock that claims to prove live behavior.
+- The exhaustive runner's success means only that executed tests passed. Reports of coverage must state which suites skipped.
+- A live suite must be opt-in (`E2E_LIVE=1`) and must not be counted as part of the default gate.
+- Performance tests must assert a finite upper bound and print the measured value so regressions are visible. They must not assert a lower bound that is machine-dependent.
+- Benchmark scripts must fail when no database URL is configured rather than quietly running only pure tests.
+- Backup/restore tests that use fake runners must be labelled as unit tests, not restore proofs.
+- UI tests that mock APIs prove rendering/navigation behavior, not backend integration.
+- The canonical verification gate is `bun scripts/project-design/build.ts --check`, plus the workspace typecheck/test/build commands in `AGENTS.md`. A green exhaustive runner is not a substitute for the full gate.
+- Skipped database/live suites must be reported explicitly when claiming completion.
+

+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Run the smallest relevant suite first, then the full gate from `AGENTS.md`.
+- For a core change, run the focused test file, then `cd core-back && bun test`. If the change touches storage, also run `test/storage-engine`; if it touches backups, run `test/backup-admin`.
+- Always state whether PostgreSQL and Redis were available. A skipped suite is not a passing suite.
+- Before claiming exhaustive coverage, run `./scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` with a real database and Redis, and report any skipped groups.
+- For benchmarks, use a dedicated test database and stable hardware. Compare the printed p50/p95 values with the previous run; do not treat the ceilings as service-level objectives.
+- For UI changes, run the relevant Playwright project. The default/exhaustive configs use mocked APIs; only `E2E_LIVE=1` proves cross-service behavior.
+- For backup daemon changes, run its unit tests and, separately, a real restore drill on a test host if the change touches recovery, WAL, Barman or scratch handling.
+- Do not add a benchmark that asserts a minimum throughput on shared CI hardware without a recorded baseline and a tolerance policy.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Broad core-back unit/integration coverage across engine, ledger, governance, workers, search, storage, backups and API routes.
+- Exhaustive schema, ledger, transform, rail, API, concurrency, workflow, security and seeder suites.
+- Storage-engine and write-path performance suites with explicit thresholds.
+- Backup control client and internal route tests.
+- Backup daemon unit tests for config, cron, engine, catalog, scheduler, server and restore drill.
+- Deploy engine tests for planning, PKI, provisioners, pipeline, rolling deploy, templates and Fake Rails.
+- Edge BFF mTLS/contract/isolation tests.
+- Frontend content/abstraction checks and Playwright UI suites.
+- A master exhaustive runner and a storage benchmark runner.
+- Opt-in live cross-service journeys.

+### Partial
+
+- The exhaustive suite has no `09-storage-backup` directory; the runner substitutes existing storage/backup suites.
+- Database/Redis suites skip when services are absent, and the runner does not fail on skips.
+- Exhaustive file names are stale in places (for example `all-15-templates-matrix.test.ts` while the ledger has 17 `LedgerScenario` values, and `all-20-gateways-24-scenarios.test.ts` while Fake Rails has 13 seeded core gateways). The filenames do not guarantee the current matrix size.
+- The Playwright exhaustive matrix runs preview frontends with mocked APIs; it does not exercise the BFF/core/Fake Rails chain.
+- The backup daemon restore drill test is a unit test with fake commands, not a live restore proof.
+- The performance tests are regression guards, not scale benchmarks.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- The 38,500+ assertion target. The working tree has about 1,964 literal declarations; the stale-claims baseline is 1,778.
+- `core-back/test/exhaustive/09-storage-backup/` and its planned ~900 tests.
+- A 1,000+ TPS sustained write benchmark.
+- A 50M-500M record-scale query benchmark with realistic indexes and data distribution.
+- A deep-search benchmark across 20 providers with p95/p99 and partial-rate measurement.
+- A live backup/restore benchmark with WAL-G/Barman, real S3, WAL replay and drill verification.
+- A multi-node concurrency benchmark for core workers, outbox relay, audit shipper and replica reads.
+- An automated check that a database-backed suite actually ran (rather than skipped) in CI.
+- Coverage reporting, mutation testing or a test-to-design traceability gate.
+- A benchmark result archive for comparing runs over time.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- Silent skips can make a green run misleading. `describeDatabase`/`describeRedis` and `test.skipIf` are explicit in code, but no runner-level summary fails when a required service is absent. Process gap.
+- The exhaustive runner's `T-EX-09` name suggests a dedicated suite that does not exist. Documentation/process drift.
+- `test.skip("... requires the live database")` placeholders inflate the skip count and can be mistaken for executed tests. Test hygiene risk.
+- Performance thresholds are generous and machine-dependent. A slow CI host can pass a regression that a fast host would have caught, and a fast host can fail a noisy run. Process risk.
+- The benchmark script's full storage regression includes live tests that skip without Redis; it does not fail when only the live Redis path was skipped. Process gap.
+- Playwright preview servers reuse an existing server (`reuseExistingServer: true`), so a stale local preview can serve old assets. Test hygiene risk.
+- Live journeys are opt-in; a default exhaustive run never proves the deployed stack. Process gap.
+- Fake Rails/backup daemon tests use fakes for external systems, so protocol/credential mismatches can survive until a live deployment. Test gap.
+- Test counts in historical docs (`38,500+`) are not reproducible from the repository and must not be cited as current coverage.

+# Deploy Engine
+
+`deploy/` is the operator workstation for the payment gateway. It validates one
+`deploy.env`, builds a host plan, creates the internal PKI, bootstraps hosts,
+provisions storage, deploys the Node/Bun services and SPAs from timestamped
+releases, runs the Fake Rails and synthetic-seed hooks, verifies the stack and
+prints an audit summary.
+
+It is not an application runtime and it does not contain the payment domain. The
+canonical design for each area lives under
+[`project-design/parts/07-deploy/`](../project-design/parts/07-deploy/); this
+README is the practical entrypoint.
+
+## 1. Prerequisites
+
+On the operator workstation:
+
+- Bun (required by `deploy/deploy.sh` and `deploy.ts`);
+- OpenSSH and `rsync`;
+- the private SSH keys referenced by `deploy.env`;
+- network access to every `sshHost`;
+- optionally `openssl` for certificate inspection.
+
+On target hosts:
+
+- a Debian/Ubuntu-family or Arch-family OS with `sudo` and systemd;
+- ports 22 and the role ports reachable;
+- public DNS and certificates if `certbot`/`custom` TLS is selected;
+- PostgreSQL 18 packages if the managed `PG_*` tier is used;
+- S3/MinIO/R2 and optional secondary-vault credentials if backups are enabled.
+
+`--fresh` installs `nginx`, `rsync`, `ufw`, `curl`, `ca-certificates`, `nodejs`,
+Bun, PM2 and enables the firewall. It does not install a PostgreSQL client, so
+the pre-migration `pg_dump` described below needs one already present on the core
+host.
+
+## 2. Files and entrypoints
+
+| Path | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `deploy/deploy.sh` | Shell guard: requires Bun and `deploy/deploy.env`, then executes `deploy.ts`. |
+| `deploy/deploy.ts` | Fourteen-step orchestrator. |
+| `deploy/deploy.env.example` | Fully commented configuration template. |
+| `deploy/deploy.env` | Operator file; gitignored, keep at mode 0600. |
+| `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` | Dotenv parser, Zod schema, cross-field validation, node grammar, precedence. |
+| `deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` | Host deduplication, services, Nginx, certs, firewall, storage plan. |
+| `deploy/lib/pkiManager.ts` | Internal CA, leaf certificates, SAN drift, distribution. |
+| `deploy/lib/firewallConfigurator.ts` | UFW command generation and application. |
+| `deploy/lib/sshRunner.ts` | SSH, sudo, rsync and remote file writes. |
+| `deploy/lib/healthVerifier.ts` | Post-deploy and edge-to-core probes. |
+| `deploy/provisioners/*.ts` | PostgreSQL 18, Redis, audit/log and backup engine provisioners. |
+| `deploy/templates/*.tpl` | Live Nginx templates. |
+| `deploy/backup-daemon/` | Backup/PITR control plane source and its own manual. |
+| `deploy/.certs/` | Local PKI vault; gitignored, keep private. |
+
+`deploy/package.json` scripts:
+
+```bash
+cd deploy
+bun run deploy       # bun run deploy.ts (deploy.env required)
+bun run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
+bun test             # deploy and planner tests
+```
+
+The supported entrypoint is `./deploy/deploy.sh`. Running `bun run deploy.ts`
+directly is equivalent once the environment file exists.
+
+## 3. Quick start
+
+```bash
+cd /home/salem/payment-gateway
+cp deploy/deploy.env.example deploy/deploy.env
+chmod 600 deploy/deploy.env
+$EDITOR deploy/deploy.env
+
+./deploy/deploy.sh --dry-run     # validate, plan, print every command
+./deploy/deploy.sh --fresh       # first deploy: bootstrap OS, PKI, firewall, storage, services
+./deploy/deploy.sh --update      # later deploys: no OS bootstrap, no firewall change
+```
+
+Start with `--dry-run`. It validates the real file, builds the whole plan and
+prints the topology map plus every local/remote command without executing
+anything.
+
+`DEPLOY_MODE=auto` does **not** inspect the remote release directory. In
+practice it behaves like `update` unless `--fresh` is passed. Use `--fresh`
+explicitly for a new host.
+
+A minimal all-in-one staging box sets every `*_SSH_HOST` to the same address and
+uses one SSH key. Ports still have to be distinct. For a managed storage tier,
+set `PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true` and fill `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`; the legacy `DB_*` block
+is then only a compatibility fallback.
+
+## 4. Command and flag reference
+
+```bash
+./deploy/deploy.sh [flags]
+```
+
+| Flag | Effect |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `--env=<path>` | Use another environment file. The path is resolved from the repository root. `deploy.sh` still requires the default `deploy/deploy.env` to exist. |
+| `--only=<roles>` | Deploy only the selected roles/provisioners. Comma-separated. |
+| `--nodes=<id,...>` | Limit compute deployment units to the named node ids. Units without a node id never match. |
+| `--rolling-batch=<n>` | Override `ROLLING_BATCH_SIZE` for this run. Must be an integer >= 1. |
+| `--keep=<n>` | Override `KEEP_RELEASES` (release directories retained per service). |
+| `--fresh` | Bootstrap packages, Bun, PM2 and apply UFW. |
+| `--update` | Do not bootstrap; also disables an environment `fresh`. |
+| `--enforce-firewall` | Apply the current UFW plan without a full bootstrap. |
+| `--skip-build` | Reuse the existing `*/dist` builds. Missing edge dist files fail later. |
+| `--skip-verify` | Skip step 12. A deploy can then report success without a live probe. |
+| `--rotate-certs` | Regenerate the internal CA and every leaf certificate. |
+| `--dry-run` | Validate and print commands; execute no remote command and skip local builds/verification. |
+
+Unknown options and unknown `--only` roles abort before any SSH connection.
+
+### Roles accepted by `--only`
+
+Compute: `db`, `core`, `admin`, `merchant`, `checkout`, `fake-rails`.
+
+Storage: `pg`, `pg-primary`, `pg-replica`, `pgbouncer`, `redis`, `audit-db`,
+`log-db`, `backup`.
+
+Aggregate: `storage` selects all storage provisioners.
+
+`--only` filters both service deployment and storage provisioning. A run that
+excludes `core` also skips the Fake Rails/synthetic seed step; the PG-tier
+pre-migration dump is skipped, while the legacy path still takes its dump when
+`db` is selected.
+
+## 5. Topology model
+
+Every node list uses:
+
+```text
+nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
+```
+
+- `nodeId` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.
+- `sshHost` and `privateIp` must be IPv4 addresses; DNS names are not accepted
+  in node lists.
+- `sshPort` and `servicePort` are 1-65535.
+- Node ids are unique across every list.
+- Private IPs are unique within a list; PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs
+  are globally unique.
+
+The node spec contains only SSH host/port, private IP and service port. SSH
+user, key path and sudo password still come from the tier's legacy fields
+(`CORE_SSH_USER`, `CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `CORE_SUDO_PASSWORD`, etc.). Roles sharing
+one SSH endpoint must use the same credentials.
+
+`planHosts()` groups targets by `sshHost:sshPort`. The topology label is based on
+unique endpoints:
+
+| Unique SSH endpoints | Topology |
+| ---: | :--- |
+| 1 | `single-host` |
+| 2 | `split` |
+| 3 or more | `distributed` |
+
+A host can carry several roles. Services, Nginx sites, certificate bundles and
+firewall rules are unioned per host. The deploy order is storage/legacy DB,
+core, Fake Rails, admin, merchant, checkout.
+
+### Compute and storage roles
+
+| Role | Default listener(s) | Exposure |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `core` | `core-back :4000` (mTLS 1.3) | Private; core port only from edge private IPs. |
+| `admin` | `admin-back :4101`, Nginx `:8443` | LAN only (`LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`). |
+| `merchant` | `merchant-back :4102`, Nginx `80/443`, LAN `:8081` | Public for 80/443; LAN listener restricted. |
+| `checkout` | `checkout-back :4103`, Nginx `80/443`, LAN `:8082` | Public for 80/443; LAN listener restricted. |
+| `fake-rails` | `fake-rails-back :4104`, Nginx `:8444` | Test network; sources from `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS`, every core private IP and the legacy `CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP` when set. |
+| `pg-primary` / `pg-replica` | PostgreSQL `:5432` | Replicas/backup/core as configured. |

+### Precedence
+
+1. Node arrays override legacy single-host fields for planning. SSH user/key/
+   sudo still come from the legacy fields.
+2. When the PG storage tier is configured (`PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, a primary/
+   replica node, or `PG_DB_PASSWORD`), `PG_DB_NAME`, `PG_DB_USER` and
+   `PG_DB_PASSWORD` are authoritative. Otherwise the legacy `DB_*` values are
+   used, falling back to `PG_DB_*`.
+3. A derived `DATABASE_URL` uses the PostgreSQL credentials, primary private IP
+   and PgBouncer port when enabled; otherwise the explicit `DATABASE_URL` is
+   used.
+4. `CORE_BACK_URLS` wins over derived `https://<core-private-ip>:<port>` URLs.
+5. A node's `servicePort` overrides the tier backend port for that node.
+6. CLI flags override the corresponding environment value for one run.
+7. `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS` wins over the legacy
+   `ADMIN_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST`.
+
+### Validation highlights
+
+- IPv4/CIDR syntax, identifier-safe database names/users and port ranges.
+- `DB_ENGINE` must be `postgresql`.
+- `DEPLOY_MODE` accepts `auto`, `fresh`, `update`, `rolling_update`.
+- `PG_VERSION` accepts one or two digits; it is not restricted to 18.
+- Backups require a node, SSH key, S3 bucket and a 64-hex encryption key.
+- WAL-G requires the backup node and PostgreSQL primary to share a private IP
+  because WAL-G reads the local data directory.
+- Node/service-port collisions, duplicate node ids/IPs and conflicting SSH
+  credentials are rejected.
+- Fake Rails requires its SSH/private-IP/tester/secret fields, rejects a
+  production deploy without `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`, and checks
+  its ports against other roles.
+- The synthetic seed requires `IS_TEST_SERVER=true`, Fake Rails enabled and, in
+  production, the Fake Rails production override.
+
+Runtime service environments are forced to `NODE_ENV=production` by the planner,
+even when `DEPLOY_ENV` is `development` or `staging`.
+
+## 7. Pipeline
+
+`deploy.ts` is strictly ordered:
+
+| Step | Action |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| 1 | Validate `deploy.env`, detect SSH conflicts, build and print the plan. |
+| 2 | Build admin, merchant and checkout SPAs locally; also Fake Rails when enabled. Admin receives the checklist/help build flags. |
+| 3 | Create/reuse/re-sign PKI material, print certificate validity, upload storage certificates. |
+| 4 | When fresh or `--enforce-firewall`: prove SSH, bootstrap packages/Bun/PM2 (fresh), apply UFW, read back status. |
+| 5 | Provision PostgreSQL 18/Redis/audit/log/backup and take a pre-migration dump; deploy the backup-daemon source when enabled. |
+| 6 | Deploy core-back. |
+| 7 | Deploy Fake Rails (only when enabled). |
+| 8 | Deploy admin. |
+| 9 | Deploy merchant. |
+| 10 | Deploy checkout. |
+| 11 | Seed Fake Rails blueprints and optional synthetic history. |
+| 12 | Run end-to-end verification. |
+| 13 | Log the retained release count. Actual pruning already happened per service. |
+| 14 | Print commit, release timestamp, topology, hosts and certificate expiry. |
+
+A failed batch, provisioning step or verification throws and exits non-zero. The
+previous release remains on disk, but there is no automatic rollback.
+
+### Release procedure
+
+For each role/node, `deployService()`:
+
+1. Creates `releases/<timestamp>/` and `shared/{certs,backups,pm2,data}`.
+2. Rsyncs the backend source, excluding dependencies, tests, builds, generated
+   files and local env/certs.
+3. Rsyncs the locally built frontend `dist` for edge/Fake Rails roles and writes
+   admin `runtime-config.js`.
+4. Writes the host's certificate set and `shared/.env` (mode 0600), then
+   symlinks `.env` into the release.
+5. Runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; core also runs `prisma generate`,
+   `migrate-deploy` and optional `db-seed`.
+6. Switches `current` to the new release.
+7. Writes the inline PM2 ecosystem and runs `pm2 delete` + `pm2 start
+   --update-env` + `pm2 save`.
+8. Renders only that role's Nginx sites, tests and reloads Nginx.
+9. Prunes older releases for that service.
+
+Release layout:
+
+```text
+<REMOTE_DIR>/
+├── releases/<TIMESTAMP>/
+│   ├── <backend>/          # source + .env symlink
+│   └── <front>/dist/       # edge/Fake Rails
+├── shared/
+│   ├── .env                # 0600
+│   ├── certs/
+│   ├── backups/
+│   ├── pm2/<service>.config.cjs
+│   └── data/
+└── current -> releases/<TIMESTAMP>
+```
+
+PM2 runs one fork instance per service with `/usr/local/bin/bun`,
+`pm2-compatible-start.js` and an **absolute** release `cwd`. There is no cluster
+mode and no connection draining.
+
+`deploy/templates/pm2.core.config.cjs.tpl` and
+`deploy/templates/pm2.edge.config.cjs.tpl` are dead files. `deploy.ts` generates
+the ecosystem inline; do not use those templates as a reference.
+
+## 8. Rolling updates and node selection
+
+Steps 6-10 split the deployment units of each role into batches:
+
+- batch size is `--rolling-batch` or `ROLLING_BATCH_SIZE` (default 1);
+- units inside a batch deploy sequentially;
+- after the batch, each unit is health-checked;
+- a failed probe stops the run; later batches are not deployed;
+- `--nodes` filters compute units by node id, but the plan is still built for the
+  whole configuration.
+
+A `--nodes` filter that matches nothing skips the role. A batch size greater than
+one can take multiple core nodes down before the post-batch check, reducing
+failover capacity.
+
+Batch checks are local liveness only: core uses loopback mTLS `/health`, edges
+use loopback HTTP `/health`. The cross-host edge-to-core mTLS and storage checks
+run only in step 12.
+
+## 9. Storage provisioning
+
+Storage provisioning runs in step 5 and is gated by the management flags and
+`--only`.
+
+### PostgreSQL 18
+
+`postgres18Provisioner.ts` installs `postgresql-<PG_VERSION>`,
+`postgresql-contrib` and PgBouncer, writes a tuned `zz-pg-switch.conf`, creates
+the application and replication roles, creates physical replication slots, and
+initializes each replica with `pg_basebackup -R`. It writes SCRAM `pg_hba`
+rules with `hostssl` for remote sources and installs the journal-partition cron.
+
+The provisioner does not write PostgreSQL `ssl`/`ssl_cert_file` settings. Remote
+connections require TLS by `pg_hba`, but the effective TLS material depends on
+the distribution defaults.
+
+### PgBouncer
+
+PgBouncer runs in transaction mode on the primary and replicas. The generated
+`pgbouncer.ini` has **no `[databases]` mapping**, so a core connection to `:6432`
+has no configured route to the application database. Enabling the pooler
+without adding that mapping can make the deployed core unable to connect.
+
+### Redis
+
+Redis is bound to the private IP plus loopback, requires a password, uses an
+RDB snapshot and an LRU memory policy. There is no TLS listener, so the
+generated `redis-client` certificate is unused.
+
+### Audit and log databases
+
+The audit database has `audit_records`, a SHA-256 hash chain, an immutability
+trigger and append-only grants. The log database has monthly
+`attempt_step_logs` and `http_access_logs` partitions, six months of initial
+partitions, a retention function and cron. Remote authentication is SCRAM over
+`hostssl`; no client certificate is requested.
+
+### Backup engine
+
+`backupEngineProvisioner.ts` installs Barman, compression tools, rclone and
+(optionally) WAL-G, creates the `pgbackup` user and directories, writes
+`/etc/pg-backup/backup.env`, the WAL-G environment files and the systemd unit,
+configures core/audit archiving, verifies targets and deploys the daemon source.
+The WAL-G binary is a moving GitHub "latest" Ubuntu 20.04 download and is not
+checksum-verified.
+
+## 10. Verification
+
+Step 12 checks:
+
+- every core node `/health` over loopback mTLS; a `DEGRADED` response fails;
+- every edge backend `/health` over loopback (liveness only);
+- each edge host's own client certificate against every derived core URL on
+  `/internal/<channel>/health`;
+- public merchant/checkout vhosts from the host (the admin LAN vhost is skipped);
+- Fake Rails backend and vhost `/health` when enabled;
+- PostgreSQL primary/replicas with `pg_isready` and `psql SELECT 1`;
+- PgBouncer `SELECT 1`, Redis `PING`, audit/log `SELECT 1`;
+- the backup daemon `/health` over mTLS when configured.
+
+Any failed result aborts the deploy. `--skip-verify` and `--dry-run` skip the
+step, so a run can report success without a live probe.
+
+The storage probes use `PGPASSWORD` on the remote command line. Password values
+therefore can appear in verbose runner output.
+
+## 11. Certificates
+
+`pkiManager.ts` creates a local RSA CA and leaves under `deploy/.certs/`:
+
+- `internal-ca.crt/.key`;
+- `core-back.crt/.key` (SAN includes every core private IP, loopback and
+  `core-back.internal`);
+- `backup-daemon.crt/.key`;
+- `fake-rails.crt/.key`;
+- `admin-back-client`, `merchant-back-client`, `checkout-back-client`;
+- optional `pg-client`, `redis-client`, `audit-db-client`, `log-db-client`,
+  `backup-client`.
+
+The CA private key never leaves the workstation. Distribution is host-level:
+
+- core receives the CA, core server pair and generated storage client pairs;
+- each edge receives the CA and its own client pair;
+- Fake Rails receives the CA and its server pair;
+- each storage host receives the CA and its own client pair;
+- the backup host receives the CA, backup-daemon server pair, `pg-client` and
+  `backup-client`.
+
+Changing a private IP requires updating every `*_PRIVATE_IP`/node-array
+`privateIp` and running `--update --enforce-firewall`. The PKI step detects SAN
+drift and re-signs leaves from the existing CA. Expiry is reported but does not
+force rotation; use `--rotate-certs`.
+
+### Storage mTLS is not consumed
+
+The storage client certificates are generated and uploaded to
+`/etc/pg-deploy/certs`, but PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, Redis, audit and log do not
+request or verify client certificates. PgBouncer's server leg uses
+`server_tls_sslmode=require` without CA verification. Treat storage mTLS as
+provisioned material, not an enforced control, until a staging run proves the
+engine configuration.
+
+### Certificate ownership
+
+Storage and backup certificates are uploaded through sudo. The backup host path
+is `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR` (default `/var/lib/pg-backup/shared/certs`).
+Certificates are mode 0644, keys 0600 and owned by root. The daemon runs as
+`pgbackup`, and the deploy does not chown those files. The daemon may therefore
+be unable to read its 0600 key. This is an open readiness gap; a staging run must
+confirm effective ownership and startup before backup mTLS is described as
+proven.
+
+## 12. Recovery and rollback
+
+### Releases
+
+Releases are immutable and `current` is a symlink. Nginx static roots follow
+`current` immediately. Backend PM2 processes do not: the inline ecosystem uses
+an absolute release `cwd`, so a plain `pm2 restart` reuses the old release path.
+
+Manual rollback of one host:
+
+```bash
+ssh <host>
+ls -1dt /var/www/pg-<role>/releases/*/
+TARGET=/var/www/pg-<role>/releases/<previous>
+ln -sfn "$TARGET" /var/www/pg-<role>/current
+"$HOME/.bun/bin/pm2" delete <service> || true
+cd "$TARGET/<backend>"
+PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH" pm2 start pm2-compatible-start.js \
+  --name <service> --interpreter /usr/local/bin/bun --update-env
+"$HOME/.bun/bin/pm2" save
+```
+
+The shared `shared/.env` is current, not historical. If configuration changed,
+the old code may not match it. Re-running the deploy from the previous commit is
+the cleaner whole-role rollback.
+
+### Pre-migration dump
+
+On a non-fresh deploy with core selected, step 5 runs `pg_dump -Fc` on the core
+host against the primary's direct port (never PgBouncer) into:
+
+```text
+<CORE_REMOTE_DIR>/shared/backups/pre-migrate-<timestamp>.dump
+```
+
+The command embeds `PGPASSWORD` in the remote command line. The fresh bootstrap
+does **not** install `postgresql-client`, so `pg_dump` must already exist. The
+dump is not verified, encrypted, copied off-host or restored automatically. A
+fresh install takes no dump. Migrations are forward-only; there is no down path.
+
+### Database and backup recovery
+
+The pre-migration dump is a manual operator decision: choose a target database
+and a compatible schema. The backup daemon's drill restores into scratch
+clusters and removes them; it does not restore the live database. There is no
+automatic restore from the dump.
+
+### Failure behaviour
+
+- A failed batch stops later batches; earlier batches remain on the new release.
+- A failed step 12 leaves the new release as `current` on every deployed host.
+- There is no automatic rollback or compensation.
+- `--skip-verify` can report success with a broken core/edge path.
+
+## 13. Security
+
+- `deploy.env` and `deploy/.certs/` are gitignored. Keep the env file at 0600
+  and the vault private.
+- The CA private key is never copied to a target host.
+- Secrets are streamed over SSH stdin, not written to local temp files.
+- Edge environments never receive `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` or another
+  host's client key.
+- Core listens on the private network; UFW is the outer ring and mTLS plus the
+  channel CN guard are the inner controls.
+- The pre-migration `PGPASSWORD` and storage probe passwords can appear in
+  verbose command output. Treat deploy logs as sensitive.
+- Fake Rails is an isolated test service. It has no gateway database credential,
+  no direct TLS listener and no inbound rail authentication. Keep it off
+  untrusted networks.
+- Storage client certificates are not yet consumed, so do not claim end-to-end
+  storage mTLS.
+- The backup daemon verifies any CA-signed client certificate but does not bind
+  a client CN to an operation; a direct mTLS client can call the policy endpoint
+  and bypass the core maker-checker workflow.
+
+## 14. Known gaps and caveats
+
+| Gap | Impact |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Storage client certificates are generated but not consumed by PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, Redis, audit or log. | Storage mTLS is not an enforced authentication control. |
+| Backup/storage certificate files can remain root-owned under a `pgbackup` daemon. | The daemon may fail to read its 0600 key; mTLS startup/probe readiness is unproven. |
+| Release pruning happens inside `deployService()`; step 13 only logs the retained count. | The guide's "prune in step 11/13" wording is stale. A multi-service host prunes each service tree separately. |
+| `pm2.core.config.cjs.tpl` and `pm2.edge.config.cjs.tpl` are not read. | They are dead templates; the inline ecosystem is authoritative. |
+| The fresh bootstrap omits a PostgreSQL client. | The non-fresh pre-migration `pg_dump` can fail on a minimal core host. |
+| PgBouncer is provisioned without a `[databases]` mapping. | Core connections to `:6432` can fail. |
+| `DEPLOY_MODE=auto` does not detect a missing remote directory. | A new host needs `--fresh`; otherwise the run behaves like an update. |
+| `DEPLOY_MODE=rolling_update` is accepted but has no distinct behavior. | It does not provide a different strategy from `auto`/`update`. |
+| No automatic rollback or connection draining. | A failed batch/verification leaves the new release current; a single-node restart has a gap. |
+| PKI expiry is reported but not enforced. | Expired leaves with matching SANs can be reused. |
+| WAL-G is downloaded from a moving "latest" Ubuntu 20.04 URL. | The binary is unpinned, unchecked and may not match the host distribution. |
+| Backup target verification uses rclone against the bucket string. | A raw S3 URL with no rclone configuration fails the deploy. |
+| Backup "all" includes `audit_db` even when audit is not configured. | A scheduled/triggered full or delta can fail on a core-only installation. |
+| Barman health uses the WAL-G `st ls` command. | Barman-only mode can report the S3 target unhealthy and needs WAL-G installed. |
+| The weekly shell restore drill only checks the core double-entry invariant. | It is narrower than the daemon's core+audit drill. |
+| The embedded Fake Rails widget is blocked by the checkout renderer allowlist/CSP and the seeded SRI array is empty. | The embedded flow cannot load end to end. |
+| Fake Rails LYPay/Evo Pay route keys do not match descriptor gateway codes, and the default webhook URL has an extra segment. | Four seeded core flows and default callbacks do not work. See [`fake-rails-back/README.md`](../fake-rails-back/README.md). |
+
+`DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md` remains a useful long-form operator guide, but several
+paragraphs are stale: `DEPLOY_MODE=auto` detection, prune location, legacy
+`DB_*` precedence, and the rollback `pm2 restart` shortcut. The canonical parts
+under `project-design/parts/07-deploy/` take precedence.
+

+catalog, exposes an mTLS HTTP API, and runs scratch restore plus ledger/audit
+invariant drills.
 
-- Runtime: Bun + TypeScript.
-- Default listener: `127.0.0.1:4090` (`/health` is the liveness probe).
-- Configuration: environment variables validated by `src/config.ts`. In a
-  deployment the entire daemon environment is generated automatically by
-  `deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts` from `deploy/deploy.env`;
-  `backup.env.example` is the local/troubleshooting reference, not a manual
-  production step.
-- Storage targets: primary S3/MinIO/R2 (WAL-G or Barman Cloud) and an optional secondary remote
-  SSH/S3 target.
-- Drills restore the core into `BACKUP_SCRATCH_DIR`/`BACKUP_SCRATCH_PORT` and the dedicated audit
-  database into `BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_DIR`/`BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_PORT`, then check double-entry zero
-  drift, sharded balance parity and the audit hash chain.
-- The in-process scheduler owns the full/delta/drill cron. Policy changes made through
-  `PUT /v1/policy` take effect without a restart. Set `SCHEDULER_ENABLED=false` only when an
-  external `/etc/cron.d/pg-backup` drives the trigger script instead.
+It is not a PostgreSQL provisioner and it is not the approval workflow. The
+deploy engine configures the cluster and archive commands; `core-back` owns the
+admin-facing proxy and maker-checker policy changes.

-### Engine and encryption
+- `target=all` expands to core plus audit, and also Redis when `REDIS_URL` is
+  set.
+- An `audit_db` target requires `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR`; the daemon refuses to
+  substitute the core data directory.
+- Full uses `wal-g backup-push <dataDir>`; delta adds `--delta`.
+- After a PostgreSQL backup it verifies the prefix with `wal-g st ls`.
+- A secondary target is mirrored with `rclone sync` (S3/rclone destination) or
+  `rsync -a --delete` (SSH path).
+- `prune("all","full")` runs `wal-g delete retain FULL <count> --confirm` for
+  core and audit. Delta pruning is a no-op.
+- `listBackups()` parses `wal-g backup-list --json`.
+- `recover()` fetches the latest base backup and returns a recovery fragment
+  containing `restore_command` and `recovery_target_time`.
+- Redis runs `BGSAVE`, `redis-cli --rdb <tmp>`, then
+  `rclone copyto <tmp> <corePrefix>/redis/dump.rdb` and removes the temp file.

+WAL-G health checks the S3 prefix, PostgreSQL (`SELECT 1`), optional secondary
+and Redis targets, WAL lag (from the first `PG_REPLICA_NODES` entry when set,
+otherwise the primary), and archive lag/bytes from `pg_stat_archiver`. It is

+### Barman
+
+- `target=all` expands the same way, including audit and optional Redis.
+- Runs `barman check`, `barman backup` or `--incremental`, then
+  `barman-cloud-backup`.
+- Reports only `primary-s3`; there is no secondary mirror in Barman mode.
+- Lists with `barman list-backup`.
+- `recover()` picks the latest backup and runs `barman recover --target-time`.
+- `prune()` is a no-op because Barman applies server-side retention.
+
+Barman health runs `barman check` for core and audit, checks the S3 target with
+the **WAL-G** `st ls` command, checks PostgreSQL, and adds optional secondary and
+Redis targets. Barman-only installations therefore need WAL-G installed for the
+health probe and still do not fully validate Barman's cloud/retention path.

+## 3. Scheduler
+
+`src/scheduler.ts` uses a strict five-field cron parser: no macros and no
+seconds field.
+
+- Jobs: `full`, `delta`, `drill`.
+- Tick cadence: `SCHEDULER_TICK_MS` (default 30 seconds).
+- The policy is re-read from the catalog on every tick; a `PUT /v1/policy`
+  change takes effect without a restart.
+- A due job is skipped when another scheduled job is running.
+- Runs are recorded as `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `PASSED` or `FAILED`.
+- A successful full backup triggers a best-effort prune.
+- A drill is recorded with a signed report.
+- Scheduled backups always use `target=all`.
+
+HTTP-triggered backups are not globally serialized with each other or with the
+scheduler; only the scheduler refuses to overlap its own jobs.
+

+## 5. mTLS
+
+`loadTlsOptions()`:
+
+- returns plain HTTP only when `BACKUP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true`;
+- otherwise requires `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_PATH`, `BACKUP_DAEMON_KEY_PATH` and
+  `BACKUP_DAEMON_CA_CERT_PATH`;
+- sets `requestCert: true` and `rejectUnauthorized: true`.
+
+The daemon verifies that a client certificate chains to the configured CA but
+does not inspect the client CN. Any CA-signed client can call every route. Core
+presents the `backup-client` certificate.
+
+Certificate/key pairing is validated at config load: the cert and key must be
+provided together, and a CA requires both.
+
+## 6. Catalog
+
+`src/catalogStore.ts` keeps runs, drills and policy in one JSON file
+(`BACKUP_CATALOG_PATH`).
+
+- Writes are serialized and atomic (temp file plus rename).
+- It keeps at most 500 runs and 100 drills.
+- A missing file is created on first use.
+- A corrupt or unwritable file is replaced in memory and reported; the daemon
+  keeps running without persistence.
+- The catalog is not encrypted and is not backed up by the daemon.
+- `fullRetentionDays` is stored in the policy; WAL-G pruning still uses
+  `BACKUP_RETENTION_FULL_COUNT` from the environment.
+
+## 7. Restore drill
+
+`src/restoreDrillRunner.ts`:
+
+1. Sets `targetTime = now - 5 minutes`.
+2. Stops prior scratch clusters and removes/creates the scratch directories.
+3. Calls `engine.recover()` for `postgres_core` and `audit_db`.
+4. Refuses `initdb` over a failed restore unless the engine explicitly reports
+   an initialized empty directory.
+5. Writes `recovery.conf` content into `postgresql.auto.conf` and creates
+   `recovery.signal`.
+6. Starts both clusters on loopback with `pg_ctl` at the configured scratch
+   ports.
+7. Runs:
+   - double-entry zero drift on `journal_lines`;
+   - sharded balance parity on `gl_accounts`/`gl_account_shards`;
+   - the audit hash chain on `audit_records`.
+8. Builds a report with status, duration, target time, replayed LSN, drift,
+   mismatch counts, broken links and per-check details.
+9. Signs the report with HMAC-SHA256 using `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX`.
+10. Stops and removes both scratch clusters in `finally`.
+
+A failed restore, start or check still produces a signed `FAILED` report when it
+goes through the scheduler or HTTP path. The drill requires an audit recovery
+target; without an audit database/`PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` (WAL-G) or audit Barman
+server, the drill fails.
+
+The provisioner also installs `/usr/local/bin/pg-backup-restore-drill`, a
+narrower shell drill that restores core and checks the double-entry invariant
+only.

-`deploy/backup-daemon` to `/opt/pg-backup-daemon` and enables the systemd unit. Every daemon

+## 9. Deploy-generated environment
+
+In a deployment, do not copy `backup.env.example` manually.
+`deploy/provisioners/backupEngineProvisioner.ts` writes
+`/etc/pg-backup/backup.env` from `deploy/deploy.env` and
+`deploy/deploy.ts` syncs `deploy/backup-daemon` to `/opt/pg-backup-daemon`.
+
+The generated file includes:
+
+- engine, compression, encryption, S3 endpoint/bucket/keys and prefixes;
+- `BARMAN_SERVER` set to `PG_DB_NAME` and `BARMAN_AUDIT_SERVER` set to
+  `BARMAN_AUDIT_SERVER` or `AUDIT_DB_NAME` from `deploy.env`;
+- secondary target, cron schedules, retention and alert lag;
+- listener port, bind host and certificate paths under
+  `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR`;
+- PostgreSQL primary host/port/user/password/database, audit database, replica
+  list, data directories and binary directory;
+- catalog, scratch paths/ports, scheduler settings and command timeout;
+- WAL-G/Barman/redis-cli binary paths and the derived Redis URL.
+
+The deploy also writes `/etc/pg-backup/wal-g.env`, plus
+`/etc/pg-backup/wal-g-core.env` and `/etc/pg-backup/wal-g-audit.env` on the
+archive hosts. It creates `/etc/systemd/system/pg-backup-daemon.service`,
+`/etc/cron.d/pg-backup`, `/usr/local/bin/pg-backup-daemon-trigger` and
+`/usr/local/bin/pg-backup-restore-drill`.
+
+`BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR` and `BACKUP_PGPASSFILE` are deploy keys. The daemon
+config does not validate `BACKUP_PGPASSFILE`, but the systemd environment still
+passes it to Barman subprocesses. `PG_DB_NAME` is also present in the generated
+environment but is not read by the daemon schema.
+
+`backup.env.example` is a local/troubleshooting reference only. It is not the
+production source of truth.
+
+## 10. systemd and source deployment
+
+The provisioner writes a unit equivalent to:
+
+```ini
+[Unit]
+Description=Payment Gateway pg-backup-daemon (WAL-G / Barman control plane)
+After=network-online.target
+Wants=network-online.target
+
+[Service]
+Type=simple
+User=pgbackup
+Group=pgbackup
+WorkingDirectory=/opt/pg-backup-daemon
+EnvironmentFile=/etc/pg-backup/backup.env
+Environment=BACKUP_DAEMON_PORT=4090
+ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/bun run src/index.ts
+Restart=always
+RestartSec=3
+LimitNOFILE=65536
+NoNewPrivileges=true
+ProtectSystem=strict
+ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/pg-backup /var/log/pg-backup <catalog dir> <cert dir> <scratch dirs> <pgpass dir>
+
+[Install]
+WantedBy=multi-user.target
+```
+
+`deployBackupDaemon()` installs `/opt/pg-backup-daemon`, rsyncs the source with
+`--delete` (excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `test`, `*.log`, `.env`),
+chowns it to `pgbackup`, ensures `/usr/local/bin/bun`, runs
+`bun install --frozen-lockfile` as `pgbackup`, and enables/restarts the unit.
+
+When the scheduler is enabled, `/etc/cron.d/pg-backup` only contains a comment.
+When it is disabled, the file drives full/delta triggers as `pgbackup` and the
+weekly shell drill as root.
+
+Certificate ownership is an open risk: the deploy uploads the daemon key/cert
+through sudo (root-owned 0600 under a directory owned by `pgbackup`) and does not
+chown the files to `pgbackup`. The daemon may be unable to read its key. Verify
+ownership and startup on a staging host before claiming mTLS readiness.
+
+## 11. Operations
+
+### Local run
+
+```bash
+cd deploy/backup-daemon
+bun install
+bun run start
+bun run typecheck
+bun test
+```
+
+For local use without certificates, set `BACKUP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true`
+explicitly. Do not use that setting in production.
+
+### Deployed service
+
+```bash
+systemctl status pg-backup-daemon
+journalctl -u pg-backup-daemon --since '1 hour ago'
+cat /etc/pg-backup/backup.env          # sensitive
+```
+
+### mTLS calls
+
+The deployed trigger script uses `internal-ca.crt`, `backup-client.crt` and
+`backup-client.key` from `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR`:
+
+```bash
+CERT_DIR=/var/lib/pg-backup/shared/certs
+HOST=10.10.13.10
+PORT=4090
+
+curl -fsS \
+  --cacert "$CERT_DIR/internal-ca.crt" \
+  --cert "$CERT_DIR/backup-client.crt" \
+  --key "$CERT_DIR/backup-client.key" \
+  "https://$HOST:$PORT/v1/overview"
+
+curl -fsS \
+  --cacert "$CERT_DIR/internal-ca.crt" \
+  --cert "$CERT_DIR/backup-client.crt" \
+  --key "$CERT_DIR/backup-client.key" \
+  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
+  -X POST \
+  --data '{"target":"all","kind":"full"}' \
+  "https://$HOST:$PORT/v1/backups/trigger"
+
+curl -fsS \
+  --cacert "$CERT_DIR/internal-ca.crt" \
+  --cert "$CERT_DIR/backup-client.crt" \
+  --key "$CERT_DIR/backup-client.key" \
+  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
+  -X POST \
+  --data '{}' \
+  "https://$HOST:$PORT/v1/drills/run"
+```
+
+Trigger and drill calls return `202`; poll `/v1/runs` and `/v1/drills` or the
+catalog for completion. `/health` is liveness only; use `/v1/overview` for engine
+health.
+
+### Admin and core workflow
+
+`core-back/lib/storageEngine/backupControlClient.ts` uses the internal CA and
+`backup-client` certificate. Core exposes overview/trigger/drill/policy/catalog
+under its internal backups API. `admin-back` applies `security:read` /
+`security:write` and proxies the calls.
+
+`PUT /policy` without an `approvalRequestId` creates a `BACKUP_POLICY` approval
+and returns `202`. With an approved request id, core checks the subject type,
+state and maker != checker, sends the approved payload to the daemon, marks the
+approval `EXECUTED` and writes an audit record. The daemon endpoint itself does
+not enforce this workflow.
+
+## 12. Routine checks
+
+- `/v1/overview` is healthy and every target has a detail.
+- The latest full/delta run is `PASSED` and within the expected schedule.
+- WAL archive lag is below `BACKUP_ALERT_LAG_SECONDS`.
+- The latest drill is `PASSED`, signed, and its target time is recent.
+- The catalog file exists and is writable; startup logs do not say
+  "catalog is running in memory only".
+- `systemctl status pg-backup-daemon` is active and the key is readable by
+  `pgbackup`.
+- The primary S3 bucket and optional secondary target are reachable.
+- Barman mode also has a working WAL-G binary for the S3 health check.
+
+## 13. Troubleshooting
+
+| Symptom | Likely cause / action |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Startup exits with a Zod message | Fix the named environment key. Cron must be five fields; the encryption key must be hex, even-length, >= 16 bytes; S3 keys must be paired. |
+| `TLS requires ...` or `mTLS requires ...` | Set both cert/key and the CA, or explicitly allow insecure HTTP for local development only. |
+| Daemon fails to start as `pgbackup` | Check ownership/mode of `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_PATH` and `BACKUP_DAEMON_KEY_PATH`; the deploy uploads them as root and does not chown them. |
+| `/v1/overview` reports `primary-s3` unhealthy | Check endpoint/bucket/keys, `rclone`, and WAL-G. Barman health still uses WAL-G `st ls`. |
+| `all` backup fails immediately | `all` includes `audit_db`; set `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` (WAL-G), or configure the audit Barman server / `BARMAN_AUDIT_SERVER`. |
+| Delta backup fails | WAL-G delta requires a prior base backup. Run a full first; the error text notes this. |
+| `redis` target fails | Set `REDIS_URL`; Redis upload also requires `rclone` and a reachable core S3 prefix. |
+| Drill fails at audit recovery | The drill requires the audit target; configure `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` or the audit Barman server. |
+| Drill leaves scratch directories | An interrupted cleanup can leave `/var/lib/pg-backup/scratch` content; inspect and remove only when no drill is running. |
+| Policy update returns `400 validation_error` | `PUT /v1/policy` requires the full policy object, not a partial patch, and valid five-field crons. |
+| Trigger returns `202` but nothing happens | Check the daemon log, `/v1/runs`, engine binary availability, and whether another scheduled job is running. HTTP triggers themselves are not serialized. |
+| Catalog warning at startup | The path is unwritable or the JSON is corrupt; the daemon is running in memory and will lose history on restart. Fix permissions or remove the corrupt file. |
+| Barman backup succeeds but health fails | Install WAL-G for the S3 check, or treat the S3 target result as a known Barman-mode limitation. |
+
+## 14. Known gaps
+
+- Backup daemon certificate/key files may be root-owned and unreadable by
+  `pgbackup`; deploy readiness is unproven until a staging run checks effective
+  ownership and mTLS startup.
+- Barman health depends on the WAL-G binary and does not fully validate Barman's
+  cloud/retention path.
+- A backup target of `all` always includes `audit_db`, even when audit is not
+  configured; WAL-G then fails without `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR`, and Barman needs an
+  audit server.
+- HTTP-triggered backups are not globally serialized; only the scheduler skips
+  overlap with its own jobs.
+- Log-database backups are not a daemon target; only core, audit and optional
+  Redis are covered.
+- The daemon accepts any CA-signed client certificate and does not authorize a
+  client CN per route. A direct client can call `PUT /v1/policy` and bypass core
+  maker-checker.
+- The provisioned weekly shell drill only checks the core double-entry
+  invariant; it does not run the balance-parity or audit-chain checks.
+- The JSON catalog is unencrypted, count-retained and not itself backed up.
+- There is no verify-only restore mode; every drill performs a full scratch
+  restore of core and audit.
+- WAL-G installation is a moving `latest` Ubuntu 20.04 binary and is not
+  checksum-verified.
+- The daemon's policy `fullRetentionDays` is metadata; WAL-G pruning uses
+  `BACKUP_RETENTION_FULL_COUNT`.
+- An interrupted drill cleanup can leave scratch clusters or directories.
+- A failed drill still produces a signed `FAILED` report on the scheduled/HTTP
+  paths; it does not restore the live database.
+

+bun run typecheck

+

+# backup-daemon blueprint
+
+Generated from: `deploy.backup`.
+
+## Backup Daemon
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+`pg-backup-daemon` is the backup and point-in-time-recovery control plane for the storage tier. It wraps WAL-G or Barman, owns the full/delta/drill schedule, keeps a local catalog, exposes an mTLS HTTP API and runs scratch restore plus ledger/audit invariant drills.
+
+It owns engine selection, scheduling, the catalog, the HTTP API, target/WAL health and drills. It does not own the PostgreSQL cluster, archive configuration (the provisioner does), the admin approval workflow (core does) or the admin UI.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The design calls for a Bun service that supports WAL-G on the database host and Barman on a dedicated backup host, streams WAL with compression and client-side encryption, takes weekly full and daily delta backups for core and audit, snapshots Redis, mirrors to an optional secondary vault, and runs a weekly scratch restore that verifies double-entry zero drift, sharded balance parity and the audit hash chain before signing and cleaning up.
+
+It exposes overview, trigger, policy, run and drill endpoints over mTLS to core, which surfaces them to the admin portal. Policy changes require core-side maker-checker. The historical design's Tripoli 03:00 and hourly Redis claims are superseded; the code uses UTC cron expressions and triggered Redis snapshots.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Process lifecycle
+
+`src/index.ts` loads and validates the environment, creates a `SpawnCommandRunner`, creates the WAL-G/Barman engine, loads the catalog (or falls back to memory), builds a default policy, creates the drill runner, scheduler and server, starts the scheduler when enabled, and logs the listener/engine/scheduler state. SIGTERM/SIGINT stops the scheduler and server, waits up to 15 seconds for in-flight work and exits.
+
+### 3.2 HTTP server and mTLS
+
+`src/server.ts` uses `Bun.serve` with a JSON handler:
+
+| Method | Path | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| GET | `/health` | Liveness, engine mode and version. Does not run engine health checks. |
+| GET | `/v1/overview` | Engine health, WAL lag, targets, schedule/policy, scheduler state, recent backups and drills. |
+| POST | `/v1/backups/trigger` | Validates `{ target, kind }`, queues a run and returns 202. |
+| PUT | `/v1/policy` | Persists cron/retention/lag and returns the policy. |
+| GET | `/v1/runs`, `/v1/drills` | Recent records with `limit` 1-500. |
+| POST | `/v1/drills/run` | Queues a drill and returns 202. |
+
+Bodies are capped at 256 KiB. Responses use `cache-control: no-store` and recursively redact credential-shaped keys/values. `HttpError` becomes a JSON envelope; unexpected errors become a generic 500 with a request id.
+
+`loadTlsOptions()` returns plain HTTP only when `BACKUP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true`. Otherwise it requires the server certificate, key and CA and sets `requestCert: true`, `rejectUnauthorized: true`. The daemon verifies the client chain but does not inspect the client CN; any CA-signed client can call every route. Core presents `backup-client`.
+
+### 3.3 Engines
+
+`createBackupEngine()` selects `WalGEngine` or `BarmanEngine`.
+
+**WAL-G**:
+
+- `triggerBackup("all", kind)` expands to `postgres_core`, `audit_db` and, when `REDIS_URL` is set, `redis`;
+- refuses `audit_db` when `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` is empty;
+- runs `wal-g backup-push <dataDir>` for full, `--delta` for delta;
+- verifies the bucket with `wal-g st ls <prefix>`;
+- mirrors with `rclone sync` or `rsync -a --delete` when a secondary target exists;
+- `prune("all","full")` runs `wal-g delete retain FULL <count> --confirm`; delta pruning is a no-op;
+- lists with `wal-g backup-list --json`; `recover()` fetches the latest base backup and returns a recovery fragment;
+- Redis backup runs `BGSAVE`, `redis-cli --rdb <tmp>` and `rclone copyto <tmp> <corePrefix>/redis/dump.rdb`, then removes the temp file.
+
+Health checks the S3 target with `wal-g st ls`, PostgreSQL with `psql SELECT 1`, optional secondary/Redis, WAL lag from the first replica or primary, and archive lag/bytes from `pg_stat_archiver`. It is healthy when every target passes and archive lag is within `BACKUP_ALERT_LAG_SECONDS`.
+
+**Barman**:
+
+- `triggerBackup` expands `all` the same way (including audit), runs `barman check`, `barman backup`/`--incremental`, then `barman-cloud-backup`; it reports only `primary-s3`, with no secondary mirror;
+- lists with `barman list-backup`; `recover()` picks the latest and runs `barman recover --target-time`; `prune()` is a no-op because Barman applies server-side retention.
+
+Barman health runs `barman check` for core and audit, checks S3 with the **WAL-G** `st ls` command, checks PostgreSQL, and adds optional secondary/Redis. Barman health therefore requires WAL-G and does not prove Barman's cloud/retention path. This document does not claim complete Barman health.
+
+### 3.4 Scheduler
+
+`src/scheduler.ts` uses a strict five-field cron parser (no macros or seconds), computes the next full/delta/drill slots, ticks every `SCHEDULER_TICK_MS` (default 30 seconds), reloads policy from the catalog, skips a due job when another job is running, records runs as `QUEUED`/`RUNNING`/`PASSED`/`FAILED`, reserves unique ids, attempts a full prune after a successful full backup, and records signed drill reports. A policy update through `PUT /v1/policy` takes effect on the next tick without a restart.
+
+### 3.5 Catalog
+
+`src/catalogStore.ts` stores runs, drills and policy in one JSON file (`BACKUP_CATALOG_PATH`), writes atomically via temp file + rename, serializes writes, keeps at most 500 runs and 100 drills, validates on load, falls back to in-memory operation when unwritable or corrupt, and reports the persistence error. The catalog is not encrypted and is not backed up by the daemon.
+
+### 3.6 Restore drill
+
+`src/restoreDrillRunner.ts`:
+
+1. Sets `targetTime = now - 5 minutes` and stops/removes prior scratch clusters.
+2. Calls `engine.recover()` for `postgres_core` and `audit_db`.
+3. Refuses `initdb` over a failed restore unless the engine explicitly reports an initialized empty directory.
+4. Writes `recovery.conf` into `postgresql.auto.conf`, creates `recovery.signal`, and starts both clusters on the configured ports over loopback.
+5. Runs the double-entry zero-drift query, the sharded-balance parity query and the audit hash-chain query.
+6. Builds a report with status, duration, target time, replayed LSN, drift, mismatch counts, broken links and per-check details.
+7. Signs it with HMAC-SHA256 using `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX`.
+8. Stops and removes both scratch clusters in `finally`.
+
+A failed restore, start or check still produces a signed `FAILED` report through the scheduler or HTTP path. The drill requires an audit recovery target; without an audit database or `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR`, the audit recovery fails and the drill fails.
+
+### 3.7 Core and admin integration
+
+`core-back/lib/storageEngine/backupControlClient.ts` builds a TLS 1.3 keep-alive agent with the internal CA and `backup-client` cert/key and calls overview/health/trigger/drill/policy/runs/drills.
+
+`core-back/api/internal/backups.ts`:
+
+- `GET /overview` requires `security:read` or `gateway:read`, fetches daemon health and upserts runs/drills with `Promise.allSettled`;
+- `POST /trigger` and `POST /drill` require `security:write`, require a configured daemon, call it and insert a local queued row;
+- `PUT /policy` requires `security:write`; without `approvalRequestId` it creates a `BACKUP_POLICY` approval (`PENDING_REVIEW`, 7-day expiry) and returns 202; with an id it checks subject type, state and maker != checker, sends the **approved payload** to the daemon, marks the approval `EXECUTED`, bumps the base version and writes an audit record;
+- `GET /catalog` returns local runs/drills.
+
+`admin-back/api/protected/backups.ts` applies `security:read`/`security:write` at the edge, forwards overview/trigger/drill/policy and relays core status. The daemon's own `PUT /v1/policy` has no maker-checker, so a direct mTLS client can bypass the core approval workflow.
+
+### 3.8 Systemd and source deployment
+
+`backupEngineProvisioner.ts` writes `/etc/systemd/system/pg-backup-daemon.service`: `User/Group=pgbackup`, `WorkingDirectory=/opt/pg-backup-daemon`, `EnvironmentFile=/etc/pg-backup/backup.env`, `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/bun run src/index.ts`, `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=3`, `LimitNOFILE=65536`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, and `ReadWritePaths` for backup, log, catalog, cert, scratch and pgpass directories.
+
+`deploy.ts` copies `deploy/backup-daemon` to `/opt/pg-backup-daemon` with rsync `--delete`, excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `test`, `*.log` and `.env`, chowns to `pgbackup`, runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` as `pgbackup`, and enables/restarts the unit.
+
+The provisioner writes `/etc/cron.d/pg-backup`: when the scheduler is enabled only a comment; otherwise full/delta trigger lines as `pgbackup` and the drill script as root. `/usr/local/bin/pg-backup-restore-drill` restores core and checks double-entry only; it is narrower than the in-process drill.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- The daemon listens over mTLS by default and refuses plain HTTP unless explicitly allowed for development.
+- Core presents a CA-signed `backup-client` certificate; the daemon does not authorize a CN per route.
+- Trigger and drill return 202 and complete asynchronously; the catalog is the state store.
+- Scheduled jobs do not overlap; HTTP triggers are not globally serialized.
+- Catalog writes are atomic; a failed write does not crash the daemon.
+- Secrets are redacted from responses and error messages.
+- Full backups are followed by a best-effort prune; delta pruning is non-destructive.
+- Audit backups require `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR`; the daemon never substitutes the core data directory.
+- Drills restore core and audit, check three invariants, sign the report and always clean up scratch clusters.
+- Policy changes through core require maker-checker; the daemon endpoint itself does not.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Group | Keys |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Engine/encryption | `BACKUP_ENGINE_MODE`, `BACKUP_COMPRESSION`, `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX`, `BACKUP_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP`, `BACKUP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` |
+| S3/secondary | `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT`, `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_BUCKET`, `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ACCESS_KEY`, `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_SECRET_KEY`, `BACKUP_CORE_S3_PREFIX`, `BACKUP_AUDIT_S3_PREFIX`, `BACKUP_SECONDARY_SSH_TARGET` |
+| Schedule/retention | `BACKUP_FULL_CRON`, `BACKUP_DELTA_CRON`, `BACKUP_DRILL_CRON`, `BACKUP_RETENTION_FULL_COUNT`, `BACKUP_RETENTION_WAL_DAYS`, `BACKUP_ALERT_LAG_SECONDS`, `SCHEDULER_ENABLED`, `SCHEDULER_TICK_MS` |

+| PostgreSQL | `PG_PRIMARY_HOST`, `PG_PRIMARY_PORT`, `PG_PRIMARY_USER`, `PG_PRIMARY_PASSWORD`, `PG_PRIMARY_DB_NAME`, `PG_AUDIT_DB_NAME`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `PG_DATA_DIR`, `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR`, `PG_BIN_DIR` |
+| Catalog/scratch | `BACKUP_CATALOG_PATH`, `BACKUP_SCRATCH_DIR`, `BACKUP_SCRATCH_PORT`, `BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_DIR`, `BACKUP_SCRATCH_AUDIT_PORT`, `PGPASSFILE` |

+| Redis | `REDIS_URL`, `REDIS_CLI_BIN` |
+
+`BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX` must be hex, at least 16 bytes and even length; the deploy requires exactly 64 hex characters. `backup.env.example` is a local/troubleshooting reference; a deployment generates `/etc/pg-backup/backup.env` from `deploy.env`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+```bash
+cd deploy/backup-daemon
+bun install
+bun run start
+bun test
+bun run typecheck
+```
+
+On a deployed host, use `systemctl status pg-backup-daemon`, `journalctl -u pg-backup-daemon`, and a curl request with `internal-ca.crt`, `backup-client.crt` and `backup-client.key` to `/v1/overview`. Admin triggers and policy changes go through core; policy changes require a second user.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- WAL-G/Barman full/delta backup, listing, restore, verification and cloud copy.
+- Optional Redis snapshot.
+- S3 primary and optional secondary mirror for WAL-G.
+- In-process cron scheduler with policy reload and overlap skipping.
+- Atomic JSON catalog with in-memory fallback.
+- Core+audit drill with double-entry, balance parity and audit-chain checks and HMAC-signed reports.
+- mTLS server with client-certificate verification and secret redaction.
+- Core proxy/approval integration and admin edge routes.
+- Provisioner-generated env, systemd unit, cron and source deployment.
+
+### Partial
+
+- Barman health depends on WAL-G for the S3 target.
+- No per-CN daemon authorization.
+- The shell drill is narrower than the in-process drill.
+- The catalog is one unencrypted JSON file with count-based retention.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- Log-database backup target.
+- HTTP trigger serialization/backpressure.
+- Automatic certificate/key ownership correction for `pgbackup`.
+- Catalog backup and encryption.
+- A verify-only restore mode.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- `all` includes `audit_db` without checking whether audit is configured; WAL-G needs `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` and Barman needs an audit server.
+- A Barman-only installation reports the primary S3 target unhealthy because health uses WAL-G.
+- The backup cert/key may be root-owned and unreadable by `pgbackup`, preventing mTLS startup and failing the deploy probe.
+- Any CA-signed certificate can call the policy endpoint directly and bypass maker-checker.
+- Concurrent HTTP triggers are not serialized.
+- The drill requires audit recovery even for a core-only intent.
+- An interrupted cleanup can leave scratch clusters/directories.
+- The catalog may contain host/run metadata and is not encrypted.
+
+## 8. Verification and tests

+cd deploy/backup-daemon && bun run typecheck && bun test
+cd deploy && bun test test/provisioners.test.ts

+## Deploy Topology and Configuration
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the deployment input contract: `deploy/deploy.env`, its parser, Zod schema, cross-field validation, topology model and the translation from logical roles to concrete hosts. It defines the node grammar, all configuration groups, precedence rules, topology classification and the validation that runs before any SSH connection.
+
+It does not own the host plan itself (see `deploy.planner`), certificate generation (`deploy.pki`), firewall application (`deploy.firewall`), the pipeline (`deploy.pipeline`) or storage provisioning (`deploy.storage`).
+
+The entrypoint is `deploy/deploy.sh`, which requires Bun and a `deploy/deploy.env`, then executes `bun run deploy/deploy.ts`.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The design requires a flexible 1..N topology:
+
+- compute tiers `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES`, `CHECKOUT_NODES`;
+- one PostgreSQL primary, zero or more streaming replicas and optional PgBouncer;
+- optional Redis, dedicated audit and log databases, and a backup node;
+- any compute or storage role may share a host, but ports must remain distinct and storage roles may not collide with compute listeners;
+- configuration is validated before the first SSH connection, so an invalid IP or missing key fails on the operator workstation rather than halfway through production;
+- node arrays override the legacy single-host fields;
+- the core certificate SAN and firewall allowlists are derived from the same private IPs.
+
+The design names three topology shapes: fully distributed, split/combined hosts, and a single all-in-one staging box. The code additionally supports horizontal compute arrays.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Loading and parsing
+
+`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` uses a small dotenv parser, not a full dotenv library:
+
+- blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored;
+- `KEY=value` is required; lines without `=` are ignored;
+- single- or double-quoted values end at the first matching quote, so an inline `#` after the quote is not part of the value;
+- unquoted values are truncated at ` #`;
+- there is no variable expansion, no `export` handling, no escaped-newline handling and no multi-line value support;
+- a duplicate key overwrites the earlier value in the parsed record.
+
+The parsed record is validated with `z.strictObject`. Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored. `loadDeployConfig()` returns either a config plus an empty problem list or a list of Zod issues and cross-field problems.
+
+### 3.2 Node grammar
+
+Every `*_NODES` list, `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE` and `BACKUP_NODE` uses:
+
+```text
+nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
+```
+
+- `nodeId` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.
+- `sshHost` and `privateIp` must be IPv4 addresses. DNS names are not accepted for nodes.
+- `sshPort` and `servicePort` must be integers from 1 to 65535.
+- Node ids must be unique across every node list.
+- A node list rejects duplicate private IPs within that list.
+- PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs must also be globally unique.
+
+The node spec carries only host, SSH port, private IP and service port. SSH user, key path and sudo password still come from the tier's legacy fields (`CORE_SSH_USER`, `CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `CORE_SUDO_PASSWORD`, and so on). Two roles on one SSH endpoint must use the same user, key and sudo password.
+

+
+### 3.4 Precedence rules
+
+1. **Node arrays over legacy host fields.** `CORE_NODES` overrides `CORE_SSH_HOST`, `CORE_SSH_PORT`, `CORE_PRIVATE_IP` and `CORE_PORT` for planning. The same applies to admin, merchant and checkout. SSH user/key/sudo are still taken from the legacy fields.
+2. **PostgreSQL storage fields over legacy database fields.** When any `PG_*` storage field is configured, `PG_DB_NAME`, `PG_DB_USER` and `PG_DB_PASSWORD` are authoritative. Otherwise `DB_*` is used, falling back to `PG_DB_*`.
+3. **Derived database URL.** When the PostgreSQL tier is configured and a host exists, `DATABASE_URL` is derived from the PG credentials, the primary private IP and `PGBOUNCER_PORT` when enabled; otherwise the explicit `DATABASE_URL` is used.
+4. **Explicit core URL list.** `CORE_BACK_URLS` wins; otherwise `https://<privateIp>:<servicePort>` for every `CORE_NODES` entry; otherwise the legacy `https://<CORE_PRIVATE_IP>:<CORE_PORT>`.
+5. **Node service port over configured backend port.** A node's `servicePort` overrides `CORE_PORT`/`ADMIN_BACK_PORT`/`MERCHANT_BACK_PORT`/`CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT` for that node.
+6. **CLI over environment.** `--fresh`, `--update`, `--only`, `--nodes`, `--rolling-batch`, `--keep`, `--rotate-certs`, `--skip-build` and `--skip-verify` override the corresponding configuration for one run.
+7. **Admin checklist master flag.** `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS` wins over the legacy `ADMIN_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST`; the legacy key is the fallback when the master key is absent.
+
+### 3.5 Topology classification
+
+`planHosts()` groups every role target by `sshHost:sshPort`. The topology label is based on the number of unique SSH endpoints, not on the number of roles:
+
+| Unique hosts | Topology |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| 1 | `single-host` |
+| 2 | `split` |
+| 3 or more | `distributed` |
+
+A host can carry several roles. Compute services, Nginx sites, certificate bundles and firewall rules are unioned per host. Storage roles are included only when their management flag is enabled (`PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `BACKUP_ENABLED`), although the storage plan itself is still constructed for display.
+
+### 3.6 Validation rules
+
+Zod field validation:
+
+- IPv4 octets and CIDR syntax are checked.
+- Database names, users and replication users must be identifier-safe.
+- Remote directories, identifiers and domain names have length and character limits.
+- `DB_ENGINE` is restricted to `postgresql`.
+- `DEPLOY_MODE` is `auto`, `fresh`, `update` or `rolling_update`.
+- `PG_VERSION` is one or two digits (default `18`).
+- `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX` must be exactly 64 hex characters, or empty; it is required when backups are enabled.
+- `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT` must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL when backups are enabled.
+- SSL mode is `certbot`, `custom` or `self_signed`.
+
+Cross-field validation:
+
+- PostgreSQL fields require `DB_ENGINE=postgresql`.
+- `PG_REPLICA_NODES` requires exactly one `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`.
+- `PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true` requires a primary, an SSH key and a non-empty database password.
+- `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED=true` requires the PostgreSQL storage fields.
+- Legacy `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true` without the PG tier requires SSH host, key and private IP.
+- When the PG tier is not configured, legacy `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL` are required.
+- An explicit `DATABASE_URL` must start with `postgresql://`; if `DB_PRIVATE_IP` is set, the URL should contain it.
+- Node arrays require the matching `*_SSH_KEY_PATH`.
+- Redis/audit/log managed-via-SSH mode requires the node, key and password.
+- Backups require `BACKUP_NODE`, an SSH key, a bucket and an encryption key.
+- WAL-G backups require `BACKUP_NODE` and `PG_PRIMARY_NODE` to have the same private IP because WAL-G reads the local data directory.
+- When the audit database is on a different host from a WAL-G backup node, `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` is required.
+- Node ids are unique across all lists; PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs are unique.
+- The same SSH endpoint may not expose the same service port for two compute roles.
+- A storage port may not collide with a compute listener on the same SSH endpoint.
+- Storage roles on one endpoint may share a port only within the PostgreSQL family (primary, replica, audit, log); Redis, PgBouncer and backup are separate families.
+- Merchant and checkout HTTP, HTTPS and LAN ports must differ within each portal; all LAN ports (admin, merchant, checkout) must differ; the two public domains must differ.
+- `CORE_PORT` must differ from all three edge backend ports.
+- `custom` SSL mode requires both certificate and key paths.
+- Fake Rails requires its SSH host/key/private IP/admin credentials/JWT secret/seeder token; it refuses production unless `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`; its backend and Nginx ports must not collide with core/edge/admin ports or public 80/443.
+- The synthetic seeder requires `IS_TEST_SERVER=true`, Fake Rails enabled and, in production, the explicit Fake Rails production override.
+- `findSshConflicts()` rejects one SSH endpoint with more than one SSH key or user across roles.
+
+### 3.7 Mode behavior
+
+`DEPLOY_MODE` is read as follows:
+
+- `fresh`: bootstrap packages, Bun, PM2 and the firewall;
+- `update`: do not bootstrap or change the firewall unless `--enforce-firewall` is passed;
+- `auto`: does not stat the remote release directory; in practice it behaves like `update` unless `--fresh` is passed;
+- `rolling_update`: accepted by the schema but not treated differently from `auto`.
+
+The CLI `--fresh` always wins; `--update` disables an environment `fresh`.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- Configuration is validated before any SSH connection.
+- The node grammar uses private IPs for peer communication; `sshHost` may be public.
+- The same private IP set drives certificate SANs, firewall sources and derived URLs.
+- Edge environments never include database or KMS secrets.
+- Core environments include `DATABASE_URL`, replication/audit/log URLs, Redis, backup control paths and `KMS_MASTER_KEY` when configured.
+- Runtime service environments are forced to `NODE_ENV=production` by the planner even when `DEPLOY_ENV` is development or staging.
+- A failure in cross-field validation aborts the run before the plan is rendered.
+- `deploy.env` and `deploy/.certs/` are gitignored; the operator must keep the environment file at mode 0600.
+
