+# fake-rails-front
+
+Tester portal and hosted-checkout simulator for the optional Fake Payment Rails
+tier. It is a Vue 3 + Vuetify 3 + TSX SPA built with Vite.
+
+This is a developer/test surface, not a payer product. It can approve a payment
+without money moving, forge webhook signatures, drop callbacks, show raw wire
+bodies and generate anomalous statements.
+
+## 1. What it does
+
+The SPA has two roles:
+
+1. A single-tester control room for the emulator: live feed, transaction
+   inspection, chaos controls, webhook composition and statement generation.
+2. Public hosted pages that emulate an upstream redirect checkout and an
+   embedded Moamalat/MPGS widget.
+
+It talks to `fake-rails-back` through the same origin. In development, Vite
+proxies `/portal-api`, `/rails`, `/sdk` and `/hosted` to the backend; in a
+deployment, the Fake Rails Nginx vhost proxies those paths and serves the built
+`dist`.
+
+## 2. Pages and routes
+
+`src/router/index.ts` uses HTML5 history mode.
+
+| Route | Page | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `/` | redirect | Sends the browser to `/dashboard`. |
+| `/login` | `pages/login/index.tsx` | Single tester login. |
+| `/dashboard` | `pages/dashboard/index.tsx` | KPI strip, live wire feed and pending actions. |
+| `/transactions` | `pages/transactions/index.tsx` | Filter by reference/status, inspect a transaction, compose a webhook. |
+| `/chaos-matrix` | `pages/chaos-matrix/index.tsx` | Per-rail chaos cards and global presets. |
+| `/statements` | `pages/statements/index.tsx` | Generate and download CSV/JSON/XLSX statements with anomalies. |
+| `/hosted/redirect/:sessionId` | `pages/hosted/redirect/[sessionId].tsx` | Interactive hosted redirect checkout. |
+| `/hosted/widget-frame` | `pages/hosted/widget-frame.tsx` | Moamalat/MPGS iframe content. |
+
+The router guard sends unauthenticated non-hosted routes to
+`/login?redirect=<path>`. Hosted routes and `/login` are public.
+
+The deployment must serve `index.html` for unknown history-mode paths and proxy
+the four API prefixes to the backend.
+
+## 3. Login and session
+
+- Username is prefilled as `tester_admin`; the password is empty.
+- `POST /portal-api/auth/login` returns a 12-hour HS256 JWT and a display user.
+- The token is stored in `localStorage` under `fake-rails-token`; the user is
+  stored under `fake-rails-user`.
+- `utils/api.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
+- A `401` clears the session and redirects to `/login`, except under `/hosted`.
+- The SSE feed uses `?token=<jwt>` because `EventSource` cannot set headers.
+
+The portal shell has four navigation links, an environment badge (`SANDBOX` or
+`PRODUCTION TEST SERVER`) and logout. It is English-only and uses the fixed
+portal theme; it does not use the admin/merchant i18n catalogues.
+
+## 4. Dashboard
+
+`pages/dashboard/index.tsx` loads `GET /portal-api/transactions/summary` and
+shows:
+
+- total, paid, awaiting-customer and failed/cancelled counts;
+- a `LiveTransactionFeed` over `GET /portal-api/transactions/stream`;
+- up to 50 pending `INITIATED`/`AWAITING_ACTION` transactions with the expected
+  OTP and quick actions:
+  - Approve;
+  - Approve amount mismatch;
+  - Approve late;
+  - Reject.
+
+The feed listens to `ready`, `rail.request`, `webhook.sent`, `webhook.failed`
+and `transaction.action`. It is process-local and has no replay cursor; a
+reconnect loses events emitted while disconnected.
+
+## 5. Transactions and wire inspector
+
+`pages/transactions/index.tsx` filters by reference and status and opens two
+components:
+
+### Wire inspector
+
+`components/WireInspectorDrawer.tsx` loads
+`GET /portal-api/transactions/:id` and shows:
+
+- our reference, provider reference, rail, status and amount;
+- expected OTP and pinned failure phase/mode;
+- step events with method/path, response status, injected fault and the first
+  400 characters of the raw request and response;
+- webhook deliveries with state, signature-valid flag and response status.
+
+It does not show the full header set, the complete raw body, the canonical
+string used for HMAC, or the signature recipe. The backend stores those raw
+values, but this drawer is deliberately compact.
+
+### Webhook composer
+
+`components/WebhookComposerModal.tsx` fires
+`POST /portal-api/webhooks/:transactionId/fire` with:
+
+- event (`payment.paid`, `payment.failed`, `payment.refunded`,
+  `transaction.pending`, `DISPUTE_OPENED`);
+- delay in seconds;
+- duplicate count;
+- forged-signature switch (100 percent corrupt chance);
+- PENDING-after-PAID switch.
+
+It can also open a dispute (`POST /portal-api/webhooks/:transactionId/dispute`).
+Replay and send-now exist only on the portal API, not in this UI.
+
+## 6. Chaos controls
+
+`pages/chaos-matrix/index.tsx` loads `GET /portal-api/scenarios`, renders one
+`RailChaosCard` per descriptor and offers global presets:
+
+- Reset all rails (`healthy`);
+- National switch instability (`flaky`, 25 percent);
+- Timeout on confirm;
+- Full outage.
+
+Each card saves `PUT /portal-api/scenarios/:railCode` and can apply per-rail
+presets (`healthy`, `flaky`, `timeout_on_confirm`, `outage`).
+
+The card exposes:
+
+- enabled/outage state;
+- overall failure chance;
+- latency minimum and maximum;
+- one primary failure mode (sets that mode to weight 100 and all others to 0);
+- duplicate webhooks (3 copies when enabled, otherwise 1);
+- out-of-order PENDING after PAID;
+- corrupt-signature chance.
+
+The full `phaseBreakdown`, individual failure-mode weights, webhook delay and
+`autoApproveAsyncAfterSec` are not edited in this UI. The save request carries
+the existing phase/mode objects through, so raw API calls are still required for
+fine-grained weights. The backend never schedules async auto-approval.
+
+## 7. Hosted flows
+
+### Redirect checkout
+
+`/hosted/redirect/:sessionId` loads the public
+`GET /portal-api/hosted/session/:id`. It displays the rail name, merchant
+reference, amount, currency and status, then offers test actions:
+
+| Action | Server effect | Browser effect |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| Approve & redirect | `PAID` plus paid webhook | Redirects to `return_url`. |
+| Approve with tampered return URL | `PAID` plus paid webhook | Redirects with `status=failed&amount=0.01`. |
+| Browser return only, drop webhook | Leaves `AWAITING_ACTION` | Redirects to `return_url`. |
+| Close tab / abandon | Leaves `AWAITING_ACTION`, sends paid webhook after 30 seconds | Redirects to `return_url`. |
+| Decline | `FAILED` plus failure webhook | Redirects to `cancel_url`. |
+| Customer cancel | `CANCELLED` | Redirects to `cancel_url`. |
+
+These actions are public by design because the payer is not a tester.
+
+### Embedded widget frame
+
+`/hosted/widget-frame` reads `MerchantReference`/`merchant_reference`/
+`reference`/`our_reference`/`merchantTransInfo`, `AmountTrxn`/`amount` and
+`rail` from the query string. It emulates a sandbox card page and posts:
+
+- `fake-rails:complete` (with `PAID`);
+- `fake-rails:error`;
+- `fake-rails:cancel`.
+
+"Complete card payment" calls the hosted approve action when a reference is
+present. "Spoof browser callback without server payment" deliberately posts a
+success without changing server state, so the checkout spoof tests can run. The
+frame posts to `window.parent` with `targetOrigin="*"`.
+
+The generated `/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js` and `/sdk/mpgs-session.js` scripts open
+this frame. Checkout's renderer allowlist and CSP currently block the fake SDK
+origin, so the embedded flow is not usable end to end in the real checkout.
+
+## 8. Statements
+
+`pages/statements/index.tsx` posts to
+`POST /portal-api/statements/generate` and downloads the result:
+
+- gateway selector (the UI lists the descriptor URLs `ly_pay` and `evopay`, not
+  the seeded core codes `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay`);
+- date window;
+- CSV, XLSX or JSON;
+- fee variance percentage with a fixed +0.150 LYD adjustment;
+- omit one line;
+- add one unrecorded line.
+
+The recent-statements table reads `GET /portal-api/statements`. Generation is
+download-only; it does not push a statement into core reconciliation.
+
+## 9. Environment and build
+
+The only frontend build/runtime input is:
+
+| Key | Default | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `VITE_FAKE_RAILS_API` | `http://127.0.0.1:4104` | Dev-server proxy target. |
+
+`vite.config.ts` also proxies `/portal-api`, `/rails`, `/sdk` and `/hosted`.
+The dev server listens on port `5104`. The build has no runtime-config file; a
+change to the API target requires a rebuild. In deployment the app is served by
+the Fake Rails Nginx vhost, which proxies to `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT`.
+
+Commands:
+
+```bash
+cd fake-rails-front
+bun install
+bun run dev        # Vite dev server on :5104
+bun run build      # production dist/
+bun run preview    # preview the build
+bun run type-check # vue-tsc --build
+```
+
+The deployment engine builds this SPA when `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true` and copies
+`dist` into the release.
+
+## 10. Tests
+
+There is no frontend unit-test script or component test suite in this workspace.
+Coverage comes from:
+
+- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/exhaustive-fake-rails-surface.spec.ts`, which visits
+  `/login` across three viewports, two locales and two themes, mocks every portal
+  API and asserts shell geometry, no `#app` transform and no horizontal
+  overflow;
+- the backend suites in `fake-rails-back/test/**`, which exercise the portal API
+  behind these pages.
+
+The Playwright suite does not exercise the dashboard, live SSE feed, chaos
+matrix, transaction inspector, statements or hosted pages.
+
+## 11. Known gaps
+
+- The only e2e coverage is login geometry with mocked APIs; there is no real
+  backend/frontend journey suite.
+- No i18n/Arabic catalogue or theme switcher; the portal is fixed English and
+  fixed theme.
+- No runtime configuration; `VITE_FAKE_RAILS_API` is baked at build time.
+- The chaos UI does not expose per-phase weights, per-mode weights, webhook
+  delay, auto-approval or the full scenario object. Those require the raw API.
+- Webhook replay and send-now are API-only; the UI can fire and dispute.
+- The wire inspector truncates raw bodies and does not show the canonical
+  signing string or signature recipe.
+- The statement gateway options use `ly_pay`/`evopay` while seeded core

+- Hosted pages are public and can approve without payment. The widget frame

+- The SSE stream loses events on reconnect and carries the JWT in the query

+- The embedded widget cannot load under the checkout CSP/renderer allowlist, and

+- The SPA has no frontend test runner, no visual regression suite and no

+# fake-rails-front blueprint
+
+Generated from: `fake-rails.chaos`, `fake-rails.integration`.
+
+## Fake Rails Chaos Engine and Tester Portal
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part covers the deterministic and probabilistic failure engine, the SQLite state it owns, outbound webhook anomalies, settlement-statement generation, the tester portal API and the `fake-rails-front` SPA.
+
+It does not cover the backend process model (`fake-rails.backend`), the route matrix (`fake-rails.protocol`) or the core seeding/deploy wiring (`fake-rails.integration`).
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The design requires a tester to answer four questions at any moment:
+
+1. What did the gateway receive and return?
+2. Is this rail healthy, flaky, delayed or completely down?
+3. If it fails, how and in which phase does it fail?
+4. Can the tester force a specific outcome, replay a webhook, forge a signature or generate an anomalous statement?
+
+The intended failure controls are:
+
+- A per-rail `overallFailureChancePercent` from 0 to 100.
+- Weighted phase choice across `INITIATE`, `SUBMIT`, `VERIFY`, `WEBHOOK` and `REFUND`.
+- Weighted failure modes: insufficient funds, customer ceiling, wrong OTP, HTTP 500, timeout/hang, socket reset, malformed 200 body, HTTP 429, amount mismatch and conflicting webhook versus inquiry.
+- Latency range.
+- Async auto-approval after N seconds.
+- Webhook delay, duplicate count, out-of-order PENDING-after-PAID and corrupt-signature chance.
+
+The intended portal has a live SSE feed, an OTP/action banner, a pending-action queue, a transaction/wire inspector, a chaos matrix, a statement generator and hosted redirect/widget pages.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Scenario model
+
+`engine/chaos/DefaultRailScenarios.ts` defines:
+
+```ts
+interface RailChaosScenarioConfig {
+  railCode: string;
+  gatewayCode: string;
+  enabled: boolean;
+  overallFailureChancePercent: number;
+  phaseBreakdown: {
+    initiateFailWeight: number;
+    submitFailWeight: number;
+    verifyFailWeight: number;
+    webhookFailWeight: number;
+    refundFailWeight: number;
+  };
+  failureModeWeights: Record<FailureMode, number>;
+  latencyMs: { min: number; max: number };
+  autoApproveAsyncAfterSec: number | null;
+  webhookBehavior: {
+    delaySeconds: number;
+    duplicateCount: number;
+    outOfOrderPendingAfterPaid: boolean;
+    corruptSignatureChancePercent: number;
+  };
+}
+```
+
+The healthy baseline is `enabled=true`, `overallFailureChancePercent=0`, latency 40-250 ms, one webhook copy and no corruption. `defaultScenario()` gives one configuration per descriptor. Defaults are inserted into `fake_rail_scenarios` on first access.
+
+`FailureMode` has ten values exactly matching the design. `FailPhase` has five values (`INITIATE`, `SUBMIT`, `VERIFY`, `WEBHOOK`, `REFUND`). The core's ten declarative phases are not the same type.
+
+### 3.2 Deterministic PRNG
+
+`engine/chaos/prng.ts` implements mulberry32 plus FNV-1a string hashing, `int`, `pick`, `chance(percent)` and `weighted(record)`. A scenario seed is `${railCode}:${reference}` for transaction fate and `${transactionId}:${phase}` for latency, so repeated runs with the same reference are reproducible.
+
+### 3.3 Evaluation priority
+
+`ChaosEvaluator.evaluate()` applies this order:
+
+1. **Magic input** in the current phase. It wins over everything.
+2. **Disabled rail.** `enabled=false` produces `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` with source `OUTAGE`; `applyFault` maps that source to HTTP 503.
+3. **Pinned transaction fate.** When the transaction row has `assigned_failure_mode` and `assigned_fail_phase` equal to the current phase.
+4. **No failure.**
+
+`assignFate()` runs once when a new transaction row is created. It rolls `overallFailureChancePercent`; if it fails, it samples a phase from `phaseBreakdown` and a mode from `failureModeWeights`, then persists both on `fake_transactions`.
+
+### 3.4 Magic inputs
+
+`detectMagicTrigger()` flattens body values and the raw body text, then checks:
+
+| Trigger | Failure mode | Phase |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| OTP `000000` or `0000` | `WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE` | `SUBMIT` |
+| OTP `999999` | `TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | `SUBMIT` |
+| OTP `500500` | `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` | `SUBMIT` |
+| OTP `408408` | `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL` | `SUBMIT` |
+| Phone ending `9901` | `TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | `SUBMIT` |
+| Phone ending `9902` | `LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CUSTOMER_CEILING` | `SUBMIT` |
+| Phone ending `9905` | `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` | `SUBMIT` |
+| Phone ending `9906` | `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL` | `SUBMIT` |
+| Phone ending `9907` | `MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY` | `SUBMIT` |
+
+OTP detection is exact per flattened value and also regex-scans the joined text. Phone detection strips non-digits and checks the suffix.
+
+### 3.5 Fault application
+
+`api/rails/common.ts` splits faults into hard transport faults and business faults.
+
+Hard faults (`applyFault`):
+
+- `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL`: sleeps `FAKE_RAILS_TIMEOUT_HANG_MS` (default 20,000 ms) then returns 504.
+- `SOCKET_RESET_MID_STREAM`: destroys the socket and returns a 499 sentinel without recording a response.
+- `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT`: 503 for outage, 500 otherwise.
+- `RATE_LIMIT_HTTP_429`: 429.
+- `MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY`: 200 with `{ unexpected_schema: true, data: null, code: "??" }`.
+
+Business faults (`finalizeFault`):
+
+- `TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: row `FAILED`, failure body.
+- `LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CUSTOMER_CEILING`: row `FAILED`, limit body.
+- `WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE`: row `AWAITING_ACTION`, retryable response.
+- `AMOUNT_ROUNDING_MISMATCH`: row `PAID`, settled amount +0.05.
+- `CONFLICTING_WEBHOOK_VS_INQUIRY`: row `PAID`, inquiry override `FAILED`, success webhook fired.
+
+Latency is drawn from the scenario range using `latencyFor()` and awaited before the handler.
+
+### 3.6 Scenario persistence and API
+
+`engine/chaos/scenarioStore.ts` stores the full config as JSON in `fake_rail_scenarios`, keyed by canonical rail code. `listScenarios()`, `getScenario()`, `saveScenario()` and `resetAllScenarios()` keep the config in sync with the descriptor list.
+
+Portal endpoints in `api/portal/scenarios.ts`:
+
+| Method | Path | Behaviour |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `GET` | `/portal-api/scenarios` | Returns descriptors and all scenarios |
+| `GET` | `/portal-api/scenarios/:railCode` | One scenario |
+| `PUT` | `/portal-api/scenarios/:railCode` | Merge a partial patch and persist |
+| `POST` | `/portal-api/scenarios/preset/:railCode/:preset` | Apply one preset |
+| `POST` | `/portal-api/scenarios/global/:preset` | Apply to all rails |
+| `POST` | `/portal-api/scenarios/reset` | Restore defaults |
+| `GET` | `/portal-api/scenarios/:railCode/audit` | Read portal audit rows for the rail |
+
+Presets are `healthy`, `flaky` (25 percent), `timeout_on_confirm` (100 percent submit timeout) and `outage` (`enabled=false`). Global preset application iterates every descriptor.
+
+### 3.7 Outbound webhook anomalies
+
+`engine/webhooks/WebhookDispatcher.ts` persists every delivery in `fake_webhook_deliveries` before scheduling it. It supports:
+
+- `delaySeconds` before the first attempt.
+- `duplicateCount` 1-5 copies.
+- `outOfOrderPendingAfterPaid`: after a paid/success/captured event, queue a `transaction.pending` copy two seconds later.
+- `corruptSignatureChancePercent`: use a tampered secret for the signature.
+
+Signature profiles exist for `dpay` (timestamp dot raw body, hex lower), `mypay` (raw body, hex lower), `ly_pay` (sorted key/value, hex upper), `plutu` (sorted values, hex upper), `moamalat` (sorted key/value with hex-decoded secret) and `mpgs` (raw body). Every other gateway uses a generic sorted-key/value HMAC-SHA256 profile.
+
+Delivery semantics:
+
+- Timeout is `FAKE_RAILS_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS`.
+- `ok` responses move to `SENT`.
+- Failures retry with exponential backoff `1s, 2s, 4s` up to three attempts, then `FAILED`.
+- Queued deliveries are resumed on process start.
+- `replay(deliveryId, tamper)` resets state and optionally forges every signature-like header.
+- The dispatcher emits `webhook.queued`, `webhook.sent` and `webhook.failed` to the SSE sink.
+
+The default URL construction has a path bug documented in `fake-rails.protocol`.
+
+### 3.8 Statement generation
+
+`api/portal/statements.ts` and `engine/statements/xlsx.ts` implement the tester statement generator.
+
+Inputs: `gatewayCode`, optional `from`/`to`, `format` (`csv`, `json`, `xlsx`) and anomalies:
+
+- `feeVariancePercent` 0-100 with `feeVarianceAmount` added to matching rows.
+- `omitOne`: drop the last line.
+- `addUnrecorded`: append a synthetic `UNRECORDED-<timestamp>` line.
+
+The generator filters `PAID`, `SUCCEEDED`, `REFUNDED` and `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` rows, writes a `fake_statements` metadata row, broadcasts `statement.generated` and returns CSV, JSON or a dependency-free XLSX built from store-only ZIP parts and OOXML.
+
+This is a download generator. It does not push the file to `core-back`, and the core reconciliation path remains an admin upload.
+
+### 3.9 Tester portal API
+
+| Router | Endpoints | Notes |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `transactions.ts` | list, stream, summary, detail, action, events | Actions: `APPROVE`, `REJECT`, `APPROVE_MISMATCH`, `APPROVE_LATE`, `FORCE_OUTCOME`, `CANCEL` |
+| `scenarios.ts` | list/get/put/presets/reset/audit | Full config persisted |
+| `webhooks.ts` | list, fire, replay, send-now, dispute | Fire accepts delay/duplicates/out-of-order/corruption |
+| `statements.ts` | list, generate | CSV/JSON/XLSX |
+| `seederSync.ts` | handshake, bulk seed | Shared seeder token |
+| `hosted.ts` | session read, session action | Public hosted flow |
+
+`transactions.ts` writes `fake_portal_audit` for actions and broadcasts `transaction.action`. `summary` returns grouped status counts, per-rail counts and up to fifty pending actions. The `sseClients` field is currently `undefined`.
+
+Hosted actions are `APPROVE`, `APPROVE_TAMPERED`, `DROP_WEBHOOK`, `ABANDON`, `DECLINE` and `CANCEL`:
+
+- `APPROVE` sets `PAID` and fires a webhook.
+- `APPROVE_TAMPERED` sets `PAID`, fires a webhook, then appends `status=failed&amount=0.01` to the redirect.
+- `DROP_WEBHOOK` leaves the row awaiting action and fires nothing.
+- `ABANDON` fires a paid webhook after 30 seconds while leaving the row awaiting action.
+- `DECLINE` sets `FAILED`, fires a failure webhook and redirects to `cancel_url`.
+- `CANCEL` sets `CANCELLED` and redirects to `cancel_url`.
+
+The hosted router is public by design because the payer is not a tester.
+
+### 3.10 SSE
+
+The only stream is `GET /portal-api/transactions/stream`, authenticated by a query-string JWT because `EventSource` cannot set headers. It emits `ready`, `rail.request`, `webhook.queued`, `webhook.sent`, `webhook.failed`, `transaction.action`, `scenario.updated`, `scenario.reset`, `statement.generated`, `hosted.action`, `seeder.bulk` and `webhook.replayed`.
+
+There is no per-replay cursor. A reconnecting client loses events that occurred while disconnected.
+
+### 3.11 Tester SPA
+
+`fake-rails-front/src/router/index.ts` defines seven routes:
+
+| Route | Page | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `/login` | `pages/login/index.tsx` | Single tester login |
+| `/dashboard` | `pages/dashboard/index.tsx` | KPIs, live feed, pending actions |
+| `/transactions` | `pages/transactions/index.tsx` | Filter, inspect, compose webhooks |
+| `/chaos-matrix` | `pages/chaos-matrix/index.tsx` | Per-rail cards and global presets |
+| `/statements` | `pages/statements/index.tsx` | Generate CSV/XLSX/JSON with anomalies |
+| `/hosted/redirect/:sessionId` | `pages/hosted/redirect/[sessionId].tsx` | Interactive hosted checkout |
+| `/hosted/widget-frame` | `pages/hosted/widget-frame.tsx` | Moamalat/MPGS iframe content |
+
+The router guard redirects unauthenticated non-hosted routes to `/login` and keeps the attempted path in `?redirect=`. Tokens live in `localStorage` under `fake-rails-token` and user info under `fake-rails-user`.
+
+The portal layout has four navigation links and an environment badge. `LiveTransactionFeed` opens the SSE stream with the query token and listens for a subset of event names. `WireInspectorDrawer` shows transaction fields, step events and webhook deliveries. `WebhookComposerModal` fires or disputes a webhook. `RailChaosCard` edits failure chance, latency, primary failure mode, duplicates, out-of-order and corruption.
+
+The SPA is fixed to the portal shell's language and theme; it does not have the admin/merchant i18n catalogue. `tests/e2e/exhaustive/exhaustive-fake-rails-surface.spec.ts` only visits `/login` across three viewports, two locales and two themes while mocking every portal API; it asserts shell geometry, no `#app` transform and no horizontal overflow.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **Scenario state is durable.** Every scenario update survives a restart because it is written to SQLite.
+2. **Failure fate is pinned per transaction.** A transaction that is assigned a `SUBMIT` timeout will not fail at `INITIATE`.
+3. **Magic inputs are phase-scoped.** The trigger is ignored when its phase differs from the current route phase.
+4. **Disabled means outage.** `enabled=false` always yields the 503 outage path.
+5. **Webhook delivery is at-least-once with bounded retries.** Duplicates and tampering are deliberate test features.
+6. **Hosted approval is a tester action, not a trusted payment signal.** The core must still verify any resulting webhook or inquiry.
+7. **Statement anomalies are deterministic for a given window.** `feeVariancePercent` uses a PRNG seeded by gateway and window.
+8. **The portal never claims to be a real switch.** It is a test surface and must remain isolated.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+- Scenario fields and failure modes: `DefaultRailScenarios.ts`.
+- Magic triggers, fate assignment, latency: `ChaosEvaluator.ts`.
+- Persistent config: `scenarioStore.ts` plus `fake_rail_scenarios`.
+- Webhook queue and signature profiles: `WebhookDispatcher.ts`.
+- Statement generator: `api/portal/statements.ts`, `engine/statements/xlsx.ts`.
+- Portal routes: `api/portal/**`.
+- SPA routes and components: `fake-rails-front/src/**`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+```bash
+# Global healthy reset
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4104/portal-api/scenarios/global/healthy \
+  -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
+
+# Make Edfali time out on confirm
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4104/portal-api/scenarios/preset/edfali/timeout_on_confirm \
+  -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
+
+# Fire three copies of a paid webhook
+curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4104/portal-api/webhooks/$TX_ID/fire \
+  -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
+  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
+  -d '{"event":"payment.paid","duplicateCount":3}'
+```
+
+- Use the transaction detail endpoint before replaying a webhook so the target URL and signature profile are known.
+- Reset all scenarios after a chaos test. The default row persists otherwise.
+- The hosted page is intentionally public; do not expose the portal port outside the test network.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Ten failure modes, probability assignment, pinned fate, magic triggers and latency.
+- SQLite-backed scenario store and four presets.
+- Webhook delay, duplicates, out-of-order PENDING and corrupt signatures.
+- Webhook replay, tamper, send-now and dispute.
+- CSV/JSON/XLSX statement generation with fee variance, omission and unrecorded-line anomalies.
+- Seven-route tester SPA with SSE feed, pending actions, wire inspector and hosted pages.
+- Portal audit rows for transaction actions.
+
+### Partial
+
+- `autoApproveAsyncAfterSec` is dead.
+- The UI exposes failure chance and a single primary failure mode; the full `phaseBreakdown` and all mode weights can only be changed through the raw API.
+- The webhook dispatcher does not consult `assignedFailPhase=WEBHOOK` or mode weights; webhook anomalies are controlled separately.
+- The dashboard's `sseClients` field is `undefined`; there is no connection count.
+- Statement generation is download-only and not linked to core reconciliation.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- Timer-driven async auto-approval.
+- Per-phase UI weight controls.
+- SSE replay/resume and multi-instance event fan-out.
+- Server-side statement push to `core-back`.
+- A real protocol-level chaos matrix (the portal edits scenario config rather than individual gateway wire failures).
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Code gap:** the tester can approve a transaction with no server-side payment, which is intentional for spoof testing but must never be reachable from an untrusted network.
+- **Code gap:** `ABANDON` leaves the row in `AWAITING_ACTION` while a paid webhook is sent after 30 seconds, producing a deliberate state conflict.
+- **Code gap:** the query-string JWT is visible to access logs and browser history.
+- **Documentation gap:** the design describes a 20-rail phase-perfect chaos matrix; the implementation is a smaller generic chaos layer.
+
+## 8. Verification and tests
+
+- `fake-rails-back/test/chaos.test.ts` (7 tests) covers descriptor count, aliases, magic OTP/phone triggers, reproducible fate, zero-percent health, magic-over-pinned priority, outage and PRNG determinism.

+## Core Integration and Deployment
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part describes how `core-back`, the synthetic seeder and `deploy/` connect to the fake rails tier:
+
+- `seedFakeRails.ts` rewrites gateway environments, widget definitions, webhook channel tokens and credential secrets.
+- The scoped SSRF allowlist permits a private fake rails host without opening private-address SSRF generally.
+- The synthetic seeder requires fake rails and performs a handshake plus bulk sync.
+- The deploy engine plans a sixth `fake-rails` role, generates a certificate, opens the portal port, renders an Nginx vhost and optionally seeds the blueprints.
+- The checkout frontend must be able to load the fake widget scripts and message origins.
+
+It does not document the emulator internals (`fake-rails.backend`), the rail protocol (`fake-rails.protocol`) or the tester portal (`fake-rails.chaos`).
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The integration is designed to make the platform work out of the box with the emulator:
+
+1. Every seeded gateway environment gets a base URL of `${FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/rails/<gateway_code>` and an `allowed_hosts` entry for the fake host.
+2. Moamalat and MPGS widget definitions load the emulator's SDK scripts.
+3. Inbound-verify crypto secrets are derived from a shared seeder token, so signatures produced by the emulator verify with real cryptography and no bypassed checks.
+4. `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS` relaxes the private-IP guard only when the target host is in both `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` and the gateway version's own `allowed_hosts`.
+5. The deployment engine adds an optional `fake-rails` host role with its own backend port, Nginx port, TLS mode, certificate SAN, firewall scope and PM2 process.
+6. The synthetic seeder refuses to run unless it is a declared test server, fake rails is enabled, production is explicitly opted in, every gateway host is fake, and the handshake succeeds.
+7. The synthetic seeder bulk-syncs its historical transactions and step events into the emulator so the tester portal shows the same history as the gateway.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 `seedFakeRails.ts`
+
+`core-back/prisma/seedFakeRails.ts` requires `FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN`. It then runs four update passes and one setting upsert.
+
+**Environments.** `updateEnvironments()` loads every `gatewayVersion` with its gateway and environments. For each environment:
+
+- It reads existing `baseUrls` and preserves the keys (or uses `api`).
+- It sets every key to `${FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/rails/${gateway.code}`.
+- It unions the environment's existing `allowedHosts` with the fake base host, optional `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`.
+- It sets `enabled=true`.
+
+**Widgets.** `updateWidgets()` loads widget definitions through their route and gateway. For `moamalat` and `mpgs` it sets:
+
+- `scriptUrls = [<base>/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js]` or `[<base>/sdk/mpgs-session.js]`.
+- `scriptSriHashes = []`.
+- `allowedOrigins = [<base>]`.
+
+No other widget is changed.
+
+**Webhook channels.** `updateWebhookChannels()` scans `confirmationChannel` rows of type `WEBHOOK`. The first channel per gateway code receives `pathToken = ${code}-webhook`; later versions keep the existing token. It does not change the channel's verification method, signature header, IP allowlist or crypto-profile reference.
+
+**Credential secrets.** `updateCredentialSecrets()` returns zero if the seeder token is empty. Otherwise, for every `PLATFORM` credential set, it walks existing entries. When an entry key matches a crypto profile `secretKeyRef`, it derives:
+
+```text
+HMAC-SHA256(seederToken, "fake-rails:<gatewayCode>:<purpose>")
+```
+
+where purpose is `webhook` if any matching profile is `INBOUND_VERIFY`, otherwise `sign`. The derived secret is encrypted through `Vault.encryptSecret(secret, "credential-set")`, the entry is marked secret and its `secretVersion` is incremented. Entries with no matching profile are left untouched. The credential set is marked `VERIFIED`.
+
+**Environment mode.** `ensureEnvironmentSetting()` upserts `server.environment_mode = { mode: "TEST_SANDBOX" }`.
+
+The script prints environment, widget, channel and credential counts and exits non-zero if the token is missing.
+
+### 3.2 Seeded gateway count
+
+`core-back/prisma/seedBlueprints.ts` creates thirteen distinct gateway codes:
+
+`edfali`, `sadad`, `moamalat`, `cbl_lypay`, `mypay`, `tlync`, `mobicash`, `onepay`, `yussor`, `sahara`, `mpgs`, `evo_pay`, `neompay`.
+
+The fake descriptor catalogue has twenty rail codes. Seven fake descriptors have no core gateway blueprint:
+
+- `dpay`
+- `plutu`
+- `masrefy`
+- `hawelli`
+- `gpay_libya`
+- `numo_pay`
+- `libyana`
+
+Conversely, the core uses `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay`, while the fake routes use `ly_pay` and `evopay`. The counts therefore agree only in spirit: 13 core gateways versus 20 fake descriptors, with two code mismatches inside the overlap.
+
+### 3.3 Scoped SSRF allowlist
+
+`core-back/engine/apiConsumer/fakeRailsAllowlist.ts` implements `isFakeRailsHostAllowed(hostname, gatewayAllowedHosts)`:
+
+1. `env.ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS` must be `true`.
+2. The normalized hostname must appear in `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
+3. The same hostname must appear in the caller's `gatewayAllowedHosts`.
+4. Trailing dots are stripped; comparison is lowercase.
+
+`ApiConsumer.ts` and `StepExecutor.ts` call this check before URL validation. When true, `requireHttps` is set to false, allowing the private/loopback fake host over plain HTTP. The general SSRF guard still rejects `169.254.169.254`, unrelated private addresses, redirects, userinfo, fragments, CRLF and path traversal.
+
+The allowlist test proves:
+
+- Closed unless explicitly enabled.
+- Both environment and gateway list must match.
+- An empty gateway list never matches.
+- A metadata address is refused even if listed.
+
+### 3.4 Synthetic seeder integration
+
+`core-back/prisma/syntheticSeeder/SeederSafetyGate.ts` enforces five gates:
+
+1. `IS_TEST_SERVER=true`.
+2. `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true` and a public base URL.
+3. Production requires `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`.
+4. At least one allowed host; every configured gateway environment URL must point at an allowed fake host, not an external host or metadata address.
+5. The `POST /portal-api/internal/seeder-handshake` call must succeed with the seeder token.
+
+`sync/fakeRailsBulkSyncClient.ts` posts transactions and step events to `/portal-api/internal/bulk-seed` with `x-fake-rails-seeder-token`. The emulator inserts both batches in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and broadcasts `seeder.bulk`.
+
+### 3.5 Deployment configuration
+
+`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` defines the fake rails keys and validates:
+
+- Host, key path and private IP when enabled.
+- Tester username/password/JWT/seeder token.
+- Production opt-in.
+- Password length and non-collision of backend/Nginx ports with every other role and public port.
+- `RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED` requires an enabled test server and fake rails.
+
+`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` maps the role to:
+
+- Service `pg-fake-rails-back`, source `fake-rails-back`, port `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT`.
+- Environment with `NODE_ENV`, `HOST`, `PORT`, `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED`, `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION`, public base URL, data directory, admin credentials, secrets, CIDRs and `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL`.
+- Nginx site `fake-rails` on `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` with `FAKE_RAILS_SSL`, domain, certificate paths and static root `current/fake-rails-front/dist`.
+- Certificate bundle `fake-rails-server`.
+- Firewall rules for SSH and the portal port restricted to `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` plus core/checkout private IPs.
+
+`deploy/lib/pkiManager.ts` includes `fakeRails` in the PKI bundle with SAN `DNS:<domain>`, `IP:<private-ip>` and `IP:127.0.0.1`. `deploy/deploy.ts` builds the SPA, deploys backend plus `dist`, renders the vhost and optionally runs `bun run seed-fake-rails` on the core host.
+
+`deploy/templates/nginx.fakerails.conf.tpl` proxies `/rails`, `/sdk`, `/portal-api` and `/hosted` to the backend and serves the SPA. Its CSP allows `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` and `frame-ancestors 'self' *`.
+
+### 3.6 Embedded widget and CSP block
+
+The embedded flow cannot currently load the emulator widget end to end:
+
+1. `checkout-front/src/components/renderers/EmbeddedWidgetRenderer.tsx` hard-codes `SCRIPT_ALLOWLIST_HOSTS` to public HTTPS partners (`payments.moamalat.ly`, `secure.moamalat.ly`, `test.mpgmerchant.test`, `pay.evowallet.net`, `js.numo-pay.com`). A fake URL such as `http://127.0.0.1:8444/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js` fails `isAllowlistedScript()` for both protocol and host.
+2. Even if the renderer allowed it, the checkout Nginx templates set `script-src 'self'` with no fake origin.
+3. The seeded widget `cspAdditions` remain `frame-src https://*.moamalat.example.ly` and `frame-src https://*.mpgs.example.ly`; `seedFakeRails.ts` does not rewrite them.
+4. `seedFakeRails.ts` writes an empty SRI array, so `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` cannot apply an integrity hash.
+
+The redirect flow is unaffected because it uses a browser navigation to the hosted URL, subject to the checkout redirect allowlist.
+
+### 3.7 Webhook and callback gaps
+
+- **Wrong path.** `WebhookDispatcher.defaultUrlFor()` inserts `/webhook/` between the inbound base and `:gateway`, while the checkout route is `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`.
+- **Token mismatch.** The default token is `${gateway_code}-webhook`. Blueprint tokens are not uniformly that string (for example `cbl-lypay-webhook`); `seedFakeRails.ts` rewrites the first webhook channel per code to `${code}-webhook`, so the default works only after that pass and only for the rewritten channel.
+- **No fake-side verification.** The emulator signs outbound webhooks but never verifies core-originated requests.
+- **Credential coverage.** `updateCredentialSecrets()` only updates existing credential entries whose key matches a crypto profile. A gateway with no secret entry or a different key shape remains unconfigured.
+- **Crypto-profile mismatch.** The emulator has six explicit webhook signature profiles plus a generic fallback. `evo_pay`'s blueprint declares RSA-SHA256 with a private key, but the fake profile for `evo_pay` is not defined, so it falls back to HMAC.
+- **Statement channels.** The core seeds statement channel rows with `<code>-statement` tokens but has no `SETTLEMENT_FETCH` flow and no fetch URL. The fake `/statement` endpoint is not consumed automatically.
+
+### 3.8 Deploy environment keys
+
+| Key | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED` | Build and deploy the tier |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION` | Explicit production opt-in |
+| `IS_TEST_SERVER` | Enables fake rails and synthetic seeding |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_SSH_HOST` / `_PORT` / `_USER` / `_KEY_PATH` / `_SUDO_PASSWORD` | Host access |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP` | Internal address and SAN |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT` | Express port, default 4104 |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` | Public portal/API port, default 8444 |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_SSL` / `_SSL_MODE` / `_DOMAIN` | TLS and vhost identity |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Rewritten into gateway base URLs |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_REMOTE_DIR` | Release and data root |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` | Firewall and service CIDR contract |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Scoped SSRF allowlist |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER` / `_PASSWORD` | Tester login |
+| `FAKE_RAILS_JWT_SECRET` / `_SEEDER_TOKEN` | Signing and seeder auth |
+| `SEED_FAKE_RAILS_BLUEPRINTS` | Run `seed-fake-rails` after deploy |
+
+`deploy/deploy.env.example` keeps `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="false"` by default. The example sets `FAKE_RAILS_SSL="false"` and an HTTP public base URL; enabling TLS requires staging verification.
+
+### 3.9 Local all-in-one path
+
+`scripts/deploy-localhost.sh` reads `deploy/deploy.env` when present, otherwise uses local defaults. It starts:
+
+- `pg-fake-rails-back` on port 4104 with `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`.
+- `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4103/api/v1/inbound`.
+- `FAKE_RAILS_DATA_DIR` under `.local/fake-rails-data` unless a deployed data directory exists.
+- `pg-fake-rails-front` preview on 5104.
+
+It then runs `seedFakeRails.ts` with `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=127.0.0.1,localhost`.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **The SSRF relaxation is triple-gated.** Environment flag, environment host list and gateway host list must all agree.
+2. **The fake host never becomes a general private-address exception.** Metadata and unrelated private ranges remain blocked.
+3. **Derived secrets must match on both sides.** Both implementations hash `fake-rails:<gatewayCode>:<purpose>` with the seeder token.
+4. **Seeded environments are enabled and point only at the fake base URL.** The pass overwrites every existing base-url key.
+5. **The synthetic seeder cannot run against real gateways.** Gate 4 rejects any non-fake host.
+6. **Deployment production mode requires an explicit opt-in at both config and process level.**
+7. **The fake rails host exposes only its portal/Nginx port.** Backend port stays loopback.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+- Core seeding: `seedFakeRails.ts`, `seedBlueprints.ts`.
+- Core URL validation: `fakeRailsAllowlist.ts`, `ApiConsumer.ts`, `StepExecutor.ts`.
+- Core seeder gate: `SeederSafetyGate.ts`, `fakeRailsBulkSyncClient.ts`.
+- Deploy schema/planner: `configSchema.ts`, `hostPlanner.ts`.
+- Deploy PKI/firewall: `pkiManager.ts`, `firewallConfigurator.ts`.
+- Deploy pipeline/template: `deploy.ts`, `templates/nginx.fakerails.conf.tpl`.
+- Checkout renderer: `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer.tsx`.
+- Local stack: `scripts/deploy-localhost.sh`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+```bash
+# Seed the fake gateway catalog in core-back
+cd core-back
+FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8444 \
+FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN='0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef' \
+FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=127.0.0.1,localhost \
+bun run seed-fake-rails
+
+# Check the scoped allowlist test
+bun test test/fake-rails-allowlist.test.ts
+
+# Deploy only the fake rails role
+cd deploy
+bun run deploy.ts --only=fake-rails
+```
+
+- If the seeded base URL is wrong, rerun `seed-fake-rails`; it overwrites existing keys.
+- If core cannot reach fake rails, check `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS`, both host lists and the gateway environment's `allowed_hosts`.
+- If the embedded widget does not load, inspect the checkout CSP, the renderer allowlist and `cspAdditions` before debugging the emulator.
+- If the seeder blocks, read the gate name in the error; each gate has a stable prefix.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- `seedFakeRails.ts` updates environments, widget URLs, webhook tokens and existing credential secrets.
+- Deterministic HMAC secret derivation shared by both sides.
+- Triple-gated SSRF allowlist with tests.
+- Five synthetic-seeder safety gates.
+- Deploy schema, host planning, certificate SAN, firewall rules, Nginx template and optional seeding.
+- Local all-in-one script that starts and seeds the emulator.
+
+### Partial
+
+- Thirteen seeded core gateways versus twenty fake descriptors.
+- `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay` URL mismatches.
+- Webhook token/path mismatch.
+- Embedded widget blocked by CSP and renderer allowlist.
+- Credential coverage only updates existing entries.
+- Fake inbound requests are not verified.
+- Statement channels not connected to a fetch flow.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- Core blueprints for the seven unseeded fake rails.
+- Automatic reconciliation pull from `/rails/:gateway/statement`.
+- SRI generation and propagation for fake SDK scripts.
+- A deployment smoke test that performs a full initiate/confirm/webhook flow through a seeded gateway.
+- TLS verification of the fake rails certificate from core in the local script.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Code bug:** `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay` cannot call their fake URLs.
+- **Code bug:** default webhook URL path is invalid.
+- **Code bug:** embedded widget loads are filtered out before CSP is even evaluated.
+- **Security risk:** `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS=true` plus a broad `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` value weakens SSRF protection for every gateway that also lists the host. Keep the list to the fake host only.
+- **Deployment risk:** the example uses HTTP; enabling HTTPS requires certificate trust in core.
+

+## 1. Purpose and boundaries
 
-Portal API, mounted under `/api/v1/merchant`:
+`merchant-back` owns:
 
-| Method | Path |
+- the portal and server API route surfaces;
+- public request validation and canonical body mapping;
+- KYB and dispute upload validation (declared MIME, magic bytes, size);
+- portal, onboarding and external rate limits;
+- the `pg_live_` prefix gate for the external API;
+- the mTLS pool and request context sent to core.
+
+`merchant-back` does not own:
+
+- database access, Prisma, migrations or `DATABASE_URL`;
+- `KMS_MASTER_KEY` or another host's certificate/key;
+- session signature verification, session revocation, MFA state or authority decisions;
+- access-token hashing, revocation or IP allowlists;
+- money arithmetic, ledger writes, maker-checker or audit writes.
+
+Trust model: the edge is untrusted from core's point of view. The edge authenticates to core with a client certificate whose common name is exactly `merchant-back`. Core verifies the internal CA, binds the certificate to `/internal/merchant`, and independently verifies the session or `pg_live_` token, merchant binding, user state, authorities and business invariants. Edge checks are UX and contract checks; core is the authority.
+
+The backend binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0` in the service schema). Deployment writes `127.0.0.1`, so the public merchant Nginx vhost is the only intended listener.
+
+## 2. Architecture and request flow
+
+`index.ts` creates a stateless Express app:
+
+1. Disables `x-powered-by`.
+2. Sets Express `trust proxy` to `false`.
+3. Enables CORS with `origin: true` and `credentials: false`.
+4. Installs request logging with request-id resolution and secret redaction.
+5. Serves unauthenticated `GET /health`.
+6. Parses JSON and URL-encoded bodies with `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`.
+7. Mounts `/api/v1`.
+8. Adds the shared JSON 404 and error handlers.
+
+Mount order in `api/index.ts`:
+
+| Mount | Router | Notes |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `/merchant/auth` | `authRouter` | Public at the edge; auth limiter applies. |
+| `/merchant/onboarding` | `onboardingRouter` | Requires an `Authorization` header at the edge (presence only); onboarding limiter applies. |
+| `/merchant` | `protectedRouter` | Portal business routes; requires an `Authorization` header at the edge. |
+| `/external` | `externalRouter` | Requires a `pg_live_` bearer prefix at the edge. |
+
+Middleware:
+
+| Layer | Behavior |
 | :--- | :--- |
-| POST | `/auth/register`, `/auth/verify-identity`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/google`, `/auth/mfa/verify` |
-| GET, PUT | `/onboarding/join-request` |

+## 4. `CORE_BACK_URLS` pool and failover
 
+The shared client is implemented in `lib/coreInternalClient.ts`. This service uses `CORE_SERVICE_NAME=merchant-back` and `CORE_CHANNEL_PREFIX=/internal/merchant`.
+
+Configuration:
+
+- `CORE_BACK_URL` is required and must be an absolute `https:` URL. It is the first URL and the fallback when `CORE_BACK_URLS` is unset.
+- `CORE_BACK_URLS` is an optional comma-separated list of absolute `https:` URLs.
+- Empty entries are rejected, URLs are de-duplicated by normalized `URL.toString()`, and the original trimmed strings are used for requests.
+- One keep-alive `https.Agent` is created per node with the client certificate, client key and internal CA. TLS 1.3 is fixed; `rejectUnauthorized` is true; `maxSockets` is 64; the agent timeout is `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`.
+- Certificate and key files are read when the pool is created. Replacing files on disk does not affect a running process; restart or rebuild the pool.
+- A missing certificate/key/CA file produces `500 MTLS_MATERIAL_UNAVAILABLE`.
+
+Selection and failover:
+
+1. The pool selects the node with the fewest in-flight requests. A round-robin cursor breaks ties.
+2. Connection errors, TLS errors and HTTP `502`/`503` mark the node unhealthy and start a 5-second cooldown.
+3. After the cooldown, a zero-in-flight unhealthy node is selected as a half-open probe before healthy nodes are considered again.
+4. A call never retries against the same node URL.
+5. `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS` retry by default. `POST` and `PATCH` do not retry unless a caller opts in. `maxAttempts` defaults to 2.
+6. Other statuses, including `4xx` and `5xx` other than `502`/`503`, mark the node healthy and are returned to the caller.
+7. If all attempts end in `502`/`503`, the last response is returned. If no eligible node remains, the edge returns `503 CORE_UNAVAILABLE`.
+8. `x-pg-min-lsn` is propagated when the caller supplies an LSN. The client does not generate one.
+
+Transport mapping:
+
+| Transport condition | Edge error |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `ETIMEDOUT`, `ESOCKETTIMEDOUT` | `504 CORE_TIMEOUT` |
+| `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `EHOSTUNREACH` | `502 CORE_UNREACHABLE` |
+| `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN` | `502 CORE_DNS_FAILURE` |
+| TLS error codes | `502 CORE_TLS_ERROR` |
+| Other failures | `502 CORE_CONNECTION_ERROR` |
+
+SSE note: the POS screen stream uses the same node selection and retries a failed handshake on another node. Once the stream is established it is not load-balanced or resumed; `POS_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` controls the proxy timeout. The edge has no pool metrics or status endpoint.

+
+| Control | `merchant-back` behavior | `core-back` behavior |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| Portal session | Requires only a non-empty `Authorization` header on protected routes. Does not verify signature, expiry, user state, MFA or revocation. | Verifies the session JWT signature, issuer, audience, expiry, user existence and `ACTIVE` status. |
+| Portal authorities | No edge role or authority guard. | Merchant internal routes scope by `merchantId`; they do not use per-route authority guards. API-token scopes are stored but not enforced per endpoint. `requireMerchantScope` has no production caller. |
+| MFA | Not checked. | Login/MFA issue an `mfa` claim, but later calls do not enforce it. |
+| Session revocation | Not checked. | Stateless 12-hour JWTs; no per-session revocation table. Disabling the user blocks the next request. |
+| External API | Checks only the `pg_live_` prefix. | Hashes the token, looks up `AccessToken`, rejects unknown/revoked tokens, and enforces the optional `AccessTokenIp` CIDR allowlist. |
+| Google login | Forwards a shaped `idToken`. | Returns `501 GOOGLE_IDENTITY_NOT_CONFIGURED`; no OIDC provider is integrated. |
+| Maker-checker | Not decided at the edge. | Database constraint/trigger and execution checks enforce maker != checker. |
+| Merchant ownership | Not decided at the edge. | Core resolves the merchant from the token and scopes every query by it. |

+
+- A random non-empty bearer string reaches core on protected portal routes. Core is the only authentication authority.
+- The external prefix check is not a credential check. Do not log or expose the token.
+- API-token scopes are not enforced per merchant endpoint. This is a core-side authorization gap relative to the design.
+- `GET /auth/me` is not protected at the edge and core's merchant `/auth/me` returns static platform/version information before core's authentication middleware.
+- Merchant internal routes do not call `requireAuthorities`. Authority enforcement is limited to the merchantId binding and core business checks.

+## 10. Security notes
+
+- No database, KMS or migration material is present at the edge. Environment-isolation tests assert this boundary.
+- The client certificate CN must be exactly `merchant-back`; core's mTLS guard rejects a valid certificate on another namespace.
+- TLS 1.3 is fixed in both directions; core verifies the internal CA and the edge verifies the core server certificate.
+- CORS reflects any origin with credentials disabled. The public reverse proxy, CSP and bearer-token model are the browser-facing controls.
+- Portal authentication is only a header-presence check at the edge. Core verifies the session and scopes data by merchant. Do not assume the edge rejected an invalid token.
+- The external token prefix check is not a credential check. Core hashes the token, checks revocation and enforces the optional IP allowlist.
+- `x-real-client-ip` is preferred over `x-real-ip` in `merchant-back/lib/net/index.ts`. When the backend is loopback-bound this is safe; if it is ever exposed and a direct peer is inside `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, the peer can spoof its client IP.
+- Raw body handling: KYB uploads are forwarded byte for byte after MIME/magic-byte/size validation. Dispute evidence is base64 encoded into JSON and is not forwarded as raw bytes.
+- Upload limits: JSON bodies 2 MiB, multipart 10 MiB, evidence file 712,704 bytes, POS stream timeout 15 minutes. Core has its own limits and must re-check uploads.
+- Logs redact sensitive keys and truncate long strings, but tokens, signatures, credentials and document contents must never be logged by application code.
+- API-token scopes are stored but not enforced per endpoint; treat portal and token-based authorization as core-enforced, not edge-enforced.
+- There is no edge session revocation or per-call MFA cache. Disabling the user in core is the effective emergency stop.

+

+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part documents the edge-to-core transport used by `admin-back`, `merchant-back` and `checkout-back`. It owns the mTLS agent, the `CORE_BACK_URLS` node pool, node selection, passive failure detection, retries, request identity headers, the `x-pg-min-lsn` consistency hint, path/channel confinement, core error mapping and the SSE stream proxy.
+
+It does not own authorization or business validation. `core-back` remains authoritative for token verification, authorities, maker-checker, amount resolution, idempotency and channel-bound client-certificate checks. The client only guarantees that a request reaches an allowed core channel over an authenticated TLS 1.3 connection.
+
+The implementation exists as three near-identical copies:
+
+- `admin-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts`
+- `merchant-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts`
+- `checkout-back/lib/coreInternalClient.ts`
+
+Each copy is 761 lines and differs only in `CORE_SERVICE_NAME` and `CORE_CHANNEL_PREFIX`. There is no workspace package, no generated shared module and no single build artifact for the pool.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The historical design requires every edge request to cross a private LAN boundary over mutual TLS 1.3. The edge authenticates with a dedicated client certificate whose CN names the service, and `core-back` binds each internal namespace to that CN. Edge services never receive `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` or another host's client key.
+
+When `core-back` scales horizontally, each edge receives `CORE_BACK_URLS`. The intended behavior is:
+
+- persistent keep-alive connections to every core node;
+- least-in-flight selection with round-robin tie-breaking;
+- passive removal of a failed node, a cooldown, and a half-open probe after the cooldown;
+- retry of idempotent requests on a different node;
+- propagation of `x-pg-min-lsn` so LSN-aware reads can wait for a replica that has replayed the caller's write;
+- no loss of the edge's identity headers (`x-request-id`, `x-real-client-ip`, `x-client-user-agent`, `x-edge-service`).
+
+The design describes this as enabling rolling core restarts without dropping edge traffic. The implementation provides that only for requests that can be retried and only while at least one other eligible node exists; it does not make an individual single-node core restart seamless.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Agent and TLS material
+
+`createCoreAgent()` in each copy builds one `https.Agent` per configured node:
+
+- client certificate from `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH`;
+- client private key from `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH`;
+- CA from `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH`;
+- `minVersion` and `maxVersion` fixed to `TLSv1.3`;
+- `rejectUnauthorized: true`;
+- keep-alive enabled with 30-second keep-alive delay and `maxSockets: 64`;
+- the agent-level timeout is `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`.
+
+Material is loaded synchronously with `fs.readFileSync` when the agent is created. A missing file becomes `MTLS_MATERIAL_UNAVAILABLE` (HTTP 500) rather than a process crash. Because the agent is cached, replacing certificate files on disk does not affect a running process until the pool is rebuilt. The pool is rebuilt when the configured URL signature changes or when `resetCoreAgent()`/`resetCorePool()` is called by tests.
+
+### 3.2 Pool lifecycle and selection
+
+`ensureNodes()` parses `CORE_BACK_URLS` or falls back to `CORE_BACK_URL`. `parseCoreBackUrls()`:
+
+- splits on commas;
+- rejects empty entries;
+- requires absolute `https:` URLs;
+- de-duplicates by normalized `URL.toString()`;
+- preserves the original trimmed strings for requests.
+
+Each node state tracks `url`, `agent`, `healthy`, `inFlight`, `failures`, `lastFailureAt` and `cooldownUntil`.
+
+`eligiblePool(excluded)` implements the cooldown/half-open state:
+
+1. If any excluded node is unhealthy, has zero in-flight requests and its cooldown has elapsed, return only those half-open nodes. This lets one request probe recovery before the node rejoins the general pool.
+2. Otherwise return every healthy, non-excluded node.
+3. If neither set is non-empty the request fails with `503 CORE_UNAVAILABLE`.
+
+`selectNode()` picks the minimum in-flight count and uses a monotonic round-robin cursor to break ties. The cursor advances on every selection and is reduced modulo the tied set size. A node selected for an attempt is added to the request-local `attempted` set, so a retry never targets the same URL within one logical call.
+
+### 3.3 Failure marking and retries
+
+`markNodeFailure()` sets `healthy=false`, increments `failures`, records `lastFailureAt` and sets `cooldownUntil = now + CORE_FAILURE_COOLDOWN_MS` (5 seconds). `markNodeHealthy()` clears all failure state.
+
+Retry eligibility is controlled by `retryAttemptsFor()`:
+
+- idempotent methods default to retrying: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`;
+- `POST` and `PATCH` do not retry by default;
+- `retryIdempotent: true` forces retries; `retryIfUnavailable: true` allows a non-idempotent call to retry;
+- `maxAttempts` defaults to 2 and is floored to at least 1; there is no upper cap.
+
+`request()` marks a node failed and retries when the node returns HTTP `502` or `503`, or when the request throws a connection/TLS error. Any other status, including other `5xx` responses, marks the node healthy and is returned to the caller. If every attempt ends in a `502`/`503`, the last response body is returned rather than converted to a local error. If every node has already been attempted and no eligible node remains, the call fails with `CORE_UNAVAILABLE`.
+
+`mapCoreTransportError()` maps transport failures to stable edge errors:
+
+| Transport condition | Edge error |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `ETIMEDOUT`, `ESOCKETTIMEDOUT` | `504 CORE_TIMEOUT` |
+| `ECONNREFUSED`, `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `EHOSTUNREACH` | `502 CORE_UNREACHABLE` |
+| `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN` | `502 CORE_DNS_FAILURE` |
+| TLS error codes | `502 CORE_TLS_ERROR` |
+| other failures | `502 CORE_CONNECTION_ERROR` |
+
+### 3.4 Headers and consistency
+
+`buildCoreHeaders()` emits:
+
+- `x-request-id`: the resolved edge request id;
+- `x-real-client-ip`: the client IP resolved from the trusted proxy;
+- `x-client-user-agent`: the caller's user agent, possibly empty;
+- `x-edge-service`: `admin-back`, `merchant-back` or `checkout-back`;
+- `accept: application/json`;
+- `content-type: application/json` when a JSON body exists, or the supplied raw content type;
+- `authorization` when present;
+- every caller-supplied header, lowercased;
+- `x-pg-min-lsn` when `minLsn` or `consistencyLsn` is non-empty.
+
+`consistencyHeader(lsn)` is a helper that returns the same header or an empty object. The client does not generate an LSN. Callers must obtain one from a write response or another trusted source. `x-pg-min-lsn` is passed through to `core-back`, where `lib/storageEngine` converts it into an `atLeastLsn` read constraint with a 250 ms wait.
+
+### 3.5 Path and channel confinement
+
+`assertCorePath()` rejects:
+
+- empty paths and non-rooted paths;
+- protocol-relative paths (`//...`), embedded `://` and backslashes;
+- invalid percent escaping;
+- decoded `.` or `..` segments;
+- any path outside the service's channel prefix.
+
+The prefixes are:
+
+| Service | Prefix |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `admin-back` | `/internal/admin` |
+| `merchant-back` | `/internal/merchant` |
+| `checkout-back` | `/internal/checkout` |
+
+`resolveCoreUrlAgainst()` pins the result to the configured base origin and appends the path to the base pathname. `resolveCoreUrl()` exposes the same behavior for callers and tests. This is a client-side guard only; `core-back` independently enforces the certificate CN with `requireEdgeIdentity()` in `core-back/api/middleware/mtlsGuard.ts`.
+
+### 3.6 SSE streams and fallback behavior
+
+`openCoreStream()` is the streaming counterpart of `request()`:
+
+- sets `accept: text/event-stream` and `cache-control: no-cache`;
+- uses the same node selection, retry count, cooldown and attempted-node set;
+- increments `inFlight` until the stream ends, closes or errors;
+- if a node answers `502`/`503` and another attempt is possible, drains that response into a buffer, records it as `lastStream`, and tries the next node;
+- if retries are exhausted, returns `lastStream` or maps the transport error.
+
+`proxyCoreStream()` converts a non-2xx upstream into the normal core HTTP error, then copies the stream to the express response with `cache-control: no-cache, no-transform`, `connection: keep-alive` and `x-accel-buffering: no`. On client disconnect it aborts the upstream request.
+
+There is no true fallback to polling at the edge. Checkout and POS SSE are implemented by the core endpoint polling PostgreSQL on a timer; an established edge stream that breaks is ended, not resumed. The buffered `lastStream` fallback only preserves a failed handshake response body for retry purposes.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- Every core URL must be an absolute `https:` URL. Plain HTTP is not accepted by the edge configuration schema.
+- TLS 1.3 is the only accepted protocol version.
+- The client cert CN must match the channel; the client path guard prevents accidental cross-channel calls, and `core-back` prevents forged ones.
+- A call never retries against the same URL twice.
+- A default retry only applies to idempotent methods.
+- A `502`/`503` from any node is interpreted as node unavailability even if generated by application code.
+- Request identity headers and `authorization` are forwarded verbatim; the edge does not mint or re-sign tokens.
+- The pool does not load-balance SSE streams after establishment; selection happens once per stream open.
+- LSN hints are propagated, not validated. A malformed value is passed to core, where the storage layer decides how to handle it.
+- The client never receives or uses `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY`, or another service's certificate.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+### Environment
+
+| Key | Required | Used by | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `CORE_BACK_URL` | yes | all BFFs | First core URL and fallback when `CORE_BACK_URLS` is unset. |
+| `CORE_BACK_URLS` | no | all BFFs | Comma-separated core pool. |
+| `MTLS_CLIENT_CERT_PATH` | yes | all BFFs | Client certificate. |
+| `MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH` | yes | all BFFs | Client private key. |
+| `MTLS_CA_CERT_PATH` | yes | all BFFs | Internal CA certificate. |
+| `CORE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | no | all BFFs | Per-request and agent timeout. Defaults: admin 60000, merchant/checkout 30000. |
+| `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | no | all BFFs | Peers whose forwarded IP headers are trusted. |
+| `POS_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` | no | merchant | Stream timeout passed by the POS SSE route (default 900000). |
+
+### Deployment surface
+
+`deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` derives `CORE_BACK_URLS` as `https://<core-private-ip>:<service-port>,...` by default. An explicit `CORE_BACK_URLS` in `deploy.env` wins. `deploy/deploy.ts` writes the URL list and `CORE_BACK_URL` (first URL) into every edge `.env`.
+
+The deploy engine installs only the CA and the edge's own client certificate on an edge host. Certificate paths in the generated `.env` are relative (`shared/certs/...`) and are expanded to the release directory by `absoluteEnv()`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- When adding a core node, add it to `CORE_NODES` or set `CORE_BACK_URLS`; re-deploy the edge tiers so their process environment changes. The pool itself would notice a changed environment only if the process configuration changes, which requires a restart in a deployed environment.
+- When rotating certificates, restart or redeploy the edge processes. Replacing files in place is not sufficient for a running pool.
+- Check `/health` on the edge only for process liveness; it does not probe core. Use `deploy/lib/healthVerifier.ts` or a manual mTLS request to check the upstream.
+- Use `x-request-id` to correlate an edge failure with core logs. The edge maps core envelopes and preserves `code`, `message`, `details` and `reference`.
+- To debug node selection, inspect `CORE_BACK_URLS` in the generated `.env`, the edge logs and the core health endpoint. There are no exported pool metrics or a status endpoint.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Per-node keep-alive TLS 1.3 agents with client certificates and CA verification.
+- Least-in-flight selection with round-robin tie-breaking.
+- Passive failure marking with a 5-second cooldown.
+- Half-open selection: one zero-in-flight request probes an unhealthy node after cooldown.
+- Idempotent retries and explicit non-idempotent retry opt-in.
+- `x-pg-min-lsn` propagation and header helper.
+- Channel path confinement and URL origin pinning.
+- Core envelope and transport error mapping.
+- SSE stream proxying with pre-establishment retry and buffering of failed handshake responses.
+
+### Partial
+
+- The "shared" client is a copy-paste implementation. Behavior is consistent today, but a change must be applied three times.
+- Certificate rotation requires a restart; there is no file watcher or hot reload.
+- The SSE fallback preserves a failed response but does not resume an interrupted stream.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No circuit-breaker metrics, pool introspection, or administrative pool status endpoint.
+- No request hedging or per-attempt deadline separate from the overall timeout.
+- No automatic retry for `POST`/`PATCH` unless a caller opts in.
+- No jitter on cooldown or randomized selection.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- Treating every upstream `502`/`503` as a node failure can evict a healthy core node that legitimately returned a gateway-style `502`/`503`.
+- A half-open node is preferred over healthy nodes while any half-open candidate exists. With several recovering nodes this can concentrate probe traffic rather than spread it.
+- `maxAttempts` can exceed the number of nodes; the attempted set then stops the loop early.
+- A pool with an empty URL list throws `CORE_UNAVAILABLE`; there is no startup-time rejection of an empty `CORE_BACK_URLS` beyond the fallback to `CORE_BACK_URL`.
+- The stream path does not retry after response headers are delivered; a mid-stream core restart is visible to the browser.
+
+### Code gap versus documentation
+
+The historical design describes zero-downtime rolling core restarts. The client enables retry-based continuity for idempotent one-shot calls and for stream establishment, but it does not guarantee zero downtime for non-idempotent calls, established SSE streams, or a single core node. This document records the as-built behavior.

+## Merchant Edge BFF
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+`merchant-back` is the public merchant edge. One Bun/Express process serves two audiences:
+
+- the authenticated merchant portal under `/api/v1/merchant/*`;
+- the merchant server API under `/api/v1/external/*`, authenticated by a `pg_live_` bearer token and a core-side IP allowlist.
+
+It owns request validation, edge translation to the canonical core contract, upload verification, rate limiting, the public merchant API shape and mTLS forwarding to `/internal/merchant/*`. It owns no database connection, no Prisma client, no `DATABASE_URL`, no `KMS_MASTER_KEY` and no authority decisions.
+
+The merchant vhost serves the SPA through Nginx. The backend itself binds to loopback in deployment.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The design splits the merchant experience into a portal API and a server-to-server API. The portal covers registration, identity verification, login/MFA, KYB onboarding, wallets, applications, links, POS terminals and cashier screens, payments, disputes, cash-outs, API tokens, credential sets, team users and overview statistics. The external API covers link creation/inspection/cancellation and payment lookup using a long-lived merchant token.
+
+All operations are forwarded over mTLS 1.3 with `CN=merchant-back`. The edge validates multipart KYB documents for MIME type, magic bytes and size before forwarding raw bytes to core. The portal may accept amounts and currencies when the merchant owns link creation; the edge never performs money arithmetic and core re-validates every monetary field. The external API is meant to enforce a `pg_live_` bearer token and an IP allowlist, with core as the authority.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Process, listener and middleware
+
+`merchant-back/index.ts`:
+
+- disables `x-powered-by`;
+- sets `trust proxy` to false;
+- enables CORS with any origin and no credentials;
+- installs request logging;
+- serves unauthenticated `GET /health`;
+- parses JSON and URL-encoded bodies with `MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`;
+- mounts `/api/v1`;
+- adds the shared 404 and error handlers.
+
+The listener binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0` in the service schema). The deploy engine overrides this to `127.0.0.1`; direct exposure of port 4102 is a configuration error.
+
+Middleware layers:
+
+| Layer | Behavior |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `authLimiter` | Fixed 15-minute window, `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 20), on `/api/v1/merchant/auth`. |
+| `onboardingLimiter` | 60-second window, `API_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 300), on `/api/v1/merchant/onboarding`. |
+| `apiLimiter` | 60-second window, `API_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 300), on the protected merchant router. |
+| `externalLimiter` | 60-second window, `EXTERNAL_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), on `/api/v1/external`. |
+| `requirePgLiveToken` | Requires `Authorization: Bearer pg_live_...` by prefix only. Applied to the whole external router. |
+| `coreForward` `requireAuth` | Rejects a missing `Authorization` header for protected portal routes. Defaults to required; auth/onboarding routes opt out with `requireAuth: false`. |
+| `requireBearer` | Helper used by dispute evidence and merchant user routes to require a header before multipart work. |
+| `requireAuthHeader` | Exported from `api/public/auth.ts` but a no-op; it is not a security control. |
+
+There is no edge session parser, role guard or token verifier in `merchant-back`. An arbitrary non-empty bearer token reaches core for every protected portal route.
+
+### 3.2 Forwarding behavior
+
+`merchant-back/api/forward.ts` implements a stricter forwarder than admin's:
+
+1. Requires `Authorization` unless `requireAuth === false`.
+2. Validates route params and query with Zod.
+3. Validates the public body with `schema`.
+4. Applies `bodyMapper()` to translate product vocabulary into the core body.
+5. Applies `bodyFrom()` when the route replaces the body entirely.
+6. Re-validates the translated body with `coreSchema` when configured, so a request that core would reject is stopped at the edge.
+7. Calls `callCoreResponse()` with request id, resolved client IP, user agent and the bearer token.
+8. Returns the core body with the declared status, or the core status when `relayStatus: true`.
+
+The external router also has its own PG-live prefix check. It does not hash or validate the token; core does the authoritative token lookup and IP check.
+
+### 3.3 Uploads
+
+`merchant-back/api/upload.ts` uses Multer memory storage with `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`, one file and at most 32 fields. `forwardUpload()` and the dispute route call `assertAllowedUpload()`:
+
+- checks the declared MIME type against `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_MIME`;
+- checks magic bytes for PNG (`89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`), JPEG (`FF D8 FF`) and PDF (`25 50 44 46 2D`);
+- enforces the size cap;
+- computes SHA-256;
+- forwards raw bytes with `x-upload-filename`, `x-upload-content-type`, `x-upload-sha256`, `x-upload-size` and base64url `x-upload-metadata`.
+
+Dispute evidence is converted into a canonical JSON body (`toCoreDisputeEvidence`) rather than raw bytes. The max evidence size is defined in `merchant-back/api/contract.ts`.
+
+### 3.4 Route map
+
+Portal auth is mounted under `/api/v1/merchant/auth`:
+
+| Method | Path |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| POST | `/register`, `/verify-identity`, `/accept-invitation`, `/login`, `/google`, `/mfa/verify` |
+| GET | `/me` |
+
+Onboarding is mounted under `/api/v1/merchant/onboarding`:
+
+| Method | Path |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| GET, PUT | `/join-request` |
+| GET | `/kyb-revalidations`, `/beneficial-owners` |
+| POST | `/kyb-documents` (multipart), `/beneficial-owners`, `/submit` |
+| DELETE | `/beneficial-owners/:id` |
+
+The protected portal API is mounted under `/api/v1/merchant`:
+
+| Area | Routes |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Wallets | `GET, POST /wallets`, `GET /wallets/:id`, `GET /wallets/:id/balance`, `GET /wallets/:id/statements`, `GET /wallets/:id/statements/:month/export` |
+| Applications | `GET, POST /applications`, `GET, PATCH /applications/:id` |
+| Links | `GET, POST /links`, `GET /links/:id`, `POST /links/:id/cancel`, `GET /links/:id/attempts` |
+| POS | `GET, POST /pos/terminals`, `GET, PATCH /pos/terminals/:id`, `POST /pos/terminals/:id/screens`, `GET /pos/screens/:screenCode/stream` (SSE) |
+| Payments | `GET /payments` |
+| Disputes | `GET /disputes`, `GET /disputes/:id`, `POST /disputes/:id/evidence` (multipart) |
+| Cash-outs | `GET, POST /cashouts` |
+| Tokens | `GET, POST /tokens`, `PUT /tokens/:id/ips`, `DELETE /tokens/:id` |
+| Credential sets | `GET, POST /credential-sets`, `GET, PUT /credential-sets/:id` |
+| Team | `GET, POST, PATCH /users`, `PATCH /users/:id` |
+| Stats | `GET /stats/overview` |
+
+`merchant-back/api/protected/options.ts` exports `optionsRouter` for `GET /options/:kind`, but the router is not imported by `api/protected/index.ts` and has no live mount.
+
+The external merchant server API is mounted under `/api/v1/external`:
+
+| Method | Path |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| POST | `/links`, `/links/:key/cancel` |
+| GET | `/links/:key`, `/payments/:reference` |
+
+### 3.5 Authentication behavior and the Google gap
+
+Portal auth routes are public at the edge (`requireAuth: false`) and forward to `/internal/merchant/auth/*`:
+
+- `POST /register` validates phone/email, password, name and optional identity fields, then creates a registration.
+- `POST /verify-identity` validates an identity type, number, phone and OTP code.
+- `POST /accept-invitation` validates an invitation token and password.
+- `POST /login` validates an identifier and password.
+- `POST /google` validates a Google `idToken` shape and forwards it, but `core-back` answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with `Google sign-in requires a configured OIDC provider` (`core-back/api/internal/merchant.ts:853`). The capability is not implemented at the core.
+- `GET /me` and `POST /mfa/verify` forward the supplied bearer/challenge state to core.
+
+The merchant portal session is a core-issued token. The edge never verifies its signature, expiry, revocation, MFA state or merchant status. Core verifies the signature, expiry, user status and authorities; it does not re-check MFA or a session revocation list on every call.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+- All portal business routes require an `Authorization` header at the edge; its validity is decided by core.
+- The external API requires a `pg_live_` prefix at the edge; access-token validity, revocation and source-IP allowlist are decided by core.
+- Every forwarded path stays under `/internal/merchant`; the shared client enforces this and core re-checks `CN=merchant-back`.
+- The edge never accepts arbitrary core paths.
+- Link creation accepts decimal-string amounts and ISO 4217 currencies; the edge does not do arithmetic and core re-validates amount, currency and fee model.
+- Checkout money semantics do not apply here: merchant link creation is an owning operation.
+- Uploaded KYB and dispute files are validated for MIME, magic bytes and size before the core call.
+- Team/user and credential-set operations are forwarded with the caller's bearer token; the core enforces merchant roles and maker-checker where applicable.
+- The POS SSE route requires a bearer header, then proxies the core stream.
+

+## 6. Operational usage
+
+```bash
+cd merchant-back
+bun install
+bun run start
+bun run dev
+bun test
+bun run typecheck
+```
+
+- Public reachability is through `https://merchant.<domain>/api`; the backend port must stay loopback-only.
+- For POS issues, verify the Nginx stream route disables buffering and the proxy read timeout exceeds the cashier idle window.
+- For upload failures, check `UPLOAD_ALLOWED_MIME`, magic bytes, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and the core-side upload limits.
+- For external API `401 INVALID_API_TOKEN`, the edge did not see a `pg_live_` bearer; for a core rejection, inspect the core token/IP state.

+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Two-audience routing with separate rate limits and external token prefix gate.
+- Full portal and external route surface, including multipart KYB and evidence uploads.
+- Public-to-core schema validation and canonical body mapping.
+- MIME/magic-byte/size validation and hashed raw upload forwarding.
+- mTLS pool, retries, LSN header propagation and channel confinement.
+- POS SSE proxy with buffering disabled.
+
+### Partial
+
+- Portal authentication is only a presence check at the edge; all session and authority enforcement is in core.
+- External token validation is prefix-only at the edge.
+- Google sign-in is exposed but not implemented by core.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- Google OIDC provider integration in core.
+- Edge session revocation/MFA cache.
+- Route-level merchant role guards at the edge.
+- A live `GET /options/:kind` mount for the merchant portal.
+- SSE resume/replay or polling fallback at the edge.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- `requireAuthHeader` is a no-op and should not be mistaken for a guard.
+- The auth limiter uses a hard-coded 15-minute window; `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` has no effect.

+- The options router is dead code; a frontend calling `/api/v1/merchant/options/:kind` receives a 404.
+- The external prefix check is not a credential check; do not log or expose token values.
