+Public Merchant Portal SPA for the payment gateway platform. It is the merchant self-service workspace for onboarding, wallets, statements, applications, payment links, POS, payments, disputes, cash-outs, API tokens, credentials, team management and the merchant/developer guides.

-## Run and build
+## 1. Purpose and trust boundary
 
+- The browser talks only to `merchant-back` under `/api`; it holds no database connection, core credential or KMS key.
+- `merchant-back` calls `core-back` over mTLS. The portal session is separate from the external merchant API, which authenticates with scoped `pg_live_` bearer tokens.
+- The merchant portal is public-facing. Login, registration, onboarding and the interactive guide are exposed to merchants; the portal APIs still enforce merchant scope and authority.
+- UI authority checks and hidden navigation are advisory. `merchant-back`/`core-back` remain authoritative.
+- Sensitive application changes are maker-checker proposals. The current configuration stays active until the change is reviewed and approved.
+- Wallet balances are ledger-derived. The portal displays available, pending and negative amounts; it never edits a balance.
+- Money and spreadsheet output use decimal.js and the shared XLSX pipeline. No floating-point money calculations.

+## 5. Route and page map
+
+Public routes:

+| `/:pathMatch(.*)*` | `NotFound` | Public 404 page. |
+
+Protected `/portal` routes (16 children; `/portal` redirects to the dashboard):

+| Path | Route name | UI gate | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `/portal/dashboard` | `Dashboard` | `stats.read` | Wallet, period volume, success rate, pending cash-outs, charts and recent payments. |
+| `/portal/onboarding` | `Onboarding` | none (authenticated only) | Five-step KYB/onboarding profile, owners, documents, payout and submission. |

+| `/portal/guide/developers` | `MerchantDeveloperGuide` | none (learning surface) | Developer API chapters D-01 to D-05 with code templates. |
+| `/portal/wallets` | `Wallets` | `wallets.read` | Wallet balances, pending/negative amounts, last use and wallet creation. |

+| `/portal/pos/screen/:code` | `PosScreen` | `pos.manage` or `pos.operate` | Full-screen real-time customer display for a paired terminal. |
+| `/portal/payments` | `Payments` | `payments.read` | Payment attempts, status, commission, net and application. |

+
+### Authority-gating gaps
+
+- `Statements` is hidden from navigation without `statements.read`/`statements.export`, but it has **no `routesAuthorities` entry**. Direct navigation is not redirected by the router; the merchant API still enforces statement access.
+- `Onboarding` intentionally has an empty gate because every authenticated merchant must be able to complete it.
+- Guide and developer-guide routes are intentionally open learning surfaces. They contain no merchant data.
+- Hiding a navigation item is not route protection. Verify both the hidden-navigation and direct-URL cases.
+
+## 6. Key capabilities
+
+### Onboarding (`/portal/onboarding`)
+
+Five steps:
+
+1. **Business profile** — legal/trade name, registration number, tax id, business category, address, contact phone/email, expected monthly volume, currency, website and sales-channel description.
+2. **Beneficial owners** — full name, ownership percent, national id, date of birth, nationality and PEP/controller flags. Total ownership is displayed with decimal.js.
+3. **Documents** — document type, file and expiry; uploads use multipart `POST v1/merchant/onboarding/kyb-documents`; open revalidation requests accept a replacement file and expiry.
+4. **Bank details** — bank name, account holder, IBAN, account number and SWIFT. Payout details must follow the approved corporate-account policy.
+5. **Review and submit** — acknowledgement and `POST v1/merchant/onboarding/submit`.
+
+The page loads the current join request and open revalidations, saves the profile, creates owners, uploads documents and displays the join status/INFO_REQUESTED state. Onboarding completion is not an activation authority: admin KYB and `core-back` decide when the merchant is live.
+
+### Wallets and statements
+
+- **Wallets** lists name, currency, balance, pending, amount due/negative balance, status and last use; it can create a wallet with application, label and currency and links to statements.
+- **Statements** selects a wallet and one of the last 12 months, then shows opening/closing balance, gross credits, commission, net credits, adjustments, cash-outs, snapshot hash and line items.
+- Statement export calls `GET v1/merchant/wallets/:id/statements/:month/export` and converts the returned CSV into a styled XLSX workbook through the shared pipeline. Export is disabled until a wallet is selected.
+- Balances are ledger-derived and displayed through `MoneyDisplay`; the portal never writes a balance.
+
+### Applications
+
+- Lists applications and their status.
+- Edits descriptive fields (display/name, sales-channel description, expected volume) directly.
+- Proposes sensitive changes for assigned wallet, rail whitelist and redirect-domain allowlist; those remain pending until reviewed and the current configuration stays active.
+- Requires `applications.read` to open; mutation authority is enforced by the merchant API. The UI reflects the maker-checker model but does not approve changes itself.
+
+### Payment links
+
+- Lists amount, currency, use count, expiry, state and attempts.
+- Creates a link with description, amount, currency, use count, expiry, redirect URL and rail whitelist.
+- Shows a QR code, opens an attempts inspector and cancels through `POST v1/merchant/links/:id/cancel`.
+- The link amount is stored server-side and is the checkout price authority. A single-use link can lock its slot while an attempt is in progress.
+
+### POS terminals and screens
+
+- **POS terminals** lists terminals and paired screens, creates a terminal with name/location, creates or pairs a screen and shows screen role/status.
+- **POS screen** loads `GET v1/merchant/pos/screens/:code/stream` and then opens an `EventSource` on the same path. It shows amount, status, rail code, screen code, reference, last update and a live/pending badge, with a manual refresh.
+- The POS screen is a real-time display surface. It does not initiate or confirm payments, and a displayed `SUCCEEDED` state must still be reconciled with the server-confirmed payment and settlement rules.
+
+### Payments and disputes
+
+- **Payments** is a searchable attempt list with reference, rail, status, amount, commission, net, application, creation and confirmation times, using `StatusBadge` tone mapping.
+- **Disputes** lists dispute reference, source, state, amount, reason code, evidence deadline and whether evidence was submitted.
+- Evidence upload is multipart with a note and optional file through `POST v1/merchant/disputes/:id/evidence`. Evidence is deadline-bound; money movement remains an admin finance action.
+
+### Cash-outs
+
+- Lists cash-out state, wallet, amount, currency and request time.
+- Requests a cash-out with wallet, amount, currency and bank details (bank name, account number and optional IBAN).
+- Shows processing states returned by the API. UI access requires `cashout.read` or `cashout.request`; the merchant API re-checks.
+
+### Developer tokens
+
+- Lists token name, status, IP-whitelist state and revocation state.
+- Creates a token with name, scopes and optional IP CIDR allowlist.
+- Shows the one-time `pg_live_` secret immediately after creation. The database stores only a hash and last four characters; the secret cannot be viewed again.
+- Revokes tokens through `DELETE v1/merchant/tokens/:id` and updates IP allowlists through `PUT v1/merchant/tokens/:id/ips`.
+- Tokens authenticate the external API. They are separate from the portal session and must never be placed in browser JavaScript, a bundled SPA, a mobile APK or source control.
+
+### Merchant credentials
+
+- Lists merchant-owned gateway credential sets.
+- Creates/edits credential name, gateway code, environment, settlement target, username, write-only secret and secret reference.
+- Shows whether a secret exists and the environment/settlement posture. Secrets are write-only after save.
+- Requires `credentials.manage`. This supports `MERCHANT_DIRECT` mode, where the merchant's gateway credentials are used and the platform records commission receivable rather than holding principal cash.
+
+### Team and roles
+
+- Lists merchant users, roles, status and authority posture.
+- Invites a member with full name, email, phone, role and temporary password.
+- Edits profile/status and scopes/authorities through `PATCH v1/merchant/users/:id` or `POST v1/merchant/users`.
+- Requires `users.manage`.
+
+## 7. Guide, developer API and help
+
+- `/portal/guide` contains 10 operations chapters (`M-01` to `M-10`) and embeds the five developer chapters. `/portal/guide/developers` is the dedicated D-01 to D-05 reader with code templates.
+- The operations guide includes a first-5 checklist (KYB, first wallet, first application, first link, POS/API setup), progress bar, chapter search, role filter tabs, chapter modal and the fee/net settlement calculator.
+- The first-5 checklist is stored in `localStorage` under `merchant-guide-checklist`. On mount the page calls onboarding, wallets, applications, links, POS terminals and tokens endpoints to auto-detect steps, and the user can still toggle steps manually. It is a training aid, not a server-issued activation record.
+- The fee calculator uses decimal.js and supports `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`, `PAYER_SURCHARGE` and `SPLIT`, showing customer total, platform commission, estimated gateway fee and net wallet credit. The gateway-fee estimate is not the ledger truth.
+- The developer code generator produces TypeScript/Node/Bun, PHP/Laravel, Python/httpx and cURL examples for creating/getting/cancelling links and reading payment status. Tokens in generated examples are placeholders; create a real scoped token in `/portal/developers/tokens`.
+- The guide teaches five webhook checks: require `X-PG-Signature`, recompute over the raw body in constant time, verify amount/currency against the created payment, deduplicate by event id and return 2xx quickly while queueing slow work.
+- Deep links: `/portal/guide?chapter=M-06`, `/portal/guide/developers?chapter=D-04`, and `?search=<term>` pre-fills search.
+- The shell `Ctrl+K`/`Cmd+K` opens merchant guide search; `?` opens the merchant contextual-help drawer. The drawer maps all 16 routes to M/D chapters and uses the same content modules as the full guide.
+- Guide v2 is **not** implemented. Merchant content remains the 10+5 baseline; the context map, safeguard cards, playbook and read tracking are future work.
+
+## 8. UI system, tables and exports
+
+- The merchant portal mirrors the admin design system: the same `--pg-*` token sheet, self-hosted Plus Jakarta Sans/Cairo/JetBrains Mono fonts, Vuetify defaults, flat surfaces, semantic status colors, 36 px buttons and outlined compact fields.
+- The authenticated shell is a 56 px app bar plus a 248 px drawer (temporary on compact screens) with Overview, Money, Commerce and Developer sections, breadcrumbs, guide search, help, theme/language controls and an operator card showing merchant role plus maker/checker dots.
+- The shared primitives are `PageHeader`, `StatusBadge`, `MoneyDisplay`, `MonoRef`, `MetricStrip`, `SurfaceCard`, `FormModal`, `FormField`, `SlideOverDrawer`, `DescriptionList`, `SegmentedTabs`, `EmptyState`, `JsonDiffViewer`, plus `SurfaceCardText`, `MetaPill`, `FormChecklist` and `SummaryExportCard`.
+- Tables use the copied shared table subsystem: compact neutral rows, semantic badges, collapsible filters, one primary row action plus `TableRowActions` overflow, and shared XLSX export. Table-header exports follow the admin convention of exporting the rendered page only.
+- Statement export and any other spreadsheet output go through the shared XLSX pipeline. Do not add a page-local spreadsheet library or floating-point money formatting.
+
+## 9. i18n, RTL and authority conventions
+
+- Locales are Arabic (`ar`) and English (`en`). Arabic is the default: `locale-name` is treated as English only when stored as exactly `en`; otherwise the app starts in Arabic.
+- The locale is stored in `localStorage`, applied to `<html lang>`/`dir` (`rtl` for Arabic, `ltr` for English) and passed to Vuetify's locale adapter.
+- User-facing text comes from `src/constants/i18nCatalogue.ts` as `[English, Arabic]` pairs plus Vuetify messages. Keep both catalogues in sync.
+- Guide content has per-chapter English/Arabic titles and bodies; coverage is chapter-dependent, with fallback to the other language where the UI supports it.
+- Route authorities use OR semantics. A missing/empty entry means no UI gate. Backend authorization and merchant scoping remain authoritative.
+- The UI shows maker/checker posture but is not a complete pending-change diff workflow for every sensitive object.
+
+## 10. Deployment and runtime behavior
+
+- The deploy engine builds `merchant-front` with `bun run build` and syncs `dist` to the merchant host.
+- Nginx serves the SPA with history fallback and proxies `/api/` to `merchant-back`. The merchant host is public-facing with deploy-managed TLS (`certbot`, `custom` or `self_signed`).
+- The production SPA uses same-origin `/api`; `VITE_API_URL` is a development convenience only.
+- There is no `runtime-config.js` and no deploy-generated SPA visibility flag for merchant-front. Merchant deploy variables cover host, ports, SSL/domain and remote directory.
+- The browser never receives core credentials. `merchant-back` holds the mTLS client identity and forwards authorized/merchant-scoped requests to `core-back`.
+
+## 11. Testing and troubleshooting
+
+### Recommended checks
+
 ```bash
-bun run test:unit        # bun test src/content/__tests__
-bun run test:unit:watch  # bun test --watch src/content/__tests__
+bun run type-check
+bun run lint
+bun run test:unit
+bun run build
 ```
 
-## Environment
+Relevant browser suites (from `tests/`): merchant shell, auth, accessibility and exhaustive merchant surface. They require the running stack.
 
-| Key | Default | Meaning |
-| :--- | :--- | :--- |
-| `VITE_API_URL` | `http://localhost:4102/` | Edge API base URL used by the dev proxy and the browser client. |
-| `VITE_SEND_NOT_FOUND_TRANSLATIONS` | `NO` | Development-only: report missing translation keys. |
-| `VITE_MY_TAILSCALE` | unset | Optional Tailscale hostname added to Vite `allowedHosts`. |
+### Common problems
 
-## Conventions
+| Symptom | Check |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Login redirects or session drops | The API returned 401 or the app-suspended error; the client logs out. Confirm `merchant-back` is reachable at `/api` and `VITE_API_URL` points at port 4102 in dev. |
+| A portal page is missing from navigation | The section item is filtered by authority. Hiding a nav item does not prove the route is protected. |
+| Direct `/portal/statements` opens for a user without statement authority | Known router gap: the route has no `routesAuthorities` entry. The merchant API remains authoritative; do not treat the page shell as access. |
+| Statement export does nothing | Select a wallet first. The export button is disabled until a wallet is selected. |
+| Onboarding looks complete but live payments are blocked | Onboarding/client progress is not activation. Wait for admin KYB approval and `ACTIVE` status. |
+| Guide checklist state is wrong | It is localStorage-backed and auto-detected from list calls; it can differ from the server. Verify the actual portal state. |
+| POS screen stops updating | The screen consumes an SSE stream and exposes a manual refresh. A dropped stream is a display issue, not payment confirmation. |
+| API token is lost | The plaintext secret is shown once. Revoke the token and create a new one. |
+| Credential secret cannot be viewed | Secrets are write-only after save. Replace/rotate instead of expecting to read them back. |
+| Google sign-in does not work | The API map includes `/auth/google`, but the backend returns 501 and no working Google flow ships. Use the supported login flow. |
+| Guide v2 features are missing | Guide v2 is future/unimplemented; the current content is the 10 operations + 5 developer chapter baseline. |
 
-- Pages, layouts and components are TSX under `src/`; API paths live in `src/constants/urlsMap`.
-- The portal uses the merchant session; the external API uses `pg_live_` bearer tokens.
-- Keep English/Arabic catalogue entries in sync.
-- All monetary calculations use `decimal.js`; all spreadsheet exports use the shared XLSX pipeline.

-# App Scaling Feature
-
-This Vue 3 TSX Vuetify application includes a comprehensive scaling system that allows you to scale the entire app to different sizes while maintaining layout integrity and functionality.
-
-## How It Works
-
-The scaling system uses CSS transform scale on the root `#app` element, which provides:
-- Consistent scaling of all UI elements
-- Preservation of layout relationships
-- No interference with Vuetify's responsive system
-- Smooth transitions between scale levels
-
-## Default Scale
-
-The app is set to scale to **0.9 (90%)** by default, making it slightly smaller than the viewport while maintaining full functionality.
-
-## Control Methods
-
-### 1. Account Actions Menu
-- Click on your user profile in the top-right corner
-- Select "App Scale" from the dropdown menu
-- Choose from preset options: 80%, 90%, 100%, or "Toggle Scale"
-
-### 2. Keyboard Shortcuts
-- **Ctrl/Cmd + Plus** (`=`): Increase scale by 10%
-- **Ctrl/Cmd + Minus** (`-`): Decrease scale by 10%
-- **Ctrl/Cmd + 0**: Reset to default scale (90%)
-
-### 3. Visual Indicator
-- A scale indicator is displayed in the app bar showing the current scale percentage
-- Click the indicator to quickly toggle between scale levels
-- Hover for tooltip with keyboard shortcut hints
-
-### 4. Programmatic Control
-
-```typescript
-import { setAppScale, getAppScale, toggleAppScale } from '@/utils/appScale';
-
-// Set specific scale
-setAppScale(0.8); // 80%
-setAppScale(1.0); // 100%
-
-// Get current scale
-const currentScale = getAppScale();
-
-// Toggle between preset scales
-toggleAppScale();
-```
-
-## Technical Implementation
-
-### CSS Variables
-The scaling uses CSS custom properties for flexibility:
-
-```scss
-:root {
-    --app-scale: 0.9;
-}
-
-#app {
-    transform: scale(var(--app-scale));
-    transform-origin: top left;
-    width: calc(100% / var(--app-scale));
-    height: calc(100% / var(--app-scale));
-}
-```
-
-### Scale Range
-- **Minimum**: 0.5 (50%)
-- **Maximum**: 1.5 (150%)
-- **Default**: 0.9 (90%)
-
-## Benefits
-
-1. **Consistent Scaling**: All elements scale proportionally
-2. **Responsive Friendly**: Works with Vuetify's breakpoint system
-3. **Performance**: Uses GPU-accelerated CSS transforms
-4. **Accessibility**: Keyboard shortcuts for easy control

+# merchant-front blueprint
+
+Generated from: `merchant-ui.portal`, `merchant-ui.guide`.
+
+## Merchant Portal
+
+> Status: `partial` · Last verified: 2026-11-03
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the merchant-facing portal in `merchant-front`: its routes, authentication entry points, 248/56 shell, onboarding flow, wallet/application/link/POS/payment/dispute/cash-out/token/credential/team pages, and the guide surfaces that are implemented in this workspace.
+
+It does not own the merchant edge API (`merchant-back`), the merchant external API (`/api/v1/external/*`), or the merchant guide content in detail. The guide and developer API are covered in `01-guide-and-developer-api.md`. Checkout is covered in `05-checkout-front/**`.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The merchant portal is the self-service business workspace:
+
+1. **One merchant identity, many applications.** A merchant owns wallets and applications; each application maps to a wallet and controls the rails/redirect domains used by its links.
+2. **KYB before live money.** A merchant can prepare onboarding and use sandbox behavior while pending, but live activation follows KYB approval.
+3. **Wallet balances are ledger-derived.** The portal shows available, pending and negative amounts; it never edits a balance column.
+4. **Sensitive changes are governed.** Descriptive application/merchant fields can change directly; wallet assignment, rail whitelist and redirect allowlist are sensitive and require review.
+5. **Links are server-priced.** The checkout cannot change the amount; the merchant link record is the price authority.
+6. **POS is a real-time surface.** A paired screen reflects the current payment state and must not be treated as a payment authority.
+7. **Disputes are evidence workflows.** The merchant uploads evidence before the deadline; money movement remains an admin finance action.
+8. **API tokens are scoped secrets.** Tokens are shown once, can be revoked, and can be constrained by IP CIDR allowlists.
+9. **Help is merchant-specific.** The shell exposes merchant guild search/help, not the admin 12-book guide.
+10. **All money and spreadsheet output uses decimal.js and the shared XLSX pipeline.**
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Public and protected routes
+
+`merchant-front/src/router/index.ts` defines:
+
+- Public `/` (`Landing`), `/login` (`Login`), `/register` (`Register`), and a catch-all `NotFound`.
+- A protected `/portal` parent using `layouts/default`, with 16 children.
+- A visitor guard for login/register and a landing-to-dashboard redirect for authenticated users.
+- A `routesAuthorities` check after authentication; missing/empty authority arrays mean no UI gate.
+- A dynamic-import retry path using `localStorage`.
+
+### 3.2 The 16 portal routes
+
+| # | Path | Name | UI authority | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| 1 | `/portal/dashboard` | `Dashboard` | `stats.read` | Wallet balance, period volume, success rate, pending cash-outs, charts and recent payments. |
+| 2 | `/portal/onboarding` | `Onboarding` | `[]` (authenticated only) | Five-step KYB/onboarding: profile, owners, documents, payout, submit; revalidation requests. |
+| 3 | `/portal/guide` | `MerchantGuide` | none | Merchant operations guide, role-filtered chapters, first-5 checklist, fee calculator, code generator, webhook checks. |
+| 4 | `/portal/guide/developers` | `MerchantDeveloperGuide` | none | Developer API chapters D-01..D-05 with code templates. |
+| 5 | `/portal/wallets` | `Wallets` | `wallets.read` | Wallet balances, pending/negative amounts, last use, create wallet, statements shortcut. |
+| 6 | `/portal/statements` | `Statements` | **none (gap)** | Monthly statement by wallet/month, line items, snapshot hash and XLSX export. |
+| 7 | `/portal/applications` | `Applications` | `applications.read` | Application list, profile edits, wallet assignment, rail whitelist and redirect allowlist proposals. |
+| 8 | `/portal/links` | `Links` | `links.read` | Create/cancel links, QR, attempts inspector, redirect URL and rail whitelist. |
+| 9 | `/portal/pos` | `PosTerminals` | `pos.manage` or `pos.operate` | Terminals, screens and pairing. |
+| 10 | `/portal/pos/screen/:code` | `PosScreen` | `pos.manage` or `pos.operate` | Realtime customer-facing screen for a paired terminal. |
+| 11 | `/portal/payments` | `Payments` | `payments.read` | Payment attempts, status, amount, commission, net and application. |
+| 12 | `/portal/disputes` | `Disputes` | `payments.read` | Chargeback list, evidence deadline/status and evidence upload. |
+| 13 | `/portal/cashouts` | `Cashouts` | `cashout.read` or `cashout.request` | Cash-out requests, wallet, amount and bank destination. |
+| 14 | `/portal/developers/tokens` | `DeveloperTokens` | `tokens.read` | API token creation, one-time secret, scopes, IP allowlist and revocation. |
+| 15 | `/portal/credentials` | `Credentials` | `credentials.manage` | Merchant-owned gateway credential sets and environments. |
+| 16 | `/portal/team` | `Team` | `users.manage` | Team members, roles, scopes and authority editing. |
+
+### 3.3 Shell and layout
+
+`merchant-front/src/layouts/default.tsx` mirrors the admin 248/56 shell:
+
+- 56 px app bar with menu toggle, brand, breadcrumbs, guide search, help, theme, AR/EN language controls and account menu.
+- 248 px drawer permanent on desktop and temporary on compact screens.
+- Drawer sections: Overview, Money, Commerce, Developer.
+- Active navigation uses `meta.parentName` or the longest matching path.
+- Guide search pill and `Ctrl+K` open the merchant guide search modal.
+- `?` opens the merchant contextual-help drawer.
+- Operator card shows merchant role and maker/checker dots.
+- Route loading bar and focused main content.
+- Skip link and RTL-aware layout.
+
+Public auth pages use `layouts/auth.tsx`. The POS screen page is still under the `/portal` layout but renders a focused full-height status surface.
+
+### 3.4 Onboarding
+
+`merchant-front/src/pages/onboarding/index.tsx` implements five steps:
+
+1. **Business Profile** — legal/trade name, registration number, tax id, business category, address, contact phone/email, expected monthly volume, currency, website, sales-channel description.
+2. **Beneficial Owners** — full name, ownership percent, national id, date of birth, nationality, PEP/controller flags; total ownership is displayed with decimal.js.
+3. **Documents** — document type, file, expiry; uploads use multipart `POST v1/merchant/onboarding/kyb-documents`. Open revalidation requests get a replacement file and expiry.
+4. **Bank Details** — bank name, account holder, IBAN, account number, SWIFT; payout account must match the approved corporate account policy.
+5. **Review and Submit** — submit with acknowledgement through `POST v1/merchant/onboarding/submit`.
+
+The page loads the current join request and open revalidations, supports profile save, owner creation, document upload and submit, and shows the join status and requested-info state. It is available to every authenticated merchant because `routesAuthorities.Onboarding = []`.
+
+Onboarding completion is not an activation authority: the admin KYB/join-request process and `core-back` decide when a merchant is live.
+
+### 3.5 Wallets and statements
+
+`Wallets` (`/portal/wallets`):
+
+- Lists wallet name, currency, balance, pending, amount due/negative balance, status and last use.
+- Can create a wallet with application, label and currency.
+- Links to the statements route for a wallet.
+- Shows values through `MoneyDisplay`; calculations use decimal utilities.
+
+`Statements` (`/portal/statements`):
+
+- Loads wallets, selects a wallet and one of the last 12 months.
+- Shows opening/closing balance, gross credits, commission, net credits, adjustments, cash-outs, snapshot hash and line items.
+- Exports the statement through `GET v1/merchant/wallets/:id/statements/:month/export`.
+- Uses the shared XLSX pipeline; export is unavailable until a wallet is selected.
+
+The `Statements` route is hidden from navigation without `statements.read`/`statements.export` but has no `routesAuthorities` entry, so a direct URL is not redirected by the merchant router.
+
+### 3.6 Applications
+
+`Applications` (`/portal/applications`):
+
+- Lists applications with status.
+- Edits descriptive fields (display/name, sales-channel description, expected volume).
+- Proposes sensitive changes: assigned wallet, rail whitelist and redirect-domain allowlist.
+- Displays pending/approved status for sensitive proposals.
+- Requires `applications.read`; mutation authority is enforced by the merchant API.
+
+The UI reflects the maker-checker model but does not itself approve changes.
+
+### 3.7 Payment links
+
+`Links` (`/portal/links`):
+
+- Lists links with amount, currency, use count, expiry, state and attempts.
+- Creates a link with description, amount, currency, use count, expiry, redirect URL and rail whitelist.
+- Shows a QR code for the link.
+- Opens an attempts inspector for the link.
+- Cancels a link through `POST v1/merchant/links/:id/cancel`.
+
+The link amount is stored server-side; the checkout page never accepts a client amount or currency. A single-use link can lock its slot while an attempt is in progress.
+
+### 3.8 POS terminals and screens
+
+`PosTerminals` (`/portal/pos`):
+
+- Lists terminals and paired screens.
+- Creates a terminal with name and location.
+- Creates/pairs a screen with a screen name and type.
+- Shows screen role/status and actions.
+
+`PosScreen` (`/portal/pos/screen/:code`):
+
+- Loads the screen state from `GET v1/merchant/pos/screens/:code/stream` and then opens an `EventSource` on the same path.
+- Shows amount, status, rail code, screen code, reference and last update.
+- Shows a live/pending badge and a manual refresh.
+- Is a real-time display surface; it does not initiate or confirm a payment from the screen page.
+
+### 3.9 Payments and disputes
+
+`Payments` (`/portal/payments`):
+
+- Searchable list of payment attempts.
+- Shows reference, rail, status, amount, commission, net, application, creation and confirmation times.
+- Uses `StatusBadge` with success/warning/danger mapping.
+
+`Disputes` (`/portal/disputes`):
+
+- Lists dispute reference, source, state, amount, reason code, evidence deadline and whether evidence was submitted.
+- Opens an evidence dialog with a note and optional file.
+- Submits multipart evidence to `POST v1/merchant/disputes/:id/evidence`.
+- Does not move money; admin finance handles adjustments.
+
+### 3.10 Cash-outs
+
+`Cashouts` (`/portal/cashouts`):
+
+- Lists cash-out state, wallet, amount, currency and request time.
+- Requests a cash-out with wallet, amount, currency and bank details (bank name, account number, optional IBAN).
+- Shows processing states and supports the maker/checker or finance processing status returned by the API.
+- Requires `cashout.read` or `cashout.request` in the UI; the merchant API re-checks.
+
+### 3.11 Developer tokens
+
+`DeveloperTokens` (`/portal/developers/tokens`):
+
+- Lists token name, status, IP-whitelist state and revocation state.
+- Creates a token with name, scopes and optional IP CIDR allowlist.
+- Shows the one-time secret in a dedicated card after creation.
+- Revokes tokens through `DELETE v1/merchant/tokens/:id`.
+- Updates IP allowlists through `PUT v1/merchant/tokens/:id/ips`.
+
+Tokens authenticate the external API (`pg_live_...`); the portal session is separate.
+
+### 3.12 Merchant credentials
+
+`Credentials` (`/portal/credentials`):
+
+- Lists merchant-owned gateway credential sets.
+- Creates/edits credential name, gateway code, environment, settlement target, username, write-only secret, secret reference.
+- Shows whether a secret exists (write-only) and environment/settlement posture.
+- Requires `credentials.manage`.
+
+This supports `MERCHANT_DIRECT` mode, where the merchant's own gateway credentials are used and the platform records commission receivable rather than holding principal cash.
+
+### 3.13 Team and roles
+
+`Team` (`/portal/team`):
+
+- Lists merchant users, roles, status and authority posture.
+- Invites a member with full name, email, phone, role and temporary password.
+- Edits profile/status and scopes/authorities.
+- Sends changes through `PATCH v1/merchant/users/:id` or `POST v1/merchant/users`.
+- Requires `users.manage`.
+
+### 3.14 Guide surfaces
+
+The portal exposes two guide routes plus shell help/search:
+
+- `/portal/guide` (`MerchantGuide`) — operations guide with first-5 checklist, role search/filter, chapter modal, fee calculator, code generator and webhook checks.
+- `/portal/guide/developers` (`MerchantDeveloperGuide`) — D-01..D-05 chapter reader with code templates.
+- Shell guide search (`Ctrl+K`) opens the merchant guide search modal and routes to the relevant chapter.
+- Shell help (`?`) opens the merchant contextual-help drawer with the M/D mapping.
+- The guide is a learning surface and has no route authority entry.
+
+The content and tooling are documented in `01-guide-and-developer-api.md`.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **The merchant SPA talks only to `merchant-back` under `/api`.** It holds no database or core credential.
+2. **The external API uses `pg_live_` bearer tokens, not the portal session.**
+3. **Sensitive application changes are maker-checker proposals.** The current configuration remains active until approved.
+4. **Wallet balances are derived from the ledger.** The portal does not write balances.
+5. **Payment-link amounts are server-authoritative.** The portal sends the intended amount at creation; checkout never supplies it.
+6. **POS screens are display surfaces.** They reflect attempts; they do not create money movement.
+7. **Evidence uploads are multipart and deadline-bound.**
+8. **Credential secrets are write-only after save.**
+9. **Money and exports use decimal.js and the shared XLSX pipeline.**
+10. **The UI authority check is advisory.** `core-back` remains authoritative.
+11. **English and Arabic catalogues remain in sync.**
+

+
+| Surface | Location |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Merchant router | `merchant-front/src/router/index.ts` |

+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Start a merchant: register/login, complete onboarding, wait for KYB approval, then create a wallet/application/link or POS screen.
+- Debug a missing page: check `routesAuthorities` for that route name, then confirm the backend authority. A hidden nav item does not prove the route is gated.
+- Debug a link: use the attempts inspector; confirm the link state and slot behavior before creating a replacement link.
+- Debug a POS screen: check the screen code, the live `EventSource` connection, and the terminal/screen pairing.
+- Debug a dispute: confirm the evidence deadline and that the file is attached; an evidence note without a file may still be accepted but is weaker.
+- Debug API integration: use the developer guide generator, then verify the token, IP allowlist and webhook signature checks.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- 16 protected portal routes and four public routes.
+- 248/56 merchant shell with RTL, theme, search, help and operator card.
+- Onboarding, wallets, statements, applications, links, POS, payments, disputes, cash-outs, tokens, credentials and team pages.
+- Merchant guide and developer guide surfaces.
+- Sensitive application proposal UI and credential/token write-only handling.
+- Shared XLSX export for statements.
+
+### Partial
+
+- `Statements` lacks a router-level authority gate.
+- The guide/developer routes are open learning surfaces, which is intentional but means any authenticated merchant can read them.
+- The portal shows maker/checker posture but does not provide a full pending-change diff workflow for every sensitive object.
+- Google OIDC is listed in the API map but the actual merchant `/auth/google` endpoint returns 501, so no working Google flow ships.
+- Merchant help and guide content are the 10+5 chapter baseline, not guide v2.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No self-service activation override; KYB approval remains admin-controlled.
+- No merchant-side certification/training gate for production authorities.
+- No guide v2 context map/playbook/read tracking.
+- No working Google sign-in.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Authorization gap:** direct navigation to `/portal/statements` is not blocked by the router even when the UI would hide it.
+- **Onboarding risk:** client-side progress and completion are convenience signals, not activation authority.
+- **POS risk:** a displayed `SUCCEEDED` screen is a reflection; the merchant must still follow the server-confirmed payment status and settlement rules.
+- **Documentation risk:** do not describe the portal as having a working Google login or a fully server-enforced route gate.
+- **Guide risk:** merchant chapter content must not be conflated with the admin 12-book guide or guide v2.

+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

+6. **Deep links.** `?chapter=` and `?search=` open a specific chapter or filtered view from the shell search.
+7. **The guide is content, not a live data console.** It explains rules and workflows; live troubleshooting uses the portal, POS screen and API.

+- The fee/net settlement calculator.
+- The developer API code generator.
+- The webhook sample and five verification checks.
+
+#### First-5 checklist behavior
+
+- Persisted in `localStorage` key `merchant-guide-checklist`.
+- On mount, the page calls onboarding, wallets, applications, links, POS terminals and tokens list endpoints.
+- Auto-detects completed steps from successful list responses and the onboarding status (`APPROVED`, `ACTIVE` or `COMPLETED`).
+- Writes the detected state back to localStorage when possible.
+- The user can manually toggle a step; storage failures fall back to in-memory state.
+
+This checklist is a guide aid. It does not grant activation and does not replace the server's onboarding/KYB state.
+
+#### Deep links
+
+- `?search=<term>` pre-fills the search field; `?search=1` is treated as an empty search.
+- `?chapter=<id>` opens that chapter modal if the id exists.
+- The shell guide search routes to `MerchantGuide` with `?chapter=<id>`.
+
+### 3.5 Fee and net settlement calculator
+
+`merchant-front/src/components/guide/MerchantFeeCalculator.tsx` uses `decimal.js` through `toDecimal` and supports:
+
+- Amount, rail, commission percent, gateway fee percent, platform share for split mode.
+- Fee bearers: `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`, `PAYER_SURCHARGE`, `SPLIT`.
+- Results: customer total, platform commission, estimated gateway fee, exact net wallet credit, and payer share in split/surcharge mode.
+
+Formulas:
+
+- Commission = amount × commission%.
+- `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`: customer total = amount; net = amount − commission.
+- `PAYER_SURCHARGE`: customer total = amount + commission; net = amount; payer share = commission.
+- `SPLIT`: payer share = commission × platform share%; customer total = amount + payer share; net = amount − (commission − payer share).
+
+The gateway fee is estimated on the customer total and shown for transparency. The actual wallet credit follows the selected fee-bearer formula and the server's commission/ledger logic. The calculator is local and does not call the commission engine.
+
+### 3.6 Developer API code generator
+
+The operations guide includes a generator with:
+
+- Application ID, bearer token and payment reference inputs.
+- Amount and fee bearer taken from the calculator.
+- Language tabs: TypeScript/Node/Bun, PHP/Laravel, Python/httpx, cURL.
+- Generated calls:
+  - `POST /api/v1/external/links` with `applicationId`, decimal amount, `currency: "LYD"`, `feeBearer`, `infiniteUse`, `useCount`, `redirectUrl`.
+  - `GET /api/v1/external/links/:key` to check `state` and `confirmedCount`.
+  - `GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference`.
+- A sample webhook request with `X-PG-Signature` and a JSON payload.
+
+The generated token is a placeholder/sample and is displayed in the browser. A real token must be created in `/portal/developers/tokens`, scoped, stored server-side, and never committed or shared.
+
+### 3.7 Webhook checks
+
+The guide lists five checks:
+
+1. Reject any webhook without a valid `X-PG-Signature` header.
+2. Recompute the signature over the raw request body and compare in constant time.
+3. Compare amount and currency with the payment you created before fulfilling the order.
+4. Deduplicate by event id so a retried delivery cannot post twice.
+5. Return a 2xx quickly and move slow work to a queue.
+
+The guide also demonstrates the raw-body signing concern: a parsed/re-serialized JSON body can change bytes and break signature verification.
+
+### 3.8 Dedicated developer guide page
+
+`merchant-front/src/pages/guide/developers/index.tsx` renders:
+
+- A PageHeader.
+- A pill list of all five D chapters.
+- The selected chapter title, id badge and Markdown body.
+- A language selector and ready-to-run code templates when present.
+- `?chapter=<id>` deep links.
+
+The page uses the same D-01..D-05 content as the operations guide's developer chapter cards, so the two surfaces stay consistent.
+
+### 3.9 Shell search and contextual help
+
+- The merchant shell `Ctrl+K` opens `GlobalGuideSearchModal`, which searches M/D chapters and routes to the appropriate guide route with `?chapter=`.
+- The shell `?` opens the merchant contextual-help drawer with the route's M/D mapping.
+- The drawer and full guide use the same content modules; the drawer is a narrower, route-specific view.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **Merchant guide content is 10 operations chapters + 5 developer chapters.** Do not split or merge them without updating the content test and the role mapping.
+2. **Roles filter, not authorize.** A role tag controls presentation; the portal route authorities and backend decide access.
+3. **Money calculations use decimal.js.** No floating point in the calculator or generated examples.
+4. **The calculator is illustrative.** It does not replace server commission calculation or ledger posting.
+5. **The code generator is illustrative.** It must not embed a real secret in source control.
+6. **The external API amount is a decimal string.** The generator uses the calculator amount and the server remains authoritative.
+7. **Redirect URLs must be allowlisted.** The guide teaches this; the external API and checkout enforce it.
+8. **Webhook verification uses the raw body.** The guide's signature checks are normative integration guidance.
+9. **First-5 checklist state is local.** It is not a server permission or activation record.
+10. **Guide v2 is not current.** Merchant content remains the 10+5 baseline until a future implementation lands.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Surface | Location |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Operations content | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/merchantOperationsGuide.ts` |
+| Developer content | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/merchantDeveloperApiGuide.ts` |
+| Content types | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/types.ts` |
+| Operations guide page | `merchant-front/src/pages/guide/index.tsx` |

+| External API routes | `/api/v1/external/links`, `/api/v1/external/links/:key`, `/api/v1/external/payments/:reference` |
+| Local storage | `merchant-guide-checklist` |
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Onboarding a merchant: point them at M-01 first; use the first-5 checklist as a training aid, then verify the actual portal state.
+- Debugging an API integration: open D-02, confirm the token and CIDR allowlist, then D-04 and the code generator for the exact request shape.
+- Explaining a payout amount: use the fee calculator with the real commission/fee-bearer configuration; do not treat the estimated gateway fee as the ledger posting.
+- Explaining a dispute: use M-08 and the disputes page; evidence is deadline-bound and money movement remains an admin action.
+- Adding content: extend the typed content modules and keep the role/tag/code-template shape; update the content test when counts change.
+- Deep-linking: use `/portal/guide?chapter=M-06` or `/portal/guide/developers?chapter=D-04` from support messages.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- 10 operations chapters and 5 developer chapters with role tags and bilingual titles/bodies where supplied.
+- First-5 checklist with localStorage persistence and API-based auto-detection.
+- Role-filtered chapter search and modal reader.
+- Decimal.js fee/net settlement calculator with all three fee bearers.
+- Four-language code generator and external API examples.
+- Five webhook verification checks and a raw-body signature example.
+- Dedicated developer guide page with code templates.
+- Shell guide search and contextual help integration.
+
+### Partial
+
+- Arabic coverage is chapter-dependent; some bodies/titles are bilingual and some are not.
+- The calculator's gateway fee is an estimate based on the customer total, not the exact gateway cost.
+- The code generator is a teaching aid; it does not validate the token, scopes or CIDR at generation time.
+- The first-5 checklist can disagree with the server if a list call is stale or fails silently.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No guide v2 content, context map, safeguard cards, playbook or read tracking for merchants.
+- No server-side checklist/progress record for the first-5 flow.
+- No interactive API sandbox that executes calls against a sandbox token.
+- No generated SDK package.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Security risk:** the token field is a plaintext browser input; a real token can be exposed on screen or in a screenshot. Use a scoped test token and rotate it.
+- **Accuracy risk:** the fee calculator's gateway-fee estimate is not the ledger truth.
+- **Training risk:** the first-5 checklist is local and can be manually toggled; it must not be used as proof of activation.
+- **Doc risk:** the 10+5 baseline is current; guide v2 is future and must not be described as shipped.
+

+# Decisions
+
+Architecture and documentation decisions are recorded here. Add a dated ADR entry for every non-trivial decision.
+
+## ADR-0001 — `project-design/` is canonical
+
+- **Date:** 2026-11-03
+- **Status:** accepted
+- **Decision:** `project-design/parts/**` is the editable source of truth. `PROJECT_DESIGN.md`, `STATUS.md`, appendices and `*/blueprint.md` are generated. `design/**` is historical/reference only.
+- **Rationale:** The historical design corpus mixes normative design, delivery logs, aspirational plans and obsolete engine versions. A single generated master plus part metadata gives one authoritative answer and a machine-checkable status.
+- **Consequences:** Agents must update part docs and `TRACKER.md` with code changes. Generated files are never hand-edited.
+
+## ADR-0002 — PostgreSQL 18 is the only runtime database
+
+- **Date:** 2026-11-03
+- **Status:** accepted
+- **Decision:** PostgreSQL 18 (`@prisma/adapter-pg` + `pg`) is the only supported runtime engine. MySQL/MariaDB runtime support and legacy migration history are removed.
+- **Consequences:** Historical MySQL notes remain only in `design/**` with historical labels. `deploy.env` defaults to PostgreSQL 18.
+
+## ADR-0003 — Storage/backup design is as-built, not aspirational
+
+- **Date:** 2026-11-03
+- **Status:** accepted
+- **Decision:** Storage/backup/search/seeder design parts must distinguish implemented behavior from partial/missing features. Read models, replica routing, keyset pagination, audit/log retention and backup drill behavior are documented as they exist, not as the blueprint originally proposed.
+- **Consequences:** P0/P1 gaps stay visible in `TRACKER.md` until the code changes.

+# Glossary and Status Rules
+
+## Vocabulary
+
+| Term | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| **Gateway** | Upstream provider/bank/aggregator catalog record. |
+| **Credential Set** | The pinned credentials and ownership mode used by a gateway version. |
+| **Rail** | Customer-facing payment method. |
+| **Route** | A rail + gateway + credential set + cost/limit/health binding. |
+| **Attempt** | One payment attempt pinned to a gateway version and route. |
+| **GL account** | Double-entry ledger account. |
+| **GL shard** | One row in `gl_account_shards`; system accounts use 16 shards, merchant wallets one. |
+| **Outbox** | `outbox_events` transactional event queue. |
+| **Audit outbox** | `audit_outbox` transactional audit queue shipped to `pg_audit_db`. |
+| **Read model** | `rm_*` projection maintained by the outbox relay. |
+| **LSN** | PostgreSQL WAL location used for replica read-your-writes. |
+| **Drill** | Scratch restore + ledger/audit invariant verification. |
+
+## Status
+
+| Status | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `implemented` | Present, tested and documented without material gaps. |
+| `partial` | Present but with documented gaps or narrow adoption. |
+| `missing` | Designed/expected but absent. |
+| `deferred` | Intentionally postponed with a recorded decision. |
+| `deprecated` | Present but should not be used for new work. |
+| `historical` | Retained for context only. |
+
+## Source-of-truth order
+
+1. Running code and migrations.
+2. Generated appendices (`schema-catalog`, `migration-catalog`, `api-route-matrix`, `env-and-config-matrix`, `test-inventory`).
+3. `project-design/parts/**`.
+4. `project-design/PROJECT_DESIGN.md` (generated).
+5. `design/**` (historical only).
+
+## Naming conventions
+
+- Part IDs: `area.part` (`core.storage`, `deploy.pipeline`, `admin-ui.routes`).
+- Code paths in frontmatter are repository-relative.
+- Design sources are repository-relative and may include `#section` anchors.
+- Generated files carry a `GENERATED FILE` header.

Purpose and scope + +The repository is a multi-rail payment gateway and payment-links platform built around a single database-owning core service. It lets an operator add a gateway by declarative configuration instead of a code release, lets a merchant create payment links and onboard through KYB/AML, and lets an anonymous payer complete a payment through one of the visible rails and collection modes. + +This part owns the product-level overview: the workspaces, product scope, the seven-service topology plus the optional Fake Rails tier, the implemented versus unimplemented capabilities, and the lineage from the historical design corpus to the current code. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) + +The historical corpus describes a national payment switch for the Libyan market with a first-party wallet rail, plus direct and aggregator integrations for the roughly twenty researched gateways. The product is not a simple redirect wrapper: the customer is in the loop, confirmations arrive late, twice, through a browser or through a statement, and money may settle days after the payment attempt. The design therefore adds a declarative flow engine, an attempt state machine, a trusted-confirmation layer and an ownership-aware double-entry ledger on top of the voucher-style provider pattern. + +The stable design intent, corrected where the code has moved on, is: + +1. **Four catalog layers.** A `Gateway` is one technical integration. A `CredentialSet` is whose account and secrets are used, per environment, with an ownership and settlement target. A `Rail` is what the customer sees and chooses. A `Route` binds a rail to a gateway through a credential set with priority, cost, limits, health and scope. +2. **Two independent axes.** Collection mode is what the customer does: `OTP_PULL`, `REDIRECT`, `EMBEDDED`, `PUSH_APPROVAL`, `QR_DISPLAY`, `PAY_CODE`, `DEEP_LINK`, `MANUAL`, `HYBRID`. Confirmation channel is how the platform learns the result: sync response, webhook, inquiry/poll, return URL, browser callback, statement, operator confirmation. +3. **Zero-trust split.** `core-back` is the only service with database credentials, the KMS master key, ledger-posting authority and outbound gateway execution. The edge backends have no database drivers or credentials and call core only over mutual TLS. +4. **Declarative engine plus escape hatch.** The engine supports a closed transform library and declarative phases. A native adapter is the escape hatch for proprietary protocols, but it still goes through the same attempt state machine, inbox, verifier and ledger poster. +5. **Nothing browser-side is trusted.** Widget callbacks and return URLs are hints that trigger a server inquiry. Money is posted only after the trusted-success facts match. +6. **Immutable configuration.** Gateway versions are snapshots; an attempt pins its gateway version, route, credential set and commission profile at creation. +7. **Uncertain outcomes become `UNKNOWN`.** A timeout, reset, 5xx or extraction failure on a money-moving step is not retried blindly. +8. **Ownership-aware ledger.** Platform-held settlement uses gateway clearing accounts; merchant-direct settlement books commission only; internal rails clear through treasury. +9. **Governance and compliance.** Maker-checker, KYB, beneficial-owner screening, AML rules, confidential AML access, disputes, adjustments, cash-outs, reconciliation and reporting are part of the product, not add-ons. +10. **Operational safety.** Durable workers, a webhook inbox, statement reconciliation, backups/PITR drills, and horizontal deployment are part of the architecture. + +The target scale stated in the historical design is a national switch with tens to hundreds of millions of records, `1..N` compute nodes per tier, `0..N` PostgreSQL streaming replicas, PgBouncer in transaction mode, Redis for cache/velocity, dedicated audit and log databases, and 5 to 30+ dedicated hosts. Contracts and invariants + +The platform-level non-negotiables are: + +1. **PostgreSQL 18 is the only runtime database.** The Prisma datasource is `provider = "postgresql"`; the runtime uses `@prisma/adapter-pg` and `pg`; `DATABASE_URL`, replica URLs, audit and log URLs are validated as PostgreSQL URLs in `core-back/lib/env/index.ts`. MySQL and MariaDB support have been removed. +2. **Money is decimal.** Runtime money uses `Decimal`/`decimal.js` and Prisma `NUMERIC(18,4)`; the transform library forbids `to_number` on monetary outputs. +3. **Database exclusivity.** Only `core-back` holds `DATABASE_URL`, database drivers, `KMS_MASTER_KEY`, ledger authority and outbound gateway credentials. Edge backends' package manifests and environment schemas contain no database driver or database URL; their only upstream is `CORE_BACK_URL` / `CORE_BACK_URLS`. +4. **mTLS and channel identity.** `core-back` requires a client certificate signed by the internal CA and binds each internal namespace to one common name: `/internal/admin/*` only `admin-back`, `/internal/merchant/*` only `merchant-back`, `/internal/checkout/*` only `checkout-back`. +5. **Authorities are enforced by core.** Edge checks are advisory. `core-back` re-authenticates the bearer credential, re-reads the user/merchant/authority state from the database, and re-validates payloads. +6. **Maker-checker is server-side.** The approval route and governance execution require a human user, a checker authority, and a checker different from the maker; the database also has a check constraint and a trigger on `approval_requests`. +7. **Atomic critical writes.** The ledger, outbox and audit outbox are written in one transaction on the critical path; the storage engine's `UnitOfWork` owns the commit LSN. +8. **Secrets and confidential data never reach logs.** Vault redaction covers sensitive field names, literal decrypted secrets and Luhn-valid PANs. Edge services never receive the KMS key or database credentials. +9. **Bilingual catalogues stay in sync.** User-facing text is maintained in English and Arabic. +10. **Deploy-time UI flags are runtime-controlled.** The deploy engine writes `showChecklists`/`showSnapshotExportChecklist` and `showHelpPanels` into the admin runtime config and injects the matching `VITE_*` build constants; source builds fall back to the documented defaults. + +## 5. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) + +The historical design defines a seven-service split: + +1. `core-back`: private-LAN mTLS server, sole database owner, KMS and secret owner, dynamic rail engine, ledger, workers and outbound gateway calls. +2. `admin-back`: LAN-only edge BFF with no database driver. +3. `merchant-back`: public-SSL merchant edge BFF with no database driver. +4. `checkout-back`: public-SSL checkout and webhook edge with no database driver. +5. `admin-front`: LAN-only admin SPA. +6. `merchant-front`: public merchant SPA. +7. `checkout-front`: public hosted-checkout SPA. + +`fake-rails-back` and `fake-rails-front` are an optional eighth and ninth workspace used for sandbox and testing; they are not part of the production seven-service core. + +The design also defines the network zones: + +- Public internet reaches only the merchant and checkout reverse proxies on `80/443`. It serves the admin SPA and forwards `/api` to `admin-back`. +- All three edge backends call `core-back` over a private LAN with mTLS 1.3 client certificates. +- `core-back` is never published by a reverse proxy and has no public listener. +- `core-back` reaches PostgreSQL, Redis, the audit database, the log database and external gateways. +- The backup daemon is a separate mTLS control plane, normally `:4090`, with backup storage in S3/MinIO/R2 and an optional secondary vault. + +The historical target for compute is `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES` and `CHECKOUT_NODES` arrays, each entry shaped `nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`. Every journal entry must have at least one debit and one credit, debit total must equal credit total, and every line amount must be strictly positive. `validateTemplate` enforces this before insertion (`LedgerPoster.ts:740`). +2. `(refType, refId)` is unique. Posting is idempotent for that pair. A duplicate returns the existing entry with `created: false`, `idempotent: true`, and an empty `lines` array. +3. Money is `Decimal(18,4)`; no floating-point arithmetic is used in posting or validation. +4. Journal lines are append-only. The application exposes no update or delete path, and retention deliberately excludes `journal_entries` and `journal_lines`. +5. A zero optional leg is omitted rather than booked as a zero line (`optionalLine`, `LedgerPoster.ts:252`). +6. Account resolution never invents an account: a missing scoped account falls back only to the same type and currency, and then fails with `GL_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`. +7. Shard projection is in the same transaction as the journal line. A shard balance is the signed sum of every line projected to that shard; the natural balance negates credit-positive accounts. +8. A checkpoint is a snapshot, not a replacement for journal lines. A live balance is checkpoint plus later lines. A checkpoint must serialize against postings to the same account. +9. The invariant equation is the authoritative system-wide check. A non-zero drift is an operational incident and opens a P1 case. +10. Adjustment, refund, chargeback, cash-out, AML release/void, and suspense postings use the same ledger and the same idempotency contract. + +## 5. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) + +The design defines ten roles (`GATEWAY_ADMIN`, `SECURITY_ADMIN`, `FINANCE`, `OPERATOR`, `COMPLIANCE`, `MLRO`, `SUPPORT`, `MERCHANT_ADMIN`, `MERCHANT_STAFF`, `MERCHANT_CASHIER`), a closed `authorities_map` catalogue, and a single `approval_requests` wrapper for every sensitive action. The intended lifecycle is `DRAFT -> PENDING_REVIEW -> APPROVED -> EXECUTED`, with a rejection returning to `DRAFT`. Maker and checker must differ, and the database enforces this with a `CHECK` constraint and an update trigger. + +The design's four-eyes matrix covers: + +| Action | Intended maker | Intended checker | +| :--- | :--- | :--- | +| Adjustment (refund, chargeback, manual credit/debit, correction) | `FINANCE`, `OPERATOR`, or system drafting | `FINANCE`, different user | +| Cash-out completion/subtraction | `FINANCE` | `FINANCE`, different user | +| Commission profile create/change | `FINANCE` | `FINANCE` or `SECURITY_ADMIN` | +| Sensitive merchant fields | `OPERATOR`, `COMPLIANCE`, or merchant request | `COMPLIANCE` or `FINANCE` by field domain | +| Sensitive application fields | merchant admin or operator | operator or compliance | +| Velocity and AML rules | `COMPLIANCE`/`FINANCE` | `MLRO` for AML; `SECURITY_ADMIN`/`FINANCE` for velocity | +| AML case release/void/freeze | `COMPLIANCE` | `MLRO` | +| Regulatory report submission | `COMPLIANCE` | `MLRO` | +| Join-request decision | `OPERATOR`/`COMPLIANCE` | per `join_request.four_eyes_policy` | +| Merchant suspension | `OPERATOR`/`COMPLIANCE` | emergency ratification within 24 h | +| Merchant reinstatement | `OPERATOR`/`COMPLIANCE` | `COMPLIANCE`/`MLRO`, never emergency | +| Gateway version go-live and credential changes | `GATEWAY_ADMIN` | `SECURITY_ADMIN` | +| Admin user/role/authority changes | `SECURITY_ADMIN` | another `SECURITY_ADMIN` | +| `platform_settings` compliance keys | `COMPLIANCE`/`FINANCE` | `MLRO`/`SECURITY_ADMIN` | + +The design also specifies the onboarding state machine, KYB document controls, field classification and pending-change semantics, the seven-layer AML program, declarative AML rules, dispute intake and automated drafting, regulatory reporting as configuration, operator cases, and strict no-tipping-off rules. + +## 3. As-built architecture + +### 3.1 Authority model + +Authentication is bearer-token based (`core-back/api/middleware/authDoubleCheck.ts`). A session resolves the user's `authoritiesMap`; an API token resolves its `scopes` and optional IP allowlist. Empty authorities are rejected for a session. `requireAuthorities` accepts a request if the principal has any one of the listed authorities or `*`; it is an OR check, not an AND check. + +`actorFromRequest` requires a human user, rejects the `SYSTEM_AUTOMATION` role, and marks the actor as a checker only when `approval:check` is present (`core-back/api/middleware/makerCheckerGuard.ts:13`). `assertCheckerIsNotMaker` is reused by the admin routes. + +The seeded production roles are inconsistent with the design matrix: only `FINANCE` receives `approval:check` and `approval:write`; `COMPLIANCE`, `MLRO`, `OPERATOR`, `SECURITY_ADMIN`, and `SUPPORT` do not (`core-back/prisma/seed.ts:160`). The approval route therefore cannot be exercised as designed by the seeded compliance roles without a custom authority grant. + +### 3.2 Approval lifecycle as implemented + +`ApprovalService` (`core-back/engine/governance/ApprovalService.ts:270`): + +- `proposeApproval` validates the maker, JSON patch shape, and base version, then creates the row directly in `PENDING_REVIEW` (not `DRAFT`); `DRAFT` exists in the enum and UI filters but most producers do not use it. +- `approveRequest` allows a request in `PENDING_REVIEW` or `APPROVED`, rejects maker = checker, verifies `baseVersion`, applies the patch callback, executes the handler callback, and sets `EXECUTED` (or `APPROVED` when `executeImmediately === false`). +- `rejectRequest` requires a reason and sets `REJECTED`; it does not return the request to `DRAFT`. +- `emergencyExecuteWithRatification` executes immediately without a checker, records `EMERGENCY_RATIFICATION`, and sets a ratification deadline. +- permits `PENDING_REVIEW` or `DRAFT`; +- rejects expired requests; +- enforces maker ≠ checker; +- adds a join-request admin-assisted maker check and a merchant payload checker-domain check; +- special-cases `BACKUP_POLICY` through the backup daemon; Emergency suspension writes status field rows tied to the approval (`admin.ts:5511`). The implemented log therefore has narrower coverage than the design's “every edit, with source/request/IP” semantics, and the actor recorded for a sensitive change is the checker rather than the maker. + +### 3.5 Onboarding and KYB + +The join-request state machine is implemented in `core-back/api/internal/admin.ts`: + +- admin-assisted creation starts in `DRAFT`; submit performs profile/owner/document checks, runs onboarding screening, computes the four-eyes decision, refreshes duplicate flags, and sets `SUBMITTED`, `IN_REVIEW`, or a screening outcome; +- assign moves to `IN_REVIEW`; +- request-info pauses the SLA by storing `slaPausedAt` and `slaRemainingSeconds` and sets `INFO_REQUESTED`; +- decide enforces readiness, blocks open confirmed-match cases, creates an approval when `fourEyesRequired`, or executes approval/rejection inline when it is not; +- withdraw invalidates a pending approval and sets `WITHDRAWN`; +- `JoinRequestExpiryWorker` expires abandoned drafts and overdue reviews. + +Readiness (`core-back/lib/joinRequestOnboarding.ts:249`) requires the canonical checklist, required accepted and unexpired documents, active beneficial owners meeting the ownership threshold, owner screening status, a non-blocked screening result, and a payout bank; it reports `approvalPending` separately rather than adding it to `blockers`. Duplicate detection compares tax id, registration, phone, and e-mail and hashes the payout account, owner national id, and document SHA-256 (`joinRequestOnboarding.ts:84`). + +The four-eyes decision (`core-back/api/internal/merchant.ts:358`) reads `join_request.four_eyes_policy` and supports `ALWAYS`, `RISK_BASED`, and `NEVER`. Risk-based triggers include high risk tier, any screening match list, PEP owners, large ownership share, high-risk category, previous rejection, duplicate/related flags, payout owner mismatch, and expected volume above threshold. + +KYB controls (`core-back/lib/kybReview.ts`) implement expiry state, actionable-document rules, duplicate justification, payout-holder name comparison, configurable required documents, refresh policy, and KYB status recomputation. `KybExpiryWorker` marks expired documents, queues 30/7-day notices, suspends after the grace period, starts periodic revalidations, and expires overdue revalidation requests. + +### 3.6 AML program + +The seven design layers map to code as follows: + +| Layer | Actual implementation | +| :--- | :--- | +| L1 onboarding screening | `MerchantScreeningService.submitOnboarding`, called from join-request submit; confirmed match raises a case and blocks activation; provider error fails closed. | +| L2 ongoing screening | `PeriodicScreeningWorker` re-screens active merchants on the configured interval, refreshes list versions, raises one confirmed-match case and suspends the merchant. | +| L3 transaction-time posture | `AttemptGuardPipeline` checks merchant status, velocity, local watch-list, and AML rules inside the attempt-creation transaction; a confirmed sanctions match or a `BLOCK` rule creates a terminal blocked attempt. | +| L4 transaction monitoring | AML rules are evaluated at attempt initiation. Submission is not integrated with an authority adapter. | +| L7 record keeping | Audit rows, rule versions, detail changes, and the retention worker. Retention is opt-in and incomplete for AML evidence. | + +Screening is a provider interface (`ScreeningProvider`) with Arabic normalization, name similarity, internal watch-list provider, mock provider, and a cached provider. `MerchantScreeningService` persists `aml_screenings` and `aml_screening_matches` with list versions and input hashes, applies owner screening status, and raises a confirmed-match case only. Potential matches remain in the screening queue for disposition. + +The AML rule engine (`core-back/engine/guards/AmlRuleEngine.ts`) supports `SINGLE_AMOUNT`, `CUMULATIVE_WINDOW`, `STRUCTURING`, `RISK_TIER`, `COUNTERPARTY_COUNTRY`, `RAIL`, and `MERCHANT_DIRECT_AMOUNT`; actions are `HOLD`, `FLAG`, `BLOCK`, `CASE_ONLY`. Severity starts at the rule base, correlates with velocity, raises for high merchant tier, volume multiple, another open case, confirmed sanctions, and potential PEP. On a `HOLD`, the guard posts `Dr GATEWAY_CLEARING` / `Cr AML_HOLD` and stores the hold journal entry on the case. + +AML case resolution (`GovernanceExecution.ts:1470`): + +- `RELEASE` posts `AML_HOLD_AND_RELEASE` release lines, sets attempt `SUCCEEDED`, commits the link slot. +- `REJECT` posts `AML_VOID`, sets attempt `FAILED`, releases the slot. +- `ESCALATE` leaves the money in `AML_HOLD`, sets `ESCALATED_STR`, and opens a P1 operator case. +- `HOLD` freezes the case without moving money. +- `MERCHANT_DIRECT` cases never post. + +### 3.7 Disputes and adjustments + +Dispute intake is exposed as `POST /admin/disputes`; the route queues an `ADJUSTMENT_EXECUTION` job with `kind: DISPUTE_INTAKE` and answers `202`. The worker transaction calls `openDisputeWithDraftedAdjustment` (`core-back/engine/workers/BackgroundJobHandlers.ts:359`), which: + +1. dedupes on `(gatewayId, externalDisputeRef)`; +2. locks the attempt, caps the chargeback to the unrefunded amount; +3. creates the dispute; +4. creates a `CHARGEBACK` adjustment in `PENDING_REVIEW` and a `SYSTEM_AUTOMATION` approval request; +5. posts the reserve leg for non-`MERCHANT_DIRECT` settlements; +6. writes audit rows. + +There is no webhook or statement dispute-intake wiring in `DynamicRailEngine` or reconciliation; the admin manual route is the implemented intake path. + +Adjustment execution supports `REFUND` (three phases: claim, gateway refund, finalize), `CHARGEBACK` (won/lost/insufficient), `CORRECTION` (fee variance), `MANUAL_DEBIT`/`CASHOUT_SUBTRACTION` (cash-out template), and `MANUAL_CREDIT` (internal confirmation with zero commission). Chargebacks require a finance checker; a missing dispute outcome or a breach of `negativeBalanceCeiling` holds the adjustment and opens an operator case. Refunds are capped to the unrefunded settled amount and are idempotent on the adjustment id. + +### 3.8 Cash-outs + +A merchant creates a `CashoutRequest` in `PENDING` with a destination bank snapshot (`core-back/api/internal/merchant.ts:1828`). Evaluation is idempotent per rule and attempt, and the confirmation path calls it after a successful settlement. + +Manual report creation (`createRegulatoryReportViaApproval`) creates a `PENDING_CHECKER` report and a `REGULATORY_REPORT` approval in one transaction. Cancellation, run-now, and retry update the schedule and the attempt's `nextCheckAt`; the poll worker owns execution and schedule reconciliation. + +### 3.11 Tipping-off and confidentiality + +`core-back/engine/compliance/tippingOff.ts` rejects non-`INTERNAL` notification templates whose subject or body references AML variables, redacts AML-like payload keys for non-`INTERNAL` classes, and renders templates. Every `/admin/aml/*` route calls `assertConfidential`. Reporting submission/acknowledgement additionally calls `assertReportingAuthority`. This gate is not applied to the generic `/admin/approvals/:id` route, so a principal with `approval:check` can approve an `AML_CASE` without confidential AML access. + +## 4. Contracts and invariants + +1. Maker and checker must be different users. The database has `approval_requests_checker_not_maker_insert` plus an update trigger; the application also checks. +2. `SYSTEM_AUTOMATION` can be a maker (for dispute drafts) but can never be a checker, ratifier, or human actor. +3. An approval can only execute from `DRAFT`/`PENDING_REVIEW` in the admin route, must not be expired, and a base-versioned approval must match the subject's current version or fail with `BASE_VERSION_MISMATCH`. +4. A rejection requires a reason and never executes. +5. A successful approval must execute its subject atomically with the state change where the handler supports it. Adjustments are queued; the job uses the checker recorded on the approval and never invents one. +6. AML release/void is the only writer for an `AML_HOLD` attempt. The expiry sweeper and customer cancel exclude held attempts. +7. A chargeback execution requires a finance checker; a chargeback without a known outcome or above the negative-balance ceiling is held, not posted. +8. A refund cannot exceed the unrefunded settled amount. A repeated refund is idempotent through the adjustment state and `(refType, refId)`. +9. `PROVISIONAL` reporting rules can create internal drafts but can never produce a live filing; submission requires `APPROVED` and a `CONFIRMED` rule. +10. Non-`INTERNAL` notification templates cannot reference AML variables. +11. AML data is restricted to confidential roles at the `/aml/*` routes; support cannot read it. + +## 5. Operational usage + +### Applying a sensitive change + +1. The maker calls the domain route (`propose-edit`, `suspend`, `aml/cases/:id/propose`, `operator-cases/:id/resolve`, `aml/reports`, etc.). +2. The route validates the request, creates the approval row, and returns `202` with the approval id. +3. A checker opens `GET /admin/approvals/:id`, reviews the subject context and diff, and calls `POST /admin/approvals/:id/approve` with the optional checklist. +4. The handler executes in the approval transaction. Adjustments are queued and executed by `BackgroundJobWorker`; the response is `202` with a job id. +5. Rejection records a reason and leaves the subject in its pre-approval state, except for audit/lifecycle side effects. + +### Onboarding + +1. Create the admin-assisted join request, add beneficial owners and KYB documents, then submit. +2. Fix any readiness blockers: required documents, owner threshold/screening, checklist, payout bank, duplicate justification. +3. If four-eyes is required, decide as maker and approve in the approvals queue; otherwise the decide route activates or rejects directly. +4. KYB expiry and periodic revalidation are handled by `KybExpiryWorker`. + +### AML case + +1. The guard or onboarding service creates the case and, for a platform-held hold, the escrow posting. +2. Compliance proposes `HOLD`/`RELEASE`/`REJECT`/`ESCALATE` through `/aml/cases/:id/propose`. +3. A checker approves. Release/void posts the ledger and finalises the attempt; escalate opens an operator case. +4. A potential screening match is dispositioned directly through `/aml/matches/:id/disposition`; that route is confidential-gated but is not an approval. + +### Regulatory report + +1. Let `ReportingRuleEvaluator` create a report on settlement, or draft one manually through `/aml/reports`. +2. Approve the `REGULATORY_REPORT` request. +3. Submit through `/aml/reports/:id/submit` with a submission reference, then acknowledge. + +## 7. Status and deviations + +### Implemented + +- Maker/checker separation at service, route, and database levels; approval queue, summary, export, detail, approve, reject, and checklists. +- Governance execution for join requests, merchants, adjustments, cash-out execution, AML cases, operator cases, regulatory reports/rules, AML rules, commission expiry, velocity deactivation, users, gateway versions, and backup policy. +- Onboarding readiness, KYB review/revalidation, duplicate detection, four-eyes policy, screening provider abstraction, Arabic normalization, L1/L2/L3 screening, AML rule engine, cases, hold escrow, release/void. +- Dispute drafting with system maker and human checker, chargeback outcomes, negative-balance ceiling, regulatory report approval/submission/acknowledgement, operator cases, persisted inquiry schedules. +- Tipping-off template guard, AML payload redaction, and the confidential AML route gate. + +### Partial + +- **Approval coverage** — several sensitive actions are direct or lack execution handlers. Application-sensitive changes cannot complete through approvals; platform settings bypass approvals; cash-out processing is a direct route; commission-profile creation and velocity-rule creation are direct. +- **Approval lifecycle** — `DRAFT` is largely unused, rejections do not return to `DRAFT`, and emergency ratification records a note but does not run a second execution. +- **Domain checker enforcement** — only merchant payloads get a role-domain check. AML, reports, users, gateway versions, and platform settings do not enforce their intended checker roles in the dispatcher. +- **Detail change log** — descriptive and approved merchant edits are logged; other entities and the `DetailChangeService` redaction/diff pipeline are not fully wired. +- **AML L4** — rule evaluation happens at attempt creation, not at confirmation or in batch analytics. There is no structuring batch job, no rule dry-run, and no 24-hour emergency tightening workflow. +- **Retention** — the worker is opt-in, does not purge AML cases/screenings/KYB documents/regulatory reports, and keeps the ledger. +- **Dispute intake** — manual admin intake is implemented; webhook and statement channels are not wired. +- **Cash-out lifecycle** — `PROCESSING` and `SUBTRACTED` are not used by the execute path. + +### Missing / deferred + +- `executeApprovalSubject` handlers for `APPLICATION`, `CASHOUT_REQUEST`, and `PLATFORM_SETTING`. +- Approval rows for cash-out processing and platform-setting changes. +- Domain-scoped checker authority (`approvals.domains` equivalent). +- Maker-checker for commission-profile creation/change and velocity-rule creation. +- Deferred/batch AML monitoring and rule dry-run. +- Retention of AML/KYB/reporting evidence by the worker. +- Regulatory authority filing adapters. + +### Known bugs / risks + +- **Security gap:** the generic approval route is not confidential-gated. Purpose and scope + +This part owns the stateless background loops that drain durable work in `core-back`: attempt expiry and polling, inbound inbox processing, notification delivery, ledger invariant checks, onboarding expiry, periodic screening, KYB lifecycle, record retention, the durable background-job queue, the transactional outbox relay, and the audit shipper. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) + +The design requires stateless worker processes that use PostgreSQL as the durable timer and queue: + +- `payment_attempts.expires_at` and `next_check_at` are polled by stateless workers using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; an expiring attempt is asked (`inquire`) before it expires when the route supports inquiry. +- `inbound_events` is drained by an inbox worker so webhook processing is inbox-first and deduplicated; `notifications` is a transactional outbox drained by a sender. +- Terminal transitions are applied at most once with a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE terminal_at IS NULL`, and the double-entry invariant is checked continuously. +- Statement reconciliation and dispute/adjustment execution use a durable queue with leases, backoff, and crash recovery. +- The retention worker removes evidence after the configured period without moving a balance; the transactional outbox maintains read models, and the audit outbox ships audit rows to a dedicated audit database with a hash chain. + +The design also presents realtime fan-out as event-driven. Contracts and invariants + +1. A worker tick must not overlap with itself in the same process. Multiple nodes are allowed; claims use `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. +2. Terminal attempt transitions are conditional on `terminal_at IS NULL`, so the same attempt is not expired, failed, or cancelled twice. +3. An `AML_HOLD` attempt is excluded from expiry sweeping, and the sweeper has a defense-in-depth check on `substatus`. +4. An expiring inquiry-capable attempt is asked before it is expired. An inquiry failure keeps it open (`UNKNOWN`/deferred) rather than silently expiring it. +5. A background job is executed at most once per claim, but handlers must be idempotent because a lease can expire and re-queue a job after a crash. +6. A notification delivery failure re-queues with backoff up to the attempt cap; a missing or tipping-off template is retried up to that cap and then marked `FAILED`. +7. The invariant worker opens at most one open `MISMATCH`/`P1` case for drift. +8. Retention never deletes ledger entries or lines and never deletes a terminal attempt whose ledger entry is missing; it stops rather than risk orphaning evidence. +9. Statement upload and dispute intake are queue-only; the service refuses to start if no background-job drain is enabled. +10. The notification worker never sends an AML variable to a non-`INTERNAL` template. +11. Outbox processing marks `processed_at`; the audit shipper marks `shipped_at`. Neither deletes rows. +12. SSE stream contract: checkout status ends on a terminal status or a 10-minute deadline; POS stream ends on a 15-minute deadline; both poll the database. + +## 5.
