+# Merchant Portal
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the merchant-facing portal in `merchant-front`: its routes, authentication entry points, 248/56 shell, onboarding flow, wallet/application/link/POS/payment/dispute/cash-out/token/credential/team pages, and the guide surfaces that are implemented in this workspace.
+
+It does not own the merchant edge API (`merchant-back`), the merchant external API (`/api/v1/external/*`), or the merchant guide content in detail. The guide and developer API are covered in `01-guide-and-developer-api.md`. Checkout is covered in `05-checkout-front/**`.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The merchant portal is the self-service business workspace:
+
+1. **One merchant identity, many applications.** A merchant owns wallets and applications; each application maps to a wallet and controls the rails/redirect domains used by its links.
+2. **KYB before live money.** A merchant can prepare onboarding and use sandbox behavior while pending, but live activation follows KYB approval.
+3. **Wallet balances are ledger-derived.** The portal shows available, pending and negative amounts; it never edits a balance column.
+4. **Sensitive changes are governed.** Descriptive application/merchant fields can change directly; wallet assignment, rail whitelist and redirect allowlist are sensitive and require review.
+5. **Links are server-priced.** The checkout cannot change the amount; the merchant link record is the price authority.
+6. **POS is a real-time surface.** A paired screen reflects the current payment state and must not be treated as a payment authority.
+7. **Disputes are evidence workflows.** The merchant uploads evidence before the deadline; money movement remains an admin finance action.
+8. **API tokens are scoped secrets.** Tokens are shown once, can be revoked, and can be constrained by IP CIDR allowlists.
+9. **Help is merchant-specific.** The shell exposes merchant guild search/help, not the admin 12-book guide.
+10. **All money and spreadsheet output uses decimal.js and the shared XLSX pipeline.**
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Public and protected routes
+
+`merchant-front/src/router/index.ts` defines:
+
+- Public `/` (`Landing`), `/login` (`Login`), `/register` (`Register`), and a catch-all `NotFound`.
+- A protected `/portal` parent using `layouts/default`, with 16 children.
+- A visitor guard for login/register and a landing-to-dashboard redirect for authenticated users.
+- A `routesAuthorities` check after authentication; missing/empty authority arrays mean no UI gate.
+- A dynamic-import retry path using `localStorage`.
+
+### 3.2 The 16 portal routes
+
+| # | Path | Name | UI authority | Purpose |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| 1 | `/portal/dashboard` | `Dashboard` | `stats.read` | Wallet balance, period volume, success rate, pending cash-outs, charts and recent payments. |
+| 2 | `/portal/onboarding` | `Onboarding` | `[]` (authenticated only) | Five-step KYB/onboarding: profile, owners, documents, payout, submit; revalidation requests. |
+| 3 | `/portal/guide` | `MerchantGuide` | none | Merchant operations guide, role-filtered chapters, first-5 checklist, fee calculator, code generator, webhook checks. |
+| 4 | `/portal/guide/developers` | `MerchantDeveloperGuide` | none | Developer API chapters D-01..D-05 with code templates. |
+| 5 | `/portal/wallets` | `Wallets` | `wallets.read` | Wallet balances, pending/negative amounts, last use, create wallet, statements shortcut. |
+| 6 | `/portal/statements` | `Statements` | **none (gap)** | Monthly statement by wallet/month, line items, snapshot hash and XLSX export. |
+| 7 | `/portal/applications` | `Applications` | `applications.read` | Application list, profile edits, wallet assignment, rail whitelist and redirect allowlist proposals. |
+| 8 | `/portal/links` | `Links` | `links.read` | Create/cancel links, QR, attempts inspector, redirect URL and rail whitelist. |
+| 9 | `/portal/pos` | `PosTerminals` | `pos.manage` or `pos.operate` | Terminals, screens and pairing. |
+| 10 | `/portal/pos/screen/:code` | `PosScreen` | `pos.manage` or `pos.operate` | Realtime customer-facing screen for a paired terminal. |
+| 11 | `/portal/payments` | `Payments` | `payments.read` | Payment attempts, status, amount, commission, net and application. |
+| 12 | `/portal/disputes` | `Disputes` | `payments.read` | Chargeback list, evidence deadline/status and evidence upload. |
+| 13 | `/portal/cashouts` | `Cashouts` | `cashout.read` or `cashout.request` | Cash-out requests, wallet, amount and bank destination. |
+| 14 | `/portal/developers/tokens` | `DeveloperTokens` | `tokens.read` | API token creation, one-time secret, scopes, IP allowlist and revocation. |
+| 15 | `/portal/credentials` | `Credentials` | `credentials.manage` | Merchant-owned gateway credential sets and environments. |
+| 16 | `/portal/team` | `Team` | `users.manage` | Team members, roles, scopes and authority editing. |
+
+### 3.3 Shell and layout
+
+`merchant-front/src/layouts/default.tsx` mirrors the admin 248/56 shell:
+
+- 56 px app bar with menu toggle, brand, breadcrumbs, guide search, help, theme, AR/EN language controls and account menu.
+- 248 px drawer permanent on desktop and temporary on compact screens.
+- Drawer sections: Overview, Money, Commerce, Developer.
+- Active navigation uses `meta.parentName` or the longest matching path.
+- Guide search pill and `Ctrl+K` open the merchant guide search modal.
+- `?` opens the merchant contextual-help drawer.
+- Operator card shows merchant role and maker/checker dots.
+- Route loading bar and focused main content.
+- Skip link and RTL-aware layout.
+
+Public auth pages use `layouts/auth.tsx`. The POS screen page is still under the `/portal` layout but renders a focused full-height status surface.
+
+### 3.4 Onboarding
+
+`merchant-front/src/pages/onboarding/index.tsx` implements five steps:
+
+1. **Business Profile** — legal/trade name, registration number, tax id, business category, address, contact phone/email, expected monthly volume, currency, website, sales-channel description.
+2. **Beneficial Owners** — full name, ownership percent, national id, date of birth, nationality, PEP/controller flags; total ownership is displayed with decimal.js.
+3. **Documents** — document type, file, expiry; uploads use multipart `POST v1/merchant/onboarding/kyb-documents`. Open revalidation requests get a replacement file and expiry.
+4. **Bank Details** — bank name, account holder, IBAN, account number, SWIFT; payout account must match the approved corporate account policy.
+5. **Review and Submit** — submit with acknowledgement through `POST v1/merchant/onboarding/submit`.
+
+The page loads the current join request and open revalidations, supports profile save, owner creation, document upload and submit, and shows the join status and requested-info state. It is available to every authenticated merchant because `routesAuthorities.Onboarding = []`.
+
+Onboarding completion is not an activation authority: the admin KYB/join-request process and `core-back` decide when a merchant is live.
+
+### 3.5 Wallets and statements
+
+`Wallets` (`/portal/wallets`):
+
+- Lists wallet name, currency, balance, pending, amount due/negative balance, status and last use.
+- Can create a wallet with application, label and currency.
+- Links to the statements route for a wallet.
+- Shows values through `MoneyDisplay`; calculations use decimal utilities.
+
+`Statements` (`/portal/statements`):
+
+- Loads wallets, selects a wallet and one of the last 12 months.
+- Shows opening/closing balance, gross credits, commission, net credits, adjustments, cash-outs, snapshot hash and line items.
+- Exports the statement through `GET v1/merchant/wallets/:id/statements/:month/export`.
+- Uses the shared XLSX pipeline; export is unavailable until a wallet is selected.
+
+The `Statements` route is hidden from navigation without `statements.read`/`statements.export` but has no `routesAuthorities` entry, so a direct URL is not redirected by the merchant router.
+
+### 3.6 Applications
+
+`Applications` (`/portal/applications`):
+
+- Lists applications with status.
+- Edits descriptive fields (display/name, sales-channel description, expected volume).
+- Proposes sensitive changes: assigned wallet, rail whitelist and redirect-domain allowlist.
+- Displays pending/approved status for sensitive proposals.
+- Requires `applications.read`; mutation authority is enforced by the merchant API.
+
+The UI reflects the maker-checker model but does not itself approve changes.
+
+### 3.7 Payment links
+
+`Links` (`/portal/links`):
+
+- Lists links with amount, currency, use count, expiry, state and attempts.
+- Creates a link with description, amount, currency, use count, expiry, redirect URL and rail whitelist.
+- Shows a QR code for the link.
+- Opens an attempts inspector for the link.
+- Cancels a link through `POST v1/merchant/links/:id/cancel`.
+
+The link amount is stored server-side; the checkout page never accepts a client amount or currency. A single-use link can lock its slot while an attempt is in progress.
+
+### 3.8 POS terminals and screens
+
+`PosTerminals` (`/portal/pos`):
+
+- Lists terminals and paired screens.
+- Creates a terminal with name and location.
+- Creates/pairs a screen with a screen name and type.
+- Shows screen role/status and actions.
+
+`PosScreen` (`/portal/pos/screen/:code`):
+
+- Loads the screen state from `GET v1/merchant/pos/screens/:code/stream` and then opens an `EventSource` on the same path.
+- Shows amount, status, rail code, screen code, reference and last update.
+- Shows a live/pending badge and a manual refresh.
+- Is a real-time display surface; it does not initiate or confirm a payment from the screen page.
+
+### 3.9 Payments and disputes
+
+`Payments` (`/portal/payments`):
+
+- Searchable list of payment attempts.
+- Shows reference, rail, status, amount, commission, net, application, creation and confirmation times.
+- Uses `StatusBadge` with success/warning/danger mapping.
+
+`Disputes` (`/portal/disputes`):
+
+- Lists dispute reference, source, state, amount, reason code, evidence deadline and whether evidence was submitted.
+- Opens an evidence dialog with a note and optional file.
+- Submits multipart evidence to `POST v1/merchant/disputes/:id/evidence`.
+- Does not move money; admin finance handles adjustments.
+
+### 3.10 Cash-outs
+
+`Cashouts` (`/portal/cashouts`):
+
+- Lists cash-out state, wallet, amount, currency and request time.
+- Requests a cash-out with wallet, amount, currency and bank details (bank name, account number, optional IBAN).
+- Shows processing states and supports the maker/checker or finance processing status returned by the API.
+- Requires `cashout.read` or `cashout.request` in the UI; the merchant API re-checks.
+
+### 3.11 Developer tokens
+
+`DeveloperTokens` (`/portal/developers/tokens`):
+
+- Lists token name, status, IP-whitelist state and revocation state.
+- Creates a token with name, scopes and optional IP CIDR allowlist.
+- Shows the one-time secret in a dedicated card after creation.
+- Revokes tokens through `DELETE v1/merchant/tokens/:id`.
+- Updates IP allowlists through `PUT v1/merchant/tokens/:id/ips`.
+
+Tokens authenticate the external API (`pg_live_...`); the portal session is separate.
+
+### 3.12 Merchant credentials
+
+`Credentials` (`/portal/credentials`):
+
+- Lists merchant-owned gateway credential sets.
+- Creates/edits credential name, gateway code, environment, settlement target, username, write-only secret, secret reference.
+- Shows whether a secret exists (write-only) and environment/settlement posture.
+- Requires `credentials.manage`.
+
+This supports `MERCHANT_DIRECT` mode, where the merchant's own gateway credentials are used and the platform records commission receivable rather than holding principal cash.
+
+### 3.13 Team and roles
+
+`Team` (`/portal/team`):
+
+- Lists merchant users, roles, status and authority posture.
+- Invites a member with full name, email, phone, role and temporary password.
+- Edits profile/status and scopes/authorities.
+- Sends changes through `PATCH v1/merchant/users/:id` or `POST v1/merchant/users`.
+- Requires `users.manage`.
+
+### 3.14 Guide surfaces
+
+The portal exposes two guide routes plus shell help/search:
+
+- `/portal/guide` (`MerchantGuide`) — operations guide with first-5 checklist, role search/filter, chapter modal, fee calculator, code generator and webhook checks.
+- `/portal/guide/developers` (`MerchantDeveloperGuide`) — D-01..D-05 chapter reader with code templates.
+- Shell guide search (`Ctrl+K`) opens the merchant guide search modal and routes to the relevant chapter.
+- Shell help (`?`) opens the merchant contextual-help drawer with the M/D mapping.
+- The guide is a learning surface and has no route authority entry.
+
+The content and tooling are documented in `01-guide-and-developer-api.md`.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **The merchant SPA talks only to `merchant-back` under `/api`.** It holds no database or core credential.
+2. **The external API uses `pg_live_` bearer tokens, not the portal session.**
+3. **Sensitive application changes are maker-checker proposals.** The current configuration remains active until approved.
+4. **Wallet balances are derived from the ledger.** The portal does not write balances.
+5. **Payment-link amounts are server-authoritative.** The portal sends the intended amount at creation; checkout never supplies it.
+6. **POS screens are display surfaces.** They reflect attempts; they do not create money movement.
+7. **Evidence uploads are multipart and deadline-bound.**
+8. **Credential secrets are write-only after save.**
+9. **Money and exports use decimal.js and the shared XLSX pipeline.**
+10. **The UI authority check is advisory.** `core-back` remains authoritative.
+11. **English and Arabic catalogues remain in sync.**
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Surface | Location |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Merchant router | `merchant-front/src/router/index.ts` |
+| Merchant navigation/gates | `merchant-front/src/layouts/sections.tsx` |
+| Merchant shell | `merchant-front/src/layouts/default.tsx` |
+| Auth layout | `merchant-front/src/layouts/auth.tsx` |
+| Pages | `merchant-front/src/pages/**` |
+| API map | `merchant-front/src/constants/urlsMap/index.ts` |
+| Guide content | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/**` |
+| Guide/help components | `merchant-front/src/components/guide/**` |
+| Environment | `VITE_API_URL`, `VITE_SEND_NOT_FOUND_TRANSLATIONS`, `VITE_MY_TAILSCALE` |
+
+The portal uses no admin checklist/help-panel flags. Its shell always exposes guide search and help.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Start a merchant: register/login, complete onboarding, wait for KYB approval, then create a wallet/application/link or POS screen.
+- Debug a missing page: check `routesAuthorities` for that route name, then confirm the backend authority. A hidden nav item does not prove the route is gated.
+- Debug a link: use the attempts inspector; confirm the link state and slot behavior before creating a replacement link.
+- Debug a POS screen: check the screen code, the live `EventSource` connection, and the terminal/screen pairing.
+- Debug a dispute: confirm the evidence deadline and that the file is attached; an evidence note without a file may still be accepted but is weaker.
+- Debug API integration: use the developer guide generator, then verify the token, IP allowlist and webhook signature checks.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- 16 protected portal routes and four public routes.
+- 248/56 merchant shell with RTL, theme, search, help and operator card.
+- Onboarding, wallets, statements, applications, links, POS, payments, disputes, cash-outs, tokens, credentials and team pages.
+- Merchant guide and developer guide surfaces.
+- Sensitive application proposal UI and credential/token write-only handling.
+- Shared XLSX export for statements.
+
+### Partial
+
+- `Statements` lacks a router-level authority gate.
+- The guide/developer routes are open learning surfaces, which is intentional but means any authenticated merchant can read them.
+- The portal shows maker/checker posture but does not provide a full pending-change diff workflow for every sensitive object.
+- Google OIDC is listed in the API map but the actual merchant `/auth/google` endpoint returns 501, so no working Google flow ships.
+- Merchant help and guide content are the 10+5 chapter baseline, not guide v2.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No self-service activation override; KYB approval remains admin-controlled.
+- No merchant-side certification/training gate for production authorities.
+- No guide v2 context map/playbook/read tracking.
+- No working Google sign-in.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Authorization gap:** direct navigation to `/portal/statements` is not blocked by the router even when the UI would hide it.
+- **Onboarding risk:** client-side progress and completion are convenience signals, not activation authority.
+- **POS risk:** a displayed `SUCCEEDED` screen is a reflection; the merchant must still follow the server-confirmed payment status and settlement rules.
+- **Documentation risk:** do not describe the portal as having a working Google login or a fully server-enforced route gate.
+- **Guide risk:** merchant chapter content must not be conflated with the admin 12-book guide or guide v2.
+
+## 8. Verification and tests
+
+- `tests/e2e/merchant/shell.spec.ts` checks the merchant shell, drawer, navigation rendering, locale re-translation, overflow, mobile behavior and removed scaling.
+- `tests/e2e/merchant/auth.spec.ts` covers authentication entry behavior.
+- `tests/e2e/merchant/a11y.spec.ts` covers accessibility basics.
+- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/exhaustive-merchant-surface.spec.ts` enumerates the portal routes and viewport/locale/theme matrix.
+- `merchant-front/src/content/__tests__/content-completeness.test.ts` checks the merchant guide chapter content and tools.
+
+The shell/auth/a11y suites require the live stack. The content test is a Bun test.
+
+## 9. Source references
+

+# Merchant Guide and Developer API
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the merchant-facing interactive guide and developer API reference in `merchant-front`:
+
+- The operations guide content (M-01 to M-10).
+- The developer API content (D-01 to D-05).
+- The guide page, role filtering, chapter search, first-5 checklist, fee/net settlement calculator, code generator, and webhook verification checks.
+- The dedicated developer guide page and its code-template viewer.
+
+It does not own the external API implementation or the merchant portal data pages. It also does not present the future guide v2 workstream as current.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The merchant guide is intentionally practical:
+
+1. **Ten operations chapters cover the merchant lifecycle.** Onboarding, wallets/applications, links, fees, POS, payment statuses, statements/cash-outs, disputes/refunds, merchant-owned credentials, and team/roles.
+2. **Five developer chapters cover the integration lifecycle.** How the API works, authentication/IP allowlists, money precision and redirect rules, endpoint reference, and production code templates.
+3. **Role-aware reading.** Chapters are tagged `MERCHANT_ADMIN`, `MERCHANT_STAFF`, `MERCHANT_CASHIER`, `DEVELOPER`, or `ALL`; the page filters by role.
+4. **First-5 checklist.** A new merchant is guided through KYB, first wallet, first application, first link, and POS or API token.
+5. **Interactive tooling.** The fee calculator explains the fee-bearer model with decimal.js; the code generator produces runnable TypeScript, PHP, Python and cURL snippets; webhook checks explain signature and replay safety.
+6. **Deep links.** `?chapter=` and `?search=` open a specific chapter or filtered view from the shell search.
+7. **The guide is content, not a live data console.** It explains rules and workflows; live troubleshooting uses the portal, POS screen and API.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Content modules
+
+| Module | Contents |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `merchant-front/src/content/guide/types.ts` | `MerchantGuideChapter`, roles, code languages and chapter shape. |
+| `merchant-front/src/content/guide/merchantOperationsGuide.ts` | M-01 to M-10. |
+| `merchant-front/src/content/guide/merchantDeveloperApiGuide.ts` | D-01 to D-05, including code templates. |
+
+Chapters have an id, number, role, English/Arabic title and body, tags, and optional code templates. The operations guide is the business manual; the developer guide is the integration reference.
+
+### 3.2 Operations chapters (10)
+
+| Id | Role | Title | Core content |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| M-01 | `MERCHANT_ADMIN` | Getting Started — Completing Your KYB Onboarding & Activating Live Payments | KYB, business profile, owners, documents, payout IBAN, review status, resubmission. |
+| M-02 | `MERCHANT_ADMIN` | Understanding Wallets & Applications — How Your Store Is Organized | Wallet/ledger relationship, application-to-wallet assignment, descriptive versus sensitive edits. |
+| M-03 | `ALL` | Creating Single-Use & Multi-Use Payment Links (`/links`) | Single-use slot lock, multi-use quota, infinite links, redirect allowlist. |
+| M-04 | `MERCHANT_ADMIN` | How Commissions & Fee Bearers Work (`MERCHANT_ABSORBS`, `PAYER_SURCHARGE`, `SPLIT`) | Customer total, platform commission, net wallet credit and split examples. |
+| M-05 | `MERCHANT_CASHIER` | In-Store Point of Sale (POS) Terminals & Realtime Cashier/Customer Screens (`/pos`) | Terminal creation, screen pairing, live payment display, idle/reconnect behavior. |
+| M-06 | `ALL` | Understanding Payment Statuses — When Is It Safe to Hand Over the Goods? | `SUCCEEDED`, `AWAITING_CUSTOMER`, `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN`, `FAILED`/`EXPIRED`/`CANCELLED`. |
+| M-07 | `MERCHANT_ADMIN` | Reading Your Wallet Balance, Monthly Statements & Requesting Cash-Outs (`/wallets` & `/cashouts`) | Balances, monthly statement, hash-sealed export, cash-out stages. |
+| M-08 | `MERCHANT_STAFF` | Responding to Customer Disputes & Refunds (`/disputes` & `/payments`) | Evidence deadlines, reserve, won/lost outcomes, negative-balance ceiling. |
+| M-09 | `DEVELOPER` | Using Your Own Gateway Credentials (`MERCHANT_DIRECT` Mode — `/credentials`) | Merchant-owned credential sets, settlement target, commission receivable. |
+| M-10 | `MERCHANT_ADMIN` | Managing Your Team, Roles, Application Scopes & Security (`/team`) | Team invitations, roles, scopes, authority principle of least privilege. |
+
+### 3.3 Developer chapters (5)
+
+| Id | Title | Core content |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| D-01 | How the API Works From Zero (For Beginners & Architects) | Request/response model, server-side amount authority, payment-link life cycle, idempotency. |
+| D-02 | Authentication (`pg_live_` Bearer Tokens) & IP CIDR Allowlists (`/developers/tokens`) | Bearer token creation/revocation, scopes, IP allowlists, secret handling. |
+| D-03 | Money Precision Rules & Redirect Allowlists (Avoid These 3 Common Mistakes) | Decimal strings, no floating point, redirect-domain allowlists, no trust in browser return. |
+| D-04 | Complete Endpoint Reference (`/api/v1/external/*`) | Create/get/cancel links and get payment status; error envelope and status codes. |
+| D-05 | Copy-Pasteable Production Code Templates (Interactive Code Generator) | TypeScript/Node/Bun, PHP/Laravel, Python/httpx, cURL; webhook verification guidance. |
+
+### 3.4 Operations guide page
+
+`merchant-front/src/pages/guide/index.tsx` renders:
+
+- `PageHeader` with the guide title and subtitle.
+- A first-5 checklist card:
+  1. Pass KYB verification.
+  2. Create the first LYD wallet.
+  3. Create the first application and connect the wallet.
+  4. Create and share a payment link.
+  5. Set up a POS screen or an API token.
+- A completion progress bar.
+- A chapter search field.
+- Role filter tabs: All, Business Owner, Manager/Accountant, In-Store Cashier, Developer (API).
+- Responsive chapter cards with role badge, tags and a plain-text excerpt.
+- A chapter modal with full Markdown render and optional code templates.
+- The fee/net settlement calculator.
+- The developer API code generator.
+- The webhook sample and five verification checks.
+
+#### First-5 checklist behavior
+
+- Persisted in `localStorage` key `merchant-guide-checklist`.
+- On mount, the page calls onboarding, wallets, applications, links, POS terminals and tokens list endpoints.
+- Auto-detects completed steps from successful list responses and the onboarding status (`APPROVED`, `ACTIVE` or `COMPLETED`).
+- Writes the detected state back to localStorage when possible.
+- The user can manually toggle a step; storage failures fall back to in-memory state.
+
+This checklist is a guide aid. It does not grant activation and does not replace the server's onboarding/KYB state.
+
+#### Deep links
+
+- `?search=<term>` pre-fills the search field; `?search=1` is treated as an empty search.
+- `?chapter=<id>` opens that chapter modal if the id exists.
+- The shell guide search routes to `MerchantGuide` with `?chapter=<id>`.
+
+### 3.5 Fee and net settlement calculator
+
+`merchant-front/src/components/guide/MerchantFeeCalculator.tsx` uses `decimal.js` through `toDecimal` and supports:
+
+- Amount, rail, commission percent, gateway fee percent, platform share for split mode.
+- Fee bearers: `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`, `PAYER_SURCHARGE`, `SPLIT`.
+- Results: customer total, platform commission, estimated gateway fee, exact net wallet credit, and payer share in split/surcharge mode.
+
+Formulas:
+
+- Commission = amount × commission%.
+- `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`: customer total = amount; net = amount − commission.
+- `PAYER_SURCHARGE`: customer total = amount + commission; net = amount; payer share = commission.
+- `SPLIT`: payer share = commission × platform share%; customer total = amount + payer share; net = amount − (commission − payer share).
+
+The gateway fee is estimated on the customer total and shown for transparency. The actual wallet credit follows the selected fee-bearer formula and the server's commission/ledger logic. The calculator is local and does not call the commission engine.
+
+### 3.6 Developer API code generator
+
+The operations guide includes a generator with:
+
+- Application ID, bearer token and payment reference inputs.
+- Amount and fee bearer taken from the calculator.
+- Language tabs: TypeScript/Node/Bun, PHP/Laravel, Python/httpx, cURL.
+- Generated calls:
+  - `POST /api/v1/external/links` with `applicationId`, decimal amount, `currency: "LYD"`, `feeBearer`, `infiniteUse`, `useCount`, `redirectUrl`.
+  - `GET /api/v1/external/links/:key` to check `state` and `confirmedCount`.
+  - `GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference`.
+- A sample webhook request with `X-PG-Signature` and a JSON payload.
+
+The generated token is a placeholder/sample and is displayed in the browser. A real token must be created in `/portal/developers/tokens`, scoped, stored server-side, and never committed or shared.
+
+### 3.7 Webhook checks
+
+The guide lists five checks:
+
+1. Reject any webhook without a valid `X-PG-Signature` header.
+2. Recompute the signature over the raw request body and compare in constant time.
+3. Compare amount and currency with the payment you created before fulfilling the order.
+4. Deduplicate by event id so a retried delivery cannot post twice.
+5. Return a 2xx quickly and move slow work to a queue.
+
+The guide also demonstrates the raw-body signing concern: a parsed/re-serialized JSON body can change bytes and break signature verification.
+
+### 3.8 Dedicated developer guide page
+
+`merchant-front/src/pages/guide/developers/index.tsx` renders:
+
+- A PageHeader.
+- A pill list of all five D chapters.
+- The selected chapter title, id badge and Markdown body.
+- A language selector and ready-to-run code templates when present.
+- `?chapter=<id>` deep links.
+
+The page uses the same D-01..D-05 content as the operations guide's developer chapter cards, so the two surfaces stay consistent.
+
+### 3.9 Shell search and contextual help
+
+- The merchant shell `Ctrl+K` opens `GlobalGuideSearchModal`, which searches M/D chapters and routes to the appropriate guide route with `?chapter=`.
+- The shell `?` opens the merchant contextual-help drawer with the route's M/D mapping.
+- The drawer and full guide use the same content modules; the drawer is a narrower, route-specific view.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **Merchant guide content is 10 operations chapters + 5 developer chapters.** Do not split or merge them without updating the content test and the role mapping.
+2. **Roles filter, not authorize.** A role tag controls presentation; the portal route authorities and backend decide access.
+3. **Money calculations use decimal.js.** No floating point in the calculator or generated examples.
+4. **The calculator is illustrative.** It does not replace server commission calculation or ledger posting.
+5. **The code generator is illustrative.** It must not embed a real secret in source control.
+6. **The external API amount is a decimal string.** The generator uses the calculator amount and the server remains authoritative.
+7. **Redirect URLs must be allowlisted.** The guide teaches this; the external API and checkout enforce it.
+8. **Webhook verification uses the raw body.** The guide's signature checks are normative integration guidance.
+9. **First-5 checklist state is local.** It is not a server permission or activation record.
+10. **Guide v2 is not current.** Merchant content remains the 10+5 baseline until a future implementation lands.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Surface | Location |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Operations content | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/merchantOperationsGuide.ts` |
+| Developer content | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/merchantDeveloperApiGuide.ts` |
+| Content types | `merchant-front/src/content/guide/types.ts` |
+| Operations guide page | `merchant-front/src/pages/guide/index.tsx` |
+| Developer guide page | `merchant-front/src/pages/guide/developers/index.tsx` |
+| Fee calculator | `merchant-front/src/components/guide/MerchantFeeCalculator.tsx` |
+| Code block renderer | `merchant-front/src/components/guide/GuideCodeBlock.tsx` |
+| Shell search/help | `merchant-front/src/layouts/default.tsx`, `components/guide/**` |
+| External API routes | `/api/v1/external/links`, `/api/v1/external/links/:key`, `/api/v1/external/payments/:reference` |
+| Local storage | `merchant-guide-checklist` |
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Onboarding a merchant: point them at M-01 first; use the first-5 checklist as a training aid, then verify the actual portal state.
+- Debugging an API integration: open D-02, confirm the token and CIDR allowlist, then D-04 and the code generator for the exact request shape.
+- Explaining a payout amount: use the fee calculator with the real commission/fee-bearer configuration; do not treat the estimated gateway fee as the ledger posting.
+- Explaining a dispute: use M-08 and the disputes page; evidence is deadline-bound and money movement remains an admin action.
+- Adding content: extend the typed content modules and keep the role/tag/code-template shape; update the content test when counts change.
+- Deep-linking: use `/portal/guide?chapter=M-06` or `/portal/guide/developers?chapter=D-04` from support messages.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- 10 operations chapters and 5 developer chapters with role tags and bilingual titles/bodies where supplied.
+- First-5 checklist with localStorage persistence and API-based auto-detection.
+- Role-filtered chapter search and modal reader.
+- Decimal.js fee/net settlement calculator with all three fee bearers.
+- Four-language code generator and external API examples.
+- Five webhook verification checks and a raw-body signature example.
+- Dedicated developer guide page with code templates.
+- Shell guide search and contextual help integration.
+
+### Partial
+
+- Arabic coverage is chapter-dependent; some bodies/titles are bilingual and some are not.
+- The calculator's gateway fee is an estimate based on the customer total, not the exact gateway cost.
+- The code generator is a teaching aid; it does not validate the token, scopes or CIDR at generation time.
+- The first-5 checklist can disagree with the server if a list call is stale or fails silently.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No guide v2 content, context map, safeguard cards, playbook or read tracking for merchants.
+- No server-side checklist/progress record for the first-5 flow.
+- No interactive API sandbox that executes calls against a sandbox token.
+- No generated SDK package.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Security risk:** the token field is a plaintext browser input; a real token can be exposed on screen or in a screenshot. Use a scoped test token and rotate it.
+- **Accuracy risk:** the fee calculator's gateway-fee estimate is not the ledger truth.
+- **Training risk:** the first-5 checklist is local and can be manually toggled; it must not be used as proof of activation.
+- **Doc risk:** the 10+5 baseline is current; guide v2 is future and must not be described as shipped.
+
+## 8. Verification and tests

+- `merchant-front/src/content/__tests__/content-completeness.test.ts` asserts the merchant guide chapter counts and required content lengths.
+- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/exhaustive-merchant-surface.spec.ts` includes `/portal/guide` in the merchant surface matrix.

+# Checkout Payer Flow
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the public payer experience in `checkout-front`:
+
+- The `/pay/:linkKey` page and its phase machine.
+- Rail selection, field rendering, validation and client-action renderers.
+- Attempt initiation, confirmation, resend, cancellation and client-event forwarding.
+- SSE status consumption, amount breakdown, receipt and return-to-merchant behavior.
+- The checkout 404 surface.
+
+It does not own `checkout-back`, the core attempt engine, gateway protocols, or the checkout help content. It also does not claim that browser return/callback signals are trusted; the core only trusts server-verified channels.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The checkout is deliberately narrow and zero-trust:
+
+1. **The server owns the amount.** The SPA never sends `amount` or `currency` on initiate/confirm; `core-back` resolves both from the payment link.
+2. **The payer sees one focused column.** The layout is centered on desktop and top-aligned on small screens.
+3. **Rail selection is catalog-driven.** Visible rails, names, collection modes and fields come from the link summary.
+4. **The rail's client action determines the next screen.** OTP form, redirect, embedded widget, QR/code, or push/transfer.
+5. **The payer does not judge success.** Browser redirects and widget callbacks are hints; the authoritative status arrives through the server/SSE and core verification.
+6. **Money is displayed as decimal strings.** The page never computes totals with floating point.
+7. **Return is opt-in and allowlisted.** The return-to-merchant button appears only after success and only for an allowlisted redirect host.
+8. **A failed link is a clear dead end.** The page shows a friendly unavailable/failed state rather than a raw error.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Route and layout
+
+- `/pay/:linkKey` (`Pay`) renders `pages/pay/[linkKey]/index.tsx`.
+- `/` (`Home`) redirects to `NotFound`.
+- `/:pathMatch(.*)*` (`NotFound`) renders the token-styled 404 page.
+- `layouts/checkout.tsx` is a single `<main class="pg-checkout">` with an optional title.
+- The page adds a max-width 560 px column with the merchant name, help button, language toggle, summary card, phase content and footer.
+
+### 3.2 Phase machine
+
+`type Phase = "SUMMARY" | "FORM" | "ACTION" | "CONFIRMING" | "RECEIPT" | "ERROR"`.
+
+| Phase | Entered when | What renders |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `SUMMARY` | Initial ref value | Declared but not used as a visible state; loading and load errors are separate. |
+| `FORM` | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` succeeds | Rail cards, per-rail banner, rail fields, "Pay Now". |
+| `ACTION` | Initiate returns a client action | Countdown, renderer for the action kind. |
+| `CONFIRMING` | Snapshot status is `VERIFYING`, `UNKNOWN` or `AUTHORIZING` | Spinner, status badge, reference, cancel. |
+| `RECEIPT` | Snapshot status is `SUCCEEDED` | Payment complete, amount, reference, optional return button. |
+| `ERROR` | Load failure, cancelled attempt, or terminal failure status (`FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `BLOCKED`) | Failure message, status, "Try Another Method". |
+
+Loading and `loadError` are rendered outside the phase switch. A load error shows "This Payment Link Is No Longer Available" and "Cannot process this payment" in a card; it is not the router 404 page.
+
+### 3.3 Summary and amount breakdown
+
+`GET v1/pay/:linkKey` returns a `PayLinkSummary`:
+
+- `linkKey`, `merchantTradeName`, optional logo/description.
+- `amount`, `currency`.
+- `feeBearerMode` (`MERCHANT_ABSORBS`, `PAYER_SURCHARGE`, `SPLIT`).
+- `baseAmount`, `feeAmount`, `totalAmount`, `merchantAmount`.
+- Optional `splitPercent`.
+- `visibleRails`, optional `expiresAt`, `status`, `redirectUrl`, `allowlistedRedirectHosts`.
+- Optional `supportConfig`.
+
+The breakdown always shows the base amount and amount charged. It inserts a service-fee row only when the fee bearer is not `MERCHANT_ABSORBS`; for `SPLIT` the row label includes the split percentage. The amount charged is `totalAmount`.
+
+`visibleRails` is computed by the backend's visible-rails resolver (merchant status, application/rail whitelist, route health/limits, credential state, amount/currency, and related predicates). The SPA does not recompute visibility.
+
+### 3.4 Rail selection and fields
+
+`RailCards`:
+
+- Shows each visible rail's localized name and collection-mode pill.
+- Uses a collection-mode icon.
+- Selects the first rail by default after summary load.
+- Resets form values and errors when the payer switches rails.
+
+`RailFieldForm`:
+
+- Renders every field in `rail.fields`.
+- `select` uses a `VSelect`; all other input types use `VTextField`.
+- PAN-sensitive fields render as password inputs.
+- Labels/placeholders fall back between Arabic and English.
+- Inputs use `autocomplete="off"`.
+
+`zReady.ts` normalizes and validates:
+
+- Arabic digits are normalized to ASCII.
+- `phone` uses local `09` normalization.
+- `numeric`/`otp` strip non-digit characters (numeric allows a decimal point in normalization, then validates digits with optional decimals).
+- `wallet_id` expects `NP-` plus 12 digits.
+- `otp` expects 4-8 digits.
+- Required/min/max/regex rules from the rail field descriptor are applied.
+
+The page validates with `schema.safeParse(normalized)` and maps the first issue per field into `formErrors`.
+
+### 3.5 Initiate
+
+`POST v1/pay/:linkKey/initiate` sends:
+
+```json
+{
+  "railCode": "<selected rail>",
+  "formData": { "<field>": "<normalized value>" },
+  "idempotencyKey": "chk-<time>-<random>"
+}
+```
+
+The client generates a fresh idempotency key per initiate/confirm attempt. The response is `InitiateResponse` with `attemptId`, `reference`, `status` and `clientAction`. The page stores the attempt, opens the SSE stream, starts a countdown if the action has `expires_at`, and sets phase `ACTION`.
+
+A client-supplied `amount` or `currency` is outside this contract and is rejected by `checkout-back`/`core-back`.
+
+### 3.6 Client-action renderers
+
+| Action kind | Renderer | Behavior |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `SHOW_OTP_FORM` | `OtpFormRenderer` | OTP input, attempt counter, resend, verify/pay; Enter submits. |
+| `HTTP_REDIRECT` | `RedirectRenderer` | Auto-redirects on mount; GET query or POST form; blocks non-allowlisted hosts; manual retry button. |
+| `RENDER_EMBEDDED` | `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` | Loads allowlisted HTTPS scripts with SRI/crossOrigin, listens for postMessage callbacks, optional iframe sandbox, removes scripts on unmount. |
+| `SHOW_QR_OR_CODE` | `QrOrCodeRenderer` | Renders QR data URL, optional pay code, bilingual instructions, deep link, expiry. |
+| `SHOW_PUSH_OR_TRANSFER` | `PushOrTransferRenderer` | Shows destination/reference/wallet hint, instructions, optional proof upload, expiry. |
+
+`OtpFormRenderer` limits the OTP to the action length and normalizes Arabic digits. `RedirectRenderer` requires a non-empty allowlist; a wildcard accepts any real host but `javascript:`/`data:` URLs still fail host parsing. `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` uses a fixed allowlist of Moamalat, MPGS test, Evo, and Numo hosts and an origin check for incoming messages.
+
+### 3.7 Confirm, resend, cancel
+
+- `confirmOtp` posts `{ otp, idempotencyKey }` to `POST .../confirm`, applies the returned snapshot, and moves to `CONFIRMING` for `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN`.
+- `resendOtp` posts to `POST .../resend` and shows a notice; it does not reset the attempt.
+- `cancelAttempt` posts to `POST .../cancel`, closes the stream and moves to `ERROR`.
+- `sendClientEvent` posts to `POST .../client-event` with `{ event, payload }`.
+
+Client events are canonicalized through a local alias map:
+
+- `ready`/`widget_ready`/`widget_ready_event` → `widgetEvent`.
+- `closed`/`widget_closed` → `widgetEvent`.
+- `complete`/`completed`/`complete_callback` → `completeCallback`.
+- `error`/`error_callback`/`cancel`/`cancelled`/`cancel_callback` → `errorCallback`.
+- `return`/`return_hint` → `returnHint`.
+
+These events are hints. The core must still verify the payment through a trusted channel.
+
+### 3.8 SSE status stream
+
+After initiate, the page creates:
+
+```text
+new EventSource("v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status")
+```
+
+- `onmessage` parses `payload.attempt ?? payload`, applies the snapshot, updates client action/reference/status, and changes the phase for success, terminal failure, or confirming states.
+- `onerror` closes the stream and sets it to null; the page does not reconnect or start polling.
+- `onBeforeUnmount` closes the stream and clears the countdown.
+
+`checkout-back` exposes the status route as an SSE proxy and `tests/e2e/checkout`/`tests/e2e-live` expect `text/event-stream`. The historical performance note that core SSE polls the database rather than subscribing to a transition bus is recorded in the edge/core parts; the SPA only knows the SSE contract.
+
+The page also starts a one-second countdown from the client action's `expires_at`; it does not itself expire or cancel the server attempt.
+
+### 3.9 Receipt and return
+
+When the snapshot status becomes `SUCCEEDED`:
+
+- Phase becomes `RECEIPT`.
+- The stream closes.
+- The page shows "Payment Receipt", a success badge, the total amount and the reference.
+
+A "Return To Merchant" button appears only when `summary.redirectUrl` exists **and** `isAllowedRedirect(redirectUrl, allowlistedRedirectHosts)` is true. The allowlist must be non-empty; matching is exact host or subdomain. The button performs `window.location.assign`.
+
+There is no automatic return redirect on success. The payer may remain on the receipt.
+
+### 3.10 Error and unavailable states
+
+- A load error shows "This Payment Link Is No Longer Available" and "Cannot process this payment".
+- A terminal attempt status (`FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `BLOCKED`) moves to `ERROR` with the status badge and a "Try Another Method" button that returns to `FORM`.
+- An `UNKNOWN`/`VERIFYING`/`AUTHORIZING` status moves to `CONFIRMING` and tells the payer not to pay again (the detailed guidance is in the help drawer).
+
+### 3.11 404 bug
+
+`checkout-front/src/pages/public/not-found/index.tsx` renders a 404 card with a button:
+
+```text
+<RouterLink to={{ name: "Dashboard" }}>
+```
+
+The checkout router has no `Dashboard` route. The link therefore resolves to the catch-all `NotFound` again. The intended recovery target is unclear because checkout has no home page; `/` itself redirects to `NotFound`. This is a real recovery bug, not a styling issue.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **No client amount/currency.** Initiate and confirm payloads must not include `amount` or `currency`; the server rejects them.
+2. **Idempotency keys are required for initiate/confirm.** The client generates one per action.
+3. **The event/action contract is canonical.** Renderers consume the five `ClientAction` kinds; widget events are translated to canonical event names before posting.
+4. **Browser hints are not trust.** Return URLs, redirects and widget callbacks never mark an attempt successful in the SPA.
+5. **Redirect hosts must be allowlisted.** Empty allowlists deny all; `javascript:`/`data:` schemes are rejected.
+6. **The SSE stream is display-only.** The server attempt state remains authoritative.
+7. **Money is displayed, not calculated, as decimal strings.** The summary provides base/fee/total; the SPA does not sum floats.
+8. **The receipt amount is the server total.** The page does not recompute it from the base amount.
+9. **Return is opt-in.** Only an allowlisted `redirectUrl` produces a return button.
+10. **Checkout is unauthenticated.** There is no payer account or session authority.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Operation | Endpoint |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Load link summary | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` |
+| Initiate attempt | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/initiate` |
+| Attempt logs | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId` |
+| Status stream | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/status` (SSE) |
+| Confirm OTP | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/confirm` |
+| Resend OTP | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/resend` |
+| Cancel | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/cancel` |
+| Client event | `POST v1/pay/:linkKey/logs/:attemptId/client-event` |
+
+Environment: `VITE_API_URL` (edge base), `VITE_SEND_NOT_FOUND_TRANSLATIONS`, `VITE_MY_TAILSCALE`. The SPA talks only to `checkout-back` under `/api`.
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Debug a stuck payer: check the attempt status badge and reference; `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN` means "do not pay again", not "failed".
+- Debug a missing return button: confirm the link has a redirect URL and the host is in the application allowlist.
+- Debug a redirect: inspect `HTTP_REDIRECT` action URL/method/form fields and the allowlist; the page does not bypass the host check.
+- Debug an OTP: confirm the OTP length, attempt count and resend state; the SPA does not reveal whether the subscriber exists.
+- Debug the status stream: confirm the SSE endpoint returns `text/event-stream` and the attempt id matches; the SPA does not poll after an SSE error.
+- Debug a 404: do not use the recovery button until the route target is fixed; navigate manually to a valid `/pay/:linkKey`.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Summary load, amount breakdown, rail cards and rail-field validation.
+- Initiate, OTP confirm/resend, cancel and client-event forwarding.
+- Five client-action renderers with redirect/script allowlists.
+- SSE status consumption and phase transitions.
+- Receipt with server total and allowlisted return.
+- Terminal/unavailable/error states.
+- RTL/Arabic labels and responsive single-column layout.
+
+### Partial
+
+- `SUMMARY` is a declared but unused visible phase.
+- SSE has no reconnect/backoff or polling fallback.
+- Embedded widgets depend on a hard-coded host allowlist; a new provider requires a code change.
+- The 404 surface exists but has a broken recovery link.
+- `PushOrTransferRenderer` has an `onCancel` prop with no rendered cancel control.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No dedicated checkout home/status lookup page.
+- No payer-initiated receipt download/email.
+- No reconnect/resume UX after a dropped SSE stream.
+- No client-side handling for a late success after the page shows `ERROR` beyond a manual reload.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **404 recovery bug:** the catch-all button targets a non-existent `Dashboard` route.
+- **Status-stream risk:** if SSE drops, the page stops updating until reload; the payer may see `CONFIRMING` indefinitely.
+- **SRI risk:** `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` selects an SRI hash by the host allowlist index rather than the script URL index, so multiple scripts can receive the wrong hash.
+- **Cancel gap:** push/transfer actions show no cancel control even though the renderer receives a callback.
+- **Trust risk:** operators must not treat browser callbacks as proof; only the server-verified status is authoritative.
+- **Documentation risk:** the checkout is not a general payment status portal; it is a single-link payer surface.
+
+## 8. Verification and tests
+
+- `tests/e2e/checkout/pay.spec.ts` renders the payer surface, checks no horizontal overflow on phone/desktop, and asserts `#app` has no transform.
+- `tests/e2e/checkout/a11y.spec.ts` checks accessibility basics.
+- `tests/unit/checkout-redirect.test.ts` covers empty allowlists, scheme rejection, exact/subdomain matching and wildcard behavior.
+- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/exhaustive-checkout-surface.spec.ts` checks the `/pay/test-key` surface across viewports/locales/themes.
+- `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts` exercises the live payer journey when the stack is available.
+
+The Playwright/live suites require the running stack; the redirect unit test is pure and does not.
+
+## 9. Source references
+

+- `design/payment_gateway_deployment_and_guides_architecture.md` — checkout deployment/help context.
+- `design/complete_zero_to_hero_guides_and_academy_specification.md` — collection modes, confirmation channels and trusted-success facts referenced by the guide.

+# Checkout Help Center
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the payer-facing help center in `checkout-front`:
+
+- The per-rail instructions banner on the payment form.
+- The "Help & Support" slide-over drawer on the payer page.
+- The `supportConfig` projection from the admin-managed platform setting.
+- The per-rail `helpGuide` projection from the rail record.
+- The state-aware guidance for in-flight, unknown, failed, expired and cancelled attempts.
+- The actual hide behavior when the admin disables support.
+
+It does not own the admin support settings page, merchant guide, admin guide, or the checkout phase machine. It documents the separation between the platform support configuration and the per-rail guides, and it records the gaps in the current authoring and visibility model.
+
+## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
+
+The checkout help center is data-driven rather than hard-coded:
+
+1. **The payer never needs a second request for help.** Support details and per-rail walkthroughs travel with the payment-link summary.
+2. **Help is contextual to the selected rail.** The banner and guide section explain the exact steps, prerequisites and troubleshooting for the rail the payer is using.
+3. **Help is state-aware.** A `VERIFYING`/`UNKNOWN`/`FAILED`/`EXPIRED`/`CANCELLED` attempt gets a clear "do not pay again" or "safe to retry" message.
+4. **Support is centrally controlled.** The admin edits one platform setting for support channels, working hours and FAQ; the change applies to all checkout links.
+5. **The merchant contact is optional and separate.** The platform can show its own support channels, the merchant's contact details, both, or neither.
+6. **Per-rail guides are content, not code.** The rail record carries bilingual steps/prerequisites/troubleshooting so operators can tune guidance per payment method.
+7. **The payer can always copy the reference.** The drawer exposes the payment reference for support conversations.
+8. **Disabling support should not break the payment flow.** It hides the contact block, not the payment or the attempt-state guidance.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 The two data sources
+
+| Data | Source | Projection |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| Platform support config | `platform_settings` key `checkout.support_config` | `buildCheckoutSupportConfig` in `core-back/api/internal/checkout.ts` |
+| Per-rail guide | `rails.help_guide_json` (seeded by `core-back/prisma/seedGuides.ts`) | Passed through `visibleRails[].helpGuide` in `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` |
+
+The checkout page receives both in `PayLinkSummary.supportConfig` and `RailDescriptor.helpGuide`.
+
+### 3.2 Support config shape
+
+```text
+SupportConfig {
+  enabled: boolean
+  working_hours_ar: string | null
+  working_hours_en: string | null
+  platform: { phone, whatsapp, email } | null
+  merchant: { phone, email, tradeName } | null
+  faq_items: Array<{ q_ar, a_ar, q_en, a_en }>
+  channels: string[]
+}
+```
+
+Projection rules in `buildCheckoutSupportConfig`:
+
+- If the setting is absent, not an object, or `enabled !== true`, return `null`.
+- If `show_platform_contact` is not false, include the platform phone/WhatsApp/email.
+- If `show_merchant_contact` is not false, include the merchant phone/email/trade name from the loaded link.
+- Pass through `working_hours_ar`/`working_hours_en`, FAQ items (all four fields, null-coalesced) and a flat `channels` list derived from non-empty platform channels.
+- The projection deliberately excludes the setting's other fields; only the support-facing shape leaks.
+
+The admin form defaults both `show_*` values to true and saves the `checkout.support_config` setting as a new immutable platform-setting version. The core handler writes `CHECKOUT_SUPPORT_UPDATED` and `CHECKOUT_SUPPORT_EDIT_CHECKLIST` audits. The admin page's live preview is not the actual drawer.
+
+### 3.3 Per-rail help guide shape
+
+```text
+RailHelpGuide {
+  steps_ar: string[]
+  steps_en: string[]
+  prerequisites_ar: string[]
+  prerequisites_en: string[]
+  troubleshooting_ar: Array<{ q_ar, a_ar }>
+  troubleshooting_en: Array<{ q_en, a_en }>
+}
+```
+
+`core-back/prisma/seedGuides.ts` defines `RAIL_HELP_GUIDES` for 14 seeded rails: `edfali`, `sadad`, `moamalat_card`, `cbl_lypay`, `lypay`, `mypay`, `tlync`, `mobicash`, `onepay`, `yussor`, `sahara`, `mpgs`, `evo_pay`, `neompay_wallet` (the comment above the map says 13, but the actual object has 14 keys). A rail without a guide returns `helpGuide: null`; the banner hides and the drawer omits the rail-guide section.
+
+The admin portal has no rail-guide editor. Rails are seeded/updated from code and the admin Rails page manages rail catalog fields, not `helpGuideJson` content.
+
+### 3.4 Per-rail banner
+
+`checkout-front/src/components/help/PerRailInstructionsBanner.tsx` renders when `selectedRail.helpGuide` exists:
+
+- A region titled "How to pay with <rail>".
+- An expand/collapse button (default expanded).
+- A help button that opens the drawer.
+- Prerequisite pills (localized with fallback).
+- Numbered step rows.
+- Localized last-resort behavior: Arabic uses Arabic when present, otherwise English; English uses English when present, otherwise Arabic.
+
+The banner is independent of `supportConfig.enabled`. Disabling support does not hide it.
+
+### 3.5 State-aware drawer
+
+`checkout-front/src/components/help/CheckoutHelpDrawer.tsx` is a `SlideOverDrawer` (width 440) titled "Help & Support". It composes:
+
+1. **State guidance** for the current attempt status.
+2. **Payment reference** with a copy action when a reference exists.
+3. **Per-rail guide** from the selected rail's `helpGuide`.
+4. **FAQ** from `supportConfig.faq_items`.
+5. **Contact support** from `supportConfig.platform` and `supportConfig.merchant`.
+
+State guidance:
+
+| Status | Tone | Message summary |
+| :--- | :--- | :--- |
+| `VERIFYING` | info | The platform is verifying; do not pay again; status updates automatically. |
+| `UNKNOWN` | warning | Could not confirm yet; do not pay again; wait/refresh; contact support with the reference. |
+| `FAILED` | error | Attempt did not complete; try another method; if charged, contact support with the reference. |
+| `EXPIRED` | warning | Payment window expired; do not use the old reference; start a new payment. |
+| `CANCELLED` | warning | Payment was cancelled; if charged, contact support with the reference; otherwise start again. |
+| Other | none | No state block. |
+
+The drawer always shows the reference block when a reference exists, regardless of support configuration. The rail-guide section shows prerequisites, numbered steps and troubleshooting when a guide is present. The FAQ section renders only when there are complete localized FAQ items. The contact section renders only when `supportConfig.enabled` is true.
+
+Contact behavior:
+
+- Platform WhatsApp builds `https://wa.me/<digits>?text=<encoded help message>`.
+- Platform phone uses `tel:` with whitespace removed.
+- Platform email uses `mailto:` with a localized subject and a body containing the link key and reference.
+- Merchant name/phone/email render when the merchant contact is present.
+- If support is enabled but no channel and no working hours exist, the drawer shows "No contact details are available right now."
+- The help message includes the link key and reference (or `N/A`).
+
+The drawer does not close/reset the payment form. It is opened by the header help button and by the banner's help button.
+
+### 3.6 Actual hide behavior
+
+This is the important distinction between design intent and code:
+
+- When `checkout.support_config.enabled` is false, `buildCheckoutSupportConfig` returns `null`.
+- The drawer's `support` computed value is null, so:
+  - **Contact support hides.**
+  - **FAQ hides** (the FAQ is derived from `supportConfig`).
+  - **Working hours hide** (inside the contact block).
+- The following remain visible/usable:
+  - The header "Help & Support" button and the drawer itself.
+  - State guidance for the current attempt.
+  - The payment reference and copy action.
+  - The per-rail guide section (from `rail.helpGuide`).
+  - The per-rail banner.
+- Therefore the admin warning "Disabling this hides the Contact Us block on every checkout page" is accurate for the contact/FAQ block, but it does not remove the entire help center. The setting is a support-channel switch, not a global help kill switch.
+
+### 3.7 Localization and fallback
+
+- `currentLocale` comes from the checkout locale adapter (`ar` or `en`).
+- Rail display names fall back between Arabic and English.
+- Guide steps/prerequisites/troubleshooting use the selected language first, then the other language.
+- FAQ questions/answers are filtered to complete localized pairs.
+- Working hours fall back between languages.
+- The drawer's section titles are bilingual inline.
+
+### 3.8 Separation from admin/merchant help
+
+- Admin contextual help uses `GUIDE_ROUTE_HELP` and the 12-book guide; it does not read `supportConfig`.
+- Merchant contextual help uses M/D chapters; it does not read `supportConfig`.
+- Checkout help uses `supportConfig` and `helpGuide`; it does not read admin/merchant guide content.
+- The admin `/settings/checkout-help` page is the only authoring surface for the platform support config.
+- Per-rail content is seeded from core code and has no admin authoring surface.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. **Help data travels with the payment-link summary.** No second help request is required.
+2. **`enabled: false` returns `null` supportConfig.** The drawer must tolerate null and still render state/reference/rail help.
+3. **Only enabled support exposes platform/merchant contacts and FAQ.** The projection enforces this; the UI does not re-enable hidden data.
+4. **Merchant contact is link-derived.** It uses the loaded merchant's contact fields, not a merchant-supplied free-form block.
+5. **Per-rail guides are bilingual arrays.** Missing entries fall back to the other language.
+6. **The drawer never changes payment state.** It only displays status/reference and opens external contact links.
+7. **The banner is independent of support enabled.** It is driven by `rail.helpGuide`.
+8. **The reference copy is a UI convenience.** It does not prove payment.
+9. **No secrets are shown.** Support details are business contact data; payment secrets/OTP/PAN are never placed in the drawer.
+10. **The admin setting is versioned.** A change creates a new `checkout.support_config` version.
+
+## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
+
+| Surface | Location |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| Public summary + support/help projection | `GET v1/pay/:linkKey` in `core-back/api/internal/checkout.ts` |
+| Support setting | `platform_settings` key `checkout.support_config` |
+| Support seed | `DEFAULT_SUPPORT_CONFIG` in `core-back/prisma/seedGuides.ts` |
+| Rail guides seed | `RAIL_HELP_GUIDES` in `core-back/prisma/seedGuides.ts` |
+| Admin config page | `admin-front/src/pages/settings/checkout-help/index.tsx` |
+| Admin endpoints | `v1/admin/settings/checkout-support`, `/history`, `/summary`, `/summary/export` |
+| Payer banner | `checkout-front/src/components/help/PerRailInstructionsBanner.tsx` |
+| Payer drawer | `checkout-front/src/components/help/CheckoutHelpDrawer.tsx` |
+| Payer page mount | `checkout-front/src/pages/pay/[linkKey]/index.tsx` |
+
+## 6. Operational usage
+
+- Enable support: set `enabled`, configure at least one platform or merchant channel, set working hours, review FAQ, and save. The change creates a new version and affects new link fetches.
+- Disable support: expect contact and FAQ to disappear; the drawer, state guidance, reference and rail guide remain. Update any support scripts accordingly.
+- Add a per-rail guide: edit `RAIL_HELP_GUIDES` and reseed; there is no admin UI. Confirm the rail is visible and the `helpGuide` is present in the link summary.
+- Debug missing contact: check `enabled`, `show_platform_contact`/`show_merchant_contact`, and whether the link has merchant contact data.
+- Debug missing FAQ: check `enabled` and whether the selected-language question/answer pair is complete.
+- Debug missing banner: check `selectedRail.helpGuide`; a null/absent guide hides the banner.
+- Debug a support message: use the reference shown in the drawer; do not ask the payer for an OTP or PIN.
+
+## 7. Status and deviations
+
+### Implemented
+
+- Data-driven `supportConfig` projection from `checkout.support_config`.
+- Per-rail `helpGuide` projection from `rails.help_guide_json`.
+- Per-rail banner with prerequisites, steps, collapse and help entry.
+- Drawer with state guidance, reference copy, rail guide, FAQ and contact channels.
+- Bilingual fallback behavior.
+- WhatsApp/phone/email deep links with reference-aware messages.
+- Admin support config with versioning, preview, history, diff and summary export.
+- Seeded support config and 14 seeded rail guides (the seed comment says 13).
+
+### Partial
+
+- Support disabling hides contact/FAQ but not the whole help center; the UI warning can be read too broadly.
+- Per-rail guide authoring is code/seed-only.
+- The admin page subtitle mentions per-rail instructions but the page only edits support config.
+- The help drawer has no analytics or feedback capture.
+- The help center has no dedicated route; it is a drawer on `/pay/:linkKey`.
+
+### Missing / deferred
+
+- No admin editor for `helpGuideJson`.
+- No per-merchant support override; support is platform-wide.
+- No content version displayed to the payer.
+- No help-content search or FAQ deep links.
+- No guide v2 context/playbook/safeguard model for checkout.
+
+### Known bugs / risks
+
+- **Wording gap:** "per-rail instructions" in the admin subtitle implies an authoring capability that does not exist.
+- **Visibility gap:** disabling support does not remove state guidance, reference, rail guide or banner.
+- **Content risk:** per-rail guides are seeded code; a rail whose guide is stale or missing gives the payer less help than expected.
+- **Support risk:** the merchant contact comes from link data; if the merchant's phone/email is missing or stale, the payer sees no merchant channel.
+- **Security risk:** support flows must never ask for OTP/PIN; the guide and default FAQ reinforce this, but contact channels are external.
+- **Future-doc risk:** guide v2 is not the current checkout help implementation.
