If flagged, inspect the linked merchant record before proceeding. 2. **Verify Antivirus & File Integrity:** Ensure every `kyb_documents` row shows `av_status = CLEAN` and open the preview to confirm it is a genuine, legible document. 3. **Cross-Check Legal Name, Registration No. & Tax Certificate:** The Arabic legal name on the Commercial Registry (`السجل التجاري`) and Tax Certificate (`شهادة السداد الضريبي`) must match `merchants.legal_name` character-for-character, and `expires_on` must be in the future. 4. **Verify Beneficial Owners (The 25% Rule):** Confirm that every natural person owning `>= 25%` (or exercising control as Director/Signatory) is listed in `beneficial_owners` with a valid National ID/Passport and `screening_status = CLEAR` (or a dispositioned false positive). 5. **Verify Payout Bank Account Ownership:** Open the `BANK_LETTER` document and confirm the IBAN belongs to the **merchant's legal entity name** (not a personal account of an unrelated individual). 6. **Verify Business Activity & Volume Plausibility:** Confirm `expected_monthly_volume` is realistic for the declared `business_category`. 7. **Assign the Appropriate `proposed_risk_tier` (`LOW`, `STANDARD`, `HIGH`).** --- ### BOOK 10: The 7-Layer AML & Compliance Program, Screening Dispositions & CBL Reporting (`/aml/*`) #### Chapter 10.1: How Our 7 AML Layers Work Together 1. **Layer 1 (Onboarding Screening):** Screens the merchant entity and all Beneficial Owners against Sanctions, PEP, Adverse Media, and Internal Watchlists upon Join Request submission. **Fail-Closed Rule:** If the screening provider is down (`result = ERROR`), the system blocks approval (`503 SCREENING_UNAVAILABLE`) until screening succeeds. 2. **Layer 2 (Periodic & List-Update Re-Screening):** Automatically re-screens active merchants when watchlists update or on their tier schedule. 3. **Layer 3 (Hot-Path Transaction Posture Check):** Runs inside the checkout initiation guard in `< 5ms` against local watchlists, merchant status, and fast `aml_rules`. 4. **Layer 4 (Confirmation-Time & Batch Monitoring):** Evaluates `SINGLE_AMOUNT`, `CUMULATIVE_WINDOW` (aggregating across all links/apps of a subject so splitting a sale across 5 links never evades a threshold—Edge Case 125!), `STRUCTURING` (clustering payments just below a threshold), and `MERCHANT_DIRECT_AMOUNT`. - **Correlated Escalation Rule:** If a payment triggers both a Velocity `FLAG` rule and an AML rule on the same attempt, case severity automatically escalates to **`CRITICAL`** (4-hour SLA). 5. **Layer 5 (Case Management — `/aml/cases`):** Compliance analysts (`COMPLIANCE`, Maker) investigate and propose **Release (`RELEASED`)**, **Void & Refund to Payer (`REJECTED_VOID`)**, **Freeze (`FROZEN`)**, or **Escalate to STR (`ESCALATED_STR`)**. Only the **`MLRO`** (Checker) can approve the resolution, which atomically posts the `AML_RELEASE` or `AML_VOID` journal entry and finalizes the payment attempt! 6. **Layer 6 (Regulatory Reporting — `/aml/reports`):** Generates `LARGE_TRANSACTION` (LTR), `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY` (STR), and `PERIODIC_RETURN` filings. **Safety Guard (`OD-1`):** A `PROVISIONAL` reporting rule can detect and record internally, but the database refuses to submit a live regulatory filing unless the rule has been promoted to `CONFIRMED` with a written CBL circular reference (`source_reference`). 7. **Layer 7 (No Tipping-Off & 5-Year Retention):** Strictly blocks `AML-CONFIDENTIAL` data from non-compliance staff and merchant notifications, and preserves all audit/ledger records under the 5-year retention policy (`OD-4`). --- ### BOOK 11: Disputes, Chargebacks, Refunds, Cash-Outs & Negative Balance Ceilings #### Chapter 11.1: How Automated Chargeback Drafting Works (`/disputes` & `/adjustments`) When an upstream switch (like Moamalat or MPGS) notifies us via webhook or statement that a cardholder disputed a payment: 1. Our system creates a `disputes` row (`UNIQUE(gateway_id, external_dispute_ref)` so duplicate webhooks never draft two chargebacks). 2. If a voluntary refund was already partially issued on that payment earlier, the system automatically caps the chargeback amount to the **unrefunded remainder** (`settled_amount - executed_refunds`, Edge Case 126). 3. The non-human service identity **`SYSTEM_AUTOMATION`** automatically creates a `DRAFT -> PENDING_REVIEW` `CHARGEBACK` Adjustment as the **Maker**. 4. **Human Authorization Required:** `SYSTEM_AUTOMATION` is strictly forbidden from acting as a Checker. No money moves until a human **`FINANCE` Checker** reviews and approves the adjustment in `/approvals`! 5. **What if the Merchant Already Cashed Out Their Wallet?** - Each merchant has a `negative_balance_ceiling` (default `0.0000 LYD` for new merchants; adjustable via Maker-Checker). - If the chargeback stays within their ceiling, the wallet balance goes negative (Journal Entry 15, e.g., `-57.0000 LYD`), and every future payment the merchant receives automatically nets against that negative balance until it returns to `+0.0000 LYD`! - If the chargeback would breach the ceiling, the adjustment is held in `PENDING_REVIEW` and opens a **`P1` Operator Case** so Finance can collect from the merchant or net against pending cash-outs. #### Chapter 11.2: Safe Refunds (Three-Phase Non-Deadlocking Execution) When a Finance Checker approves a `REFUND` adjustment on a settled payment: - **Phase 1 (Claim):** Locks the attempt, verifies that `rail.capabilities.refund` (or `partial_refund`) is supported, verifies `refund_window_days` has not expired, checks `SUM(refunds) + new_refund <= settled_amount`, and sets adjustment state to `EXECUTING`. - **Phase 2 (Gateway Call):** Executes the gateway's `REFUND` flow over the network with no database lock held open. If the gateway times out, the adjustment safely stays in `EXECUTING` (never double-refunding) until inquiry/reconciliation confirms the outcome. - **Phase 3 (Finalize):** Once the gateway returns `provider_refund_ref`, posts Journal Entry 9 (or 14 for NeomPay) and marks the adjustment `EXECUTED`. --- ### BOOK 12: Platform Profitability, Liquidity, Solvency & The 12 Go-Live Gates #### Chapter 12.1: Reading the Profitability & Liquidity Dashboards (`/finance/profitability` & `/finance/liquidity`) Every number on our Finance dashboards is computed directly from `journal_lines`: - **Gross Commission Revenue:** Total credits minus debits on `PLATFORM_INCOME` (note: commission on `AML_HOLD` payments is recognized only after the hold is released). - **Realized Gateway Cost:** Total `PROVIDER_FEE_EXPENSE` + `GATEWAY_FEE_EXPENSE` (including statement fee variance true-ups). - **Net Revenue:** Gross Commission minus Realized Gateway Cost. - **Treasury Cover Ratio:** `(TREASURY Balance + GATEWAY_CLEARING Balances) / (MERCHANT_WALLET Balances + AML_HOLD + CHARGEBACK_RESERVE)`. - **Clearing Ageing Buckets:** Shows how much money sits in `GATEWAY_CLEARING` for `T+0`, `T+1`, `T+2`, and `> settlement_lag_days`. If a gateway has not wired funds past its lag window, follow up with the partner bank before approving large cash-outs. - **Ledger Invariant Monitor (`/finance/invariant-check`):** Must always read **`0.0000 LYD` drift**. If any drift is detected, automated payouts halt immediately (`Runbook RB-04`). --- # PART II: THE ADMIN PORTAL A-TO-Z EMPLOYEE ACADEMY & CERTIFICATION LMS (`admin-front/src/pages/academy/index.tsx`) ## 4. Verbatim Content: All 8 Academy Modules, Lessons, Interactive Labs & Quizzes (`modulesTrackA.ts` & `modulesTrackB.ts`) OpenCode MUST include all 8 modules below verbatim in `admin-front/src/content/academy/`. --- ### MODULE 1 (A–C): Foundations From Zero — How Digital Payments, Links, Slots & Zero-Trust Security Work #### Lesson M1-L1: The Life of a Payment (Who Are the 4 Players?) Imagine a customer named **Tariq** wants to pay **`250.000 LYD`** to **Al-Madina Clinic** for a medical checkup. There are **4 players** in this story: 1. **The Merchant (Al-Madina Clinic):** Uses our **Merchant Portal** to create a digital bill called a **Payment Link** for `250.000 LYD`. 2. **The Payer (Tariq):** Clicks the link on his phone, opening our **Checkout Page**. 3. **Our Platform (The Payment Gateway):** Shows Tariq the available payment methods (**Rails** like Sadad, Edfali, Moamalat Card, LYPay), locks the link so nobody else can pay the same bill at the same time, talks to the bank, and records the accounting entry. 4. **The Upstream Gateway / Bank Switch (e.g., Almadar Sadad or Moamalat National Switch):** The external institution that actually holds Tariq's money and verifies his SMS OTP or card PIN. #### Lesson M1-L2: Wallets, Applications, Payment Links & The Single-Use Slot Lock Before a Merchant can create a Payment Link, they set up two building blocks inside their account: - **A Wallet (`wallets`):** The digital account where the merchant's money accumulates on our platform. Each wallet has a single currency (default `LYD`) and is tied 1-to-1 to a **`MERCHANT_WALLET` General Ledger Account**. - **An Application (`applications`):** Represents one sales channel of the merchant (for example, *"Clinic Website"*, *"WhatsApp Billing Desk"*, or *"Main Reception POS"*). - **Hard Rule:** Every Application is connected to **exactly one Wallet** (`assigned_wallet_id`). Why? So there is never any confusion about which wallet receives the money when a link is paid! When a customer opens a **Single-Use Payment Link (`use_count = 1`)** and clicks "Pay with Sadad", what stops them from opening the same link on a second phone and paying the same invoice twice? - **The Atomic Slot Reservation (`active_locked_count`):** The instant Tariq clicks "Pay", our database locks the link row and sets `active_locked_count = 1`. - Our database enforces the formula: **`confirmed_count + active_locked_count <= use_count`**. - While Tariq's attempt is in progress (`active_locked_count = 1`), anyone else opening that single-use link sees *"A payment is currently in progress for this link"*. - The lock is released **only** if Tariq's attempt ends in `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, or `EXPIRED`. If Tariq's attempt becomes **`UNKNOWN`** (because the bank timed out), the lock stays **HELD** so Tariq cannot accidentally pay twice while we verify with the bank! #### Lesson M1-L3: Why We Never Trust the Customer's Browser (Zero-Trust Checkout) In web browsers, customers (or attackers) can change anything on their screen: - They can modify the URL bar after a redirect to say `?status=success&amount=250.000`. - They can open the browser's Developer Console (`F12`) and trigger a JavaScript callback like `Lightbox.completeCallback()`. - They can try to send `"amount": 0.01` in an API request body. **How our platform defeats all three attacks automatically:** 1. **Checkout Never Accepts Amounts from the Browser:** The `/initiate` and `/confirm` APIs do not even have an `amount` field! `core-back` reads the amount strictly from `payment_links.amount` in the database. 2. **Return URLs and Browser Callbacks Are "Doorbells", Not Proof:** When a browser hits `/return/:token` or `/client-event`, our server transitions the attempt to `VERIFYING` and makes a secure, server-to-server **`VERIFY` (Inquiry)** call directly to the bank's server. Money is posted **only** when the bank's server confirms all **5 Trusted Success Facts** (Status = Success, Our Reference Matches, Settled Amount Matches, Currency Matches, Environment Matches). #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 1 (`LAB-01`): The Payment & Tamper-Detection Tracer - **What the Student Sees in the Lab UI:** An interactive 4-column visual simulation showing `[Payer's Browser] -> [checkout-back] -> [core-back + Database] -> [Bank Switch]`. - **Step 1 Task:** The student clicks **"Start 250.000 LYD Payment"**, observes `active_locked_count` change from `0` to `1`, and must answer what happens when a second browser tab tries to initiate on the same link (*Correct action: Block second tab with `SLOT_RESERVATION_FAILED`*). - **Step 2 Task (Attack Simulation):** The simulated payer intercepts the browser redirect and changes the URL to `/return/tok_123?status=PAID&amount=250.000` without paying at the bank. The lab asks the student to choose how `core-back` responds: - *Option A (Fatal Error):* Mark the attempt `SUCCEEDED` and credit the merchant wallet. *(Triggers red incident screen: "You just credited 250 LYD of fake money from a forged browser URL!")* - *Option B (Fatal Error):* Mark the attempt `FAILED` immediately. *(Triggers warning: "A real customer might have paid while their browser query string was stripped!")* - *Option C (Correct):* Treat `/return` as an untrusted hint, transition to `VERIFYING`, and run the server-to-server `VERIFY` inquiry against the bank switch. #### Module 1 Verification Quiz (`QUIZ-M1` — 8 Questions, 100% Required) 1. **Q1:** Why is every Merchant `Application` required by the database schema to have `assigned_wallet_id NOT NULL` (connected to exactly one Wallet)? - *A)* To limit merchants to one currency across their entire company. - *B)* **Correct:** To eliminate settlement ambiguity so every Payment Link and POS terminal under that Application has a single, deterministic destination Wallet. - *C)* Because a Merchant is only allowed to create one Wallet in total. - *Explanation:* A Merchant can create multiple Wallets and multiple Applications, but each Application binds to one specific Wallet so the ledger always knows which `MERCHANT_WALLET` GL account to credit. 2. **Q2:** A customer opens a Single-Use Payment Link (`use_count = 1`, `infinite_use = false`), enters their phone number for Sadad, and receives an SMS OTP. At this exact moment, what are `confirmed_count` and `active_locked_count` on the link? - *A)* `confirmed_count = 1`, `active_locked_count = 0` - *B)* `confirmed_count = 0`, `active_locked_count = 0` - *C)* **Correct:** `confirmed_count = 0`, `active_locked_count = 1` - *Explanation:* The slot is reserved (`active_locked_count = 1`) at initiation and only moves to `confirmed_count = 1` (releasing `active_locked_count = 0`) when the payment reaches `SUCCEEDED`. 3. **Q3:** While a customer's payment attempt is in `UNKNOWN` status (because the bank timed out during OTP confirmation), what happens to `active_locked_count` on that single-use link? - *A)* Immediately credits the merchant's wallet. - *B)* **Correct:** Treats the browser event as an untrusted hint (`must_inquire = true`), transitions to `VERIFYING`, and calls Moamalat's server-to-server `FilterTransactions` inquiry API. - *C)* Ignores the event completely and waits for tomorrow's CSV file. - *Explanation:* Browser callbacks can be spoofed via browser developer tools (`T-06`), so they only trigger a server inquiry. 6. **Q6:** Which service in our 7-project architecture is the **only** service that holds the PostgreSQL 18 database connection and `KMS_MASTER_KEY`? - *A)* Browser IP, User-Agent, Link Key, Merchant Name, and Timezone. - *B)* **Correct:** Status is Success, Our Reference matches, Settled Amount matches within route tolerance, Currency matches, and Environment (`SANDBOX` vs `LIVE`) matches. - *C)* Only that HTTP status is `200 OK`. --- ### MODULE 2 (D–F): The Four-Eyes (Maker-Checker) Governance Engine & Field Control #### Lesson M2-L1: Descriptive vs. Sensitive Fields — What Requires Four Eyes? Not every edit requires a second person. If a merchant fixes a typo in their store's display trade name, making them wait for a Checker would slow down support. However, if someone changes a merchant's **payout bank IBAN**, **commission rate**, **risk tier**, or **application wallet binding**, a single mistake or malicious insider action could misdirect funds. Therefore, our platform divides every field into two classes: 1. **Descriptive Fields (Direct Edit + Logged in `detail_change_logs`):** - Merchant `trade_name`, display logo, POS terminal name/location, application `name` and `business_use_description`. - Takes effect immediately, and writes an unchangeable before/after row in `detail_change_logs` so Support can always see who changed what and when. 2. **Sensitive Fields (Strictly Governed by Maker-Checker `approval_requests`):** - **Merchant:** `legal_name`, `tax_id`, `registration_no`, `business_category`, `payout_bank_details_json`, `risk_tier`, `kyb_status`, `commission_receivable_ceiling`, `negative_balance_ceiling`. - **Application:** `assigned_wallet_id`, `rail_whitelist`, `redirect_domain_allowlist`. - **Platform & Money:** All `adjustments` (refunds, chargebacks, manual credits/debits), `commission_profiles`, `velocity_rules`, `aml_rules`, `aml_cases` resolutions, `regulatory_reports`, `gateway_versions` promotions to `LIVE`, and admin `users` authority changes. #### Lesson M2-L2: Optimistic Concurrency (`base_version`) & Stale Approvals What happens if Maker 1 proposes changing a Merchant's `risk_tier` when the Merchant record is at `version = 4` (`base_version = 4`), and before a Checker reviews it, another approved request updates the Merchant to `version = 5`? - When the Checker clicks **Approve** on Maker 1's request, `ApprovalService` compares `base_version (4)` against the Merchant's current version (`5`). - Because they no longer match, the system **refuses to overwrite the newer record** and returns the request to `DRAFT` (`BASE_VERSION_MISMATCH`) so the Maker can review the updated record first! #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 2 (`LAB-02`): The Checker Approval Desk Simulator - **What the Student Sees:** A simulated `/approvals` queue containing **4 pending requests** with full JSON-Patch diffs and attached evidence documents. If Merchant B uploads the exact same file that Merchant A uploaded, the reviewer screen lights up with a **`DUPLICATE_DOCUMENT`** warning badge (Edge Case 120). 3. **Beneficial Owners & The 25% Threshold (`beneficial_owners`):** - Every natural person who owns **`25%` or more** (`aml.owner_threshold_percent`) or exercises control (`DIRECTOR`, `SIGNATORY`, `CONTROLLER`) must be declared and screened. - If a beneficial owner is added or edited *after* the join request was submitted, the system automatically triggers a new AML screening, invalidates any pending approval, and returns the request to `IN_REVIEW` (Edge Case 121). #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 3 (`LAB-03`): The KYB & Fraud Detection Desk - **What the Student Sees:** Three submitted `join_requests` in a simulated reviewer console: - **Applicant A (*Al-Waha Pharmacy*):** Clean Commercial Registry, valid Tax Certificate, 2 owners (60% / 40%) with `CLEAR` screening, Bank Letter matching *Al-Waha Pharmacy*, `LOW` risk. *(Correct action: Complete 7-point checklist & **Approve**).* - **Applicant B (*Desert Star Trading*):** Commercial Registry expired 8 months ago, and the Tax Certificate scan is illegible/blurry. *(Correct action: Click **Request Info (`INFO_REQUESTED`)**, selecting `COMMERCIAL_REGISTRY` and `TAX_CERTIFICATE`, which pauses the SLA timer).* - **Applicant C (*Barqa Express Electronics*):** System displays a red `DUPLICATE_DOCUMENT` badge on the Commercial Registry PDF (matching a merchant rejected last week for prohibited activity) and a `DUPLICATE_OR_RELATED` match on the owner's National ID. *(Correct action: **Reject** with code `PROHIBITED_ACTIVITY` / `POLICY` and flag for Compliance).* #### Module 3 Verification Quiz (`QUIZ-M3` — 8 Questions, 100% Required) 1. **Q1:** What happens to the review SLA timer (`sla_due_at`) when a reviewer moves a Join Request to `INFO_REQUESTED`? If someone changes a flow step URL to an unlisted external domain, the engine refuses to attach any secrets from `credential_sets`! 4. **The Unmapped Money-Step Rule:** In `StatusRule`, if a `MOVES_MONEY` step receives a response that matches **none** of your status rules, the engine transitions the attempt to **`UNKNOWN`** (never `FAILED`). #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 5 (`LAB-05`): Build & Verify a Two-Step OTP Rail + Moamalat Hex-HMAC Profile - **What the Student Does in the Lab:** 1. Our server tries to call our primary route (`plutu`), and Plutu's server returns `503 Service Unavailable`. - Because no OTP was sent and no money could possibly have moved yet, our engine **transparently fails over** within milliseconds to our backup route (`edfali_direct`), sends the OTP through BCD Bank, and the customer never even notices Plutu was down! - **Case B — Gateway Times Out at `SUBMIT` (At Point of No Return — `MOVES_MONEY`):** - Customer received their OTP, typed `482910`, and clicked Confirm. Our server sent the debit call to the bank, and after 15 seconds (`timeout_ms`), the bank hadn't replied. - Did the bank take the customer's `250 LYD` right before the connection dropped, or did the request never reach them? **We do not know.** - Therefore, our engine moves the attempt to **`UNKNOWN`**, keeps the link slot locked (`active_locked_count = 1`), shows the customer *"We are confirming your payment with the bank—please do not pay again"*, starts background `PollWorker` inquiries, and opens an **`OperatorCase`** in `/operator-cases`. #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 6 (`LAB-06`): Incident & `UNKNOWN` Queue Simulator - **What the Student Resolves in the Lab:** 1. **Ticket 1 (`UNKNOWN` on LYPay — Supports Inquiry):** Student clicks **"Inquire Gateway Now"**, inspects the `VERIFY` response (`status: "Confirmed", provider_ref: "LYP-99201", amount: "250.000"`), and watches the attempt transition to `SUCCEEDED` and post the ledger entry. 2. **Ticket 2 (`UNKNOWN` on Edfali Direct — No Inquiry API):** The "Inquire" button is disabled because Edfali direct has no inquiry endpoint. Every candidate hit in `aml_screening_matches` must be reviewed by a `COMPLIANCE` analyst and given a disposition: 1. **`FALSE_POSITIVE`:** Common name similarity, but Date of Birth, Nationality, or National ID proves it is a different person. You may toggle **`suppress_future = true`** with a `suppress_until` expiry date so periodic re-screens don't re-alert on the exact same list entry—unless the owner's identifying data changes! 2. **`TRUE_MATCH` / `ESCALATED`:** Genuine match on a PEP or Sanctions list. For a Sanctions match, the merchant is immediately restricted (`SUSPENDED` via emergency path), cash-outs are frozen, and an STR draft is opened for the `MLRO`. #### Lesson M7-L2: The Strict "No Tipping-Off" Law Under AML law and CBL regulations, **Tipping-Off**—telling a merchant, beneficial owner, or payer (directly or indirectly) that their payment or account is being held for AML suspicion or that a Suspicious Activity Report (`STR`) is being prepared—is a severe legal violation. - If a merchant contacts Support asking why a payment is taking time to settle or why their account was suspended, Support (`SUPPORT` role) **cannot even see** the `AML-CONFIDENTIAL` tables (`403 Forbidden`), and all merchant-facing messages use neutral operational wording. #### Interactive Sandbox Lab 7 (`LAB-07`): Compliance & MLRO Investigation Simulator - **What the Student Resolves in the Lab:** 1. **Screening Match 1:** Beneficial Owner *"محمد علي المبروك"* born `1994-05-12` (Libyan National ID verified) matches a PEP list entry with a `78%` name score, but the PEP entry was born in `1952` in another country. *(Correct action: Disposition as `FALSE_POSITIVE` with notes comparing DOB and National ID, and set `suppress_future` for 12 months).* 2. **AML Case 2 (`CRITICAL` Correlated Escalation):** A merchant declared `expected_monthly_volume = 5,000 LYD` (small stationery shop), but today processed 8 rapid payments of `4,900 LYD` each (`39,200 LYD` total in 2 hours) just below the `5,000 LYD` threshold, triggering both a Velocity `FLAG` and the `STRUCTURING` AML rule! *(Correct action: Propose `ESCALATED_STR` / `FROZEN` for `MLRO` Checker approval, and verify that the merchant notification template contains zero mention of AML/Structuring).* #### Module 7 Verification Quiz (`QUIZ-M7` — 8 Questions, 100% Required) 1. **Q1:** What happens when a single payment attempt triggers **both** a `FLAG` Velocity Rule and an AML Rule? A week later, the customer's bank sends a `100.0000 LYD` **Chargeback (`DISPUTE_OPENED`)** webhook for that same payment! - If our system blindly drafted a `100.0000 LYD` chargeback adjustment, the merchant would lose `40 + 100 = 140 LYD` on a `100 LYD` sale! - **How Our Platform Protects the Merchant (Edge Case 126):** When the dispute arrives, our engine locks the attempt (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), sums all `EXECUTED` and `EXECUTING` refunds (`40.0000 LYD`), and automatically caps the drafted `CHARGEBACK` adjustment to the unrefunded remainder (**`60.0000 LYD`**). Once saved, no human being (not even you or our staff) can ever read the secret back—it can only be replaced. 2. **How Money & Commission Work in `MERCHANT_DIRECT` Mode:** - Because the gateway is using **your own account**, when a customer pays `100.000 LYD`, the gateway sends that `100.000 LYD` **directly to your company's bank account**! - Therefore, our platform **does not credit your Merchant Wallet** for `MERCHANT_DIRECT` payments. Instead, we record our software commission (e.g., `3.000 LYD`) in your **Commission Receivable** balance (`COMMISSION_RECEIVABLE`), which is automatically netted against your platform Wallet balance or settled by invoice. - **Important:** Keep your Commission Receivable below your account's `commission_receivable_ceiling`; if unpaid commission exceeds your ceiling, `MERCHANT_DIRECT` routes automatically pause until settled! --- ### CHAPTER M-10: Managing Your Team, Roles, Application Scopes & Security (`/team`) **Who this is for:** Business Owners (`MERCHANT_ADMIN`) Never share your owner login password with cashiers or accountants! Instead, open **Team (`/team`)** and invite each staff member with only the permissions they need: - **`MERCHANT_CASHIER`:** Can only operate assigned in-store POS screens (`/pos`). Cannot see company bank accounts, cannot create API tokens, and cannot request cash-outs. - **`MERCHANT_STAFF`:** You choose their exact checkboxes (`links.create`, `payments.read`, `stats.read`, etc.) and you can restrict them to **specific Applications (`app_scope_ids`)**—so the manager of *Branch A* can only see links and payments for *Branch A*, never *Branch B*! - **`MERCHANT_ADMIN`:** Full business owner access (requires mandatory Multi-Factor Authentication `MFA`). --- # PART IV: THE MERCHANT DEVELOPER & API INTEGRATION GUIDE (`merchant-front/src/pages/guide/developers/index.tsx`) ## 8. Verbatim Content: Complete Zero-to-Production API & Webhook Reference (`merchantDeveloperApiGuide.ts`) This guide is written so that **both** a junior web developer building their first e-commerce site and a senior backend architect can integrate with our External Merchant API (`/api/v1/external/*`) cleanly and securely on the first try. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-01: How the API Works From Zero (For Beginners & Architects) If your company has an online store, mobile app, hospital billing system, or ERP (like Odoo, WooCommerce, Laravel, or a custom Node/Python app), you can automate payment link creation and payment verification so no human has to click buttons in the portal: ```text 1. Customer clicks "Checkout (150.000 LYD)" on Your Website │ ▼ 2. Your Backend Server calls: POST https://merchant./api/v1/external/links (Using your secret `pg_live_...` Bearer Token + Amount: "150.000") │ ▼ 3. Our Platform returns: { "key": "lnk_01J...", "checkoutUrl": "https://pay./pay/lnk_01J..." } │ ▼ 4. Your Website sends the Customer to `checkoutUrl` (where they pay with Sadad, Edfali, Moamalat, LYPay, etc.) │ ▼ 5. When the Customer finishes, Your Backend Server verifies the truth by calling: GET https://merchant./api/v1/external/links/lnk_01J... (or GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference) — and ONLY marks the order paid when `state === "COMPLETED"` / `status === "SUCCEEDED"`! ``` --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-02: Authentication (`pg_live_` Bearer Tokens) & IP CIDR Allowlists (`/developers/tokens`) #### 1. Creating Your API Access Token 1. In the Merchant Portal, open **Developers -> API Tokens (`/developers/tokens`)** and click **Create Token**. 2. Select the **Application** this token will belong to, and select the minimum required **Scopes** (`links:create`, `links:read`, `links:cancel`, `payments:read`). 3. Copy your token immediately (it starts with **`pg_live_`** followed by 32 random base64url bytes). - **Why can't I view the token again later?** For your security, our database never stores your plaintext token—it stores only a one-way `SHA-256` hash (`token_hash`) and the last 4 characters (`last_four`). If you lose the token, revoke it and create a new one. 4. **NEVER put a `pg_live_` token inside frontend browser JavaScript, a React/Vue bundle, or a mobile APK!** `pg_live_` tokens must only be called from your own backend server. #### 2. Locking Your Token to Your Server's IP Address (`ip_whitelist_enabled`) To make a stolen token useless to an attacker, enable **IP Whitelist (`ip_whitelist_enabled = true`)** and add your backend server's static public IP in CIDR notation: - Single server IP example: `203.0.113.45/32` - Subnet example: `203.0.113.0/24` If any request arrives with your token from an IP address outside your CIDR list, our edge and core guards reject it immediately with `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-03: Money Precision Rules & Redirect Allowlists (Avoid These 3 Common Mistakes) 1. **Always Send Amounts as Decimal Strings (Never Floats!):** - Libyan Dinars have **3 decimal places (Dirhams)**, and our ledger uses `DECIMAL(18,4)`. - Always pass amounts as strings like `"150.000"` or `"76.255"`, **never** JavaScript floats like `150.00000000000003`. 2. **`redirectUrl` Rules:** - A custom `redirectUrl` is permitted **only on Single-Use links** (`infiniteUse: false, useCount: 1`). - The hostname of `redirectUrl` (e.g., `https://shop.yourcompany.ly/orders/4092/return`) **must** be pre-registered in your Application's `redirect_domain_allowlist` in `/applications`, otherwise link creation will fail with `400 REDIRECT_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`. 3. **Never Trust the Browser Return Alone:** - When the customer's browser lands back on your `redirectUrl`, treat that page load only as a trigger for your backend server to call `GET /api/v1/external/links/:key` (or `GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference`). Only fulfill the order when our API returns `state: "COMPLETED"` and the attempt `status: "SUCCEEDED"`. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-04: Complete Endpoint Reference (`/api/v1/external/*`) #### Endpoint 1: Create a Payment Link — `POST /api/v1/external/links` - **Required Header:** `Authorization: Bearer pg_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` - **Request Body Schema:** ```json { "applicationId": "0192d4a0-7c10-7000-8000-000000000001", "amount": "150.000", "currency": "LYD", "feeBearer": "MERCHANT_ABSORBS", "infiniteUse": false, "useCount": 1, "redirectUrl": "https://shop.yourcompany.ly/checkout/return?orderId=ORD-9012", "railWhitelist": null, "expiresAt": "2026-11-01T18:00:00.000Z" } ``` - **Success Response (`201 Created`):** ```json { "id": "0192d8f0-1122-7000-8000-000000000099", "key": "lnk_0192d8f0112270008000000000000099", "checkoutUrl": "https://pay.yourdomain.ly/pay/lnk_0192d8f0112270008000000000000099", "amount": "150.0000", "currency": "LYD", "feeBearer": "MERCHANT_ABSORBS", "state": "PENDING", "confirmedCount": 0, "activeLockedCount": 0, "expiresAt": "2026-11-01T18:00:00.000Z" } ``` #### Endpoint 2: Get Link & Attempts Status — `GET /api/v1/external/links/:key` - Returns the current link `state` (`PENDING | COMPLETED | EXPIRED | CANCELLED`), slot counters (`confirmedCount`, `activeLockedCount`), and the array of attempts with their `reference`, `status`, `railCode`, `requestedAmount`, `surchargeAmount`, `totalChargedAmount`, `platformCommissionAmount`, `netMerchantAmount`, and `terminalAt`. #### Endpoint 3: Get Single Payment Attempt by Reference — `GET /api/v1/external/payments/:reference` - Looks up a specific attempt by its unique platform reference (`reference`) and returns its authoritative status and settlement breakdown. #### Endpoint 4: Cancel an Unpaid Payment Link — `POST /api/v1/external/links/:key/cancel` - Cancels a `PENDING` link as long as no attempt is currently past the point of no return. --- ### DEV CHAPTER D-05: Copy-Pasteable Production Code Templates (Interactive Code Generator) The interactive widget in `/guide/developers` pre-fills your selected `applicationId` and generates ready-to-run code in 4 languages: #### 1. TypeScript / Node.js / Bun ```ts const PG_BASE_URL = "https://merchant.yourdomain.ly/api/v1/external"; const PG_API_TOKEN = process.env.PG_LIVE_TOKEN!; // pg_live_... export async function createCheckoutLink(orderId: string, amountLyd: string) { const response = await fetch(`${PG_BASE_URL}/links`, { method: "POST", headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${PG_API_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ applicationId: process.env.PG_APPLICATION_ID!, amount: amountLyd, // Always pass a decimal string, e.g. "150.000" currency: "LYD", feeBearer: "MERCHANT_ABSORBS", infiniteUse: false, useCount: 1, redirectUrl: `https://shop.yourcompany.ly/orders/${encodeURIComponent(orderId)}/verify`, }), }); if (!response.ok) { const err = await response.json(); throw new Error(`Payment Gateway Error [${err.code}]: ${err.message}`); } return (await response.json()) as { key: string; checkoutUrl: string; state: string }; } export async function isLinkPaidAndConfirmed(linkKey: string): Promise { const response = await fetch(`${PG_BASE_URL}/links/${encodeURIComponent(linkKey)}`, { headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${PG_API_TOKEN}` }, }); if (!response.ok) return false; const link = await response.json(); return link.state === "COMPLETED" && Number(link.confirmedCount) >= 1; } ``` #### 2. PHP (Laravel / Guzzle) ```php acceptJson() ->post(config('services.payment_gateway.base_url') . '/links', [ 'applicationId' => config('services.payment_gateway.app_id'), 'amount' => $amountLyd, // e.g. "150.000" 'currency' => 'LYD', 'feeBearer' => 'MERCHANT_ABSORBS', 'infiniteUse' => false, 'useCount' => 1, 'redirectUrl' => route('checkout.verify', ['orderId' => $orderId]), ]); $response->throw(); return $response->json(); } } ``` #### 3.  # STANDALONE FAKE PAYMENT RAILS EMULATOR & CHAOS TESTING PORTAL — MASTER ARCHITECTURE & TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION
 
 **Target Repository:** `selmotamed-ctrl/payment-gateway-monolith`  
 **Service Workspace Directories:** `fake-rails-back` · `fake-rails-front` · `deploy` · `core-back`  
 **Runtime & Stack Conventions:** Bun (`^1.4.1`) + Express 5 (`^5.2.1`) + Zod 4 (`^4.5.4`) + `bun:sqlite` (zero-dependency isolated persistence) · Vue 3 (`^3.5.22`) TSX/JSX + Vuetify 3 (`^3.10.7`) + `kt-dc` + Vite (`rolldown-vite`)
 
 ## Executive Summary & Architectural Vision
 
 Testing a zero-code, multi-rail payment gateway platform across 20 heterogeneous Libyan and international payment switches (each with distinct collection modes, cryptographic signature schemes, amount scales, asynchronous webhook shapes, and T+N statement formats) cannot rely solely on unit mocks or unstable partner sandboxes. Partner sandboxes frequently suffer from strict hourly rate limits, unannounced downtime, inability to deterministically trigger edge cases (such as `MOVES_MONEY` socket resets, conflicting webhook vs. inquiry states, or T+N fee variances), and lack of visibility into what the upstream switch actually received.
 
 This specification designs a **Standalone Fake Payment Rails Emulator & Chaos Testing Service** (`fake-rails-back` + `fake-rails-front`) that acts as a complete, self-contained external payment ecosystem:
 
 1. **Zero Shared Database with the Payment Gateway (`100% Out-of-Process Isolation`):**
    - `fake-rails-back` has zero access to `core-back`'s PostgreSQL 18 database and shares no memory with `core-back`. It persists its own transactions, webhook delivery queues, and chaos rules in an isolated embedded SQLite WAL database (`bun:sqlite` at `shared/data/fake-rails.sqlite`).
    - To `core-back`, the Fake Rails Service is indistinguishable from 20 real external bank switches and aggregators over HTTPS.
 2. **All 9 Collection Modes, All 10 Flow Phases, and All 20 Gateway Profiles:**
    - Emulates every collection mode (`OTP_PULL`, `REDIRECT`, `EMBEDDED`, `PUSH_APPROVAL`, `QR_DISPLAY`, `PAY_CODE`, `DEEP_LINK`, `MANUAL`, `HYBRID`) and every lifecycle phase (`CREDENTIAL_CHECK`, `PRE_INITIATE`, `INITIATE`, `SUBMIT`, `VERIFY`, `CANCEL`, `REFUND`, `VOID`, `CAPTURE`, `SETTLEMENT_FETCH`), plus interactive Hosted Checkout pages (`REDIRECT`) and drop-in JavaScript widget scripts (`EMBEDDED` Moamalat Lightbox & MPGS Hosted Session).
 3. **Production-Deployable via the Multi-Host Deployment Engine (`deploy/`):**
    - Integrates into `deploy/deploy.env` and `deploy/deploy.ts` as an optional 6th logical host role (`FAKE_RAILS_HOST`, colocated or dedicated) gated by explicit safety flags (`FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="true"` and `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION="true"`), with configurable ports, TLS modes, PM2 process management, Nginx reverse-proxy templates, and UFW firewall rules.
    - Automatically relaxes `core-back`'s SSRF private-IP guard **only** for the explicitly allowlisted Fake Rails host/IP when `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS="true"` is set, preserving full SSRF protection against all other private/loopback addresses.
 4. **Single-User Tester Portal & Live Chaos Matrix (`fake-rails-front`):**
    - Protected by a single tester credential pair (`FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER` and `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`) injected directly from `deploy.env`.
    - Streams incoming requests, outbound responses, and webhook deliveries in real time over Server-Sent Events (SSE).
    - Provides per-rail and per-phase **probabilistic failure sliders (0%–100%)** and **deterministic scenario overrides** so testers can configure any rail to fail at a given percentage chance with specific failure modes (`TIMEOUT_HANG`, `SOCKET_RESET`, `HTTP_500`, `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `WRONG_OTP`, `AMOUNT_MISMATCH`, `DUPLICATE_WEBHOOK`, `FORGED_SIGNATURE`, `CONFLICTING_INQUIRY`), manually approve/reject pending `PUSH_APPROVAL` / `QR_DISPLAY` / `PAY_CODE` payments, and generate downloadable CSV/XLSX/JSON settlement statements.

 ### 2.2 Startup & Deployment Safety Gates (`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` & `fake-rails-back/lib/env/index.ts`)
 
 Both the deployment orchestrator (`deploy/deploy.ts`) and the service startup (`fake-rails-back/lib/env/index.ts`) enforce three non-negotiable rules:
 
 1. **Explicit Production Opt-In Gate:**
    - If `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED === "true"` and `NODE_ENV === "production"`, startup immediately checks `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION === "true"`. If false or omitted, `configSchema.ts` and `fake-rails-back` abort with exit code `1` (`FAKE_RAILS_PRODUCTION_GUARD_BLOCKED: Set FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION="true" to run Fake Rails in production mode`).
 2. **Non-Empty Single-User Portal Credentials Gate:**
    - When `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED === "true"`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER` (min 4 chars) and `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (min 12 chars, never default/empty) are strictly validated by Zod 4 before any SSH connection or process startup.
 3. **Port Collision & Firewall Isolation Gate:**
    - `configSchema.ts` verifies that `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT` (`4104`) and `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` (`8444`) do not collide with `CORE_PORT` (`4000`), `ADMIN_BACK_PORT` (`4101`), `MERCHANT_BACK_PORT` (`4102`), `CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT` (`4103`), `ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT` (`8443`), or public `80`/`443`.
    - `firewallConfigurator.ts` opens `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` (`8444`) to `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` (plus `CORE_PRIVATE_IP` and `CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP`), while keeping `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT` (`4104`) bound strictly to `127.0.0.1`.
 
 ### 2.3 Scoped SSRF & TLS Allowlist in `core-back` for Fake Rails
 
 In `core-back`, Safeguard 10 (`StepExecutor.ts` custom DNS hook) blocks outbound calls to private/loopback IP ranges (`10.0.0.0/8`, `192.168.0.0/16`, `127.0.0.0/8`) to prevent SSRF. When `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="true"` is deployed on a LAN IP (e.g., `https://10.10.0.20:8444`) or `127.0.0.1:8444`:
 
 - `deploy/deploy.ts` writes `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS="true"` and `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS="fakerails.internal,10.10.0.20,127.0.0.1"` into `core-back`'s `shared/.env`, and trusts the generated `fake-rails-ca.crt` (or `internal-ca.crt` used to sign the Fake Rails Nginx TLS certificate) in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.
 - `core-back/engine/flow/StepExecutor.ts` checks: if `env.ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS === true` and the target hostname/IP is **both** in `env.FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` **and** in the gateway version's `gateway_environments.allowed_hosts`, the private-IP rejection is bypassed for that exact host:port. All other private/loopback/metadata IPs (`169.254.169.254`, database ports, internal admin ports) remain strictly blocked.
 
 ### 2.4 Extension to the 12-Step Deployment Pipeline (`deploy/deploy.ts`)
 
 When `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED="true"` (or `./deploy/deploy.sh --only=fake-rails`), the orchestrator executes:
 - **Step 2b (Local SPA Build):** Builds `fake-rails-front` via Vite (`bun run build`) alongside `admin-front`, `merchant-front`, and `checkout-front`.
 - **Step 3b (Certificate Minting):** Mints `fake-rails.crt` / `fake-rails.key` signed by the deployment CA with `SAN = DNS:${FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN}, IP:${FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP}, IP:127.0.0.1` so `core-back` verifies HTTPS TLS 1.3 cleanly without disabling TLS verification.
 - **Step 6b (Deploy `fake-rails-back` & `fake-rails-front` to `FAKE_RAILS_HOST`):**
   - Rsyncs `fake-rails-back/` and `fake-rails-front/dist/` to `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/releases/<TS>/`.
   - Creates `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/shared/data/` (for persistent `fake-rails.sqlite`) and `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/shared/.env` (`chmod 600`) containing `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL=https://${CHECKOUT_DOMAIN}/api/v1/inbound`, and deterministic signing secrets matching `seedFakeRails.ts`.
   - Switches `/var/www/pg-fake-rails/current` symlink, starts PM2 process `pg-fake-rails-back`, renders `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/pg-fake-rails.conf` on `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT`, runs `nginx -t`, and reloads Nginx.
   - If `SEED_FAKE_RAILS_BLUEPRINTS="true"`, runs `bun run seed-fake-rails` on `CORE_HOST` so all 20 gateway configurations in `core-back` have their `base_urls` and `script_urls` pointed to `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and their `ConfirmationChannel` path tokens synced with `fake-rails-back`.
 
 ## 3. Single-User Authentication Architecture (Configured via `deploy.env`)
 
 Per the specification, the Fake Rails Portal has **one user** whose username and password are provided in `deploy.env`.
 
 ### 3.1 Authentication Flow (`fake-rails-back/api/portal/auth.ts`)
 
 1. **Zero Database User Table Required:**
    - On startup, `fake-rails-back/lib/env/index.ts` reads `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and `FAKE_RAILS_JWT_SECRET` from `.env` (populated by `deploy.ts` from `deploy.env`).
    - Startup derives a SHA-256 digest of both credentials in memory for constant-time comparison via `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
 2. **Login Endpoint (`POST /portal-api/auth/login`):**
    - Validates `{ username, password }` using Zod 4.
    - Enforces a sliding-window brute-force rate limiter (max 10 failed attempts per IP per 15 minutes).
    - Compares `username` and `password` against the `deploy.env` credentials using `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
    - On match, issues a signed HS256 JWT (`exp: 12h`, `sub: env.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER`, `role: "FAKE_RAILS_TESTER"`) and returns `{ token, user: { username: env.FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_USER, allowInProduction: env.FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION } }`.
 3. **Portal Guard Middleware (`portalAuthGuard.ts`):**
    - Protects all `/portal-api/*` endpoints (except `/portal-api/auth/login` and `/portal-api/internal/bulk-seed`, which requires the `X-Fake-Rails-Seeder-Token: ${FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN}` header).

 ## 5. Probabilistic Chaos & Failure Injection Engine
 
 A core requirement is configuring whether a given rail is going to fail or succeed with a **given percentage chance**, alongside fine-grained control over *how* it fails at each lifecycle phase.
 
 ### 5.1 Chaos Configuration Data Model (`fake_rail_scenarios` in SQLite)
 
 Each of the 20 rails has a persisted configuration row in `fake-rails-back` (editable live from the Tester Portal with zero restart):
 
 ```ts
 export interface RailChaosScenarioConfig {
   railCode: string;                       // e.g. "edfali", "sadad", "moamalat", "lypay", "tlync", "neompay"
   enabled: boolean;                       // If false, returns HTTP 503 Connection Refused (simulates full outage / RB-01)
   overallFailureChancePercent: number;    // 0 to 100 (e.g. 25 means 25% of transactions on this rail will fail)
 
   // Phase-specific failure distribution (when the PRNG rolls a failure, which phase & error mode is chosen)
   phaseBreakdown: {
     initiateFailWeight: number;           // Weight for failing during INITIATE (before point_of_no_return -> tests Route Failover)
     submitFailWeight: number;             // Weight for failing during SUBMIT / CONFIRM (MOVES_MONEY -> tests UNKNOWN & Lockout)
     verifyFailWeight: number;             // Weight for failing during VERIFY / INQUIRE
     webhookFailWeight: number;            // Weight for webhook delivery anomalies
     refundFailWeight: number;             // Weight for failing during REFUND / VOID (tests Adjustment EXECUTING state)
   };
 
   // Weighted distribution of failure modes when a failure is triggered
   failureModeWeights: {
     TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: number; // Explicit 200/400 decline -> FAILED
     LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CUSTOMER_CEILING: number;     // Customer ceiling hit -> FAILED (must NOT trip circuit breaker)
     WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE: number;                 // Mistyped OTP -> stays AWAITING_CUSTOMER (otp_attempts + 1)
     HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT: number;              // 500 Internal Server Error -> UNKNOWN on money step, trips breaker on initiate
     TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL: number;         // Sleeps 20,000ms so core-back AbortController times out -> UNKNOWN
     SOCKET_RESET_MID_STREAM: number;             // Destroys TCP socket after receiving body -> UNKNOWN
     MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY: number;      // Returns 200 OK with broken/changed JSON schema -> UNKNOWN (Edge Case 57)
     RATE_LIMIT_HTTP_429: number;                 // Returns 429 Too Many Requests
     AMOUNT_ROUNDING_MISMATCH: number;            // Settles +/- 0.050 LYD or 2-decimal rounded amount -> tests mismatch_policy
     CONFLICTING_WEBHOOK_VS_INQUIRY: number;      // Webhook says PAID, Inquiry says FAILED -> P1 CONFLICT (Edge Case 20)
   };
 
   // Latency & Async Confirmation Timing
   latencyMs: { min: number; max: number };       // Artificial network latency range (e.g. 50ms - 400ms)
   autoApproveAsyncAfterSec: number | null;       // For PUSH_APPROVAL / QR_DISPLAY: auto-confirm after N sec (null = wait for manual click in Portal)
   webhookBehavior: {
     delaySeconds: number;                        // Delay before sending webhook (set > session TTL to test Late Success Recovery)
     duplicateCount: number;                      // Send 1 (normal) or 2..5 identical webhooks (tests dedupe_key)
     outOfOrderPendingAfterPaid: boolean;         // Send PAID webhook followed 2s later by PENDING (tests forward-only rule)
     corruptSignatureChancePercent: number;       // 0 to 100% chance of sending an invalid HMAC signature (tests RB-02)
   };
 }
 ```
 
 ### 5.2 Deterministic Magic Inputs + Probabilistic PRNG Evaluation (`ChaosEvaluator.ts`)
 
 Every incoming request to `/rails/:gatewayCode/*` passes through `ChaosEvaluator.evaluate(req, railConfig)`:
 
 1. **Priority 1 — Deterministic Magic Test Inputs (100% Reproducible Contract & 15-Scenario Suite):**
    - Before rolling the percentage dice, `ChaosEvaluator` checks if the request contains a deterministic magic phone number, OTP, or amount suffix (used by `core-back`'s 15-scenario sandbox runner and automated tests):
      - OTP `000000` or `0000` -> Always returns `WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE`.
      - OTP `999999` or Phone ending in `9901` -> Always returns `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`.
      - Phone ending in `9902` -> Always returns `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
      - Phone ending in `9905` or OTP `500500` -> Always returns `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` on `SUBMIT` (`MOVES_MONEY`).
      - Phone ending in `9906` or OTP `408408` -> Always hangs for `20,000ms` (`TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL`).
      - Phone ending in `9907` -> Always returns `200 OK` with `{ unexpected_schema: true }` (`MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY`).
 2. **Priority 2 — Per-Transaction Override from the Tester Portal:**
    - If the tester clicked **"Force Next Outcome"** on an active transaction in the Portal (while the customer is on the OTP, QR, Push, or Redirect screen), that explicit outcome wins.
 3. **Priority 3 — Configured Percentage Chance (`overallFailureChancePercent`):**
    - For normal traffic, when a transaction first hits `INITIATE` (or `PRE_INITIATE`), `ChaosEvaluator` draws `roll = Math.random() * 100`.
    - If `roll < railConfig.overallFailureChancePercent`, the transaction is assigned a failure fate (`assignedFailPhase` and `assignedFailureMode`) sampled from `phaseBreakdown` and `failureModeWeights` and stored on its `fake_transactions` row in SQLite.
    - Pinning the roll at transaction creation ensures coherent multi-step behavior: for example, if the roll decides this transaction will fail at `SUBMIT` with `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL`, `INITIATE` succeeds normally (sending the OTP), and when `SUBMIT` arrives, it hangs as scheduled.
 
 ### 5.3 Embedded SQLite Schema (`fake-rails-back/engine/db/schema.sql`)
 
 ```sql
 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fake_rail_scenarios (
   rail_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
   gateway_code TEXT NOT NULL,

 );
 
 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fake_transactions (
   id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- UUIDv7

   our_reference TEXT NOT NULL,              -- ATTEMPT.gateway_reference sent by core-back

 );
 
 CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fake_events_tx ON fake_step_events(transaction_id, created_at ASC);
 ```
 
 ## 6. Single-User Tester Portal & Dashboard Architecture (`fake-rails-front`)
 
 Built in Vue 3 TSX (`dc()` from `kt-dc`) + Vuetify 3, `fake-rails-front` gives the tester complete visibility and control over all 20 fake rails.
 
 ### 6.1 Portal Views & Capabilities

 ## 7. `core-back` Pre-Seeded Fake Gateway Blueprints (`seedFakeRails.ts`)
 
 To make `core-back` work out-of-the-box with `fake-rails-back`, `core-back/prisma/seedFakeRails.ts` configures all 20 gateways and their active `LIVE` / `SANDBOX` versions to point their `gateway_environments.base_urls` to `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (`https://<FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN>:8444/rails/<gateway_code>`) and their `allowed_hosts` to `[FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN, FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP]`.

 # Fix 0001 — Operator Cases list, bulk inquiry and case details
 
 ## Why
 
 The current `/operator-cases` page is not aligned with the design:
 
 - `admin-front/src/pages/operator-cases/index.tsx` uses `DataTable`, which is already
   in server mode because `tableRegistry.OperatorCases` exists. The page's own
   `load()` and header Case Type select are disconnected from the table and do
   nothing.
 - Bulk inquiry loops over `attemptId`s, never checks eligibility, silently skips
   cases without attempts, and can move terminal attempts to `VERIFYING`.
 - The “Attempts” column renders a checkbox. Selection is not tied to the case,
   has no select-all or eligibility summary, and reports no per-case result.
 - The list API only searches `attempt.reference`; there is no merchant-name or
   case-reference filter.
 - The detail API returns only the bare `OperatorCase` row: no attempt, step
   logs, inbound events, reconciliation item, approval or assignee.
 - `POST /operator-cases/:id/resolve` only writes notes/state. The edge mapper
   discards the selected action, so “Mark succeeded/failed” does nothing.
 - `POST /attempts/:id/inquire` directly sets any attempt to `VERIFYING`, which
   violates the forward-only lifecycle for terminal attempts.
 
 ## Scope
 
 1. Rebuild the list page on `ApiTable` with server-side pagination/filtering.
 2. Add real bulk inquiry with per-case eligibility and result reporting.
 3. Add a logical, explainable case details page.
 4. Make case resolutions real Maker-Checker operations:
    `MARK_SUCCEEDED`, `MARK_FAILED`, `CLOSE_CASE`.
 5. Add help tooltips and show every database identifier with its source.
 6. Keep all money movement inside the existing ledger and slot infrastructure.
 
 ## 1. Table strategy: `ApiTable`
 
 Use `admin-front/src/components/Table/ApiTable.tsx`, following the pattern in
 `example.ignore.tsx`:
 
 - `ApiTable` owns server pagination, sorting, refresh, search, XLSX and rendering.
 - `TopSlot` contains:
   - `TableFilters` from the current design system (not the older
     `FiltersContainer` from the example).
   - The bulk-selection bar.
   - Result count and active filters.
 - `onRefresh` sends:
   `page`, `pageSize`, `search`, `caseRef`, `merchantName`,
   `providerReference`, `kind`, `priority`, `state`, `assigneeUserId`, `from`,
   `to`, `dateFrom`, `dateTo`, `sortKey`, `sortDirection`.
 - `setRefreshHook` refreshes after bulk inquiry and actions.
 - `apiDataExtractor` / `apiTotalExtractor` feed page-local row and total refs for
   selection and the bulk bar.
 
 Low-risk `ApiTable` improvements (no current admin page uses it):
 
 1. `localSearch?: boolean` (default `true`). Operator cases disables it because
    the server already searched.
 2. `onData?: (rows, total) => void` so pages do not need extractor side effects.
 3. Use `extractApiErrorMessage` instead of the hardcoded “Something Went Wrong!”.
 4. Pass the internal `loading.value` to `TableHeader` (currently it passes
    `props.loading`).
 
 ## 2. Shared clarity improvements
 
 ### Table header tooltips
 
 - Add `headerTooltip?: string` to `TableHeader` in
   `components/Table/types.ts`.
 - Render a help icon beside the header label in `Table.tsx` with `VTooltip`.
 - Every operator-case column has a tooltip explaining meaning, derivation and
   database source.
 
 ### Detail field tooltips
 
 - Extend `FieldProps` with:
   - `hint?: string` — plain-language explanation.
   - `source?: string` — exact table/column or derivation.
 - `Field` renders a help icon with a `VTooltip` containing hint and source.
 - Add optional `title` / `description` to `FieldsSections` sections so grouped
   detail cards have explicit headings.
 - Add optional `hint` to `StatusChip` for case-specific enums.
 
 ### Help content
 
 `operatorCaseHelp.ts` contains one source of truth for:
 
 - case kinds (`UNKNOWN`, `HELD`, `CONFLICT`, `MISMATCH`, `LATE_SUCCESS`,
   `MANUAL_REVIEW`, `UNMATCHED_STATEMENT`);
 - case states (`OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PENDING_CHECKER`, `RESOLVED`);
 - priorities (`P1`, `P2`, `P3`);
 - reconciliation results;
 - inquiry support;
 - runbook names.
 
 The same definitions drive table tooltips, detail field hints and warnings.
 
 ## 3. List page
 
 ### Columns
 
 1. Selection checkbox
 2. Case reference — links to detail; derived value explained in tooltip
 3. Type — chip with tooltip
 4. Priority — chip with tooltip
 5. State — chip with tooltip
 6. Merchant
 7. Rail / Gateway
 8. Amount — charged amount when an attempt exists, otherwise statement amount;
    source explained in the tooltip
 9. Attempt — reference plus status/substatus
 10. Link slot — confirmed/use counts and active lock
 11. Provider reference
 12. Reconciliation result
 13. Approval state
 14. Opened at
 15. SLA due — overdue / due-soon chip
 16. Assignee
 17. Actions — Open, Inquire (disabled with reason when ineligible)
 
 Use `rowColor` from `statusTone` so P1/overdue/conflict rows stand out.
 
 ### Filters
 
 Configure in `tableRegistry.OperatorCases`, reused by the page:
 
 - Case reference (`caseRef`)
 - Merchant name (`merchantName`)
 - Provider reference (`providerReference`)
 - Case type, multi (`kind`)
 - Priority, multi (`priority`)
 - State, multi (`state`)
 - Assignee (`assigneeUserId`)
 - Opened date range (`from`, `to`)
 - SLA due range (`dateFrom`, `dateTo`)
 
 Header search matches case reference, attempt reference, provider reference,
 merchant trade name and merchant legal name.
 
 Filter changes are debounced, then call `reset()`. `TableFilters` supplies
 active chips and “Clear all”.
 
 ### Bulk inquiry
 
 - Selection stores **case IDs**, never attempt IDs.
 - Header checkbox selects all rows on the current server page.
 - Selection persists across pages and clears when search/filters change.
 - Bulk bar shows selected / inquiry-ready / will-be-skipped.
 - `POST /operator-cases/bulk-inquire` accepts case IDs and returns per-case
   results.
 - Eligibility:
   - case state is not `RESOLVED` or `PENDING_CHECKER`;
   - attempt exists;
   - attempt is `UNKNOWN` or `VERIFYING`;
   - pinned gateway version has `supportsStatusCheck = true`.
 - Result dialog lists scheduled and skipped cases with exact reasons.
 
 ## 4. Case details page
 
 The page is an investigation narrative, not a raw dump.
 
 1. **Header** — reference, type, priority, state, SLA, actions:
    Back, Assign to me, Start working, Inquire Gateway Now, Propose Resolution.
 2. **Workflow strip** — `OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → PENDING_CHECKER → RESOLVED`,
    current state highlighted, assignee and SLA.
 3. **“What this case means”**
    - What happened (from kind + attempt status + reconciliation result).
    - Why it matters (money and slot impact).
    - What to do next (runbook and available actions).
 4. **Key statistics** — charged amount, attempt status, SLA remaining, age,
    priority.
 5. **Case and ownership** — IDs, state, priority, assignee, opened, updated,
    SLA, approval.
 6. **Merchant and application**.
 7. **Payment attempt and money** — status/substatus, environment, mode,
    requested/surcharge/charged/settled/fee/commission/net, references,
    timestamps, ledger entry.
 8. **Route, gateway and slot** — rail, collection mode, gateway, route health,
    pinned version, inquiry support, link slot counters.
 9. **Reconciliation and statement**.
 10. **Evidence** — expandable panels:
     - Timeline;
     - Gateway step logs;
     - Inbound webhooks;
     - Reconciliation items;
     - Adjustments and disputes;
     - Audit trail;
     - Raw evidence (collapsed, monospace, copyable, LTR, scroll-contained).
 11. **Resolution and approval** — current notes, approval state, maker/checker,
     payload, rejection reason; approve/reject only for an eligible checker who
     is not the maker.
 12. **All identifiers** — every ID with entity label, database table/column and
     copy button.
 
 ## 5. Backend/API
 
 ### List endpoint
 
 `GET /operator-cases` returns explicit fields:
 
 - `caseId`, `caseRef`, `caseReferenceSource`
 - `caseType`, `priority`, `state`
 - `merchantId`, `merchantTradeName`, `merchantLegalName`
 - `railId`, `railCode`, `railNameEn`
 - `gatewayId`, `gatewayCode`, `gatewayName`
 - `routeId`, `attemptId`, `attemptReference`
 - `attemptStatus`, `attemptSubstatus`
 - `chargedAmount`, `statementAmount`, `currency`
 - `providerReference`, `gatewayReference`
 - `linkSlot` object
 - `reconciliationItemId`, `reconciliationResult`
 - `approvalRequestId`, `approvalState`
 - `assigneeUserId`, `assigneeEmail`
 - `openedAt`, `slaDueAt`
 - `gatewaySupportsStatusCheck`
 - `inquiryEligibility` (`eligible`, `reason`)
 
 Search and filters:
 
 - search over case reference, attempt reference, provider reference, merchant
   trade/legal name;
 - `contains` filters for `caseRef`, `merchantName`, `providerReference`;
 - multi-value `in` filters for `kind`, `priority`, `state`;
 - sort allowlist for priority, state, kind, opened, SLA, case reference,
   merchant.
 
 ### Detail endpoint
 
 `GET /operator-cases/:id` includes safe nested data:
 
 - case, assignee, approval maker/checker, reconciliation item/run/source;
 - attempt, link, attempt group, merchant, application, rail, route, gateway,
   gateway version/settings;
 - step logs;
 - inbound events with decoded raw-body preview;
 - adjustments, disputes, reconciliation items;
 - audit trail.
 
 `contextCiphertext` and secret material are never returned.
 
 ### Actions
 
 - `POST /operator-cases/bulk-inquire` — inquiry scheduling with per-case
   results.
 - `PATCH /operator-cases/:id` — assign and move `OPEN` ↔ `IN_PROGRESS`.
 - `POST /operator-cases/:id/resolve` — Maker-Checker proposal:
   - `MARK_SUCCEEDED`, `MARK_FAILED`, `CLOSE_CASE`;
   - creates an `OPERATOR_CASE` approval;
   - sets case `PENDING_CHECKER`;
   - no attempt or ledger change until approval.
 - `POST /approvals/:id/approve` — executes the resolution atomically.
 - `POST /approvals/:id/reject` — returns the case to `IN_PROGRESS`.
 
 Resolution execution:
 
 - `MARK_SUCCEEDED` requires a provider reference; allowed for `UNKNOWN`,
   `VERIFYING`, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED`; uses existing ledger and slot
   infrastructure; routes to suspense when no slot remains.
 - `MARK_FAILED` allowed for `UNKNOWN`/`VERIFYING`; releases the reservation and
   sets `FAILED`.
 - `CLOSE_CASE` only when the attempt is terminal or absent.
 - Forward-only violations and attempts with conflicting ledger entries are
   rejected.
 
 ### Roles
 
 - Add `case:write` to seeded `OPERATOR`.
 - Add `approval:read`, `approval:check`, `approval:write` to the operator-case
   checker role, at minimum `FINANCE`.
 - Update `core-back/prisma/seed.ts` and
   `core-back/scripts/createAdminPlan.ts`.
 
 ## 6. Routing
 
 - Add `/operator-cases/:id` as `OperatorCaseDetail`.
 - Add authority mapping `case:read` / `operator:read`.
 - Add `parentName: "OperatorCases"` route meta so the sidebar and help drawer
   keep the Operator Cases context.
 - Map the detail route to Guide Book 7.2.
 - Keep the detail route out of the sidebar.
 
 ## 7. Tests and verification
 
 Backend:
 
 - `core-back`: `contains` query tests, inquiry eligibility, maker-checker
   resolution, idempotency, rejection reset, suspense routing, conflicting
   ledger rejection.
 - `admin-back`: route forwarding, schemas and contract mapping.
 - role-plan tests.
 
 Frontend:
 
 - `ApiTable` pagination against mocked responses.
 - Header search and filters send the correct query parameters.
 - Bulk selection uses case IDs and shows per-case results.
 - Case reference navigates to detail.
 - Detail page renders narrative sections, evidence panels, tooltips, approval
   controls and all identifier rows.
 - Maker proposal shows `PENDING_CHECKER`; checker approval resolves the case.
 
 Commands:
 
 - `core-back`: `bun run typecheck && bun test`
 - `admin-back`: `bun run typecheck && bun test`
 - `admin-front`: `bun run typecheck && bun run build && bun run lint`
 - Playwright operator-case tests.
 - Manual verification at `http://localhost:8443/operator-cases` and
   `/operator-cases/:id`.
 
 ## 8. Guardrails
 
 - No attempt outcome change from the list page.
 - Bulk inquiry only schedules inquiries.
 - No terminal attempt downgrade.
 - No ledger posting without a unique attempt ledger reference.
 - Maker ≠ checker enforced at API and execution layers.
 - Every displayed ID is labelled with its entity and database source.
 - Every derived value says it is derived and from where.
 
 ## Implementation order
 
 1. Shared backend query support and operator-case endpoints.
 2. Maker-Checker execution in governance and approval reject/reset.
 3. Admin-back routes and contracts.
 4. Shared frontend clarity components (`ApiTable`, `Table` tooltips, `Field`,
    `FieldsSections`, `StatusChip`) and help content.
 5. List page on `ApiTable`.
 6. Detail page, router and navigation.
 7. Tests, typechecks, build, lint and manual verification.

 # PART 0 — READ THIS FIRST: RULES FOR THE IMPLEMENTING AGENT
 
 You are implementing a safety-critical training and reference system for people who will move real money. The people who read it may know **nothing** about payments, accounting, compliance or software. The most expensive failure is a human acting wrongly because the guide was unclear or wrong. Therefore:

 # PART I — PRODUCT DESIGN
 
 ## I-1. Why this is being rebuilt
 
 The current guide is a searchable list of ten short "books" plus three simulators. It reads like a feature tour. It assumes the reader already knows what a gateway, a ledger, an OTP, a webhook or AML is. A new employee cannot learn the platform from it, and nothing in it stops a tired operator from clicking the wrong button.
 
 The new Guide has three jobs, in this order of importance:
 
 1. **Prevent human error at the moment of action.** Every screen has a "?" drawer; every risky action shows a checklist before it executes.
 2. **Teach from zero.** Anyone who can read can understand the whole system, A to Z, with no prior knowledge. Every unfamiliar word is explained where it first appears and again in the glossary.
 3. **Be the reference during incidents.** Calm, step-by-step runbooks, a symptom-to-action playbook and a plain-language catalog of the 140 edge cases.
 
 ## I-2. Audience
 
 | Audience | What they need | How the guide serves them |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | Brand-new employee, any role, no background | Vocabulary, the big picture, safety rules | Book 0 → Book 1 → Book 2, glossary tooltips everywhere |
 | `OPERATOR`, `SUPPORT` | Daily queues, reading statuses, what to do about `UNKNOWN` | Books 3, 5, 7, 10 |
 | `FINANCE` | Ledger, settlement, cash-outs, refunds, disputes | Books 4, 7, 8 |
 | `COMPLIANCE`, `MLRO` | AML program, cases, reporting, confidentiality | Books 4, 5, 9 |
 | `GATEWAY_ADMIN`, `SECURITY_ADMIN` | Gateways, rails, routes, credentials, deployment, security | Books 4, 6, 11, 12 |
 | Management | One place to see the rules everybody is held to | Book 0 (Golden Rules), Book 4, Book 13 |
 
 All seven admin roles can open every article. Roles only change **recommendation** ("Recommended for you") and the reading path. The guide contains **no live data, no real thresholds, no real names, no secrets**; it explains rules, not records, so it is safe for everyone to read.
 
 ## I-3. Writing principles (already applied to PART III; use them to judge any future edit)
 
 1. **Zero assumed knowledge.** Define every term at first use, in a short parenthesis or sentence. Never write "obviously", "simply", "just".
 2. **Say who, where, what, why, and what if I get it wrong.** Instructions name the role, the exact screen, the exact button, the reason, and the recovery.
 3. **Short sentences, concrete numbers.** Use real examples (100 LYD, 3% commission) rather than abstractions.
 4. **One meaning per word.** The same concept is always called the same thing (see glossary). UI labels appear in **bold** exactly as on screen.
 5. **Honest about gaps.** If a feature exists in the design but has no screen yet, the article says so (`ui=NOT_YET` banner) and names who performs it today.
 6. **Safety first, in plain voice.** Warnings use the `warning` / `danger` callouts and explain the consequence, not just the rule.
 7. **No secrets, no live data, no external links.** The platform's admin side is LAN-only; the guide never links outside it.
 8. **Versioned.** Every build carries `contentVersion`; reading progress records the version read so a major change can request a re-read.
 
 ## I-4. Scope
 
 **In scope:** the Admin Guide (`/guide/**`), global command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K), contextual "?" drawer on every admin screen, safeguard checklists on risky actions, five simulators, glossary with auto-linking, symptom playbook, 140-case catalog, reading paths, read-tracking, English content (Arabic-ready).
 
 **Out of scope:** Merchant Guide, Checkout Help, any change to payment, ledger or engine behaviour, server-side search, analytics, external links, AI/LLM features.
 
 **Arabic:** the platform is Arabic-first (RTL). This file ships **English content in full** plus an Arabic term table (the `ar=` attribute in the glossary) so translation is consistent. The loader must support `articles.ar.json` and show English with a visible "Arabic version pending" chip until it exists (§II-8). Do **not** machine-translate; translation is a separate human-reviewed work package.
 
 ## I-5. Information architecture
 
 ```text
 /guide                      Home: search, "Start here", reading path for my role, continue reading, books, tools, "I'm stuck"
 /guide/book/:bookId         One book: summary, ordered article list, progress ring
 /guide/a/:articleId         Article reader (TOC, glossary tooltips, mark-as-read, prev/next)
 /guide/glossary/:slug?      A–Z glossary with filter; one entry deep-linkable
 /guide/tools/:tool?         Simulators gallery (transform, crypto, ledger, visible-rails, attempt-states)
 /guide/playbook/:id?        "What you may see, and what to do" — situation cards
 /guide/cards/:id?           Safeguard cards (checklists for risky actions)
 /guide/edge-cases           The full 140-case catalog with filters
 (global)  Ctrl/Cmd+K        Command palette (articles, glossary, cards, situations, error codes, edge cases)
 (global)  "?" in PageHeader Contextual drawer for the current screen
 ```

 ## II-2. Content format and the extractor
 
 ### II-2.1 Block syntax (everything in PART III uses exactly this)
 
 All content blocks begin with a line that starts with `@@` and end with `@@end` (except one-line `@@term` and `@@term`-style lines). **Attributes** are `key=value` or `key="value with spaces"`. Parsing rule for attributes: regex `([a-zA-Z_][\w-]*)=("([^"\\]|\\.)*"|[^\s]+)`.
 
 | Block | Opening line | Body | Closed by |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | Book | `@@book id=2 title="..." audience="..." summary="..."` | none | (single line) |
 | Article | `@@article id=b02-03 book=2 order=3 title="..." roles=ALL minutes=6 ui=AVAILABLE related=b07-01,b08-02` | Markdown | `@@end` |
 | Term | `@@term slug=ledger term="Ledger" aliases="books;general ledger" ar="دفتر الأستاذ" related=double-entry :: Short definition.` | none | (single line) |
 | Card | `@@card id=sg-approve-adjustment title="..." screen=Approvals risk=HIGH irreversible=true` | Markdown with 4 fixed bold headings (§II-7) | `@@end` |
 | Situation | `@@situation id=s-unknown-attempt title="..." screens=OperatorCases cases=5,8,20 articles=b07-03` | Markdown | `@@end` |
 | Path | `@@path role=OPERATOR title="..." :: b00-01,b00-03,...` (`role` is a staff role or `ALL` for the new-employee path) | none | (single line) |
 | Data | `@@data id=ledger-events` | one fenced ```json block | `@@end` |
 | Map | `@@map id=context-map` | one fenced ```json block | `@@end` |
 | FAQ | `@@faq id=q-001 article=b07-03` | first line `Q: ...` then answer text | `@@end` |
 
 Lines outside blocks (headings such as `### BOOK 4`, blank lines) are ignored. Inside `@@data` and `@@map` only the single fenced `json` block is read. `roles` is `ALL` or a comma list from `GATEWAY_ADMIN,SECURITY_ADMIN,FINANCE,OPERATOR,COMPLIANCE,MLRO,SUPPORT`. `ui` is `AVAILABLE`, `PARTIAL` or `NOT_YET`. IDs are lowercase `[a-z0-9-]`.
 
 ### II-2.2 Markdown dialect inside article bodies
 
 * CommonMark + tables (via `markdown-it`, `html:false`, `linkify:false`, `typographer:false`).
 * **Callout containers** (implemented by you as a small `markdown-it` core/block rule, no extra package): a line `:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::warning`, `:::danger`, `:::example`, `:::do`, `:::dont`, optionally followed by a title (`:::warning Never do this`), content lines, closing line `:::`. Render as `<aside class="callout callout-{type}" role="note">` with an icon and a visible type label (Note / Tip / Warning / Danger / Example / Do / Don't) — meaning must not rely on color alone.
 * **Widget placeholder:** a line `{{widget:ledger-explorer}}` (allowed ids: `transform-sandbox`, `crypto-lab`, `ledger-explorer`, `visible-rails`, `attempt-states`). Replaced by the component.
 * **Article link:** `[[a:b07-03]]` → link to the article using its title; `[[a:b07-03|custom text]]` → custom text. **Card link:** `[[c:sg-approve-adjustment]]`. **Situation link:** `[[s:s-unknown-attempt]]`. **Glossary link:** `[[g:ledger]]` (explicit; auto-linking also exists, §II-4).
 * Fenced code blocks tagged ` ```diagram ` render monospace, `dir="ltr"`, horizontally scrollable; they are used for text diagrams.
 * Headings inside articles start at `###` (the page supplies the `##` title). Every heading gets a stable id = slug of its text, de-duplicated with `-2`, `-3`.
 * Tables are wrapped in an `overflow-x:auto` container. No raw HTML, no images, no external links (an `http(s)://` link in content fails the content test).
 
 ### II-2.3 `scripts/extract-guide-content.ts` — required behaviour
 
 Run with `bun run content:guide`. Steps:
 
 1. Locate the design file: `design/guide_system_design_and_content.md` (relative to repo root, found via `../design/` from `admin-front`). If absent: print an error and exit 1.
 2. Read the file as UTF-8, normalise `\r\n` to `\n`. **Only parse content between the two marker lines `<!-- CONTENT:BEGIN -->` and `<!-- CONTENT:END -->` (each marker is a whole line by itself; mentions of them inside other text are not markers)** (markers exist in PART III).
 3. Parse blocks line by line with the grammar above. Unknown `@@` keywords, duplicate ids, a missing `@@end`, or an unparsable JSON fence → exit 1 with file line number.
 4. Validate cross-references: every `related`, `[[a:]]`, `[[c:]]`, `[[s:]]`, `[[g:]]`, `articles=`, `article=`, path entry and context-map id must exist.
 5. Emit into `src/content/guide/generated/`: `books.json`, `articles.en.json` (array of `{id, book, order, title, roles, minutes, ui, related, body, headings[], plainText}`), `glossary.en.json`, `cards.en.json` (with parsed `checklist: string[]` from lines beginning `- [ ] `), `playbook.en.json`, `paths.json`, `faq.en.json`, `data.json` (`{ [id]: parsedJson }`), `context-map.json`, `meta.json` (`{contentVersion, generatedAt, counts, sourceSha256}`). `contentVersion` is the value of the `<!-- CONTENT_VERSION: x.y.z -->` marker (initially `1.0.0`).
 6. Also generate `error-codes.en.json` from article `b13-01`: for every table row whose first cell is a single backticked token, emit `{code, where, meaning, action}` (the four cells, markdown stripped). Then generate `edge-cases.en.json` by parsing the 140-row tables of Section 13 of the repository file matched by glob `design/payment-gateway-refined-design-v4*.md` (the file in the repo is named `payment-gateway-refined-design-v4.1.md`). Row format: `| **N** | scenario | resolution | severity |`; group headings are `### **Group X: Name (Cases a–b)**`. Strip markdown bold and backslash escapes (`\_`, `\#`, `\\+`, `\\-`). Output `{n, group, groupName, scenario, resolution, severity}`; must yield exactly **140** rows or exit 1.
 7. Generated files are **committed**. A unit test (§II-10) re-runs the extractor in a temp dir and asserts byte equality with the committed output, so a design edit without regeneration fails CI.

 ## II-4. Glossary auto-linking and popovers
 
 * Build a matcher from every term's `term` and `aliases` (case-insensitive, whole word, longest match first; Arabic and Latin boundaries handled with Unicode-aware lookarounds).
 * When rendering an article body, wrap the **first occurrence per article** of each term in `<button class="gl-term" data-slug="...">`. Do **not** wrap inside headings, code, links, table header cells, callout titles, or the term's own glossary page.
 * Click/Enter/Space opens a popover (`role="dialog"`, focus-trapped, Esc closes): term, `short` definition, Arabic term (if any), "Open in glossary", related terms. It never navigates away by itself. Hover alone must not be the only way to read the definition (touch/keyboard users).
 
 ## II-5. Search and command palette
 
 * Index with `minisearch`: fields `title` (boost 5), `headings` (3), `aliases` (4), `plainText` (1); options `prefix:true`, `fuzzy:0.2`, `combineWith:"AND"` falling back to `"OR"` if zero results. Document types: `article`, `term`, `card`, `situation`, `edge-case`, `faq`, `error-code` (the codes in article b13-01).
 * Normalise **both** index text and query: lowercase; strip Arabic diacritics and tatweel; unify alef variants (أ إ آ → ا), ya/alef-maqsura (ى → ي), ta-marbuta (ة → ه); convert Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII (reuse `src/utils/arabic.ts`).  @@article id=b00-01 book=0 order=1 title="Welcome: what this system is and why this guide exists" roles=ALL minutes=2 ui=AVAILABLE related=b00-02,b00-03,b02-01
 ### In one sentence
 This platform lets shops and businesses in Libya accept payments from many different payment methods through one single system, and keeps exact, auditable records of every dinar that moves.
 
 ### What the platform does
 A customer wants to pay a shop. The customer might use a mobile wallet, a bank app, a card, or a code sent by SMS. Each of those is run by a different company with different technical rules. The platform sits in the middle: the shop connects once to us, and we connect to all the others. The customer sees a simple payment page. Behind it, our system talks to the right payment company, waits for a trustworthy answer, and then writes the money movement into our books.
 
 ### Why a guide this long?
 Because the work is serious. The people reading this may be new to payments, to accounting, to compliance or to software. A wrong click can pay the wrong person, release held money, or tell a suspect that we are investigating them. This guide exists so that **nobody has to guess**.
 
 ### What you will find
 * **Books 1–2** explain the world from zero: payments, computers, trust, money records, compliance, and the parts of our platform.
 * **Books 3–5** teach you how to work in the Back Office, how approvals work, and how merchants are handled.
 * **Books 6–9** go deep: gateways, payments, the ledger (our accounting books), and anti-money-laundering.
 * **Books 10–12** are for emergencies, security and hosting.
 * **Book 13** is a reference: tables, codes, a symptom playbook and quick answers.
 
 :::tip How to start
 If today is your first day, read Book 0 and Book 1 in order. They take about two hours and make everything else easier. Then follow the reading path for your role (button on the guide home page).
 :::
