references from a large recursive key list (`reference`, `merchant_reference`, `order_id`, `idempotency_key`, `ref`, and others), then from `idempotency-key` or `x-request-id`, then generates `FK--`. The descriptor `defaultOtp` field is never read; the expected OTP always comes from `deriveOtp()`. `normalizeAmount()` implements: - `moamalat`: integer dirhams, `LYD * 1000`, wire string integer. - `ly_pay` and `neompay`: string decimal with four-decimal normalisation and scale `1000`. - Everything else: string decimal with four-decimal normalisation and scale `100`. `maskCustomer()` masks cards for Moamalat/MPGS, wallets for NeomPay and phones otherwise. `extractOtp()` accepts common OTP key names. `deriveOtp()` hashes the seeder token, rail code and reference and truncates to the descriptor length. `phaseForPath()` exists but the dispatcher uses the route's declared phase rather than inferring from the path. ### 3.7 Wire shapes `successBase()` returns our reference, provider reference, transaction id, network reference, amount, currency and process id. `successResponse()` adds `status`, `success` and `ActionCode`. `failureBody()` adds a stable error code and action code. Handlers return protocol-shaped payloads: - `otpInitiate`: `AWAITING_CUSTOMER`, `process_id`, OTP, expiry. - `otpConfirm`: `PAID` or retryable wrong OTP. - `asyncInitiate`: QR payload, deep link, push reference, pay code and expiry. - `redirectInitiate`: hosted `redirect_url`, return/cancel URLs and expiry. - `inquiry`: `PAID`, `FAILED` or `PENDING` with a nested `payment.status`. - `refund`: `REFUNDED` or `NOT_REFUNDABLE`. - `cancel`: `CANCELLED`. - `tokenEndpoint`: fake Bearer token with gateway-dependent expiry. ### 3.8 Actual route mismatches Two gateway codes are seeded into `core-back` but are not the codes used by the route definitions: 1. **`cbl_lypay`.** The blueprint seeds the gateway as `cbl_lypay` and the flow URL template as `{api}/api/v1/payments/funds-transfers`, where `{api}` becomes `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/rails/cbl_lypay`. The descriptor resolves `cbl_lypay` to gateway code `cbl_lypay`, but `qrAndPushRouter.ts` registers those paths under `gatewayCodes: ["ly_pay"]`. `matchRailRoute()` therefore returns no route and the request gets `404 UNKNOWN_RAIL_ENDPOINT`. Calling `/rails/ly_pay/...` works, but the seeded gateway never uses that URL. 2. **`evo_pay`.** The blueprint seeds `evo_pay` with `POST /Payment` and `GET /Payment/:id`. The descriptor's gateway code is `evo_pay`, but the routes are registered under `gatewayCodes: ["evopay"]`. The seeded URL `/rails/evo_pay/Payment` therefore returns `404 UNKNOWN_RAIL_ENDPOINT`. The clean fix is to make route definitions use descriptor `gatewayCode` values, or make the dispatcher match `descriptor.railCode` as well as `descriptor.gatewayCode`. Until then, the four affected core flows cannot run against the emulator. A related mismatch exists in `statementRouter.ts`: `STATEMENT_GATEWAYS` lists `ly_pay` and `evopay`, not `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay`, so those two seeded gateways also lack a statement route. ### 3.9 Default webhook path bug `WebhookDispatcher.defaultUrlFor()` builds: ```text ${CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL}/webhook/${gateway_code}/${env.toLowerCase()}/${gateway_code}-webhook ``` With the default base `http://127.0.0.1:4103/api/v1/inbound`, this becomes `/api/v1/inbound/webhook/...`. The actual checkout route is `POST /api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`. The literal `webhook` segment is interpreted as `:gateway`, so every default webhook is routed to the wrong handler/404 path. The third segment is also hard-coded as `${gateway_code}-webhook`. Blueprint channel tokens are not uniformly that string: examples include `cbl-lypay-webhook` and `evo-pay-webhook`. `seedFakeRails.ts` rewrites the first webhook channel per gateway code to `${code}-webhook`, which masks the token problem only when that pass has run; it does not fix the extra path segment. ### 3.10 Missing inbound signature verification The design says the emulator verifies the gateway auth and crypto recipes. The implementation does not: - No route checks `Authorization`, `X-API-KEY`, `Basic`, `Secret-Key`, `X-Store-Token` or `X-Store-Id`. - No route verifies HMAC, RSA, `SecureHash`, timestamp tolerance or canonical string. - No idempotency conflict is refused; an existing reference is silently reused. - No source-IP allowlist is applied to rail routes. - No `422` duplicate-reference response exists. Only the outbound webhook path computes signatures (`FakeCryptoSigner` plus six gateway profiles). Inbound verification is therefore a protocol-fidelity gap, not just a missing test. ### 3.11 Dead auto-approve `RailChaosScenarioConfig.autoApproveAsyncAfterSec` is defined, persisted, merged by `PUT /portal-api/scenarios/:railCode`, and returned to the UI. Nothing reads it. No timer, worker or request path schedules an automatic approval after the configured number of seconds. Async rails only settle when a caller hits `/confirm`, the hosted page approves, or the tester approves a transaction. ### 3.12 Statement route mismatch `GET /rails/:gateway/statement` is implemented for every descriptor code. It filters the last 1,000 transactions by gateway and date window and returns CSV or JSON. There is no auth and no XLSX on this route. `core-back` has no `SETTLEMENT_FETCH` engine flow. The seeded statement channels are inbound channel records with `pathToken = -statement`; reconciliation is driven by uploaded files through the admin reconciliation route, not by fetching `/statement`. The emulator's statement endpoint is therefore a tester convenience, not part of the automated core lifecycle. ## 4. Contracts and invariants 1. **Alias resolution is case-insensitive.** `cbl_lypay`, `ly_pay` and `lypay` all resolve to the same descriptor. 2. **Route matching is exact after alias resolution.** Path segment count must match; `:param` matches one segment. 3. **A transaction reference is created once and reused.** Subsequent requests with the same reference do not create a second row. 4. **Amount normalisation is gateway-specific and text-only.** No floating-point arithmetic is used to store money. 5. **OTP generation is deterministic per transaction.** The portal exposes the current expected OTP. 6. **Successful confirmation generates a webhook.** Confirmation handlers call `dispatchSuccessWebhook`, except where a fault suppresses or delays it. 7. **Webhook signatures are derived from the seeder token.** The signature profile depends on the gateway code, with a generic fallback. ## 5. Purpose and scope This part covers the deterministic and probabilistic failure engine, the SQLite state it owns, outbound webhook anomalies, settlement-statement generation, the tester portal API and the `fake-rails-front` SPA. It does not cover the backend process model (`fake-rails.backend`), the route matrix (`fake-rails.protocol`) or the core seeding/deploy wiring (`fake-rails.integration`). ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) The design requires a tester to answer four questions at any moment: 1. What did the gateway receive and return? 2. Is this rail healthy, flaky, delayed or completely down? 3. If it fails, how and in which phase does it fail? 4. Can the tester force a specific outcome, replay a webhook, forge a signature or generate an anomalous statement? The intended failure controls are: - A per-rail `overallFailureChancePercent` from 0 to 100. - Weighted phase choice across `INITIATE`, `SUBMIT`, `VERIFY`, `WEBHOOK` and `REFUND`. - Weighted failure modes: insufficient funds, customer ceiling, wrong OTP, HTTP 500, timeout/hang, socket reset, malformed 200 body, HTTP 429, amount mismatch and conflicting webhook versus inquiry. - Latency range. - Async auto-approval after N seconds. - Webhook delay, duplicate count, out-of-order PENDING-after-PAID and corrupt-signature chance. The intended portal has a live SSE feed, an OTP/action banner, a pending-action queue, a transaction/wire inspector, a chaos matrix, a statement generator and hosted redirect/widget pages. ## 3. As-built architecture ### 3.1 Scenario model `engine/chaos/DefaultRailScenarios.ts` defines: ```ts interface RailChaosScenarioConfig { railCode: string; gatewayCode: string; enabled: boolean; overallFailureChancePercent: number; phaseBreakdown: { initiateFailWeight: number; submitFailWeight: number; verifyFailWeight: number; webhookFailWeight: number; refundFailWeight: number; }; failureModeWeights: Record; latencyMs: { min: number; max: number }; autoApproveAsyncAfterSec: number | null; webhookBehavior: { delaySeconds: number; duplicateCount: number; outOfOrderPendingAfterPaid: boolean; corruptSignatureChancePercent: number; }; } ``` The healthy baseline is `enabled=true`, `overallFailureChancePercent=0`, latency 40-250 ms, one webhook copy and no corruption. `defaultScenario()` gives one configuration per descriptor. Defaults are inserted into `fake_rail_scenarios` on first access. `FailureMode` has ten values exactly matching the design. `FailPhase` has five values (`INITIATE`, `SUBMIT`, `VERIFY`, `WEBHOOK`, `REFUND`). The core's ten declarative phases are not the same type. ### 3.2 Deterministic PRNG `engine/chaos/prng.ts` implements mulberry32 plus FNV-1a string hashing, `int`, `pick`, `chance(percent)` and `weighted(record)`. A scenario seed is `${railCode}:${reference}` for transaction fate and `${transactionId}:${phase}` for latency, so repeated runs with the same reference are reproducible. ### 3.3 Evaluation priority `ChaosEvaluator.evaluate()` applies this order: 1. **Magic input** in the current phase. It wins over everything. 2. **Disabled rail.** `enabled=false` produces `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` with source `OUTAGE`; `applyFault` maps that source to HTTP 503. 3. **Pinned transaction fate.** When the transaction row has `assigned_failure_mode` and `assigned_fail_phase` equal to the current phase. 4. **No failure.** `assignFate()` runs once when a new transaction row is created. It rolls `overallFailureChancePercent`; if it fails, it samples a phase from `phaseBreakdown` and a mode from `failureModeWeights`, then persists both on `fake_transactions`. ### 3.4 Magic inputs `detectMagicTrigger()` flattens body values and the raw body text, then checks: | Trigger | Failure mode | Phase | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | OTP `000000` or `0000` | `WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE` | `SUBMIT` | | OTP `999999` | `TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | `SUBMIT` | | OTP `500500` | `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` | `SUBMIT` | | OTP `408408` | `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL` | `SUBMIT` | | Phone ending `9901` | `TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` | `SUBMIT` | | Phone ending `9902` | `LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CUSTOMER_CEILING` | `SUBMIT` | | Phone ending `9905` | `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT` | `SUBMIT` | | Phone ending `9906` | `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL` | `SUBMIT` | | Phone ending `9907` | `MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY` | `SUBMIT` | OTP detection is exact per flattened value and also regex-scans the joined text. Phone detection strips non-digits and checks the suffix. ### 3.5 Fault application `api/rails/common.ts` splits faults into hard transport faults and business faults. Hard faults (`applyFault`): - `TIMEOUT_HANG_ABOVE_STEP_TTL`: sleeps `FAKE_RAILS_TIMEOUT_HANG_MS` (default 20,000 ms) then returns 504. - `SOCKET_RESET_MID_STREAM`: destroys the socket and returns a 499 sentinel without recording a response. - `HTTP_500_GATEWAY_FAULT`: 503 for outage, 500 otherwise. - `RATE_LIMIT_HTTP_429`: 429. - `MALFORMED_OR_UNMAPPED_200_BODY`: 200 with `{ unexpected_schema: true, data: null, code: "??" }`. Business faults (`finalizeFault`): - `TERMINAL_DECLINE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`: row `FAILED`, failure body. - `LIMIT_EXCEEDED_CUSTOMER_CEILING`: row `FAILED`, limit body. - `WRONG_OTP_RETRYABLE`: row `AWAITING_ACTION`, retryable response. - `AMOUNT_ROUNDING_MISMATCH`: row `PAID`, settled amount +0.05. - `CONFLICTING_WEBHOOK_VS_INQUIRY`: row `PAID`, inquiry override `FAILED`, success webhook fired. Latency is drawn from the scenario range using `latencyFor()` and awaited before the handler. ### 3.6 Scenario persistence and API `engine/chaos/scenarioStore.ts` stores the full config as JSON in `fake_rail_scenarios`, keyed by canonical rail code. `listScenarios()`, `getScenario()`, `saveScenario()` and `resetAllScenarios()` keep the config in sync with the descriptor list. Portal endpoints in `api/portal/scenarios.ts`: | Method | Path | Behaviour | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `GET` | `/portal-api/scenarios` | Returns descriptors and all scenarios | | `GET` | `/portal-api/scenarios/:railCode` | One scenario | | `PUT` | `/portal-api/scenarios/:railCode` | Merge a partial patch and persist | | `POST` | `/portal-api/scenarios/preset/:railCode/:preset` | Apply one preset | | `POST` | `/portal-api/scenarios/global/:preset` | Apply to all rails | | `POST` | `/portal-api/scenarios/reset` | Restore defaults | | `GET` | `/portal-api/scenarios/:railCode/audit` | Read portal audit rows for the rail | Presets are `healthy`, `flaky` (25 percent), `timeout_on_confirm` (100 percent submit timeout) and `outage` (`enabled=false`). Global preset application iterates every descriptor. ### 3.7 Outbound webhook anomalies `engine/webhooks/WebhookDispatcher.ts` persists every delivery in `fake_webhook_deliveries` before scheduling it. It supports: - `delaySeconds` before the first attempt. - `duplicateCount` 1-5 copies. - `outOfOrderPendingAfterPaid`: after a paid/success/captured event, queue a `transaction.pending` copy two seconds later. - `corruptSignatureChancePercent`: use a tampered secret for the signature. Signature profiles exist for `dpay` (timestamp dot raw body, hex lower), `mypay` (raw body, hex lower), `ly_pay` (sorted key/value, hex upper), `plutu` (sorted values, hex upper), `moamalat` (sorted key/value with hex-decoded secret) and `mpgs` (raw body). Every other gateway uses a generic sorted-key/value HMAC-SHA256 profile. Delivery semantics: - Timeout is `FAKE_RAILS_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS`. - `ok` responses move to `SENT`. - Failures retry with exponential backoff `1s, 2s, 4s` up to three attempts, then `FAILED`. - Queued deliveries are resumed on process start. - `replay(deliveryId, tamper)` resets state and optionally forges every signature-like header. - The dispatcher emits `webhook.queued`, `webhook.sent` and `webhook.failed` to the SSE sink. The default URL construction has a path bug documented in `fake-rails.protocol`. ### 3.8 Statement generation `api/portal/statements.ts` and `engine/statements/xlsx.ts` implement the tester statement generator. Inputs: `gatewayCode`, optional `from`/`to`, `format` (`csv`, `json`, `xlsx`) and anomalies: - `feeVariancePercent` 0-100 with `feeVarianceAmount` added to matching rows. - `omitOne`: drop the last line. - `addUnrecorded`: append a synthetic `UNRECORDED-` line. The generator filters `PAID`, `SUCCEEDED`, `REFUNDED` and `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED` rows, writes a `fake_statements` metadata row, broadcasts `statement.generated` and returns CSV, JSON or a dependency-free XLSX built from store-only ZIP parts and OOXML. This is a download generator. It does not push the file to `core-back`, and the core reconciliation path remains an admin upload. ### 3.9 Tester portal API | Router | Endpoints | Notes | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `transactions.ts` | list, stream, summary, detail, action, events | Actions: `APPROVE`, `REJECT`, `APPROVE_MISMATCH`, `APPROVE_LATE`, `FORCE_OUTCOME`, `CANCEL` | | `scenarios.ts` | list/get/put/presets/reset/audit | Full config persisted | | `webhooks.ts` | list, fire, replay, send-now, dispute | Fire accepts delay/duplicates/out-of-order/corruption | | `statements.ts` | list, generate | CSV/JSON/XLSX | | `seederSync.ts` | handshake, bulk seed | Shared seeder token | | `hosted.ts` | session read, session action | Public hosted flow | `transactions.ts` writes `fake_portal_audit` for actions and broadcasts `transaction.action`. `summary` returns grouped status counts, per-rail counts and up to fifty pending actions. The `sseClients` field is currently `undefined`. Hosted actions are `APPROVE`, `APPROVE_TAMPERED`, `DROP_WEBHOOK`, `ABANDON`, `DECLINE` and `CANCEL`: - `APPROVE` sets `PAID` and fires a webhook. - `APPROVE_TAMPERED` sets `PAID`, fires a webhook, then appends `status=failed&amount=0.01` to the redirect. - `DROP_WEBHOOK` leaves the row awaiting action and fires nothing. - `ABANDON` fires a paid webhook after 30 seconds while leaving the row awaiting action. - `DECLINE` sets `FAILED`, fires a failure webhook and redirects to `cancel_url`. - `CANCEL` sets `CANCELLED` and redirects to `cancel_url`. The hosted router is public by design because the payer is not a tester. ### 3.10 SSE The only stream is `GET /portal-api/transactions/stream`, authenticated by a query-string JWT because `EventSource` cannot set headers. It emits `ready`, `rail.request`, `webhook.queued`, `webhook.sent`, `webhook.failed`, `transaction.action`, `scenario.updated`, `scenario.reset`, `statement.generated`, `hosted.action`, `seeder.bulk` and `webhook.replayed`. There is no per-replay cursor. A reconnecting client loses events that occurred while disconnected. ### 3.11 Tester SPA `fake-rails-front/src/router/index.ts` defines seven routes: | Route | Page | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/login` | `pages/login/index.tsx` | Single tester login | | `/dashboard` | `pages/dashboard/index.tsx` | KPIs, live feed, pending actions | | `/transactions` | `pages/transactions/index.tsx` | Filter, inspect, compose webhooks | | `/chaos-matrix` | `pages/chaos-matrix/index.tsx` | Per-rail cards and global presets | | `/statements` | `pages/statements/index.tsx` | Generate CSV/XLSX/JSON with anomalies | | `/hosted/redirect/:sessionId` | `pages/hosted/redirect/[sessionId].tsx` | Interactive hosted checkout | | `/hosted/widget-frame` | `pages/hosted/widget-frame.tsx` | Moamalat/MPGS iframe content | The router guard redirects unauthenticated non-hosted routes to `/login` and keeps the attempted path in `?redirect=`. Tokens live in `localStorage` under `fake-rails-token` and user info under `fake-rails-user`. The portal layout has four navigation links and an environment badge. `LiveTransactionFeed` opens the SSE stream with the query token and listens for a subset of event names. `WireInspectorDrawer` shows transaction fields, step events and webhook deliveries. `WebhookComposerModal` fires or disputes a webhook. `RailChaosCard` edits failure chance, latency, primary failure mode, duplicates, out-of-order and corruption. The SPA is fixed to the portal shell's language and theme; it does not have the admin/merchant i18n catalogue. `tests/e2e/exhaustive/exhaustive-fake-rails-surface.spec.ts` only visits `/login` across three viewports, two locales and two themes while mocking every portal API; it asserts shell geometry, no `#app` transform and no horizontal overflow. ## 4. Contracts and invariants 1. **Scenario state is durable.** Every scenario update survives a restart because it is written to SQLite. 2. **Failure fate is pinned per transaction.** A transaction that is assigned a `SUBMIT` timeout will not fail at `INITIATE`. 3. **Magic inputs are phase-scoped.** The trigger is ignored when its phase differs from the current route phase. 4. **Disabled means outage.** `enabled=false` always yields the 503 outage path. 5. **Webhook delivery is at-least-once with bounded retries.** Duplicates and tampering are deliberate test features. 6. **Hosted approval is a tester action, not a trusted payment signal.** The core must still verify any resulting webhook or inquiry. 7. **Statement anomalies are deterministic for a given window.** `feeVariancePercent` uses a PRNG seeded by gateway and window. 8. **The portal never claims to be a real switch.** It is a test surface and must remain isolated. ## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface - Scenario fields and failure modes: `DefaultRailScenarios.ts`. - Magic triggers, fate assignment, latency: `ChaosEvaluator.ts`. - Persistent config: `scenarioStore.ts` plus `fake_rail_scenarios`. - Webhook queue and signature profiles: `WebhookDispatcher.ts`. - Statement generator: `api/portal/statements.ts`, `engine/statements/xlsx.ts`. - Portal routes: `api/portal/**`. - SPA routes and components: `fake-rails-front/src/**`. ## 6. Operational usage ```bash # Global healthy reset curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4104/portal-api/scenarios/global/healthy \ -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" # Make Edfali time out on confirm curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4104/portal-api/scenarios/preset/edfali/timeout_on_confirm \ -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" # Fire three copies of a paid webhook curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4104/portal-api/webhooks/$TX_ID/fire \ -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"event":"payment.paid","duplicateCount":3}' ``` - Use the transaction detail endpoint before replaying a webhook so the target URL and signature profile are known. - Reset all scenarios after a chaos test. The default row persists otherwise. - The hosted page is intentionally public; do not expose the portal port outside the test network. ## 7. Purpose and scope This part describes how `core-back`, the synthetic seeder and `deploy/` connect to the fake rails tier: - `seedFakeRails.ts` rewrites gateway environments, widget definitions, webhook channel tokens and credential secrets. - The scoped SSRF allowlist permits a private fake rails host without opening private-address SSRF generally. - The synthetic seeder requires fake rails and performs a handshake plus bulk sync. - The deploy engine plans a sixth `fake-rails` role, generates a certificate, opens the portal port, renders an Nginx vhost and optionally seeds the blueprints. - The checkout frontend must be able to load the fake widget scripts and message origins. It does not document the emulator internals (`fake-rails.backend`), the rail protocol (`fake-rails.protocol`) or the tester portal (`fake-rails.chaos`). ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) The integration is designed to make the platform work out of the box with the emulator: 1. Every seeded gateway environment gets a base URL of `${FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/rails/` and an `allowed_hosts` entry for the fake host. 2. Moamalat and MPGS widget definitions load the emulator's SDK scripts. 3. Inbound-verify crypto secrets are derived from a shared seeder token, so signatures produced by the emulator verify with real cryptography and no bypassed checks. 4. `ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS` relaxes the private-IP guard only when the target host is in both `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS` and the gateway version's own `allowed_hosts`. 5. The deployment engine adds an optional `fake-rails` host role with its own backend port, Nginx port, TLS mode, certificate SAN, firewall scope and PM2 process. 6. The synthetic seeder refuses to run unless it is a declared test server, fake rails is enabled, production is explicitly opted in, every gateway host is fake, and the handshake succeeds. 7. The synthetic seeder bulk-syncs its historical transactions and step events into the emulator so the tester portal shows the same history as the gateway. ## 3. As-built architecture ### 3.1 `seedFakeRails.ts` `core-back/prisma/seedFakeRails.ts` requires `FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN`. It then runs four update passes and one setting upsert. **Environments.** `updateEnvironments()` loads every `gatewayVersion` with its gateway and environments. For each environment: - It reads existing `baseUrls` and preserves the keys (or uses `api`). - It sets every key to `${FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/rails/${gateway.code}`. - It unions the environment's existing `allowedHosts` with the fake base host, optional `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`. - It sets `enabled=true`. **Widgets.** `updateWidgets()` loads widget definitions through their route and gateway. For `moamalat` and `mpgs` it sets: - `scriptUrls = [/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js]` or `[/sdk/mpgs-session.js]`. - `scriptSriHashes = []`. - `allowedOrigins = []`. No other widget is changed. **Webhook channels.** `updateWebhookChannels()` scans `confirmationChannel` rows of type `WEBHOOK`. The first channel per gateway code receives `pathToken = ${code}-webhook`; later versions keep the existing token. It does not change the channel's verification method, signature header, IP allowlist or crypto-profile reference. **Credential secrets.** `updateCredentialSecrets()` returns zero if the seeder token is empty. Otherwise, for every `PLATFORM` credential set, it walks existing entries. When an entry key matches a crypto profile `secretKeyRef`, it derives: ```text HMAC-SHA256(seederToken, "fake-rails::") ``` where purpose is `webhook` if any matching profile is `INBOUND_VERIFY`, otherwise `sign`. The derived secret is encrypted through `Vault.encryptSecret(secret, "credential-set")`, the entry is marked secret and its `secretVersion` is incremented. Entries with no matching profile are left untouched. The credential set is marked `VERIFIED`. **Environment mode.** `ensureEnvironmentSetting()` upserts `server.environment_mode = { mode: "TEST_SANDBOX" }`. The script prints environment, widget, channel and credential counts and exits non-zero if the token is missing. ### 3.2 Seeded gateway count `core-back/prisma/seedBlueprints.ts` creates thirteen distinct gateway codes: `edfali`, `sadad`, `moamalat`, `cbl_lypay`, `mypay`, `tlync`, `mobicash`, `onepay`, `yussor`, `sahara`, `mpgs`, `evo_pay`, `neompay`. The fake descriptor catalogue has twenty rail codes. Seven fake descriptors have no core gateway blueprint: - `dpay` - `plutu` - `masrefy` - `hawelli` - `gpay_libya` - `numo_pay` - `libyana` Conversely, the core uses `cbl_lypay` and `evo_pay`, while the fake routes use `ly_pay` and `evopay`. The counts therefore agree only in spirit: 13 core gateways versus 20 fake descriptors, with two code mismatches inside the overlap. ### 3.3 Scoped SSRF allowlist `core-back/engine/apiConsumer/fakeRailsAllowlist.ts` implements `isFakeRailsHostAllowed(hostname, gatewayAllowedHosts)`: 1. `env.ALLOW_FAKE_RAILS_HOSTS` must be `true`. 2. The normalized hostname must appear in `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. 3. The same hostname must appear in the caller's `gatewayAllowedHosts`. 4. Trailing dots are stripped; comparison is lowercase. `ApiConsumer.ts` and `StepExecutor.ts` call this check before URL validation. When true, `requireHttps` is set to false, allowing the private/loopback fake host over plain HTTP. The general SSRF guard still rejects `169.254.169.254`, unrelated private addresses, redirects, userinfo, fragments, CRLF and path traversal. The allowlist test proves: - Closed unless explicitly enabled. - Both environment and gateway list must match. - An empty gateway list never matches. - A metadata address is refused even if listed. ### 3.4 Synthetic seeder integration `core-back/prisma/syntheticSeeder/SeederSafetyGate.ts` enforces five gates: 1. `IS_TEST_SERVER=true`. 2. `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED=true` and a public base URL. 3. Production requires `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`. 4. At least one allowed host; every configured gateway environment URL must point at an allowed fake host, not an external host or metadata address. 5. The `POST /portal-api/internal/seeder-handshake` call must succeed with the seeder token. `sync/fakeRailsBulkSyncClient.ts` posts transactions and step events to `/portal-api/internal/bulk-seed` with `x-fake-rails-seeder-token`. The emulator inserts both batches in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and broadcasts `seeder.bulk`. ### 3.5 Deployment configuration `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` defines the fake rails keys and validates: - Host, key path and private IP when enabled. - Tester username/password/JWT/seeder token. - Production opt-in. - Password length and non-collision of backend/Nginx ports with every other role and public port. - `RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED` requires an enabled test server and fake rails. `deploy/lib/hostPlanner.ts` maps the role to: - Service `pg-fake-rails-back`, source `fake-rails-back`, port `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT`. - Environment with `NODE_ENV`, `HOST`, `PORT`, `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED`, `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION`, public base URL, data directory, admin credentials, secrets, CIDRs and `CORE_INBOUND_BASE_URL`. - Nginx site `fake-rails` on `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` with `FAKE_RAILS_SSL`, domain, certificate paths and static root `current/fake-rails-front/dist`. - Certificate bundle `fake-rails-server`. - Firewall rules for SSH and the portal port restricted to `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` plus core/checkout private IPs. `deploy/lib/pkiManager.ts` includes `fakeRails` in the PKI bundle with SAN `DNS:`, `IP:` and `IP:127.0.0.1`. `deploy/deploy.ts` builds the SPA, deploys backend plus `dist`, renders the vhost and optionally runs `bun run seed-fake-rails` on the core host. `deploy/templates/nginx.fakerails.conf.tpl` proxies `/rails`, `/sdk`, `/portal-api` and `/hosted` to the backend and serves the SPA. Its CSP allows `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` and `frame-ancestors 'self' *`. ### 3.6 Embedded widget and CSP block The embedded flow cannot currently load the emulator widget end to end: 1. `checkout-front/src/components/renderers/EmbeddedWidgetRenderer.tsx` hard-codes `SCRIPT_ALLOWLIST_HOSTS` to public HTTPS partners (`payments.moamalat.ly`, `secure.moamalat.ly`, `test.mpgmerchant.test`, `pay.evowallet.net`, `js.numo-pay.com`). A fake URL such as `http://127.0.0.1:8444/sdk/moamalat-lightbox.js` fails `isAllowlistedScript()` for both protocol and host. 2. Even if the renderer allowed it, the checkout Nginx templates set `script-src 'self'` with no fake origin. 3. The seeded widget `cspAdditions` remain `frame-src https://*.moamalat.example.ly` and `frame-src https://*.mpgs.example.ly`; `seedFakeRails.ts` does not rewrite them. 4. `seedFakeRails.ts` writes an empty SRI array, so `EmbeddedWidgetRenderer` cannot apply an integrity hash. The redirect flow is unaffected because it uses a browser navigation to the hosted URL, subject to the checkout redirect allowlist. ### 3.7 Webhook and callback gaps - **Wrong path.** `WebhookDispatcher.defaultUrlFor()` inserts `/webhook/` between the inbound base and `:gateway`, while the checkout route is `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`. - **Token mismatch.** The default token is `${gateway_code}-webhook`. Blueprint tokens are not uniformly that string (for example `cbl-lypay-webhook`); `seedFakeRails.ts` rewrites the first webhook channel per code to `${code}-webhook`, so the default works only after that pass and only for the rewritten channel. - **No fake-side verification.** The emulator signs outbound webhooks but never verifies core-originated requests. - **Credential coverage.** `updateCredentialSecrets()` only updates existing credential entries whose key matches a crypto profile. A gateway with no secret entry or a different key shape remains unconfigured. - **Crypto-profile mismatch.** The emulator has six explicit webhook signature profiles plus a generic fallback. `evo_pay`'s blueprint declares RSA-SHA256 with a private key, but the fake profile for `evo_pay` is not defined, so it falls back to HMAC. - **Statement channels.** The core seeds statement channel rows with `-statement` tokens but has no `SETTLEMENT_FETCH` flow and no fetch URL. Contracts and invariants 1. **The SSRF relaxation is triple-gated.** Environment flag, environment host list and gateway host list must all agree. 2. **The fake host never becomes a general private-address exception.** Metadata and unrelated private ranges remain blocked. 3. **Derived secrets must match on both sides.** Both implementations hash `fake-rails::` with the seeder token. 4. **Seeded environments are enabled and point only at the fake base URL.** The pass overwrites every existing base-url key. 5. **The synthetic seeder cannot run against real gateways.** Gate 4 rejects any non-fake host. 6. **Deployment production mode requires an explicit opt-in at both config and process level.** 7. **The fake rails host exposes only its portal/Nginx port.** Backend port stays loopback. ## 5. Purpose and scope This part owns the deployment input contract: `deploy/deploy.env`, its parser, Zod schema, cross-field validation, topology model and the translation from logical roles to concrete hosts. It defines the node grammar, all configuration groups, precedence rules, topology classification and the validation that runs before any SSH connection. It does not own the host plan itself (see `deploy.planner`), certificate generation (`deploy.pki`), firewall application (`deploy.firewall`), the pipeline (`deploy.pipeline`) or storage provisioning (`deploy.storage`). The entrypoint is `deploy/deploy.sh`, which requires Bun and a `deploy/deploy.env`, then executes `bun run deploy/deploy.ts`. ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) The design requires a flexible 1..N topology: - compute tiers `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES`, `CHECKOUT_NODES`; - one PostgreSQL primary, zero or more streaming replicas and optional PgBouncer; - optional Redis, dedicated audit and log databases, and a backup node; - any compute or storage role may share a host, but ports must remain distinct and storage roles may not collide with compute listeners; - configuration is validated before the first SSH connection, so an invalid IP or missing key fails on the operator workstation rather than halfway through production; - node arrays override the legacy single-host fields; - the core certificate SAN and firewall allowlists are derived from the same private IPs. The design names three topology shapes: fully distributed, split/combined hosts, and a single all-in-one staging box. The code additionally supports horizontal compute arrays. ## 3. As-built architecture ### 3.1 Loading and parsing `deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` uses a small dotenv parser, not a full dotenv library: - blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored; - `KEY=value` is required; lines without `=` are ignored; - single- or double-quoted values end at the first matching quote, so an inline `#` after the quote is not part of the value; - unquoted values are truncated at ` #`; - there is no variable expansion, no `export` handling, no escaped-newline handling and no multi-line value support; - a duplicate key overwrites the earlier value in the parsed record. The parsed record is validated with `z.strictObject`. Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored. `loadDeployConfig()` returns either a config plus an empty problem list or a list of Zod issues and cross-field problems. ### 3.2 Node grammar -Every `*_NODES` list, `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE` and `BACKUP_NODE` uses: +Every `*_NODES` list, `FAKE_RAILS_NODE`, `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE` and `BACKUP_NODE` uses: ```text nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort ``` - `nodeId` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`. - `sshHost` and `privateIp` must be IPv4 addresses. DNS names are not accepted for nodes. - `sshPort` and `servicePort` must be integers from 1 to 65535. - Node ids must be unique across every node list. -- A node list rejects duplicate private IPs within that list. -- PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs must also be globally unique. +- A node list rejects duplicate node ids and duplicate `privateIp:servicePort` endpoints. Two nodes may share a private IP when their service ports differ. +- PostgreSQL primary/replica endpoints (`privateIp:servicePort`) must be globally unique. `CORE_PORT` for planning. The same applies to admin, merchant and checkout. SSH user/key/sudo are still taken from the legacy fields. 2. **PostgreSQL storage fields over legacy database fields.** When any `PG_*` storage field is configured, `PG_DB_NAME`, `PG_DB_USER` and `PG_DB_PASSWORD` are authoritative. Otherwise `DB_*` is used, falling back to `PG_DB_*`. 3. **Derived database URL.** When the PostgreSQL tier is configured and a host exists, `DATABASE_URL` is derived from the PG credentials, the primary private IP and `PGBOUNCER_PORT` when enabled; otherwise the explicit `DATABASE_URL` is used. 4. **Explicit core URL list.** `CORE_BACK_URLS` wins; otherwise `https://:` for every `CORE_NODES` entry; otherwise the legacy `https://:`. 5. **Node service port over configured backend port.** A node's `servicePort` overrides `CORE_PORT`/`ADMIN_BACK_PORT`/`MERCHANT_BACK_PORT`/`CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT` for that node. 6. **CLI over environment.** `--fresh`, `--update`, `--only`, `--nodes`, `--rolling-batch`, `--keep`, `--rotate-certs`, `--skip-build` and `--skip-verify` override the corresponding configuration for one run. 7. **Admin checklist master flag.** `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS` wins over the legacy `ADMIN_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST`; the legacy key is the fallback when the master key is absent. ### 3.5 Topology classification `planHosts()` groups every role target by `sshHost:sshPort`. The topology label is based on the number of unique SSH endpoints, not on the number of roles: | Unique hosts | Topology | | :--- | :--- | | 1 | `single-host` | | 2 | `split` | | 3 or more | `distributed` | A host can carry several roles. Compute services, Nginx sites, certificate bundles and firewall rules are unioned per host. Storage roles are included only when their management flag is enabled (`PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `BACKUP_ENABLED`), although the storage plan itself is still constructed for display. ### 3.6 Validation rules Zod field validation: - IPv4 octets and CIDR syntax are checked. - Database names, users and replication users must be identifier-safe. - Remote directories, identifiers and domain names have length and character limits. - `DB_ENGINE` is restricted to `postgresql`. - `DEPLOY_MODE` is `auto`, `fresh`, `update` or `rolling_update`. - `PG_VERSION` is one or two digits (default `18`). - `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_HEX` must be exactly 64 hex characters, or empty; it is required when backups are enabled. - `BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT` must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL when backups are enabled. - SSL mode is `certbot`, `custom` or `self_signed`. Cross-field validation: - PostgreSQL fields require `DB_ENGINE=postgresql`. - `PG_REPLICA_NODES` requires exactly one `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`. - `PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true` requires a primary, an SSH key and a non-empty database password. - `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED=true` requires the PostgreSQL storage fields. - Legacy `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true` without the PG tier requires SSH host, key and private IP. - When the PG tier is not configured, legacy `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL` are required. - An explicit `DATABASE_URL` must start with `postgresql://`; if `DB_PRIVATE_IP` is set, the URL should contain it. - Node arrays require the matching `*_SSH_KEY_PATH`. - Redis/audit/log managed-via-SSH mode requires the node, key and password. - Backups require `BACKUP_NODE`, an SSH key, a bucket and an encryption key. - WAL-G backups require `BACKUP_NODE` and `PG_PRIMARY_NODE` to have the same private IP because WAL-G reads the local data directory. - When the audit database is on a different host from a WAL-G backup node, `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` is required. - Node ids are unique across all lists; PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs are unique. - The same SSH endpoint may not expose the same service port for two compute roles. - A storage port may not collide with a compute listener on the same SSH endpoint. - Storage roles on one endpoint may share a port only within the PostgreSQL family (primary, replica, audit, log); Redis, PgBouncer and backup are separate families. - Merchant and checkout HTTP, HTTPS and LAN ports must differ within each portal; all LAN ports (admin, merchant, checkout) must differ; the two public domains must differ. - `CORE_PORT` must differ from all three edge backend ports. - `custom` SSL mode requires both certificate and key paths. - Fake Rails requires its SSH host/key/private IP/admin credentials/JWT secret/seeder token; it refuses production unless `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION=true`; its backend and Nginx ports must not collide with core/edge/admin ports or public 80/443. - The synthetic seeder requires `IS_TEST_SERVER=true`, Fake Rails enabled and, in production, the explicit Fake Rails production override. - `findSshConflicts()` rejects one SSH endpoint with more than one SSH key or user across roles. ### 3.7 Mode behavior `DEPLOY_MODE` is read as follows: - `fresh`: bootstrap packages, Bun, PM2 and the firewall; - `update`: do not bootstrap or change the firewall unless `--enforce-firewall` is passed; - `auto`: does not stat the remote release directory; in practice it behaves like `update` unless `--fresh` is passed; - `rolling_update`: accepted by the schema but not treated differently from `auto`. The CLI `--fresh` always wins; `--update` disables an environment `fresh`. ## 4. Contracts and invariants - Configuration is validated before any SSH connection. - The node grammar uses private IPs for peer communication; `sshHost` may be public. - The same private IP set drives certificate SANs, firewall sources and derived URLs. - Edge environments never include database or KMS secrets. - Core environments include `DATABASE_URL`, replication/audit/log URLs, Redis, backup control paths and `KMS_MASTER_KEY` when configured. - Runtime service environments are forced to `NODE_ENV=production` by the planner even when `DEPLOY_ENV` is development or staging. - A failure in cross-field validation aborts the run before the plan is rendered. - `deploy.env` and `deploy/.certs/` are gitignored; the operator must keep the environment file at mode 0600. ## 5. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) The design requires "smart host deduplication": if two roles share an SSH endpoint, they are one machine. The planner must bootstrap that machine once, merge PM2 services, Nginx vhosts, certificate material and UFW rules, and still keep each horizontal node as its own service identity. -Storage roles are independently scalable. The plan must preserve the intended network policy: the database only accepts core/replica/backup sources, the core only accepts edge sources, and edge backends bind their private IP with a LAN-scoped firewall rule so local or remote Nginx upstreams can reach them. The rendered topology is intended to be the operator's first confirmation that deduplication and node arrays mean what they intended. ## 3. It does not re-check them. The validation rules relevant to the plan are: - compute roles on the same SSH endpoint may not claim the same service port; - a storage listener may not collide with a compute listener on the same endpoint; - storage roles on the same endpoint may share a port only inside the PostgreSQL family (`pg-primary`, `pg-replica`, `audit-db`, `log-db`); PgBouncer, Redis and backup are separate families; - PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs are unique; - node ids are unique across all lists; - merchant/checkout/admin LAN and public ports are distinct; - the two public domains differ; - core and edge backend ports differ. Contracts and invariants - A host key is `sshHost:sshPort`; roles sharing it are one machine and must share SSH user/key/sudo. - Every compute node gets a distinct service name; duplicate node ids are rejected before planning. - A host's firewall is the union of its roles' rules; an unrestricted rule widens the result. - Nginx sites are unique by site name per host. - Certificates are the union of role bundles for display and the least-privilege set from `certFilesForHost()` for upload. - Storage plan structure is stable even when management is disabled. - `plan.topology` depends on unique host count only. - Edge service env never contains database or KMS material. - The planner does not mutate the config and does not touch the network. ## 5. Purpose and scope This part owns the internal certificate authority, leaf certificate generation, SAN binding, rotation, SAN-drift handling, verification and least-privilege distribution. It does not own the TLS server implementations. It documents how `core-back`, the three edge BFFs, the backup daemon, Fake Rails and the storage provisioners do or do not consume the generated material. The implementation is `deploy/lib/pkiManager.ts`. The default vault is `deploy/.certs/`, gitignored and mode 0700. The CA private key never leaves the deployment workstation. ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) The design requires: - one offline internal root CA; - a core server certificate whose SAN contains every core private IP, loopback and `core-back.internal`; - client certificates with exact CNs `admin-back`, `merchant-back` and `checkout-back`; - a backup-daemon server certificate bound to the backup private IP and loopback; - a Fake Rails server certificate bound to its domain and private IP; - optional `pg-client`, `redis-client`, `audit-db-client`, `log-db-client` and `backup-client` certificates for storage/backup mTLS links; - TLS 1.3 with `requestCert: true`, `rejectUnauthorized: true` on core; the edge verifies the core certificate against the CA; - least-privilege distribution: edge hosts receive only their own client certificate, storage hosts only their own client certificate, and no host receives the CA private key. The design describes storage mTLS as provisioned end to end. The code generates the material but does not wire it into the database engines; see the deviations below. ## 3. If any SAN is missing, the leaves are re-signed from the existing CA (the CA is not rotated), covering all current leaves. This is how a private-IP change is handled without `--rotate-certs`. The backup host path is `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR` (default `/var/lib/pg-backup/shared/certs`). Certificates are mode 0644, keys 0600, owned by root because they are written through sudo. As written, the daemon may be unable to read the 0600 server key. The deploy health probe would then fail, but the deploy does not repair ownership. This is an open readiness gap; storage/backup mTLS must not be described as proven until a staging run confirms the effective ownership and startup. ## 4. Contracts and invariants - The internal CA private key is never copied to a target host. - Every edge client CN must be exactly the service name expected by the core channel guard. - The core server SAN must include every configured core private IP; a rolling core deploy must not invalidate mTLS on the other nodes. - The backup daemon certificate SAN must include the backup private IP when the daemon binds to it. - Fake Rails SAN must include its configured domain or the fallback `fakerails.internal`. - TLS 1.3 is required between edges and core. - Edge hosts receive no database credential, KMS key or other service's private key. - Rotation is explicit. A normal deploy reuses existing material unless SAN drift requires re-signing. - `verifyPki()` is advisory; a failed or expiring certificate does not block the deploy. ## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface ### PKI inputs | Key | Default | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `ROTATE_MTLS_CERTS` | `false` | Regenerate CA and all leaves. | | `MTLS_VALIDITY_DAYS` | `825` | Leaf validity. | | `CORE_NODES` / `CORE_PRIVATE_IP` | required | Core SAN IPs. | | `BACKUP_NODE` | optional | Backup SAN IP. | | `FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN`, `FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP` | optional | Fake Rails SAN. | | `PG_*`, `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE`, `BACKUP_ENABLED` | optional | Which storage client certificates are generated. | ### Files - `deploy/.certs/internal-ca.crt`, `internal-ca.key` - `deploy/.certs/core-back.crt`, `core-back.key` - `deploy/.certs/backup-daemon.crt`, `backup-daemon.key` - `deploy/.certs/fake-rails.crt`, `fake-rails.key` - `deploy/.certs/admin-back-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/merchant-back-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/checkout-back-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/pg-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/redis-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/audit-db-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/log-db-client.crt`, `.key` - `deploy/.certs/backup-client.crt`, `.key` ### Target paths - Edge/core: `/shared/certs/`. - Storage hosts: `/etc/pg-deploy/certs/`. - Backup daemon: `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR`, default `/var/lib/pg-backup/shared/certs/`. ## 6. Operational usage ```bash # Normal deploy: create missing material, reuse and verify existing material ./deploy/deploy.sh --update # Force a full CA and leaf rotation ./deploy/deploy.sh --update --rotate-certs # Inspect a certificate manually openssl x509 -in deploy/.certs/core-back.crt -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName ``` Changing a private IP: 1. Update every `*_PRIVATE_IP` and node-array `privateIp` in `deploy/deploy.env`. 2. Run `./deploy/deploy.sh --update --enforce-firewall`. 3. The PKI step detects SAN drift and re-signs the leaves from the existing CA. 4. Restart or redeploy processes that cache the certificate material; the edge pool does not reload files in place. Keep `deploy/deploy.env` and `deploy/.certs/` at restrictive permissions. Do not copy `internal-ca.key` to a target host. ## 7. Status and deviations ### Implemented - Offline RSA CA with a 10-year validity. - Multi-SAN core server certificate covering every core private IP. - Exact edge client CNs, backup daemon and Fake Rails server certificates. - Optional storage client certificates. - SAN-drift detection and leaf re-signing without CA rotation. - Explicit CA/leaf rotation. - `certFilesForHost()` least-privilege distribution. - CA private key never distributed. - Real consumption by core TLS, edge clients, backup daemon and Fake Rails. ### Partial - Storage client certificates exist but are not consumed by PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, Redis, audit DB or log DB. - The backup daemon's cert/key ownership is not aligned with its `pgbackup` user. - Expiry is reported but does not force rotation. - The backup daemon does not authorize a client CN per route. ### Missing / deferred - end-to-end storage mTLS configuration (`ssl=on` with internal certs, `clientcert=verify-full`, Redis TLS, PgBouncer client TLS). - Automatic renewal before expiry. - A CRL/OCSP or short-lived certificate workflow. - Per-service certificate isolation on a co-located edge host. - Client-CN authorization on the backup daemon. ### Known bugs / risks - A deploy can complete its PKI step and still fail the backup daemon mTLS probe because the key is unreadable by `pgbackup`. - `verifyPki()` does not gate the deploy on expired or soon-to-expire certificates. - The storage certificate material is uploaded to `/etc/pg-deploy/certs` but no storage provisioner references that directory. - `core-back` trusts any certificate signed by the internal CA for the TLS handshake; the CN guard is the only channel authorization. ## 8. Verification and tests ```bash cd deploy && bun run typecheck && bun test test/pkiScale.test.ts test/exhaustive-deploy-matrix.test.ts test/provisioners.test.ts cd deploy/backup-daemon && bun test test/server.test.ts ``` Covered: - core SAN includes every core private IP, loopback and DNS name; - backup SAN includes the backup private IP; - storage client certificates are created only for configured tiers; - `certFilesForHost()` distributes only allowed leaves; - SAN drift re-signs leaves without rotating the CA; - backup daemon refuses plain HTTP unless explicitly allowed and requires CA + server pair; - mTLS requires a client certificate when a CA is configured. Not covered by automated tests: - a real TLS handshake from an edge host to a core node; - PostgreSQL/PgBouncer/Redis consumption of the storage certificates; - backup daemon startup as `pgbackup` with the deployed file ownership. ## 9. Change history - 2026-11-03: initial canonical part at `5a24f6f+working-tree`. --- > **Part ID:** `deploy.firewall` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-03 · **Verified against:** `5a24f6f+working-tree` # Firewall Policy and Application ## 1. Purpose and scope This part owns the host-aware UFW policy: the abstract rules derived by the planner, the merge behavior for co-located roles, the exact `ufw` commands, installation and application order. It does not own the host plan, the service bind addresses or the Nginx `allow`/`deny` rules, although the two layers share `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS` and the same private IPs. ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) Every host gets a default-deny inbound policy. Only role-specific ports are opened, and private services are restricted to the private IPs that need them: - database only from core (and replicas/backup); - core only from the three edge tiers; - admin only from the LAN; - merchant/checkout public ports open, backends loopback-only; - storage services only from core, backup and peer storage nodes; - backup daemon only from core. If several roles share a host, the rules are the union of the role rules. The SSH rule is always emitted first and `ufw --force enable` is last, so a failed rule cannot lock the operator out. ## 3. As-built architecture ### 3.1 Base policy `baseUfwCommands()` emits, in order: ```text ufw default deny incoming ufw default allow outgoing ufw default deny routed ``` Every rule is `tcp`. No UDP rule is generated. The base policy is applied before role rules. ### 3.2 Rule model `FirewallRulePlan` has: - `port`; - `proto: "tcp"`; - optional `fromCidrs`; - a human-readable comment. `ufwCommandsForRule()`: - if `fromCidrs` is absent or empty: `ufw allow /tcp comment `; - otherwise one command per CIDR: `ufw allow from to any port proto tcp comment `. CIDRs are not coalesced or deduplicated at command generation; the planner's union deduplicates source lists. ### 3.3 Role matrix `buildComputeFirewall()`: | Role | Opened ports | Sources | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `db` (legacy) | SSH, `DB_PORT` | DB port only from every core private IP. | | `core` | SSH, core service port | Core port only from every admin/merchant/checkout private IP (node arrays or legacy). | | `admin` | SSH, `ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT` | Admin vhost only from `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`. Backend `ADMIN_BACK_PORT` is not opened; it binds loopback. | | `merchant` | SSH, `MERCHANT_HTTP_PORT`, `MERCHANT_HTTPS_PORT` when SSL, `MERCHANT_LAN_PORT` when > 0 | HTTP/HTTPS unrestricted; LAN port from `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`. Backend port is not opened. | | `checkout` | SSH, `CHECKOUT_HTTP_PORT`, `CHECKOUT_HTTPS_PORT` when SSL, `CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT` when > 0 | HTTP/HTTPS unrestricted; LAN port from `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`. Backend port is not opened. | | `fake-rails` | SSH, `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` | From `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS`, every core private IP, and the legacy `CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP` when set. | `buildStorageFirewall()`: | Role | Opened ports | Sources | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `pg-primary` | SSH, PostgreSQL port, PgBouncer port when enabled | PostgreSQL from replicas + backup + core (core omitted when PgBouncer is enabled); PgBouncer from core. | | `pg-replica` | SSH, PostgreSQL port, PgBouncer port when enabled | PostgreSQL from the other PostgreSQL nodes + backup + core (core omitted when PgBouncer is enabled); PgBouncer from core. | | `pgbouncer` | PgBouncer port | Core only. | | `redis` | SSH, Redis port | Core + backup. | | `audit-db` | SSH, PostgreSQL port | Core + backup. | | `log-db` | SSH, PostgreSQL port | Core + backup. | | `backup` | SSH, `BACKUP_DAEMON_PORT` | Core only. | The `core` rule does not include Fake Rails or backup IPs: the core initiates backup calls and Fake Rails calls outbound, so neither needs inbound access to core. The Fake Rails rule uses `allCorePrivateIps(config)` but only `CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP`, not the checkout node-array IPs. On a multi-node checkout tier, additional checkout nodes may not be able to reach Fake Rails unless they are also in `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS`. ### 3.4 Co-located hosts and union `HostPlan.firewall` starts as the first target's rules and is merged with each additional role's rules by `mergeFirewall()`: - same port/proto: union the CIDR lists; - if either rule is unrestricted, remove the source restriction so the broader access wins; - concatenate comments with `; `. Examples: - core + admin on one host: core port restricted to all edge IPs, admin LAN port restricted to the LAN, both SSH rules collapse to one port; - merchant + checkout on one host: public HTTP/HTTPS likely produce one unrestricted rule per port after merging; both LAN ports are separate; - PostgreSQL primary + audit + log on one host: all three may share port 5432 because they are in the same PostgreSQL family (this is checked by config validation, not by the merge). The union can widen access. A role that opens a port publicly (merchant/checkout HTTP/HTTPS) makes that port public for the entire host, including any co-located role. Port collisions are rejected before planning when they cross families. ### 3.5 Application `applyFirewall()`: 1. Builds the complete command list. 2. Requires an SSH rule whose port equals `host.ssh.port`; otherwise it refuses to enable UFW. 3. In dry-run, logs every `ufw` command through the runner and returns. 4. Checks whether `ufw` exists. 5. If absent, detects the OS (`deploy/lib/osDetector.ts`) and installs `ufw` with `apt-get` or `pacman`. 6. Re-checks; if still absent, logs a warning and skips firewall application. 7. Runs every command with sudo in order, with `ufw --force enable` last. 8. `deploy.ts` reads back `ufw status verbose` and prints the first 12 lines. The installer supports Debian/Ubuntu-family and Arch-family hosts. Unknown OSes get no automatic install. ### 3.6 When rules are applied `deploy.ts` applies the firewall only when: - `--fresh` or `DEPLOY_MODE=fresh`, or - `--enforce-firewall`. `--update` alone skips bootstrap and firewall changes. `--dry-run` prints commands without executing them. ## 4. Contracts and invariants - Default inbound is deny. - The SSH port is always allowed before UFW is enabled; enabling without an SSH rule is refused. - Only TCP rules are generated. - Private services are source-restricted by private IPs or LAN CIDRs. - Backend ports (`4101`, `4102`, `4103`, core `4000`) are not publicly opened. - An unrestricted rule wins over a restricted rule for the same port on a co-located host. - `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS` is shared by admin UFW rules, LAN vhost UFW rules and Nginx allow rules. - The firewall is the outer network ring; mTLS and core authorization are independent inner controls. - `--update` is not a firewall reconciliation mode; use `--enforce-firewall`. ## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface ### Inputs | Key | Meaning | | :--- | :--- | | `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS` | Admin and LAN vhost sources. | | `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS` | Additional Fake Rails sources. | | `CORE_NODES` / `CORE_PRIVATE_IP` | Core sources and core host identity. | | `ADMIN_NODES` / `MERCHANT_NODES` / `CHECKOUT_NODES` and legacy private IPs | Edge sources for core. | | `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED`, `BACKUP_NODE` | Storage rule sources. | | `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE` | Storage rule sources. | | `BACKUP_DAEMON_PORT` | Backup control-plane port. | | `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT` | Fake Rails ingress port. | | `*_HTTP_PORT`, `*_HTTPS_PORT`, `*_LAN_PORT`, `ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT` | Public and LAN listeners. | ### Generated artifacts - `HostPlan.firewall`: abstract rules used by the deployment audit and the renderer. - UFW commands in `deploy/lib/firewallConfigurator.ts`. - `ufw status verbose` readback in the deployment log. ## 6. Operational usage ```bash # Re-apply the plan after changing private IPs or ports ./deploy/deploy.sh --update --enforce-firewall # Preview without executing ./deploy/deploy.sh --dry-run # Inspect a host ssh 'sudo ufw status verbose' ``` If a host becomes unreachable after a firewall change, use the provider console. The SSH rule should prevent lockout, but a wrong `*_SSH_PORT`, an external security group, or a missing route can still block access. ## 7. Status and deviations ### Implemented - Default-deny inbound, allow outgoing, deny routed. - Role-specific source restrictions for compute and storage. - Co-located union with unrestricted-rule precedence. - SSH-rule prerequisite before enabling UFW. - OS-aware UFW installation. - Enable-last ordering. - Dry-run command logging. - Post-apply status readback. ### Partial - Application is best-effort: no firewall is installed if the package manager is unknown or installation fails. - Rules are not reconciled or diffed against a previously applied set; a stale rule from an older plan remains. - The readback is printed, not parsed as a gate. ### Missing / deferred - UDP policy. - IPv6-specific rules. - Automatic removal of obsolete rules. - A per-host firewall diff or rollback. - An explicit Fake Rails allowlist union for every checkout node. ### Known bugs / risks - A broad rule from one co-located role widens the same port for every role on that host. - Fake Rails may reject checkout traffic from additional `CHECKOUT_NODES` private IPs because only the legacy `CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP` is unioned. - The isolated `pgbouncer` rule set contains no SSH rule. In the current plan PgBouncer is emitted on a PostgreSQL host, which supplies SSH; a future standalone PgBouncer plan would be refused by `applyFirewall()`. - The firewall does not protect against a compromised host on an allowed source CIDR; mTLS and core authorization are still required. - `--update` does not enforce the current policy, which can leave an old, wider rule in place. ## 8. Verification and tests ```bash cd deploy && bun run typecheck && bun test test/hostPlanner.test.ts test/hostPlannerScale.test.ts test/exhaustive-deploy-matrix.test.ts test/fakeRails.test.ts ``` Covered: - single-host union includes core, admin and public ports; - database port sources are restricted to core; - core port sources are the three edge private IPs; - merchant public HTTP/HTTPS plus LAN port rules; - LAN listeners can be HTTP; - Fake Rails sources and ports; - exhaustive matrix rule generation. Not covered: - a real `ufw` apply on a remote host; - rule persistence across reboot; - removal of stale rules; - provider-level firewall interaction. ## 9. Change history - 2026-11-03: initial canonical part at `5a24f6f+working-tree`. --- > **Part ID:** `deploy.pipeline` · **Status:** `partial` · **Last verified:** 2026-11-03 · **Verified against:** `5a24f6f+working-tree` # Deployment Pipeline ## 1. Purpose and scope This part documents the actual `deploy/deploy.ts` pipeline: step order, source synchronization, release layout, PM2 and Nginx activation, rolling batches, seeding, verification, pruning, the pre-migration backup and the backup-daemon source deployment. It does not own configuration validation (`deploy.topology`), planning (`deploy.planner`), PKI (`deploy.pki`), firewall policy (`deploy.firewall`), storage provisioning (`deploy.storage`) or the backup daemon internals (`deploy.backup`). ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design) The design requires a strictly ordered deployment so storage and migrations are live before edge traffic switches: validate and plan; build SPAs; ensure PKI; bootstrap hosts and firewall; provision storage and take a pre-migration backup; deploy core; optionally Fake Rails; admin; merchant; checkout; seed; verify; prune; audit summary. It also requires atomic releases, a symlinked `current`, least-privilege environment/certificate delivery, rolling batches with health checks and a clean rollback path. The code follows this order but differs in several operational details recorded below. ## 3. As-built architecture ### 3.1 Step 1: validate and plan `main()` parses CLI options, checks that `deploy.env` exists, loads and validates it, runs `findSshConflicts()`, calls `planHosts()`, prints `renderTopology()` and creates an `SshRunner` with `verbose: true`. A missing file, schema error, cross-field error or SSH credential conflict aborts before any remote command. With `--dry-run`, every later command is logged instead of executed. ### 3.2 Step 2: build SPAs locally `buildFrontends()` runs `bun run build` locally for `admin-front`, `merchant-front`, `checkout-front` and, when enabled, `fake-rails-front`. Admin builds receive `VITE_SHOW_CHECKLISTS`, `VITE_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST` and `VITE_SHOW_HELP_PANELS` from the deploy config. The step is skipped with `--skip-build` or `--dry-run`; it builds all three SPAs regardless of `--only`. ### 3.3 Step 3: PKI `buildPki()` creates missing material, reuses valid SAN-covering material, or re-signs leaves on SAN drift. `verifyPki()` prints every certificate and remaining days. `uploadStorageCertificates()` writes storage/backup certificate material to `/etc/pg-deploy/certs` or `BACKUP_DAEMON_CERT_DIR` for hosts that carry a storage role. See `deploy.pki` for certificate roles, distribution and the known storage/backup ownership gaps. ### 3.4 Step 4: bootstrap and firewall `fresh` is computed as: ```text options.fresh || (options.update ? false : config.DEPLOY_MODE === "fresh") ``` It is **not** `auto` detection of a missing remote directory. For every host, when `fresh` or `--enforce-firewall`: - assert the SSH key exists (unless dry-run); - run `true` to prove connectivity; - if fresh, detect the OS, install `nginx rsync ufw curl ca-certificates nodejs` (or the Arch equivalent), install Bun if absent, symlink Bun/bunx into `/usr/local/bin`, install PM2 if absent and best-effort register `pm2 startup systemd`; - apply UFW, print the command count and read back `ufw status verbose`. The firewall is only applied in fresh or enforce mode. An ordinary `--update` does not reconcile it. ### 3.5 Step 5: storage and pre-migration backup The step requires a core host in the plan. Provisioning is gated by `--only` and by the management flags: - PostgreSQL 18 primary/replicas/PgBouncer when `PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` and the relevant `--only` selection; - Redis when `REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`; - audit/log databases when either management flag is set; - backup engine plus daemon when `BACKUP_ENABLED`. The legacy path creates the database/role when `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` and no PG tier is configured. The PG path takes a pre-migration dump from the primary's direct port (never PgBouncer) when the run is not fresh and core is selected. The legacy path takes the dump after database provisioning. #### Pre-migration backup details `preMigrationBackup()` resolves the primary direct port (never PgBouncer) and the PG or legacy credentials, then builds `PGPASSWORD="" pg_dump -h -p -U -Fc > .dump`. `backupDatabase()` creates `/shared/backups`, chowns it to the SSH user, and runs the command on the **core host** as that user. The file is `pre-migrate-.dump`. No dump is taken on a fresh install. A failure aborts before migrations. `pg_dump` must already exist (the bootstrap package list omits `postgresql-client`), `PGPASSWORD` appears in the verbose remote command, and the dump is not automatically verified or restored. #### Backup daemon source deployment After `provisionBackupEngine()`, `deployBackupDaemon()`: - creates `/opt/pg-backup-daemon` owned by the SSH user; - rsyncs `deploy/backup-daemon` with `--delete`, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `test`, `*.log` and `.env`; - chowns the install directory to `pgbackup:pgbackup`; - ensures `/usr/local/bin/bun` exists; - runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` as `pgbackup`; - runs `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable pg-backup-daemon && systemctl restart pg-backup-daemon`. The systemd unit and `/etc/pg-backup/backup.env` are written by the provisioner, not by `deployBackupDaemon()`. If `BACKUP_ENABLED` is true but the plan has no backup host, the deploy warns and skips the daemon; validation normally prevents that. ### 3.6 Steps 6-10: service deployment The role order is fixed: | Step | Role | Title | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 6 | core | Deploy core-back to CORE_HOST | | 7 | fake-rails | Deploy fake-rails-back + fake-rails-front (only when enabled) | | 8 | admin | Deploy admin-back + admin-front | | 9 | merchant | Deploy merchant-back + merchant-front | | 10 | checkout | Deploy checkout-back + checkout-front | For each role, the pipeline skips excluded roles, collects units for that role (filtered by `--nodes`), splits them into batches of `--rolling-batch` or `ROLLING_BATCH_SIZE` (default 1), deploys each batch sequentially, then probes every unit in the batch. The first failure throws and later batches do not run. A `--nodes` filter that matches nothing skips the role. Units without a node id never match a node filter. ### 3.7 Per-service release procedure `deployService()`: 1. Creates the timestamped release and `shared/{certs,backups,pm2,data}` directories and chowns the remote tree. 2. Syncs the backend source with rsync, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `generated`, `test`, `certs`, `.certs`, `*.log` and `.env`; syncs the locally built frontend `dist` for edge roles and writes admin `runtime-config.js`. -3. Writes the host's certificate set and the 0600 `shared/.env`, then symlinks `.env` into the app directory. +3. Writes the host's certificate set and the 0600 per-node environment (`shared/.env` for a single node, `shared/.env.` for a multi-node tier), then symlinks it to `.env` in the release app directory. 4. Runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; for core also `bunx prisma generate`, `bun run migrate-deploy` and optional `db-seed`. 5. Switches `current` with `ln -sfn`, writes the inline PM2 ecosystem, runs `pm2 delete`, `pm2 start --update-env` and `pm2 save`. 6. Renders the Nginx sites for that role, symlinks them, removes the default site, runs `nginx -t` and reloads. 7. Prunes with `ls -1dt /releases/*/ | tail -n + | xargs -r rm -rf`. The PM2 config uses `pm2-compatible-start.js`, the `/usr/local/bin/bun` interpreter, the absolute release app directory as `cwd`, one fork instance, autorestart with 10 restarts, a 3-second delay and a 15-second kill timeout. There is no cluster mode and no connection draining. ### 3.8 Release layout ```text / ├── releases//{/,/dist/} ├── shared/{.env,certs/,backups/,pm2/,data/} └── current -> releases/ ``` The timestamp is generated once per run and reused across services and hosts. Releases are immutable; `current` is the only mutable pointer. ### 3.9 Step 11: seed When Fake Rails is enabled and core is selected: - `bun run seed-fake-rails` in `/current/core-back` when `SEED_FAKE_RAILS_BLUEPRINTS` is true, with a 30-minute timeout; - `bun run seed-synthetic-history` when `RUN_SYNTHETIC_HISTORY_SEED` is true, with a 60-minute timeout, and a log summary. The synthetic seed requires `IS_TEST_SERVER=true` and Fake Rails enabled at config validation. The step is skipped in dry-run, when Fake Rails is disabled, or when `--only` excludes core. ### 3.10 Step 12: verify `verifyDeployment()` collects: - every core node `/health` over mTLS from that core host (loopback); - every edge backend `/health` over loopback; - each edge host's `admin-back`, `merchant-back` and `checkout-back` client certificate against every derived core URL on its channel health endpoint; - public merchant/checkout vhosts from the host itself (admin LAN vhost skipped); - Fake Rails backend and vhost when enabled; - PostgreSQL primary/replicas with `pg_isready` and `psql SELECT 1`; - PgBouncer `SELECT 1` when enabled; - Redis `PING` with `REDISCLI_AUTH`; - audit/log `SELECT 1`; - backup-daemon `/health` over mTLS when configured. The run throws if any probe fails. With `--skip-verify` or `--dry-run`, the step is skipped and the deploy can report success without a live probe. ### 3.11 Step 13: prune Step 13 only logs: ```text Prune old releases kept the last release(s) per host ``` Actual pruning already happened inside each `deployService()` call. The guide's statements that pruning is step 13 or step 11 are historical/wrong. Because pruning is per service, a host with several services prunes each service's release tree separately. ### 3.12 Step 14: audit summary The final step prints: - short git commit, if `git` is available; - release timestamp; - topology and host count; - every host and its roles; - certificate expiry for every PKI certificate, unless dry-run. It then prints `Deployment complete.` There is no post-deploy state file and no automatic notification. ### 3.13 Dead PM2 templates `deploy/templates/pm2.core.config.cjs.tpl` and `deploy/templates/pm2.edge.config.cjs.tpl` exist in the repository but are not read by any code path. `deploy.ts` generates the ecosystem file inline in `pm2Ecosystem()`. Treat the templates as dead/deprecated. ## 4.
