 # Storage Provisioners
 
 ## 1. Purpose and scope
 
 This part documents the four modular storage provisioners invoked by the deployment pipeline:
 
 - `postgres18Provisioner.ts`: PostgreSQL 18 primary, replicas, replication slots, `pg_hba`, PgBouncer, tuning and journal partition cron;
 - `redisProvisioner.ts`: Redis cache/velocity nodes;
 - `auditAndLogDbProvisioner.ts`: append-only audit database and partitioned log database;
 - `backupEngineProvisioner.ts`: WAL-G/Barman archive engine, daemon environment/unit, schedules and S3/secondary target checks.
 
 It covers what is installed, what is written, what is not consumed (especially TLS/mTLS) and the operational consequences.
 
 It does not own the backup daemon runtime (`deploy.backup`), the host plan (`deploy.planner`), the firewall (`deploy.firewall`) or the pipeline ordering (`deploy.pipeline`).
 
 ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
 
 The storage plane is PostgreSQL 18 only. The design specifies:
 
 - a tuned primary with streaming replicas initialized by `pg_basebackup -R` and physical replication slots;
 - PgBouncer in transaction mode on the primary and replicas;
 - SCRAM authentication and TLS-only remote database connections;
 - Redis bound to the private LAN with a password and no public exposure;
 - an append-only audit database with a SHA-256 hash chain and immutable rows;
 - a monthly-partitioned log database with a retention function and cron;
 - WAL-G or Barman for continuous WAL archiving and full/delta backups, with an S3 primary and optional secondary vault;
 - journal-line partition maintenance on a daily cron;
 - storage client certificates for mTLS links.
 
 The code implements most of the topology, authentication and scheduling. The TLS/mTLS wiring is incomplete and is recorded explicitly below.
 
 ## 3. As-built architecture
 
 ### 3.1 PostgreSQL 18
 
-`bootstrapCommands()` installs `postgresql-${PG_VERSION}`, `postgresql-contrib-${PG_VERSION}` and `pgbouncer` with `apt-get`, enables PostgreSQL and PgBouncer (on the primary and on replicas that also run PgBouncer), and creates the data directory with owner `postgres`.
+`bootstrapCommands()` installs `postgresql-${PG_VERSION}`, `postgresql-contrib-${PG_VERSION}` and `pgbouncer` with `apt-get`, ensures the Debian cluster (`main` on 5432, or a named cluster on another port) exists, starts it, enables `postgresql@18-<cluster>` and PgBouncer where applicable, and creates the data directory with owner `postgres`.
 
 The version comes from `PG_VERSION` (default `18`). The schema allows any one- or two-digit major version; there is no runtime assertion that it is exactly 18.
 
-`postgresConfigSnippet()` writes `/etc/postgresql/<version>/main/conf.d/zz-pg-switch.conf` with `listen_addresses='*'`, 300 connections, 8 GB shared buffers, 24 GB effective cache, 32 MB work memory, 1 GB maintenance memory, `io_method='io_uring'`, `synchronous_commit=on`, `wal_level=replica`, 16 WAL senders/slots, 16 GB max WAL, `pg_stat_statements` and `track_io_timing=on`.
+`postgresConfigSnippet()` writes `/etc/postgresql/<version>/<cluster>/conf.d/zz-pg-switch.conf` (where `<cluster>` is `main`, `replica_<nodeId>`, `audit` or `log`) with `listen_addresses='*'`, 300 connections, 8 GB shared buffers, 24 GB effective cache, 32 MB work memory, 1 GB maintenance memory, `io_method='io_uring'`, `synchronous_commit=on`, `wal_level=replica`, 16 WAL senders/slots, 16 GB max WAL, `pg_stat_statements` and `track_io_timing=on`.
 
 The file contains no `ssl`, `ssl_cert_file`, `ssl_key_file`, `ssl_ca_file` or `ssl_crl_file` settings. The database listens on all interfaces and relies on UFW plus `pg_hba`.
 
 `primaryBootstrapSql()`:
 
 - creates the application role if absent, otherwise resets its password;
 - creates the application database owned by that role if absent;
 - creates the replication role with `REPLICATION LOGIN`, or resets its password;
 - creates one physical replication slot per replica using a sanitized node id;
 - emits a comment listing the intended `pg_hba` sources.
 
 `pgHbaSnippet()` writes `local ... peer`, loopback `host ... scram-sha-256`, and `hostssl` all/replication lines with `scram-sha-256` for every allowed source. There is no `clientcert=verify-full` and no `cert` auth method, so the generated `pg-client` certificate is not part of database authentication.
 
 The primary source list includes the primary itself, every replica, every core private IP, and the backup/audit/log node private IPs. The replica source list includes the primary and the backup nodes.
 
 The provisioner writes `pg_hba.conf`, applies the bootstrap SQL through `su - postgres`, restarts PostgreSQL, and installs `/etc/cron.d/pg-journal-partitions`:
 
 ```text
 30 1 * * * root su - postgres -c "psql -d <PG_DB_NAME> -c 'SELECT ensure_journal_line_partitions(18)'" >/var/log/pg-journal-partitions.log 2>&1
 ```
 
 The function `ensure_journal_line_partitions` must already exist from the core migrations. The same cron file is also written by the backup provisioner; the last writer wins with identical content.
 
 ### 3.2 Replicas and slots
 
 For each replica, `replicaCommands()`:
 
 - creates `/var/lib/postgresql` and writes `/var/lib/postgresql/.pgpass` with the replication credentials;
-- runs `pg_basebackup -h <primary> -p <port> -U <replicationUser> -D <dataDir> -Fp -Xs -P -R -S <slot>` only when the data directory has no `PG_VERSION`;
+- stops the empty cluster, replaces its data directory with `pg_basebackup -h <primary> -p <port> -U <replicationUser> -D <dataDir> -Fp -Xs -P -R -S <slot>`, writes the slot into `postgresql.auto.conf`, starts the cluster and enables its systemd unit;
 - ensures `primary_slot_name` in `postgresql.auto.conf`;
 - enables and starts PostgreSQL.
 
 The slots are created on the primary by `primaryBootstrapSql()`. Replication is asynchronous; `synchronous_commit=on` is local commit durability, not synchronous replication. There is no quorum or automatic failover.
 
 `pg_basebackup` and the replica `.pgpass` use the replication password. The `.pgpass` is created under `/var/lib/postgresql` with a restrictive umask.
 
 ### 3.3 PgBouncer
 
 When `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED=true`, PgBouncer is installed and configured on the primary and every replica. `/etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini` sets `listen_addr=0.0.0.0`, `listen_port=6432`, transaction pooling, `server_tls_sslmode=require`, 2000 client connections, pool size 50, reserve 10, 256 prepared statements, SCRAM auth and `/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt`. The userlist contains the application and replication users with plaintext passwords, mode 0600. PgBouncer is restarted after writing it.
 
 Important as-built facts:
 
 - There is no `[databases]` section. PgBouncer has no mapping from a client database name to a PostgreSQL host/port/database. A client connecting to `:6432` cannot be routed to the application database by this configuration.
 - `server_tls_sslmode = require` encrypts the PgBouncer-to-PostgreSQL leg but does not verify the server certificate (`verify-full` would) and supplies no client certificate.
 - There is no `client_tls_sslmode`, `client_tls_cert_file` or `client_tls_key_file`; clients are not required to present a certificate.
 - `listen_addr = 0.0.0.0` is protected by UFW only; the plan opens 6432 to core sources.
 
 The core environment points `PG_PRIMARY_PORT` and `DATABASE_REPLICA_URLS` at `PGBOUNCER_PORT` when the pooler is enabled. Because the generated PgBouncer has no database mapping, this is a deployment-breaking gap until a `[databases]` entry (or wildcard) is supplied.
 
 ### 3.4 Redis
 
 `redisProvisioner.ts` installs `redis-server`, enables it, and writes both `/etc/redis/redis.conf.d/zz-pg-switch.conf` and `/etc/redis/redis.conf` with a private-IP + loopback bind, `protected-mode yes`, the node port, `requirepass <REDIS_PASSWORD>`, `save 3600 1`, maxmemory/policy `allkeys-lru`, no append-only file and daemonize on. It runs `ufw allow` for core and backup sources and restarts Redis with `redis-cli PING`.
 
 There is no `tls-port`, `tls-cert-file`, `tls-key-file`, `tls-ca-cert-file` or `tls-auth-clients` setting. Redis traffic is plaintext inside the private network. The generated `redis-client` certificate is unused.
 
 ### 3.5 Audit database
 
 `auditAndLogDbProvisioner.ts` installs PostgreSQL on `AUDIT_DB_NODE` when `AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` is true, applies a minimal PostgreSQL config (`listen_addresses='*'`, `wal_level=replica`, senders/slots), writes a `pg_hba` restricted to core and backup sources, restarts PostgreSQL, creates the audit role/database, and applies:
 
 - `pg_trgm`;
 - `audit_records` with `seq_no` identity, UUID primary key, actor/action/entity fields, before/after JSON, `prev_hash`, `row_hash`;
 - entity, actor, BRIN and trigram GIN indexes;
 - `forbid_audit_mutation()` and `trg_audit_immutable` on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE;
 - least-privilege grants: `SELECT, INSERT` only for the audit writer, plus sequence usage and default privileges.
 
 The audit DDL is applied to the audit database. The `pg_hba` has the same `hostssl`-without-client-cert pattern as the core database.
 
 ### 3.6 Log database
 
 The log provisioner installs PostgreSQL on `LOG_DB_NODE` when `LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` is true and applies:
 
 - `attempt_step_logs` with a `(id, created_at)` primary key, partitioned by `RANGE (created_at)`;
 - `http_access_logs` with a `(id, created_at)` primary key, partitioned by `RANGE (created_at)`;
 - attempt/created indexes and BRIN indexes;
 - `ensure_log_partitions(months_ahead, retention_months)`, which creates missing monthly partitions and drops partitions older than the retention cutoff;
 - initial partitions six months ahead;
 - `GRANT SELECT, INSERT` only for the log writer;
 - `/etc/cron.d/pg-log-partitions` at `15 1 * * *` calling `ensure_log_partitions(6, <LOG_RETENTION_MONTHS>)`.
 
 The retention function only drops partitions whose names match the monthly suffix pattern; it never drops the default partition or non-monthly tables. The log database `pg_hba` is restricted to core and backup sources and has no client-certificate requirement.
 
 ### 3.7 Backup engine provisioner
 
 `provisionBackupEngine()` installs:
 
 - `barman`, `zstd`, `lz4`, `brotli`, `xz-utils`, `rclone`, `curl`, `ca-certificates`;
 - WAL-G when `BACKUP_ENGINE_MODE=wal-g`, by downloading `wal-g-pg-ubuntu-20.04-amd64` from the GitHub "latest" release and chmod +x;
 - the `pgbackup` system user and `/var/lib/pg-backup`, log and cert directories;
 - `/etc/pg-backup/backup.env` from `backupDaemonEnv()`;
 - `/etc/pg-backup/wal-g.env` for the core target;
 - the systemd unit and `/etc/cron.d/pg-backup`;
 - `/usr/local/bin/pg-backup-daemon-trigger` and `/usr/local/bin/pg-backup-restore-drill`;
 - Barman configuration and `.pgpass` in Barman mode;
 - target reachability checks.
 
 Archive configuration:
 
 - WAL-G: writes `/etc/pg-backup/wal-g-core.env` on the primary and sets `archive_mode=on`, `archive_command` to `wal-g wal-push %p` with the core prefix, `restore_command` to `wal-g wal-fetch`, and `archive_timeout=60s`; restarts PostgreSQL.
 - Barman: sets `wal_level=replica`, `archive_mode=off`, creates the `barman` slot and uses `barman-wal-archive <backupIp> <server> %p` from `streaming_archiver=on`. It writes `/etc/barman.conf` with a server section using the replication user, a `slot_name`, and `backup_method=postgres`.
 
 The same archive configuration is applied to the audit database when `AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` is true, with `archive_command` targeting the audit prefix/server.
 
 The provisioner also runs `verifyBackupTargetCommands()`:
 
-- `rclone lsd <BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_BUCKET> --max-depth 1`;
+- `curl -fsS <BACKUP_PRIMARY_S3_ENDPOINT>/minio/health/live`;
 - an SSH `true` to the secondary target when configured;
 - a non-empty encryption key check.
 
-The `rclone` check assumes the bucket string is a configured rclone remote or a path rclone understands; an S3 URL with no rclone configuration fails the deploy.
+The MinIO health check verifies the local S3-compatible endpoint without requiring an rclone remote configuration.
 
 The systemd unit runs `bun run src/index.ts` as `pgbackup` with `EnvironmentFile=/etc/pg-backup/backup.env`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`, and `ReadWritePaths` for the backup, log, catalog, cert, scratch and pgpass directories.
 
 ## 4. Contracts and invariants
 
 - PostgreSQL 18 is the only runtime database; `DB_ENGINE` is restricted to `postgresql`.
 - Application and replication roles use SCRAM passwords; replication slots are physical.
 - Replicas are initialized only when the data directory is empty.
 - Remote database connections use `hostssl` rules; loopback uses SCRAM without TLS.
 - The audit table is append-only at the trigger and grant level.
 - Log partitions are monthly; retention only affects matching monthly partitions.
 - Redis is bound to the private IP plus loopback and requires a password.
 - No storage provisioner writes database credentials to an edge host.
 - The journal partition cron is installed on the primary and must call an existing database function.
 - Backup archiving is configured on the primary/audit database, not on replicas.
 
 ## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
 
 ### Key configuration
 
 | Area | Keys |
 | :--- | :--- |
 | PostgreSQL | `PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `PG_VERSION`, `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `PG_SSH_*`, `PG_DB_*`, `PG_REPLICATION_*`, `PG_DATA_DIR`, `PG_AUDIT_DATA_DIR` |

-- `/etc/postgresql/<version>/main/conf.d/zz-pg-switch.conf`

 ## 7. Status and deviations
 
 ### Implemented
 
 - PostgreSQL 18 installation and tuning.
 - Application/replication roles, physical slots and `pg_basebackup -R` replicas.
 - SCRAM `pg_hba` with `hostssl` for remote sources.
 - PgBouncer installation and transaction-mode settings.

 - Audit hash-chain table, immutability trigger and append-only grants.
 - Log tables, monthly partitions, retention function and cron.
 - WAL-G/Barman installation, archive/restore commands, daemon environment/unit, backups schedule and target checks.
 - Journal and log partition cron entries.
 - Storage health probes.
 
 ### Partial
 
 - TLS is required for remote PostgreSQL connections by `hostssl`, but the provisioner does not configure the server certificate or a client-certificate requirement.
 - PgBouncer is installed but has no `[databases]` mapping.

 # Health Verification, Rollback and Recovery
 
 ## 1. Purpose and scope
 
 This part documents the end-to-end verification performed by the deploy engine, the release layout used for rollback, the rollback procedure and its limits, common failure modes and the security constraints around recovery.
 
 It does not own the application health payloads, the storage provisioners or the backup daemon's internal drill. It records how deployment observes them and what an operator can safely do when something fails.
 
 ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
 
 The design requires verification stronger than "the process is running":
 
 - every core node answers `/health` over mTLS;
 - every edge host completes a mutually authenticated TLS 1.3 handshake with a core node on its own channel;
 - every edge backend and public vhost answers;
 - PostgreSQL primary/replicas, PgBouncer, Redis, audit/log databases and the backup daemon are reachable;
 - a failed rolling batch stops the deploy, leaving the previous release on disk for rollback;
 - releases are immutable and `current` is a symlink, so rollback is a pointer change;
 - recovery from a bad deploy is possible without rebuilding from scratch.
 
 The design describes zero-downtime rolling updates. The code provides rolling batches with health gates but not connection draining or automatic compensation.
 
 ## 3. As-built architecture
 
 ### 3.1 Core health
 
 `GET /health` in `core-back/index.ts`:
 
 - is reachable without authentication (but the TLS listener still requires a client certificate);
 - reads the background-job queue health when workers are enabled;
 - returns `msg: "OK"`, `status: "ok"` when workers are enabled, the queue is reachable and the oldest job is below the threshold;
 - returns `msg: "DEGRADED"`, `status: "degraded"` when workers are disabled, the queue cannot be inspected, or the oldest queued job exceeds the threshold;
 - stays reachable when the database cannot be read, with `queue.degraded=true` and `QUEUE_HEALTH_UNAVAILABLE`.
 
 `probeCoreHealth()` and `probeCoreService()` run on the core host and use `curl` with the CA and the core certificate as both server and client material. They pass when the body contains `"msg":"OK"` or the literal `OK`. A degraded core fails the probe.
 
 The core certificate also carries clientAuth so this loopback probe can present it.
 
 ### 3.2 Edge health
 
 Each edge `GET /health` is unauthenticated and returns `{ status: "ok", service, uptime }`. It does not query core, the database or any dependency.
 
 `probeEdgeService()` and `probeEdgeBackend()` call this endpoint over `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health` with a 10-second timeout. They pass on `"status":"ok"` or the literal `ok`.
 
 A running edge with a broken core pool therefore passes its local health check; core/SAN/certificate problems are caught only by the cross-host probe or final verification, so the rolling batch gate for edges is liveness, not readiness.
 
 ### 3.3 Edge-to-core mTLS
 
 `probeEdgeToCore()` runs on each edge host with that host's own client certificate:
 
 - for each of `admin`, `merchant`, `checkout` present on the host;
 - for every derived core URL;
 - calls `<coreUrl>/internal/<channel>/health` with `--cacert`, `--cert` and `--key`.
 
 The core channel health routes return `{ status: "ok", channel: "<channel>" }` after the CN guard. The probe passes on `ok` or the channel marker.
 
 This is the critical cross-host check. It verifies:
 
 - DNS/route/reachability to every core node;
 - TLS 1.3 handshake and CA trust;
 - the server SAN contains the core private IP;
 - the client certificate is accepted;
 - the CN matches the channel;
 - the core process is up.
 
 It does not verify business authorization, database writes or a specific gateway flow.
 
 ### 3.4 Public and Fake Rails vhosts
 
 `probePublicVhost()` runs on the edge host and probes every Nginx site except the admin LAN site:
 
 - scheme from the site's `ssl` flag;
 - `-k` for self-signed certificates;
 - `/health` first, then `/` with an HTTP status fallback;
 - passes when any non-empty body is returned.
 
 Fake Rails gets backend and vhost `/health` probes, with `-k` when SSL is enabled. The admin LAN vhost is covered by the edge backend probe; the deploy does not probe it through Nginx.
 
 ### 3.5 Storage and backup probes
 
 `probeStorage()` includes:
 
 | Target | Probe |
 | :--- | :--- |
 | PostgreSQL primary | `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p <port>` and `psql SELECT 1` with the application user/password. |
 | PostgreSQL replicas | Same two probes per replica. |
 | PgBouncer | `psql SELECT 1` on `PGBOUNCER_PORT` with the application user/password. |
 | Redis | `REDISCLI_AUTH=<password> redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p <port> PING`, expecting `PONG`. |
 | Audit DB | `psql SELECT 1` with the audit user/password. |
 | Log DB | `psql SELECT 1` with the log user/password. |
 | Backup daemon | HTTPS `/health` with the CA and the `backup-daemon` certificate/key, expecting `"status":"ok"` or `ok`. |
 
 The backup probe uses the daemon's server certificate (which also has clientAuth) rather than `backup-client`. It depends on the daemon being able to read its own 0600 key; if the key is root-owned and the daemon runs as `pgbackup`, the probe fails.
 
 ### 3.6 Verification aggregation
 
 `verifyDeployment()`:
 
 - probes every core node;
 - probes each Fake Rails host;
 - for each edge host, probes the edge backends, the edge-to-core handshake for every core URL and the public vhosts;
 - appends storage probes;
 - returns `{ ok, results }`.
 
 `deploy.ts` prints `PASS`/`FAIL` per result and throws if any result fails. The error message says the previous release is still on disk. It does not switch back automatically.
 
 `--skip-verify` and `--dry-run` skip the step.
 
 ### 3.7 Rolling batch gates
 
 For steps 6-10, after deploying every unit in a batch:
 
 - core units use `probeCoreService()`: loopback mTLS `/health` on that service port;
 - edge units use `probeEdgeService()`: loopback HTTP `/health`.
 
 A failed probe throws immediately. The cross-host mTLS, public vhost and storage checks run only in step 12 after all roles are deployed.
 
 This means a batch can be declared healthy while the edge cannot reach core, or while the core cannot reach the database. The final verification is the real gate.
 
 ### 3.8 Release layout
 
 ```text
 <REMOTE_DIR>/
 ├── releases/<TIMESTAMP>/
 │   ├── <backend>/            # source, dependencies, .env symlink
 │   └── <front>/dist/         # edge hosts
 ├── shared/
 │   ├── .env                  # 0600
 │   ├── certs/
 │   ├── backups/
 │   ├── pm2/<service>.config.cjs
 │   └── data/
 └── current -> releases/<TIMESTAMP>
 ```
 
 - Releases are immutable.
 - `current` is the only release pointer.
 - Nginx static roots use `<remote>/current/<front>/dist`.
 - The inline PM2 ecosystem uses an **absolute** `cwd` and script path inside `<releaseDir>`, not the `current` symlink.
 - Environment and certificate paths in the service env are absolute after `absoluteEnv()`.
 
 The PM2 detail matters for rollback: changing `current` changes Nginx static assets immediately, but a `pm2 restart <name>` reuses the absolute script/cwd from the process's original start. It does not automatically follow the new symlink.
 
 ## 4. Contracts and invariants
 
 - Verification runs after all deployments and before the deploy is declared successful.
 - Any failed probe aborts the run with a non-zero exit.
 - A core `/health` response of `DEGRADED` is a failure.
 - Edge `/health` success is not a readiness guarantee for core connectivity.
 - A batch is not a full verification; step 12 is.
 - `KEEP_RELEASES` controls how many release directories remain; pruning happens inside `deployService`.
 - Rollback does not revert database migrations or restore the pre-migration dump.
 
 ## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
 
 ### Verification commands
 
 - `curl --cacert ... --cert ... --key ... https://127.0.0.1:<corePort>/health`
 - `curl http://127.0.0.1:<edgePort>/health`
 - `curl ... https://<coreIp>:<corePort>/internal/<channel>/health`
 - `curl -k https://127.0.0.1:<nginxPort>/health` for self-signed public vhosts
 - `pg_isready`, `psql SELECT 1`, `redis-cli PING`
 
 ### Release paths
 
 | Role | Default remote directory |
 | :--- | :--- |
 | core | `/var/www/pg-core` |
 | admin | `/var/www/pg-admin` |
 | merchant | `/var/www/pg-merchant` |
 | checkout | `/var/www/pg-checkout` |
 | Fake Rails | `/var/www/pg-fake-rails` |
 
 ### Flags
 
 | Flag | Effect on verification/recovery |
 | :--- | :--- |
 | `--skip-verify` | Skips step 12. |
 | `--dry-run` | Prints probes as commands, executes none. |
 | `--keep=<n>` | Changes how many releases remain for rollback. |
 | `--fresh` | Bootstraps hosts; no pre-migration dump. |
 
 ## 6. Operational usage
 
 ### Normal verification
 
 Run the deploy without `--skip-verify`. The output lists every PASS/FAIL with host and check. Treat any FAIL as a release blocker even if the process started.
 
 ### Manual rollback of one host
 
 1. List releases:
 
 ```bash
 ssh <host>
 ls -1dt /var/www/pg-<role>/releases/*/
 ```
 
-2. Choose the previous timestamp and confirm its `shared` environment is compatible. The release-specific app directory has an `.env` symlink to `<remote>/shared/.env`; the shared env is current, not historical. If the env changed, the old code may not match it.
+2. Choose the previous timestamp and confirm its `shared` environment is compatible. The release-specific app directory has an `.env` symlink to `<remote>/shared/.env` (or `shared/.env.<nodeId>` on a multi-node tier); the shared env is current, not historical. If the env changed, the old code may not match it.
 
 3. Stop and restart the service from the target release, not with `pm2 restart`:
 
 ```bash
 TARGET=/var/www/pg-<role>/releases/<previous>
 ln -sfn "$TARGET" /var/www/pg-<role>/current
 "$HOME/.bun/bin/pm2" delete <service> || true
 cd "$TARGET/<backend>"
 PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH" pm2 start pm2-compatible-start.js   --name <service> --interpreter /usr/local/bin/bun --update-env
 "$HOME/.bun/bin/pm2" save
 ```
 
 The shared PM2 config is regenerated on every deploy and points at the latest release. A plain `pm2 restart` is not sufficient because it reuses the absolute path of the currently running release. Re-running the deploy from the previous commit is the cleanest whole-role rollback.
 
 4. Nginx static files follow `current` immediately; verify the vhost after the switch.
 
 5. Re-run verification for that host or role.
 
 ### Rollback of the whole deployment
 
 The reliable path is to check out the previous commit and re-run `./deploy/deploy.sh --update --only=<roles>`. Releases are immutable, but the shared `.env`, PM2 config and Nginx config are rewritten by the new run.
 
 ### Database recovery
 
 The pre-migration dump is a `pg_dump -Fc` file in `<CORE_REMOTE_DIR>/shared/backups/pre-migrate-<timestamp>.dump`. It is not restored automatically. Recovery requires an operator decision, a target database and a compatible schema. Migrations are forward-only; restoring an old code release against a migrated schema can fail.
 
 ### Backup drill recovery
 
 Use the backup daemon's `/v1/drills/run` or the admin backup control to verify a restore. The drill restores into scratch directories and removes them; it does not restore the live database.
 
 ### Common failures
 
 | Symptom | Likely cause |
 | :--- | :--- |
 | `SSH key ... does not exist` | The `*_SSH_KEY_PATH` is wrong or missing on the workstation. |
 | `core /health (mTLS) FAIL` | Core did not start, DB credentials are wrong, or workers/queue are degraded. |
 | `mTLS -> core /internal/... FAIL` | Wrong client CN/cert, core SAN missing the target IP, or core down. |
 | `backup-daemon /health FAIL` | Certificate ownership, missing S3/Barman prerequisite, or daemon config. |
 | Pre-migration dump fails | `pg_dump` is absent on the core host or the primary is unreachable. |
 | PgBouncer connection fails | No `[databases]` mapping in the generated `pgbouncer.ini`. |
 
 ### Security notes
 
 - Keep `deploy.env` at 0600 and `deploy/.certs` private; the CA key never leaves the workstation. Secrets are streamed over SSH stdin, but the pre-migration `PGPASSWORD` is embedded in the verbose command and may appear in logs.
 - The core port is private and mTLS-only; edge hosts never receive `DATABASE_URL` or `KMS_MASTER_KEY`.
 - Protect the edge host and make the backup key readable by `pgbackup`.
 - The deploy's `--skip-verify` is not a security control and should not be used for production acceptance.
 
 ## 7. Status and deviations
 
 ### Implemented
 
 - Core loopback mTLS health.
 - Edge local health.
 - Edge-to-core mTLS channel health across every core URL.
 - Public merchant/checkout vhost probes.
 - Fake Rails backend and vhost probes.
 - PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, Redis, audit/log and backup-daemon probes.
 - Batch-level health gate and final fail-fast verification.
 - Immutable release layout and `current` pointer.
 - Pre-migration dump artifact.
 
 ### Partial
 
 - Batch gates are liveness-only for edges and do not test cross-host mTLS.
 - The guide's symlink + `pm2 restart` rollback is incomplete for backend processes.
 
 ### Missing / deferred
 
 - Automatic rollback on a failed batch or failed verification.
 - Connection draining and a zero-downtime single-node switch.
 - Blue/green or canary routing.
 - Database down-migrations or an automated point-in-time restore path.
 - Post-deploy alerting or a health history.
 
 ### Known bugs, risks and limits
 
 - A single-node service has a restart gap; a core restart can make all edges fail for the cooldown window.
 - A failed verification leaves the new release as `current` on every deployed host.
 - `--skip-verify` can report success with a broken core/edge path.
 - Shared `.env` is not versioned per release; backup probe failures can be cert ownership.
 
 ## 8. Verification and tests
 
 ```bash
 cd deploy && bun run typecheck && bun test test/healthVerifierScale.test.ts test/pipeline.test.ts test/rollingDeploy.test.ts
 cd deploy/backup-daemon && bun test test/restoreDrillRunner.test.ts
 ```
 
 Covered:
 
 - probe aggregation at scale;
 - pipeline presence and daemon deployment ordering;
 - rolling batch splitting;
 - restore drill invariant checks and cleanup.
 
 Not covered: a real edge-to-core handshake, Nginx reload/vhost probe, PostgreSQL/PgBouncer/Redis probe, PM2 rollback or live backup-daemon mTLS probe.

 # Testing Strategy
 
 ## 1. Purpose and scope
 
 This part defines how the monorepo is verified: the test philosophy, the gate progression, database and Redis expectations, the zero-tautology rule, and which suites currently skip, mock or fail to exist.
 
 It does not list every test file or count (see `testing.suites`), the fixture and live-stack wiring (see `testing.fixtures`) or the benchmark gates (see `testing.benchmarks`). Per-workspace test evidence is repeated in each workspace part.
 
 ## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)
 
 The exhaustive test plan was written to prevent a small happy-path suite from missing intersection defects: rounding remainders, confirmation races, SSRF notations, JSX binding failures and seeded historical attempts that fail when an operator clicks Inquire or Refund.
 
 Its non-negotiable rules are:
 
 1. **Zero-tautology.** Every test must invoke the real production module, real Express router, real PostgreSQL constraint or rendered Vue DOM. `expect(true).toBe(true)` and mock-against-mock tests are forbidden.
 2. **Combinatorial and property-based generation.** Use data-driven Cartesian products and a seeded PRNG so permutations are named and reproducible.
 3. **Continuous double-entry invariant.** Every database suite runs the ledger invariant after writes and requires `drift === "0.0000"`.
 4. **Fail-fast gate progression.** Implement and pass suites `T-EX-01` through `T-EX-11` in order; fix production defects before advancing.
 5. **Fail loudly when the environment is absent.** A suite that needs PostgreSQL, Redis or a live host either skips with a named reason or fails; it must not silently pass against a stub.
 
 The plan targets 38,500 or more assertions across eleven suites, plus a unified runner.
 
 ## 3. As-built architecture
 
 ### 3.1 Test roots
 
 | Root | Runner | Primary scope |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `core-back/test` | `bun test` | Unit, route, engine, ledger, storage, exhaustive |
 | `admin-back/test` | `bun test` | Edge contract, mTLS, env isolation, admin surface |
 | `merchant-back/test` | `bun test` | Edge contract, forwarding, KYB/external surface |
 | `checkout-back/test` | `bun test` | Zero-trust checkout, mTLS, env isolation |
 | `fake-rails-back/test` | `bun test` | Real Express app over SQLite |
 | `deploy/test` | `bun test` | Config, host planning, PKI, firewall, pipeline |
 | `deploy/backup-daemon/test` | `bun test` | Backup engine, catalog, scheduler, restore drill |
 | `tests/e2e` | Playwright | Portal geometry, auth, dialogs, mocked API surface |
 | `tests/e2e-live` | Playwright | Deployed-stack smoke journeys |
 | `tests/unit` | Vitest | Frontend utility and authority helpers |
 
 `tests/run-playwright.sh` is the Playwright wrapper used by local runs. `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` is the master gate runner and forces one Bun worker for database suites.
 
 ### 3.2 The zero-tautology rule in practice
 
 The core exhaustive suites are structurally honest about production code:
 
 - `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts` drives real Prisma clients, real schema files and real production services. It says explicitly that it only provisions fixtures and reads metadata.
 - `_dbFactory.ts` builds rows from the real `schema.prisma` and live catalog; it does not replace constraints.
 - Suite 01 reads `information_schema`, `pg_catalog`, `pg_indexes` and real constraint metadata.
 - Suite 02 invokes `LedgerPoster.validateTemplate` and real `buildLedgerTemplate` output.
 - Suite 03 invokes the real transform, canonicalisation, signing and Vault code.
 - Suite 04 invokes `DynamicRailEngine` through `_engineHarness.ts`, not the live fake-rails HTTP tier.
 - Suite 05 drives real authority/session helpers and the real list-query parser.
 - Suite 06 uses live PostgreSQL concurrency primitives.
 - Suite 07 uses real parsers, KYB sniffers, AML rules and go-live validators.
 - Suite 08 uses real SSRF/URL/response-hardening helpers.
 
 The UI and edge tests are weaker:
 
 - `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` `mockApi()` fulfills every `/api/v1/**` call with `{}` or a small fixture. The exhaustive surface tests only assert rendering, layout, direction and theme.
 - Auth tests intercept the login endpoint and return a fixture session; they assert the shape of the posted body, not a real login.
 - The fake-rails surface test mocks every `/portal-api/**` and only visits `/login`.
 - `tests/unit` tests real frontend utility functions, not the full pages.
 
 These are useful regression tests, but they do not satisfy the design's zero-tautology claim for UI behaviour.
 
 ### 3.3 Gate progression
 
 `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` implements this sequence:
 
 | Gate | Command target | Notes |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `T-EX-01` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/01-schema` | Live PostgreSQL required for most tests |
 | `T-EX-02` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/02-ledger` | Some tests are pure; checkpoints need PostgreSQL |
 | `T-EX-03` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/03-transforms-crypto` | Pure |
 | `T-EX-04` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/04-rail-engine` | Pure engine harness |
 | `T-EX-05` | core plus all edge backends plus fake rails plus deploy | Mixed Bun suites |
 | `T-EX-06` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/06-concurrency` | Live PostgreSQL |
 | `T-EX-07` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/07-workflows` | Mostly pure |
 | `T-EX-08` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/08-security-edge` | Pure |
 | `T-EX-09` | `core-back/test/storage-engine`, `test/backup-admin`, backup daemon | There is no `09-storage-backup` directory |
 | `T-EX-09b` | `tests` unit plus exhaustive Playwright | Mocked UI |
 | `T-EX-10` | `10-seeder-and-deploy` plus optional cross-service journeys | Journeys skip without `E2E_LIVE=1` |
 | Final | `core-back bun test` | Full regression |
 
 The design's numbering differs from the runner: the runner calls the UI matrix `T-EX-09b` and the seeder/deploy suite `T-EX-10`, while the design calls them Suite 10 and Suite 11.
 
 ### 3.4 Database provisioning
 
 There is no single test database configuration. The suites use these variables:
 
 | Variable | Default | Used by |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | `DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/payment_gateway_monolith_test` | `test/setup.ts`, storage helpers, postgres payment test |
 | `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | fallback | Postgres payment test, exhaustive harness fallback |
 | `EXHAUSTIVE_DATABASE_URL` | fallback to `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | Exhaustive harness |
 | `STORAGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | fallback to `DATABASE_URL` | Storage-engine helpers |
 | `STORAGE_TEST_REDIS_URL` | `redis://127.0.0.1:56379` | Cache/velocity and performance |
 | `REDIS_URL` | `redis://127.0.0.1:56379` | Storage performance and production adapters |
 
 The expected local server is PostgreSQL 18 on port 55432 and Redis on 56379, not the default service ports. The test database must already be migrated (`bun run migrate-deploy`) before the DB-backed suites run. `_harness.ts` uses a dedicated Prisma client so it does not share the cached application client. The storage helpers create dedicated schemas or sandboxes with `search_path` so files can run in parallel.
 
 `bun test --parallel=1` is mandatory for the database suites in the runner because they share one database and the invariant hook.
 
 ### 3.5 Double-entry invariant
 
 `_harness.ts` exposes `verifyInvariant()` and `assertZeroDrift()`, which wrap the production `InvariantVerifier`. Suite 02 and the storage write-path suites use it after batches. A non-zero drift throws with left/right sides and drift printed.
 
 The invariant hook is not applied to every file that touches the database. The runner enforces one worker, but not a universal `afterEach` hook.
 
 ### 3.6 Skipping behaviour
 
 Current named skips:
 
 - `describeDatabase` becomes `describe.skip` when `SELECT 1` fails against the storage database.
 - `describeRedis` becomes `describe.skip` when the Redis connection or `PING` fails.
 - Storage files register a `test.skip("... requires the live database")` placeholder so a skipped file is still visible.
 - `core-back/test/e2e/postgres-payment.test.ts` uses `test.skipIf(!reachable)` for every payment test.
 - `write-path.integration.test.ts`, `uow.test.ts`, `ledger-shards.test.ts`, `audit-chain.test.ts`, `outbox-workers.test.ts`, `engine-factory.test.ts` and `performance/*.test.ts` have explicit skips.
 - `tests/e2e/exhaustive/full-platform-lifecycle-journeys.spec.ts` skips unless `E2E_LIVE=1`.
 - The link-journey test also skips unless `E2E_LINK_KEY` is set.
 - `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts` has no skip guard; it fails if the deployed host is unreachable.
 
 No suite currently sets a CI fail-on-skip policy. A run can be green with most DB or live coverage skipped.
 
 ### 3.7 Mocked surfaces
 
 | Surface | Mocking approach | Consequence |
 | :--- | :--- | :--- |
 | Admin UI | `mockApi()` intercepts every `/api/v1/**` call | No real permissions, validation or data flow |
 | Merchant UI | Same | Same |
 | Checkout UI | Route intercepts `/api/v1/pay/**` | No real payment state machine |
 | Fake-rails UI | Route intercepts `/portal-api/**` and `/hosted/**` | Only login geometry is tested |
 | Login flows | Route intercept returns fixture session | Body-shape assertions only |
 | Edge BFF tests | Real Express routers with fake core clients in places | Contract coverage, not live mTLS |
 | Engine suite 04 | In-process harness with scripted step results | Deterministic and broad, not live fake-rails |
 | Seeder safety | Fake Prisma objects and stubbed handshake | Gate logic only |
 
 ## 4. Contracts and invariants
 
 1. **A test that asserts only on a stub is not acceptance evidence.** Behaviour claims need a real module or live service.
 2. **A skipped DB suite is not a passing DB suite.** Reports must name the skip reason.
 3. **The test database is disposable.** Tests must not depend on rows left by another file; use unique references and clean up.
 4. **Money invariants are checked after database writes.** Any suite that posts ledger entries must verify zero drift.
 5. **Seeded PRNGs must be fixed and named.** A failure must be reproducible from the printed seed.
 6. **Live credentials belong in the environment, not in source.** This invariant is currently violated by `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts`.
 7. **The runner must fail when a required gate fails.** It currently does so for command failures, but not for skips.
 
 ## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface
 
 - Runner: `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh`.
 - Playwright wrapper: `tests/run-playwright.sh`.
 - Playwright configs: `tests/playwright.config.ts`, `playwright.exhaustive.config.ts`, `playwright.live.config.ts`.
 - Vitest config: `tests/vitest.config.ts`.
 - Core setup: `core-back/test/setup.ts`.
 - Exhaustive harness: `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts`, `_dbFactory.ts`.
 - Storage helpers: `core-back/test/storage-engine/helpers/db.ts`.
 - E2E fixture: `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts`.
 
 ## 6. Operational usage
 
 ```bash
 # Core unit and integration
 cd core-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
 
 # Exhaustive gates
 ./scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh
 
 # Playwright mocked UI
 cd tests && bun run test
 
 # Deployed-stack live smoke
 cd tests && bun run test:live
 
 # With a local test database
 export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/payment_gateway_monolith_test
 export STORAGE_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:56379
 ./scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh
 ```
 
 Report skipped suites explicitly. A run without PostgreSQL 18 and Redis is not evidence for any DB or storage claim.
 
 ## 7. Status and deviations
 
 ### Implemented
 
 - Core exhaustive suites 01-08 and 10 with real production modules.
 - Live schema, constraint and query-plan checks.
 - Deterministic PRNGs and broad combinatorial matrices.
 - Storage-engine, backup-control and backup-daemon suites.
 - Edge BFF contract suites.
 - Mocked Playwright surface walkers for four portals.
 - A single master runner.
 
 ### Partial
 
 - Suite 09 exists only as storage-engine/backup commands, not an exhaustive directory.
 - UI coverage is geometry-heavy and API-mocked.
 - Live journeys are opt-in and require a seeded link.
 - The invariant hook is not universal.
 - The claimed assertion volume is not present.
 
 ### Missing / deferred
 
 - A fail-on-skip CI mode.
 - A real browser E2E journey through checkout, fake rails and admin without mocks.
 - A restored-database drill in CI.
 - A deep-search latency and relevance suite.
 - A seeder volume/runtime benchmark.
 - A consistency check that every suite in the design exists.
 
 ### Known bugs / risks
 
 - **Documentation bug:** the plan claims 38,500+ assertions; the actual literal declaration count is about 1,807.
 - **Coverage gap:** suite numbering in the runner differs from the plan.
 - **Security risk:** live credentials are hard-coded as defaults in `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts`.
 - **False-green risk:** database and live suites can skip while the runner still reports success.
 
 ## 8. Verification and tests
 
 This part is verified by inspecting the runner, configs and suite files. It has no tests of its own. The relevant commands are listed in section 6.
 
 - The master runner and configs exist and are syntactically valid.
 - The suites referenced by the runner exist except `core-back/test/exhaustive/09-storage-backup`.
 - The claims in this part are derived from the working tree, not from a test run.

+# Two-Machine Multi-Topology Matrix
+
+## 1. Purpose and scope
+
+This part owns the executable two-machine lab: SSH/bootstrap, MinIO S3 and SSH vault provisioning, topology config generation for T1–T8, teardown, the 11 verification gates, the stress workload, the self-healing retry loop and the certification report.
+
+It does not own the production deploy engine (`07-deploy`), the storage adapters (`01-core-back/06-storage-engine.md`) or the ledger invariant (`01-core-back/03-ledger.md`).
+
+## 2. Design intent
+
+The historical plan requires eight production topology permutations across `HOST_A` and `HOST_B`:
+
+| ID | Shape |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| T1 | Single-host multi-node density, co-located PostgreSQL/Redis/audit/log, WAL-G |
+| T2 | Compute on A / storage on B, Barman on A |
+| T3 | Primary on A, replica + Redis + audit/log on B, WAL-G |
+| T4 | Primary on B, local + remote replicas, Redis/audit/log on A, Barman on A |
+| T5 | Public checkout/merchant DMZ on B, private core/DB/Redis on A, UFW penetration checks |
+| T6 | Symmetric mesh: 4 core, 4 checkout, 4 merchant, 2 admin, 2 replicas, 120k seed |
+| T7 | Live scale-out/scale-in under 500 TPS |
+| T8 | Chaos: core/replica/Redis/log-DB kills and full primary PITR |
+
+Every topology runs the same 11 gates: provisioning/mTLS/UFW, replica routing and LSN RYOW, Fake Rails/seeder invariants, 500+ TPS checkout/ledger stress, cross-node SSE/POS, concurrent workers, audit immutability/hash chain, log-DB outage, search/pagination, backup/PITR, and chaos/failover.
+
+## 3. As-built architecture
+
+### 3.1 Bootstrap and lab services
+
+`deploy/test-matrix/hosts.ts`:
+
+- discovers `HOST_A_LAN_IP` with `ip -4 route get 10.209.250.205`;
+- creates `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_lab_matrix`, authorizes it on `HOST_A` and `HOST_B` (`salem@10.209.250.205`, password `1234`);
+- creates a separate `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_peer` on `HOST_B` and authorizes it on `HOST_A` for Barman/`pg_basebackup`;
+- installs/launches MinIO on `HOST_B:9000` with bucket `pg-backups-test`;
+- creates the SSH vault directories on both hosts;
+- writes `/etc/pg-lab-matrix`, the marker that lets teardown know the host is disposable lab hardware.
+
+### 3.2 Topology generation
+
+`deploy/test-matrix/topologies.ts` builds the eight configs. It uses the real node grammar (`nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`), sets `STORAGE_SHARD_COUNT` to 16 or 32, sets `SYNTHETIC_SEED_PROFILE`, and emits `FAKE_RAILS_NODE` plus a reachable `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` for every topology.
+
+`generateTopologyConfigs.ts` writes `deploy/test-matrix/configs/deploy.T1.env` … `deploy.T8.env` with mode `0600`. `deploy/test/testMatrix.test.ts` validates all eight through the real Zod schema.
+
+### 3.3 Multi-instance deploy support
+
+The matrix depends on the deploy engine supporting several instances of one tier on one host:
+
+- PM2 names are node-suffixed (`pg-core-back-core-1`, `pg-core-back-core-2`);
+- each node has `shared/.env.<nodeId>` and its own `.env` symlink;
+- each node has `releases/<nodeId>/<timestamp>` and `current-<nodeId>`;
+- Nginx renders `upstream` blocks with `least_conn` and `max_fails=2 fail_timeout=3s` over all local and remote nodes;
+- edge backends bind the node private IP so a remote Nginx can reach them;
+- PostgreSQL roles use independent Debian clusters (`main`, `replica_<nodeId>`, `audit`, `log`) with their own data directory, config, HBA and systemd unit.
+
+### 3.4 Runner and self-healing loop
+
+`runAllTopologiesAndHeal.ts`:
+
+1. bootstraps the lab and writes all eight configs;
+2. tears down lab-owned PM2 apps, vhosts, release trees and PostgreSQL clusters;
+3. deploys with `deploy/deploy.ts --fresh`;
+4. runs all 11 gates in order;
+5. on failure, captures PM2 logs and service journals, tears down and retries once;
+6. writes `deploy/test-matrix/TOPOLOGY_CERTIFICATION_REPORT.md`.
+
+The runner never stops at the first failed topology; it records the failure and continues to the next configured topology.
+
+## 4. Contracts and invariants
+
+1. The lab is disposable. Teardown only drops clusters when `/etc/pg-lab-matrix` exists.
+2. Secrets stay in generated `0600` config files and are redacted from the report.
+3. A topology is certified only when all 11 gates pass.
+4. Every gate that writes money must finish with zero double-entry drift and `gl_account_shards == journal_lines`.
+5. The audit hash chain is computed by the PostgreSQL trigger under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(994001)`, not by competing Node processes.
+
+## 5. Verification
+
+```bash
+cd deploy
+bun test ./test/testMatrix.test.ts
+bun run test-matrix:bootstrap
+bun run test-matrix --topologies=T1,T2
+```
+
+Live certification requires `HOST_B` reachable and root/sudo on both hosts. The environment used during implementation could not reach `10.209.250.205`, so only config generation, schema validation and unit tests were executed.
+
+## 6. Known gaps
+
+- Live T1–T8 execution is pending lab availability.
+- Gate 4's concurrent webhook/confirm race uses the checkout API but does not yet assert the exact single-ledger-row count through a direct query.
+- Gate 10 polls the admin overview for backup completion; the daemon's own `/v1/runs` endpoint is not used directly.
+- Gate 11's full primary wipe/PITR restore is orchestration code only; it must be run on the lab.

// deploy/test-matrix/generateTopologyConfigs.ts
import type { LabHostsConfig } from './bootstrapTwoMachineLab';

export interface TopologyMatrixSpec {

  name: string;
  description: string;
  glShardCount: 16 | 32;
  seedProfile: 'COMPACT' | 'STANDARD';
  backupMode: 'wal-g' | 'barman';
  buildEnv: (lab: LabHostsConfig) => Record<string, string>;
}

export function buildAllTopologySpecs(): TopologyMatrixSpec[] {

    DEPLOY_MODE: 'fresh',

## 6. Mandatory Autonomous "Test -> Diagnose -> Fix -> Re-Verify" Self-Healing Loop for OpenCode

When OpenCode runs the 8-topology test matrix, **stopping on an error and reporting failure to the user is forbidden**. OpenCode must follow this autonomous self-healing loop for every gate in `T1` through `T8`:

1. **Step 1 — Capture Structured Failure Telemetry:**
   - If any deployment step or verification gate fails, automatically collect:
     - SSH stdout/stderr from the failed command on `HOST_A` or `HOST_B` (`salem@10.209.250.205`),
     - PM2 logs (`pm2 logs --nostream --lines 100`) from the relevant node,
     - PostgreSQL 18 / PgBouncer / Barman / WAL-G / Nginx journal logs (`sudo -S journalctl -u <service> -n 80 --no-pager`).
2. **Step 2 — Root-Cause Classification & Immediate Code/Config Remediation:**
   - **Case A — Port Collision or Stale Process Between Topologies:** Update `deploy/test-matrix/teardownTopology.ts` to cleanly stop previous topology PM2 apps, release ports, and reset test clusters before starting the next topology.
   - **Case B — `pg_hba.conf` or `listen_addresses` Rejection Across LAN (`HOST_A <-> 10.209.250.205`):** Patch `postgres18Provisioner.ts` to ensure `host all all <LAN_SUBNET>/24 scram-sha-256` and `host replication pg_replicator <LAN_SUBNET>/24 scram-sha-256` are present before reloading Postgres.
   - **Case C — mTLS Certificate `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID` on Multi-Node:** Patch `pkiManager.ts` so every IP in `CORE_NODES`, `BACKUP_NODE`, `127.0.0.1`, and `localhost` is included in the X.509 `subjectAltName` extension and redistribute certs.
   - **Case D —PgBouncer Prepared Statement Error (`prepared statement "s0" already exists` or `does not exist`):** Verify `pool_mode = transaction` and `max_prepared_statements = 256` in `pgbouncer.ini` and reload PgBouncer.
   - **Case E — Multi-Node Worker Duplicate Execution or Lock Contention:** Patch the worker's SQL claim query to wrap `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status/lease `UPDATE` inside a single `storage.uow.run()` transaction.
   - **Case F — WAL-G or Barman Archive/Restore Failure:** Inspect bucket/SSH permissions, `archive_command`, or `pg_receivewal` slot initialization in `backupEngineProvisioner.ts`, fix the script, and re-run the backup and scratch PITR restore drill.
3. **Step 3 — Re-Run the Failed Gate + Full Topology Regression:**
   - After applying the fix, re-deploy the current topology and re-run **all 11 gates (`Gate 1` to `Gate 11`)** from the beginning of that topology to confirm the fix did not introduce any regression.

## 6. Mandatory Autonomous "Test -> Diagnose -> Fix -> Re-Verify" Self-Healing Loop for OpenCode

When OpenCode runs the 8-topology test matrix, **stopping on an error and reporting failure to the user is forbidden**. OpenCode must follow this autonomous self-healing loop for every gate in `T1` through `T8`:

1. **Step 1 — Capture Structured Failure Telemetry:**
   - If any deployment step or verification gate fails, automatically collect:
     - SSH stdout/stderr from the failed command on `HOST_A` or `HOST_B` (`salem@10.209.250.205`),
     - PM2 logs (`pm2 logs --nostream --lines 100`) from the relevant node,
     - PostgreSQL 18 / PgBouncer / Barman / WAL-G / Nginx journal logs (`sudo -S journalctl -u <service> -n 80 --no-pager`).
2. **Step 2 — Root-Cause Classification & Immediate Code/Config Remediation:**
   - **Case A — Port Collision or Stale Process Between Topologies:** Update `deploy/test-matrix/teardownTopology.ts` to cleanly stop previous topology PM2 apps, release ports, and reset test clusters before starting the next topology.
   - **Case B — `pg_hba.conf` or `listen_addresses` Rejection Across LAN (`HOST_A <-> 10.209.250.205`):** Patch `postgres18Provisioner.ts` to ensure `host all all <LAN_SUBNET>/24 scram-sha-256` and `host replication pg_replicator <LAN_SUBNET>/24 scram-sha-256` are present before reloading Postgres.
   - **Case C — mTLS Certificate `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID` on Multi-Node:** Patch `pkiManager.ts` so every IP in `CORE_NODES`, `BACKUP_NODE`, `127.0.0.1`, and `localhost` is included in the X.509 `subjectAltName` extension and redistribute certs.
   - **Case D —PgBouncer Prepared Statement Error (`prepared statement "s0" already exists` or `does not exist`):** Verify `pool_mode = transaction` and `max_prepared_statements = 256` in `pgbouncer.ini` and reload PgBouncer.
   - **Case E — Multi-Node Worker Duplicate Execution or Lock Contention:** Patch the worker's SQL claim query to wrap `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status/lease `UPDATE` inside a single `storage.uow.run()` transaction.
   - **Case F — WAL-G or Barman Archive/Restore Failure:** Inspect bucket/SSH permissions, `archive_command`, or `pg_receivewal` slot initialization in `backupEngineProvisioner.ts`, fix the script, and re-run the backup and scratch PITR restore drill.
3. **Step 3 — Re-Run the Failed Gate + Full Topology Regression:**
   - After applying the fix, re-deploy the current topology and re-run **all 11 gates (`Gate 1` to `Gate 11`)** from the beginning of that topology to confirm the fix did not introduce any regression.

## 7. OpenCode Execution Checklist

- [ ] **Task 1 — Implement Multi-Instance & Multi-Cluster Support in `deploy/`:** Ensure PM2 process names, `.env.<nodeId>` files, Nginx upstreams, and Debian/Ubuntu `pg_createcluster 18 <name> -p <port>` support running multiple nodes of any service or database role on the same machine (`HOST_A` or `HOST_B`) as well as across separate machines.
- [ ] **Task 2 — Bootstrap Two-Machine Lab (`HOST_A` <-> `salem@10.209.250.205` pass `1234`):** Run `bootstrapTwoMachineLab.ts` to auto-discover `HOST_A_LAN_IP`, establish bidirectional Ed25519 SSH keys between `HOST_A` and `salem@10.209.250.205`, verify passwordless/stdin-sudo (`1234`), and provision the local MinIO S3 test bucket (`:9000`) + SSH backup vault directory on `HOST_B`.
- [ ] **Task 3 — Execute & Verify Topologies `T1`, `T2`, `T3`, and `T4`:** Run all 11 verification gates across `T1` (Single-Host Multi-Node + `wal-g`), `T2` (Compute on A / Storage on B + `barman`), `T3` (DB & Redis Separated + Cross-Host Streaming Replica + `wal-g`), and `T4` (Reversed DB/Redis Separation + 2 Replicas + Standby-Offloaded `barman`), healing any issues discovered.
- [ ] **Task 4 — Execute & Verify Topologies `T5`, `T6`, `T7`, and `T8`:** Run all 11 verification gates across `T5` (DMZ Edge Isolation + UFW Penetration Test), `T6` (Full Symmetric 4-Core / 4-Checkout / 4-Merchant / 2-Admin / 2-Replica Mesh with 120,000-attempt `STANDARD` seed), `T7` (Live Rolling Horizontal Scale-Out & Scale-In under 500 TPS load), and `T8` (Chaos Engineering Node/Replica/Redis/LogDB Kills + Full Primary DB Wipe & PITR Recovery).
- [ ] **Task 5 — Emit Final Multi-Topology Benchmark & Certification Report:** Write `deploy/test-matrix/TOPOLOGY_CERTIFICATION_REPORT.md` recording the measured p50/p95/p99 latencies, sustained TPS, replica failover times, PITR restore durations, and `0.0000 LYD` ledger invariant proofs across all 8 topologies.

# AGENTS.md — Payment Gateway Monorepo

## Start here

1. Read `project-design/INDEX.md`.
2. Read the relevant `project-design/parts/**` file for the area you will change.
3. Read the code and tests that the part references.
4. If `project-design/` is missing or conflicts with the code, update `project-design/` first (or record the deviation in `TRACKER.md` before proceeding).

`design/**` is historical/reference material only. It is not current authority.

## Project map

| Workspace | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| `core-back/` | PostgreSQL 18 storage engine, domain engine, ledger, governance, workers, backup control, synthetic seeder. |
| `admin-back/`, `merchant-back/`, `checkout-back/` | mTLS-only edge BFFs with least-in-flight `CORE_BACK_URLS` pools. |
| `admin-front/`, `merchant-front/`, `checkout-front/` | Vue 3 + Vuetify 3 + TSX portals. |
| `fake-rails-back/`, `fake-rails-front/` | Optional Fake Payment Rails emulator and tester portal. |
| `deploy/` | Multi-host deploy engine, storage provisioners, PKI, firewall, backup daemon. |
| `tests/` | Playwright/Vitest suites, including live-stack journeys. |
| `project-design/` | Canonical design, status, tracker and generated appendices. |

## Non-negotiable invariants

- PostgreSQL 18 is the only runtime database (`@prisma/adapter-pg` + `pg`). Do not reintroduce MySQL/MariaDB.
- Money uses `Decimal`/`decimal.js`; never floating point.
- Sensitive actions use maker-checker; maker ≠ checker is enforced server-side.
- Authorities are enforced by `core-back`; edge/UI checks are advisory.
- Edge services never receive `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` or another host's client key.
- Ledger, outbox and audit writes for critical paths are atomic.
- Secrets, ciphertext, AML-confidential data and master keys must never be logged.
- Keep English/Arabic catalogues in sync for user-facing text.
- All spreadsheet exports use the shared XLSX pipeline.
- Deploy-generated UI flags (`ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS`, `ADMIN_SHOW_HELP_PANELS`) are runtime-config controlled.

## Documentation workflow

Any change to behavior, APIs, schema/migrations, env/config, deploy, UI routes, tests or invariants must update the affected `project-design/parts/**` file and `project-design/TRACKER.md` in the same change.

- Generated files: `project-design/PROJECT_DESIGN.md`, `project-design/STATUS.md`, `project-design/appendices/*-catalog.md`, `project-design/appendices/*-matrix.md`, `project-design/appendices/*-inventory.md`, and `*/blueprint.md`.
- Never hand-edit generated files. Edit `project-design/parts/**` and run the generator.
- Status values: `implemented`, `partial`, `missing`, `deferred`, `deprecated`, `historical`.
- Unimplemented features go under `project-design/parts/09-future-and-unimplemented/`.
- Keep the YAML frontmatter accurate (`status`, `last_verified`, `code`, `design_sources`, `tests`, `gaps`).

## Verification

Run the smallest relevant checks first, then the full gate:

```bash
bun scripts/project-design/build.ts --check
cd core-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd deploy && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd deploy/backup-daemon && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd admin-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd merchant-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd checkout-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd admin-front && bun run build
cd merchant-front && bun run build
cd checkout-front && bun run build
```

Database-backed suites require PostgreSQL 18 and Redis; report skipped suites explicitly. Run `scripts/run-benchmarks.sh` for storage benchmarks.

## Before finishing

- `bun scripts/project-design/build.ts --check` passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Typechecks/tests/builds relevant to the change pass, or the environment limitation is stated.
- `project-design/TRACKER.md` has a dated entry for material changes.

2. Read the relevant `project-design/parts/**` file for the area you will change.
3. Read the code and tests that the part references.
4. If `project-design/` is missing or conflicts with the code, update `project-design/` first (or record the deviation in `TRACKER.md` before proceeding).

`design/**` is historical/reference material only. It is not current authority.

## Project map

| Workspace | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| `core-back/` | PostgreSQL 18 storage engine, domain engine, ledger, governance, workers, backup control, synthetic seeder. |
| `admin-back/`, `merchant-back/`, `checkout-back/` | mTLS-only edge BFFs with least-in-flight `CORE_BACK_URLS` pools. |
| `admin-front/`, `merchant-front/`, `checkout-front/` | Vue 3 + Vuetify 3 + TSX portals. |
| `fake-rails-back/`, `fake-rails-front/` | Optional Fake Payment Rails emulator and tester portal. |
| `deploy/` | Multi-host deploy engine, storage provisioners, PKI, firewall, backup daemon. |
| `tests/` | Playwright/Vitest suites, including live-stack journeys. |
| `project-design/` | Canonical design, status, tracker and generated appendices. |

## Non-negotiable invariants

- PostgreSQL 18 is the only runtime database (`@prisma/adapter-pg` + `pg`). Do not reintroduce MySQL/MariaDB.
- Money uses `Decimal`/`decimal.js`; never floating point.
- Sensitive actions use maker-checker; maker ≠ checker is enforced server-side.
- Authorities are enforced by `core-back`; edge/UI checks are advisory.
- Edge services never receive `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` or another host's client key.
- Ledger, outbox and audit writes for critical paths are atomic.
- Secrets, ciphertext, AML-confidential data and master keys must never be logged.
- Keep English/Arabic catalogues in sync for user-facing text.
- All spreadsheet exports use the shared XLSX pipeline.
- Deploy-generated UI flags (`ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS`, `ADMIN_SHOW_HELP_PANELS`) are runtime-config controlled.

## Documentation workflow

Any change to behavior, APIs, schema/migrations, env/config, deploy, UI routes, tests or invariants must update the affected `project-design/parts/**` file and `project-design/TRACKER.md` in the same change.

- Generated files: `project-design/PROJECT_DESIGN.md`, `project-design/STATUS.md`, `project-design/appendices/*-catalog.md`, `project-design/appendices/*-matrix.md`, `project-design/appendices/*-inventory.md`, and `*/blueprint.md`.
- Never hand-edit generated files. Edit `project-design/parts/**` and run the generator.
- Status values: `implemented`, `partial`, `missing`, `deferred`, `deprecated`, `historical`.
- Unimplemented features go under `project-design/parts/09-future-and-unimplemented/`.
- Keep the YAML frontmatter accurate (`status`, `last_verified`, `code`, `design_sources`, `tests`, `gaps`).

## Verification

Run the smallest relevant checks first, then the full gate:

```bash
bun scripts/project-design/build.ts --check
cd core-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd deploy && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd deploy/backup-daemon && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd admin-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd merchant-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd checkout-back && bun run typecheck && bun test
cd admin-front && bun run build
cd merchant-front && bun run build
cd checkout-front && bun run build
```

Database-backed suites require PostgreSQL 18 and Redis; report skipped suites explicitly. Run `scripts/run-benchmarks.sh` for storage benchmarks.

## Before finishing

- `bun scripts/project-design/build.ts --check` passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Typechecks/tests/builds relevant to the change pass, or the environment limitation is stated.
- `project-design/TRACKER.md` has a dated entry for material changes.

import { z } from "zod";

/**
 * The multi-host deployment configuration.
 *
 * `deploy/deploy.env` is parsed by this schema. Everything is validated before
 * a single SSH connection is opened: a typo in an IP address must fail on the
 * operator's machine, not halfway through a production deploy.
 */

const ipv4 = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .regex(/^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/, "must be an IPv4 address")
  .refine((value) => value.split(".").every((octet) => Number(octet) >= 0 && Number(octet) <= 255), "octet out of range");

const cidrList = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .min(1)
  .refine((value) => {
    return value.split(",").every((entry) => {
      const [address, bits] = entry.trim().split("/");
      if (!address || bits === undefined) return false;
      const isV4 = /^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/.test(address);
      const isV6 = /^[0-9a-fA-F:]+$/.test(address);
      const width = Number(bits);
      if (!Number.isInteger(width)) return false;
      return isV4 ? width >= 0 && width <= 32 : isV6 && width >= 0 && width <= 128;
    });
  }, "must be a comma separated list of CIDRs (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.0.0/16)");

const sshPath = z.string().trim().min(1, "must point at an SSH key");

const domain = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .min(3)
  .max(253)
  .regex(/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+$/i, "must be a fully qualified domain name");

// A vhost name may be a FQDN, a bare IP, or "_" (nginx catch-all) so a box can
// be served without DNS during staging.
const serverName = z.union([domain, z.literal("_"), ipv4]);

const port = z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(65535);
const positive = z.coerce.number().int().min(1);
const booleanish = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .toLowerCase()
  .pipe(z.enum(["true", "false", "1", "0", "yes", "no"]))
  .transform((value) => value === "true" || value === "1" || value === "yes");

export const DEPLOY_MODES = ["auto", "fresh", "update", "rolling_update"] as const;
export const DB_ENGINES = ["postgresql"] as const;
export const SSL_MODES = ["certbot", "custom", "self_signed"] as const;
export const ROLE_NAMES = ["db", "core", "admin", "merchant", "checkout", "fake-rails"] as const;
export type DeployRole = (typeof ROLE_NAMES)[number];
export const STORAGE_ROLE_NAMES = ["pg-primary", "pg-replica", "pgbouncer", "redis", "audit-db", "log-db", "backup"] as const;
export type StorageRole = (typeof STORAGE_ROLE_NAMES)[number];
export type HostRole = DeployRole | StorageRole;

/**
 * One entry of a horizontal node array:
 *
 *   nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
 *
 * `sshHost` is the address the orchestrator connects to (it may be public),
 * `privateIp` is the LAN address the node advertises to its peers (it is the
 * address written into TLS SANs and firewall allowlists), and `servicePort` is
 * the port the application/storage daemon listens on.
 */
export interface NodeSpec {
  nodeId: string;
  sshHost: string;
  sshPort: number;
  privateIp: string;
  servicePort: number;
}

const NODE_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$/;
const IPV4 = /^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/;

const validateIpv4 = (value: string, label: string): void => {
  if (!IPV4.test(value) || value.split(".").some((octet) => Number(octet) < 0 || Number(octet) > 255)) {
    throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' must be an IPv4 address`);
  }
};

const parsePort = (value: string, label: string): number => {
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(value)) throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' must be a port number`);
  const port = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' is out of range`);
  return port;
};

/**
 * Parses a comma separated horizontal node list and rejects malformed entries,
 * duplicate node ids and duplicate private IPs *within the same list*.
 */
export const parseNodeList = (value: string | undefined | null): NodeSpec[] => {
  if (!value || value.trim().length === 0) return [];
  const nodes: NodeSpec[] = [];
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  const ips = new Set<string>();
  for (const rawEntry of value.split(",")) {
    const entry = rawEntry.trim();
    if (entry.length === 0) continue;
    const at = entry.indexOf("@");
    if (at <= 0 || at === entry.length - 1) {
      throw new Error(`node '${entry}' must use nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`);
    }
    const nodeId = entry.slice(0, at).trim();
    const parts = entry.slice(at + 1).split(":");
    if (parts.length !== 4) {
      throw new Error(`node '${entry}' must have exactly sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort after '@'`);
    }
    const [sshHostRaw, sshPortRaw, privateIpRaw, servicePortRaw] = parts as [string, string, string, string];
    const sshHost = sshHostRaw.trim();
    const privateIp = privateIpRaw.trim();
    if (!NODE_ID.test(nodeId)) throw new Error(`node id '${nodeId}' is invalid`);
    validateIpv4(sshHost, `node '${nodeId}' sshHost`);
    validateIpv4(privateIp, `node '${nodeId}' privateIp`);
    const sshPort = parsePort(sshPortRaw.trim(), `node '${nodeId}' sshPort`);
    const servicePort = parsePort(servicePortRaw.trim(), `node '${nodeId}' servicePort`);
    if (ids.has(nodeId)) throw new Error(`duplicate node id '${nodeId}'`);
    if (ips.has(privateIp)) throw new Error(`duplicate private IP '${privateIp}' in node list`);
    ids.add(nodeId);
    ips.add(privateIp);
    nodes.push({ nodeId, sshHost, sshPort, privateIp, servicePort });
  }
  return nodes;
};

  DB_SSH_PORT: port.default(22),
  DB_SSH_USER: z.string().trim().min(1).max(64).default("ubuntu"),
  DB_SSH_KEY_PATH: sshPath.optional(),
  DB_SUDO_PASSWORD: z.string().max(256).default(""),
  DB_PRIVATE_IP: ipv4.optional(),
  DB_ENGINE: z.enum(DB_ENGINES).default("postgresql"),
  DB_PORT: port.default(5432),
  DB_NAME: z

    .trim()
    .min(1)
    .max(64)
    .regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/, "must be an identifier")
    .optional(),
  DB_USER: z

    .trim()
    .min(1)
    .max(64)
    .regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/, "must be an identifier")
    .optional(),
  DB_PASSWORD: z.string().min(8).max(256).optional(),
  DATABASE_URL: z.string().trim().min(1).max(1000).optional(),

  // 1b. Horizontal compute node arrays (override the single-host fields above)
  CORE_NODES: nodeList,
  ADMIN_NODES: nodeList,
  MERCHANT_NODES: nodeList,
  CHECKOUT_NODES: nodeList,
  CORE_BACK_URLS: z.string().trim().max(4000).optional(),

  // 2. Core
  CORE_SSH_HOST: ipv4.optional(),
  CORE_SSH_PORT: port.default(22),
  CORE_SSH_USER: z.string().trim().min(1).max(64).default("ubuntu"),
  CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH: sshPath.optional(),
  CORE_SUDO_PASSWORD: z.string().max(256).default(""),
  CORE_PRIVATE_IP: ipv4.optional(),
  CORE_PORT: port.default(4000),
  CORE_REMOTE_DIR: z.string().trim().min(1).max(200).default("/var/www/pg-core"),
  RUN_PRISMA_SEED: booleanish.default(false),

  // 3. Admin
  ADMIN_SSH_HOST: ipv4.optional(),

  ADMIN_SSH_USER: z.string().trim().min(1).max(64).default("ubuntu"),

  ADMIN_PRIVATE_IP: ipv4.optional(),

  ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT: port.default(8443),
  ADMIN_SSL: booleanish.default(true),
  ADMIN_DOMAIN: serverName.default("admin.internal"),
  ADMIN_REMOTE_DIR: z.string().trim().min(1).max(200).default("/var/www/pg-admin"),
  ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS: booleanish.optional(),

  // 4. Merchant

export type DeployConfig = z.infer<typeof base>;

/** True when any PostgreSQL 18 storage field is configured. */
export const pgStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH
  || config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE.trim().length > 0
  || config.PG_REPLICA_NODES.trim().length > 0
  || config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length > 0;

export const redisStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || parseNodeList(config.REDIS_NODES).length > 0;

export const auditDbConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.AUDIT_DB_NODE.trim().length > 0;

export const logDbConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.LOG_DB_NODE.trim().length > 0;

export const backupStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.BACKUP_ENABLED || config.BACKUP_NODE.trim().length > 0;

/**
 * The core upstream URLs every edge service receives. The helper is the single
 * source of truth: an explicit CORE_BACK_URLS wins, otherwise the core node
 * array, otherwise the legacy single-host fields.
 */
export const edgeCoreUrls = (config: DeployConfig): string[] => {
  if (config.CORE_BACK_URLS && config.CORE_BACK_URLS.trim().length > 0) {
    return config.CORE_BACK_URLS.split(",").map((entry) => entry.trim()).filter((entry) => entry.length > 0);
  }
  const coreNodes = parseNodeList(config.CORE_NODES);
  if (coreNodes.length > 0) {
    return coreNodes.map((node) => `https://${node.privateIp}:${node.servicePort}`);
  }
  if (config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP) {
    return [`https://${config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP}:${config.CORE_PORT}`];
  }
  return [];
};

/** The effective relational database (legacy DB_* or the PG 18 settings). */
export const effectiveDatabase = (config: DeployConfig): {
  engine: DeployConfig["DB_ENGINE"];
  host: string | null;
  port: number;
  name: string;
  user: string;
  password: string;
  url: string | null;
  privateIp: string | null;
  managedViaSsh: boolean;
} => {
  const primary = parseNodeList(config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE)[0] ?? null;
  const pg = pgStorageConfigured(config);
  // When the PostgreSQL 18 storage tier is configured its credentials are
  // authoritative; the legacy DB_* block is only a compatibility path for an
  // externally managed database.
  const name = pg ? config.PG_DB_NAME : (config.DB_NAME ?? config.PG_DB_NAME);
  const user = pg ? config.PG_DB_USER : (config.DB_USER ?? config.PG_DB_USER);
  const password = pg ? config.PG_DB_PASSWORD : (config.DB_PASSWORD ?? config.PG_DB_PASSWORD);
  const host = primary?.privateIp ?? config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? null;
  const port = primary?.servicePort ?? config.DB_PORT;
  const derivedPort = config.PGBOUNCER_ENABLED ? config.PGBOUNCER_PORT : port;
  const url = pg && host
    ? `postgresql://${encodeURIComponent(user)}:${encodeURIComponent(password)}@${host}:${derivedPort}/${name}`
    : (config.DATABASE_URL ?? null);
  return {
    engine: config.DB_ENGINE,
    host,
    port,
    name,
    user,
    password,
    url,
    privateIp: pg ? (primary?.privateIp ?? config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? null) : (config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? primary?.privateIp ?? null),
    managedViaSsh: config.DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH,
  };
};

/**
 * Cross-field rules. A value can be valid in isolation and still make the
 * topology impossible (the database URL not matching the engine, a certbot
 * domain with no certificate path, a database host with no SSH target, …).
 */
export const validateDeployConfig = (config: DeployConfig): string[] => {
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const pgConfigured = pgStorageConfigured(config);

  if (pgConfigured && config.DB_ENGINE !== "postgresql") {
    problems.push("DB_ENGINE must be 'postgresql' when PostgreSQL 18 storage fields are configured");
  }
  const replicaNodes = (() => {
    try {
      return parseNodeList(config.PG_REPLICA_NODES);
    } catch (error) {
      problems.push(`PG_REPLICA_NODES: ${(error as Error).message}`);
      return [];
    }
  })();
  const primaryNodes = (() => {
    try {
      return parseNodeList(config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE);
    } catch (error) {
      problems.push(`PG_PRIMARY_NODE: ${(error as Error).message}`);
      return [];
    }
  })();
  if (primaryNodes.length > 1) problems.push("PG_PRIMARY_NODE must describe exactly one primary");
  if (replicaNodes.length > 0 && primaryNodes.length === 0) {
    problems.push("PG_REPLICA_NODES requires PG_PRIMARY_NODE");
  }
  if (config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH) {
    if (primaryNodes.length === 0) problems.push("PG_PRIMARY_NODE is required when PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
    if (!config.PG_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("PG_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
    if (config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length === 0) problems.push("PG_DB_PASSWORD is required when PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
  }
  if (pgConfigured && config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length > 0 && config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length < 8) {
    problems.push("PG_DB_PASSWORD must be at least 8 characters");
  }
  if (config.PGBOUNCER_ENABLED && !pgConfigured) {
    problems.push("PGBOUNCER_ENABLED requires the PostgreSQL 18 storage fields");
  }

  if (config.DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH && !pgConfigured) {
    if (!config.DB_SSH_HOST) problems.push("DB_SSH_HOST is required when DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
    if (!config.DB_SSH_KEY_PATH) problems.push("DB_SSH_KEY_PATH is required when DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
    if (!config.DB_PRIVATE_IP) problems.push("DB_PRIVATE_IP is required when DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH=true");
  }

  if (!pgConfigured) {
    if (!config.DB_NAME) problems.push("DB_NAME is required");
    if (!config.DB_USER) problems.push("DB_USER is required");
    if (!config.DB_PASSWORD) problems.push("DB_PASSWORD is required");
    if (!config.DATABASE_URL) problems.push("DATABASE_URL is required");
  }
  if (config.DATABASE_URL) {
    const enginePrefix = "postgresql://";
    if (!config.DATABASE_URL.startsWith(enginePrefix)) {
      problems.push(`DATABASE_URL must start with ${enginePrefix} (DB_ENGINE=${config.DB_ENGINE})`);
    }
    if (config.DB_PRIVATE_IP && !config.DATABASE_URL.includes(config.DB_PRIVATE_IP)) {
      problems.push("DATABASE_URL should point at DB_PRIVATE_IP");
    }
  }
  // A single-box installation legitimately co-locates the database with the
  // core (the database binds to 127.0.0.1 and is never exposed); on separate
  // nodes the operator points DATABASE_URL at the database host's private IP.

  // --- Horizontal compute node arrays -------------------------------------
  const tiers = [
    { name: "CORE_NODES", value: config.CORE_NODES, legacy: [["CORE_SSH_HOST", config.CORE_SSH_HOST], ["CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["CORE_PRIVATE_IP", config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP]] },
    { name: "ADMIN_NODES", value: config.ADMIN_NODES, legacy: [["ADMIN_SSH_HOST", config.ADMIN_SSH_HOST], ["ADMIN_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.ADMIN_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["ADMIN_PRIVATE_IP", config.ADMIN_PRIVATE_IP]] },
    { name: "MERCHANT_NODES", value: config.MERCHANT_NODES, legacy: [["MERCHANT_SSH_HOST", config.MERCHANT_SSH_HOST], ["MERCHANT_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.MERCHANT_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["MERCHANT_PRIVATE_IP", config.MERCHANT_PRIVATE_IP]] },
    { name: "CHECKOUT_NODES", value: config.CHECKOUT_NODES, legacy: [["CHECKOUT_SSH_HOST", config.CHECKOUT_SSH_HOST], ["CHECKOUT_SSH_KEY_PATH", config.CHECKOUT_SSH_KEY_PATH], ["CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP", config.CHECKOUT_PRIVATE_IP]] },
  ];
  for (const [name, value, keyPath] of [
    ["CORE_NODES", config.CORE_NODES, config.CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH],
    ["ADMIN_NODES", config.ADMIN_NODES, config.ADMIN_SSH_KEY_PATH],
    ["MERCHANT_NODES", config.MERCHANT_NODES, config.MERCHANT_SSH_KEY_PATH],
    ["CHECKOUT_NODES", config.CHECKOUT_NODES, config.CHECKOUT_SSH_KEY_PATH],
  ] as const) {
    if (value.trim().length > 0 && !keyPath) {
      problems.push(`${name} requires the matching *_SSH_KEY_PATH`);
    }
  }
  const parsedTiers = new Map<string, NodeSpec[]>();
  for (const tier of tiers) {
    if (tier.value.trim().length === 0) {
      for (const [field, value] of tier.legacy) {
        if (!value) problems.push(`${field} is required when ${tier.name} is empty`);
      }
      parsedTiers.set(tier.name, []);
      continue;
    }
    try {
      parsedTiers.set(tier.name, parseNodeList(tier.value));
    } catch (error) {
      problems.push(`${tier.name}: ${(error as Error).message}`);
      parsedTiers.set(tier.name, []);
