import { z } from "zod";

/**
 * The multi-host deployment configuration.
 *
 * `deploy/deploy.env` is parsed by this schema. Everything is validated before
 * a single SSH connection is opened: a typo in an IP address must fail on the
 * operator's machine, not halfway through a production deploy.
 */

const ipv4 = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .regex(/^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/, "must be an IPv4 address")
  .refine((value) => value.split(".").every((octet) => Number(octet) >= 0 && Number(octet) <= 255), "octet out of range");

const cidrList = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .min(1)
  .refine((value) => {
    return value.split(",").every((entry) => {
      const [address, bits] = entry.trim().split("/");
      if (!address || bits === undefined) return false;
      const isV4 = /^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/.test(address);
      const isV6 = /^[0-9a-fA-F:]+$/.test(address);
      const width = Number(bits);
      if (!Number.isInteger(width)) return false;
      return isV4 ? width >= 0 && width <= 32 : isV6 && width >= 0 && width <= 128;
    });
  }, "must be a comma separated list of CIDRs (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8,192.168.0.0/16)");

const sshPath = z.string().trim().min(1, "must point at an SSH key");

const domain = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .min(3)
  .max(253)
  .regex(/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+$/i, "must be a fully qualified domain name");

// A vhost name may be a FQDN, a bare IP, or "_" (nginx catch-all) so a box can
// be served without DNS during staging.
const serverName = z.union([domain, z.literal("_"), ipv4]);

const port = z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(65535);
const positive = z.coerce.number().int().min(1);
const booleanish = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .toLowerCase()
  .pipe(z.enum(["true", "false", "1", "0", "yes", "no"]))
  .transform((value) => value === "true" || value === "1" || value === "yes");

/**
 * One entry of a horizontal node array:
 *
 *   nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
 *
 * `sshHost` is the address the orchestrator connects to (it may be public),
 * `privateIp` is the LAN address the node advertises to its peers (it is the
 * address written into TLS SANs and firewall allowlists), and `servicePort` is
 * the port the application/storage daemon listens on.
 */
export interface NodeSpec {
  nodeId: string;
  sshHost: string;
  sshPort: number;
  privateIp: string;
  servicePort: number;
}

const NODE_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$/;
const IPV4 = /^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$/;

const validateIpv4 = (value: string, label: string): void => {
  if (!IPV4.test(value) || value.split(".").some((octet) => Number(octet) < 0 || Number(octet) > 255)) {
    throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' must be an IPv4 address`);
  }
};

const parsePort = (value: string, label: string): number => {
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(value)) throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' must be a port number`);
  const port = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) throw new Error(`${label}: '${value}' is out of range`);
  return port;
};

/**
 * Parses a comma separated horizontal node list and rejects malformed entries,
 * duplicate node ids and duplicate private IPs *within the same list*.
 */
export const parseNodeList = (value: string | undefined | null): NodeSpec[] => {
  if (!value || value.trim().length === 0) return [];
  const nodes: NodeSpec[] = [];
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  const ips = new Set<string>();
  for (const rawEntry of value.split(",")) {
    const entry = rawEntry.trim();
    if (entry.length === 0) continue;
    const at = entry.indexOf("@");
    if (at <= 0 || at === entry.length - 1) {
      throw new Error(`node '${entry}' must use nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`);
    }
    const nodeId = entry.slice(0, at).trim();
    const parts = entry.slice(at + 1).split(":");
    if (parts.length !== 4) {
      throw new Error(`node '${entry}' must have exactly sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort after '@'`);
    }
    const [sshHostRaw, sshPortRaw, privateIpRaw, servicePortRaw] = parts as [string, string, string, string];
    const sshHost = sshHostRaw.trim();
    const privateIp = privateIpRaw.trim();
    if (!NODE_ID.test(nodeId)) throw new Error(`node id '${nodeId}' is invalid`);
    validateIpv4(sshHost, `node '${nodeId}' sshHost`);
    validateIpv4(privateIp, `node '${nodeId}' privateIp`);
    const sshPort = parsePort(sshPortRaw.trim(), `node '${nodeId}' sshPort`);
    const servicePort = parsePort(servicePortRaw.trim(), `node '${nodeId}' servicePort`);
    if (ids.has(nodeId)) throw new Error(`duplicate node id '${nodeId}'`);
    if (ips.has(privateIp)) throw new Error(`duplicate private IP '${privateIp}' in node list`);
    ids.add(nodeId);
    ips.add(privateIp);
    nodes.push({ nodeId, sshHost, sshPort, privateIp, servicePort });
  }
  return nodes;
};

export type DeployConfig = z.infer<typeof base>;

/** True when any PostgreSQL 18 storage field is configured. */
export const pgStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH
  || config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE.trim().length > 0
  || config.PG_REPLICA_NODES.trim().length > 0
  || config.PG_DB_PASSWORD.length > 0;

export const redisStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.REDIS_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || parseNodeList(config.REDIS_NODES).length > 0;

export const auditDbConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.AUDIT_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.AUDIT_DB_NODE.trim().length > 0;

export const logDbConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.LOG_DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.LOG_DB_NODE.trim().length > 0;

export const backupStorageConfigured = (config: DeployConfig): boolean =>
  config.BACKUP_ENABLED || config.BACKUP_NODE.trim().length > 0;

/**
 * The core upstream URLs every edge service receives. The helper is the single
 * source of truth: an explicit CORE_BACK_URLS wins, otherwise the core node
 * array, otherwise the legacy single-host fields.
 */
export const edgeCoreUrls = (config: DeployConfig): string[] => {
  if (config.CORE_BACK_URLS && config.CORE_BACK_URLS.trim().length > 0) {
    return config.CORE_BACK_URLS.split(",").map((entry) => entry.trim()).filter((entry) => entry.length > 0);
  }
  const coreNodes = parseNodeList(config.CORE_NODES);
  if (coreNodes.length > 0) {
    return coreNodes.map((node) => `https://${node.privateIp}:${node.servicePort}`);
  }
  if (config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP) {
    return [`https://${config.CORE_PRIVATE_IP}:${config.CORE_PORT}`];
  }
  return [];
};

/** The effective relational database (legacy DB_* or the PG 18 settings). */
export const effectiveDatabase = (config: DeployConfig): {
  engine: DeployConfig["DB_ENGINE"];
  host: string | null;
  port: number;
  name: string;
  user: string;
  password: string;
  url: string | null;
  privateIp: string | null;
  managedViaSsh: boolean;
} => {
  const primary = parseNodeList(config.PG_PRIMARY_NODE)[0] ?? null;
  const pg = pgStorageConfigured(config);
  // When the PostgreSQL 18 storage tier is configured its credentials are
  // authoritative; the legacy DB_* block is only a compatibility path for an
  // externally managed database.
  const name = pg ? config.PG_DB_NAME : (config.DB_NAME ?? config.PG_DB_NAME);
  const user = pg ? config.PG_DB_USER : (config.DB_USER ?? config.PG_DB_USER);
  const password = pg ? config.PG_DB_PASSWORD : (config.DB_PASSWORD ?? config.PG_DB_PASSWORD);
  const host = primary?.privateIp ?? config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? null;
  const port = primary?.servicePort ?? config.DB_PORT;
  const derivedPort = config.PGBOUNCER_ENABLED ? config.PGBOUNCER_PORT : port;
  const url = pg && host
    ? `postgresql://${encodeURIComponent(user)}:${encodeURIComponent(password)}@${host}:${derivedPort}/${name}`
    : (config.DATABASE_URL ?? null);
  return {
    engine: config.DB_ENGINE,
    host,
    port,
    name,
    user,
    password,
    url,
    privateIp: pg ? (primary?.privateIp ?? config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? null) : (config.DB_PRIVATE_IP ?? primary?.privateIp ?? null),
    managedViaSsh: config.DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH || config.PG_MANAGE_VIA_SSH,
  };
};

/**
 * Cross-field rules. A value can be valid in isolation and still make the

model RailRoute {
  id                 String           @id @default(uuid(7)) @db.Uuid
  createdAt          DateTime         @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt          DateTime         @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  railId             String           @map("rail_id") @db.Uuid
  gatewayId          String           @map("gateway_id") @db.Uuid
  credentialPolicy   CredentialPolicy @map("credential_policy")
  priority           Int              @default(0)
  routingStrategy    RoutingStrategy  @default(EFFECTIVE_COST) @map("routing_strategy")
  weight             Int              @default(100)
  costModel          Json             @map("cost_model")
  mismatchPolicy     Json             @map("mismatch_policy")
  minAmount          Decimal          @default(0) @map("min_amount") @db.Decimal(18, 4)
  maxAmount          Decimal?         @map("max_amount") @db.Decimal(18, 4)
  dailyCapAmount     Decimal?         @map("daily_cap_amount") @db.Decimal(18, 4)
  status             RouteStatus      @default(ACTIVE)
  healthState        HealthState      @default(HEALTHY) @map("health_state")
  maintenanceWindows Json?            @map("maintenance_windows")
  scope              Json

  rail                 Rail                  @relation(fields: [railId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  gateway              Gateway               @relation(fields: [gatewayId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  pollPolicies         PollPolicy[]
  widgetDefinitions    WidgetDefinition[]
  redirectDefinitions  RedirectDefinition[]
  gatewayHealthSamples GatewayHealthSample[]
  confirmationChannels ConfirmationChannel[]
  paymentAttempts      PaymentAttempt[]

  @@unique([railId, gatewayId, credentialPolicy])
  @@index([status, healthState])
  @@index([credentialPolicy])
  @@map("rail_routes")
}

  createdAt            DateTime             @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt            DateTime             @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  gatewayVersionId     String               @map("gateway_version_id") @db.Uuid
  name                 String
  purpose              CryptoPurpose

  secretKeyRef         String?              @map("secret_key_ref") @db.Text

  templateString       String?              @map("template_string") @db.Text
  includedFields       Json                 @map("included_fields")
  excludedFields       Json                 @map("excluded_fields")
  outputEncoding       OutputEncoding       @map("output_encoding")

  gatewayVersion       GatewayVersion        @relation(fields: [gatewayVersionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  stepParameters       StepParameter[]

  @@unique([gatewayVersionId, name])
  @@map("crypto_profiles")

model Flow {

# Testing Strategy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part defines how the monorepo is verified: the test philosophy, the gate progression, database and Redis expectations, the zero-tautology rule, and which suites currently skip, mock or fail to exist.

It does not list every test file or count (see `testing.suites`), the fixture and live-stack wiring (see `testing.fixtures`) or the benchmark gates (see `testing.benchmarks`). Per-workspace test evidence is repeated in each workspace part.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The exhaustive test plan was written to prevent a small happy-path suite from missing intersection defects: rounding remainders, confirmation races, SSRF notations, JSX binding failures and seeded historical attempts that fail when an operator clicks Inquire or Refund.

Its non-negotiable rules are:

1. **Zero-tautology.** Every test must invoke the real production module, real Express router, real PostgreSQL constraint or rendered Vue DOM. `expect(true).toBe(true)` and mock-against-mock tests are forbidden.
2. **Combinatorial and property-based generation.** Use data-driven Cartesian products and a seeded PRNG so permutations are named and reproducible.
3. **Continuous double-entry invariant.** Every database suite runs the ledger invariant after writes and requires `drift === "0.0000"`.
4. **Fail-fast gate progression.** Implement and pass suites `T-EX-01` through `T-EX-11` in order; fix production defects before advancing.
5. **Fail loudly when the environment is absent.** A suite that needs PostgreSQL, Redis or a live host either skips with a named reason or fails; it must not silently pass against a stub.

The plan targets 38,500 or more assertions across eleven suites, plus a unified runner.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Test roots

| Root | Runner | Primary scope |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `core-back/test` | `bun test` | Unit, route, engine, ledger, storage, exhaustive |
| `admin-back/test` | `bun test` | Edge contract, mTLS, env isolation, admin surface |
| `merchant-back/test` | `bun test` | Edge contract, forwarding, KYB/external surface |
| `checkout-back/test` | `bun test` | Zero-trust checkout, mTLS, env isolation |
| `fake-rails-back/test` | `bun test` | Real Express app over SQLite |
| `deploy/test` | `bun test` | Config, host planning, PKI, firewall, pipeline |
| `deploy/backup-daemon/test` | `bun test` | Backup engine, catalog, scheduler, restore drill |
| `tests/e2e` | Playwright | Portal geometry, auth, dialogs, mocked API surface |
| `tests/e2e-live` | Playwright | Deployed-stack smoke journeys |
| `tests/unit` | Vitest | Frontend utility and authority helpers |

`tests/run-playwright.sh` is the Playwright wrapper used by local runs. `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` is the master gate runner and forces one Bun worker for database suites.

### 3.2 The zero-tautology rule in practice

The core exhaustive suites are structurally honest about production code:

- `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts` drives real Prisma clients, real schema files and real production services. It says explicitly that it only provisions fixtures and reads metadata.
- `_dbFactory.ts` builds rows from the real `schema.prisma` and live catalog; it does not replace constraints.
- Suite 01 reads `information_schema`, `pg_catalog`, `pg_indexes` and real constraint metadata.
- Suite 02 invokes `LedgerPoster.validateTemplate` and real `buildLedgerTemplate` output.
- Suite 03 invokes the real transform, canonicalisation, signing and Vault code.
- Suite 04 invokes `DynamicRailEngine` through `_engineHarness.ts`, not the live fake-rails HTTP tier.
- Suite 05 drives real authority/session helpers and the real list-query parser.
- Suite 06 uses live PostgreSQL concurrency primitives.
- Suite 07 uses real parsers, KYB sniffers, AML rules and go-live validators.
- Suite 08 uses real SSRF/URL/response-hardening helpers.

The UI and edge tests are weaker:

- `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` `mockApi()` fulfills every `/api/v1/**` call with `{}` or a small fixture. The exhaustive surface tests only assert rendering, layout, direction and theme.
- Auth tests intercept the login endpoint and return a fixture session; they assert the shape of the posted body, not a real login.
- The fake-rails surface test mocks every `/portal-api/**` and only visits `/login`.
- `tests/unit` tests real frontend utility functions, not the full pages.

These are useful regression tests, but they do not satisfy the design's zero-tautology claim for UI behaviour.

### 3.3 Gate progression

`scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` implements this sequence:

| Gate | Command target | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `T-EX-01` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/01-schema` | Live PostgreSQL required for most tests |
| `T-EX-02` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/02-ledger` | Some tests are pure; checkpoints need PostgreSQL |
| `T-EX-03` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/03-transforms-crypto` | Pure |
| `T-EX-04` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/04-rail-engine` | Pure engine harness |
| `T-EX-05` | core plus all edge backends plus fake rails plus deploy | Mixed Bun suites |
| `T-EX-06` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/06-concurrency` | Live PostgreSQL |
| `T-EX-07` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/07-workflows` | Mostly pure |
| `T-EX-08` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/08-security-edge` | Pure |
| `T-EX-09` | `core-back/test/storage-engine`, `test/backup-admin`, backup daemon | There is no `09-storage-backup` directory |
| `T-EX-09b` | `tests` unit plus exhaustive Playwright | Mocked UI |
| `T-EX-10` | `10-seeder-and-deploy` plus optional cross-service journeys | Journeys skip without `E2E_LIVE=1` |
| Final | `core-back bun test` | Full regression |

The design's numbering differs from the runner: the runner calls the UI matrix `T-EX-09b` and the seeder/deploy suite `T-EX-10`, while the design calls them Suite 10 and Suite 11.

### 3.4 Database provisioning

There is no single test database configuration. The suites use these variables:

| Variable | Default | Used by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/payment_gateway_monolith_test` | `test/setup.ts`, storage helpers, postgres payment test |
| `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | fallback | Postgres payment test, exhaustive harness fallback |
| `EXHAUSTIVE_DATABASE_URL` | fallback to `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | Exhaustive harness |
| `STORAGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | fallback to `DATABASE_URL` | Storage-engine helpers |
| `STORAGE_TEST_REDIS_URL` | `redis://127.0.0.1:56379` | Cache/velocity and performance |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://127.0.0.1:56379` | Storage performance and production adapters |

The expected local server is PostgreSQL 18 on port 55432 and Redis on 56379, not the default service ports. The test database must already be migrated (`bun run migrate-deploy`) before the DB-backed suites run. `_harness.ts` uses a dedicated Prisma client so it does not share the cached application client. The storage helpers create dedicated schemas or sandboxes with `search_path` so files can run in parallel.

`bun test --parallel=1` is mandatory for the database suites in the runner because they share one database and the invariant hook.

### 3.5 Double-entry invariant

`_harness.ts` exposes `verifyInvariant()` and `assertZeroDrift()`, which wrap the production `InvariantVerifier`. Suite 02 and the storage write-path suites use it after batches. A non-zero drift throws with left/right sides and drift printed.

The invariant hook is not applied to every file that touches the database. The runner enforces one worker, but not a universal `afterEach` hook.

### 3.6 Skipping behaviour

Current named skips:

- `describeDatabase` becomes `describe.skip` when `SELECT 1` fails against the storage database.
- `describeRedis` becomes `describe.skip` when the Redis connection or `PING` fails.
- Storage files register a `test.skip("... requires the live database")` placeholder so a skipped file is still visible.
- `core-back/test/e2e/postgres-payment.test.ts` uses `test.skipIf(!reachable)` for every payment test.
- `write-path.integration.test.ts`, `uow.test.ts`, `ledger-shards.test.ts`, `audit-chain.test.ts`, `outbox-workers.test.ts`, `engine-factory.test.ts` and `performance/*.test.ts` have explicit skips.
- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/full-platform-lifecycle-journeys.spec.ts` skips unless `E2E_LIVE=1`.
- The link-journey test also skips unless `E2E_LINK_KEY` is set.
- `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts` has no skip guard; it fails if the deployed host is unreachable.

No suite currently sets a CI fail-on-skip policy. A run can be green with most DB or live coverage skipped.

### 3.7 Mocked surfaces

| Surface | Mocking approach | Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Admin UI | `mockApi()` intercepts every `/api/v1/**` call | No real permissions, validation or data flow |
| Merchant UI | Same | Same |
| Checkout UI | Route intercepts `/api/v1/pay/**` | No real payment state machine |
| Fake-rails UI | Route intercepts `/portal-api/**` and `/hosted/**` | Only login geometry is tested |
| Login flows | Route intercept returns fixture session | Body-shape assertions only |
| Edge BFF tests | Real Express routers with fake core clients in places | Contract coverage, not live mTLS |
| Engine suite 04 | In-process harness with scripted step results | Deterministic and broad, not live fake-rails |
| Seeder safety | Fake Prisma objects and stubbed handshake | Gate logic only |

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. **A test that asserts only on a stub is not acceptance evidence.** Behaviour claims need a real module or live service.
2. **A skipped DB suite is not a passing DB suite.** Reports must name the skip reason.
3. **The test database is disposable.** Tests must not depend on rows left by another file; use unique references and clean up.
4. **Money invariants are checked after database writes.** Any suite that posts ledger entries must verify zero drift.
5. **Seeded PRNGs must be fixed and named.** A failure must be reproducible from the printed seed.
6. **Live credentials belong in the environment, not in source.** This invariant is currently violated by `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts`.
7. **The runner must fail when a required gate fails.** It currently does so for command failures, but not for skips.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

- Runner: `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh`.
- Playwright wrapper: `tests/run-playwright.sh`.
- Playwright configs: `tests/playwright.config.ts`, `playwright.exhaustive.config.ts`, `playwright.live.config.ts`.
- Vitest config: `tests/vitest.config.ts`.
- Core setup: `core-back/test/setup.ts`.
- Exhaustive harness: `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts`, `_dbFactory.ts`.
- Storage helpers: `core-back/test/storage-engine/helpers/db.ts`.
- E2E fixture: `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts`.

## 6. Operational usage

```bash
# Core unit and integration
cd core-back && bun run typecheck && bun test

# Exhaustive gates
./scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh

# Playwright mocked UI
cd tests && bun run test

# Deployed-stack live smoke

# Deploy Topology and Configuration

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part owns the deployment input contract: `deploy/deploy.env`, its parser, Zod schema, cross-field validation, topology model and the translation from logical roles to concrete hosts. It defines the node grammar, all configuration groups, precedence rules, topology classification and the validation that runs before any SSH connection.

It does not own the host plan itself (see `deploy.planner`), certificate generation (`deploy.pki`), firewall application (`deploy.firewall`), the pipeline (`deploy.pipeline`) or storage provisioning (`deploy.storage`).

The entrypoint is `deploy/deploy.sh`, which requires Bun and a `deploy/deploy.env`, then executes `bun run deploy/deploy.ts`.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The design requires a flexible 1..N topology:

- compute tiers `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES`, `CHECKOUT_NODES`;
- one PostgreSQL primary, zero or more streaming replicas and optional PgBouncer;
- optional Redis, dedicated audit and log databases, and a backup node;
- any compute or storage role may share a host, but ports must remain distinct and storage roles may not collide with compute listeners;
- configuration is validated before the first SSH connection, so an invalid IP or missing key fails on the operator workstation rather than halfway through production;
- node arrays override the legacy single-host fields;
- the core certificate SAN and firewall allowlists are derived from the same private IPs.

The design names three topology shapes: fully distributed, split/combined hosts, and a single all-in-one staging box. The code additionally supports horizontal compute arrays.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Loading and parsing

`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` uses a small dotenv parser, not a full dotenv library:

- blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored;
- `KEY=value` is required; lines without `=` are ignored;
- single- or double-quoted values end at the first matching quote, so an inline `#` after the quote is not part of the value;
- unquoted values are truncated at ` #`;
- there is no variable expansion, no `export` handling, no escaped-newline handling and no multi-line value support;
- a duplicate key overwrites the earlier value in the parsed record.

The parsed record is validated with `z.strictObject`. Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored. `loadDeployConfig()` returns either a config plus an empty problem list or a list of Zod issues and cross-field problems.

### 3.2 Node grammar

Every `*_NODES` list, `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE` and `BACKUP_NODE` uses:

```text
nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
```

- `nodeId` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.
- `sshHost` and `privateIp` must be IPv4 addresses. DNS names are not accepted for nodes.
- `sshPort` and `servicePort` must be integers from 1 to 65535.
- Node ids must be unique across every node list.
- A node list rejects duplicate private IPs within that list.
- PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs must also be globally unique.

The node spec carries only host, SSH port, private IP and service port. SSH user, key path and sudo password still come from the tier's legacy fields (`CORE_SSH_USER`, `CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `CORE_SUDO_PASSWORD`, and so on). Two roles on one SSH endpoint must use the same user, key and sudo password.

### 3.3 Configuration groups

| Group | Keys | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Global | `DEPLOY_MODE`, `DEPLOY_ENV`, `KEEP_RELEASES`, `ROTATE_MTLS_CERTS`, `MTLS_VALIDITY_DAYS`, `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`, `ROLLING_BATCH_SIZE` | Pipeline mode, release retention, certificate rotation and LAN policy. |
| Legacy database | `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `DB_SSH_HOST`, `DB_SSH_PORT`, `DB_SSH_USER`, `DB_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `DB_SUDO_PASSWORD`, `DB_PRIVATE_IP`, `DB_ENGINE`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DATABASE_URL` | Compatibility path for one externally managed PostgreSQL 18 database. |
| Compute node arrays | `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES`, `CHECKOUT_NODES`, `CORE_BACK_URLS` | Horizontal compute tiers and an optional explicit edge upstream list. |

# Host Planner

## 1. Purpose and scope

The host planner converts a validated `DeployConfig` into a `DeployPlan`:

- unique hosts keyed by `sshHost:sshPort`;
- per-host roles, services, Nginx sites, certificate bundles, firewall rules and deploy order;
- per-tier node plans for core, admin, merchant and checkout;
- the PostgreSQL/Redis/audit/log/backup storage plan;
- the backup plan and topology label.

It owns grouping and unioning only. It does not validate the raw environment (that is `deploy.topology`), generate certificates (`deploy.pki`), apply firewall rules (`deploy.firewall`) or execute the pipeline (`deploy.pipeline`).

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The design requires "smart host deduplication": if two roles share an SSH endpoint, they are one machine. The planner must bootstrap that machine once, merge PM2 services, Nginx vhosts, certificate material and UFW rules, and still keep each horizontal node as its own service identity.

Storage roles are independently scalable. A PostgreSQL primary, replicas, PgBouncer, Redis, audit DB, log DB and backup daemon may be dedicated or co-located. The plan must preserve the intended network policy: the database only accepts core/replica/backup sources, the core only accepts edge sources, and the edge backends bind to loopback.

The rendered topology is intended to be the operator's first confirmation that deduplication and node arrays mean what they intended.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Target collection

`planHosts()` starts from `findSshConflicts()`. Any endpoint shared by roles with different SSH keys or users aborts planning.

`allTargets()` builds a `RoleTarget` for:

1. every compute node from `buildComputeNodes()`, with its service, Nginx sites and firewall rules;
2. legacy database role (only when `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` and the legacy DB path is active);
3. Fake Rails (only when enabled and configured);
4. managed storage nodes from `storageTargets()`.

A compute node is built from the node array when present, otherwise from the legacy single-host fields. The service name is the tier base (`pg-core-back`, `pg-admin-back`, `pg-merchant-back`, `pg-checkout-back`, `pg-fake-rails-back`) for the first node; later nodes get `-<slug(nodeId)>` appended. A node's `servicePort` becomes the service port.

### 3.2 SSH endpoint grouping

The grouping key is `sshHost:sshPort` only. Hostnames, private IPs and role names do not participate. For every target:

- a new host gets the target's service, Nginx sites, certs, firewall and `deployOrder`;
- an existing host appends missing roles, unions certs, merges firewall rules, appends services by unique name, appends Nginx sites by unique site name, and takes the minimum role order.

`ROLE_ORDER` places storage and legacy database first (1), core second (2), Fake Rails third (3), admin fourth (4), merchant fifth (5), checkout sixth (6). Hosts are sorted by `deployOrder` and then by key. This is the order used by `renderTopology` and by compute deployment through the explicit pipeline steps, not a generic host loop.

### 3.3 Service plans

`buildService()` combines the tier's `sourceDir` and `remoteDir` with the node's port and environment:

- core receives `coreEnv()`: database URL, mTLS server material, KMS key, Redis URL, storage environment, Fake Rails and seed flags;
- edge roles receive `edgeEnv()`: core URL list, own client certificate paths, LAN CIDRs for admin, PG-live prefix for merchant, checkout front URL for checkout;
- Fake Rails receives `fakeRailsEnv()`.

Edge environments are built from a base that deliberately excludes `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` and storage credentials. `NODE_ENV` is forced to `production`.

### 3.4 Nginx plans

`buildNginx()` always produces:

- `admin-lan` on `ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT`, SSL by default, server name `ADMIN_DOMAIN`, static root from the admin release;
- `merchant-public` on HTTP/HTTPS ports, with certbot/custom/self-signed mode;
- `checkout-public` on HTTP/HTTPS ports, with certbot/custom/self-signed mode;
- optional `merchant-lan` when `MERCHANT_LAN_PORT > 0`;
- optional `checkout-lan` when `CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT > 0`;
- optional `fake-rails` when enabled.

Nginx plans are filtered per role and attached to the matching compute host(s). The public merchant/checkout vhosts use the configured domains; the LAN vhosts use the node private IP or `_`. The admin vhost is not attached to a non-admin host.

# Testing Strategy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part defines how the monorepo is verified: the test philosophy, the gate progression, database and Redis expectations, the zero-tautology rule, and which suites currently skip, mock or fail to exist.

It does not list every test file or count (see `testing.suites`), the fixture and live-stack wiring (see `testing.fixtures`) or the benchmark gates (see `testing.benchmarks`). Per-workspace test evidence is repeated in each workspace part.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The exhaustive test plan was written to prevent a small happy-path suite from missing intersection defects: rounding remainders, confirmation races, SSRF notations, JSX binding failures and seeded historical attempts that fail when an operator clicks Inquire or Refund.

Its non-negotiable rules are:

1. **Zero-tautology.** Every test must invoke the real production module, real Express router, real PostgreSQL constraint or rendered Vue DOM. `expect(true).toBe(true)` and mock-against-mock tests are forbidden.
2. **Combinatorial and property-based generation.** Use data-driven Cartesian products and a seeded PRNG so permutations are named and reproducible.
3. **Continuous double-entry invariant.** Every database suite runs the ledger invariant after writes and requires `drift === "0.0000"`.
4. **Fail-fast gate progression.** Implement and pass suites `T-EX-01` through `T-EX-11` in order; fix production defects before advancing.
5. **Fail loudly when the environment is absent.** A suite that needs PostgreSQL, Redis or a live host either skips with a named reason or fails; it must not silently pass against a stub.

The plan targets 38,500 or more assertions across eleven suites, plus a unified runner.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Test roots

| Root | Runner | Primary scope |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `core-back/test` | `bun test` | Unit, route, engine, ledger, storage, exhaustive |
| `admin-back/test` | `bun test` | Edge contract, mTLS, env isolation, admin surface |
| `merchant-back/test` | `bun test` | Edge contract, forwarding, KYB/external surface |
| `checkout-back/test` | `bun test` | Zero-trust checkout, mTLS, env isolation |
| `fake-rails-back/test` | `bun test` | Real Express app over SQLite |
| `deploy/test` | `bun test` | Config, host planning, PKI, firewall, pipeline |
| `deploy/backup-daemon/test` | `bun test` | Backup engine, catalog, scheduler, restore drill |
| `tests/e2e` | Playwright | Portal geometry, auth, dialogs, mocked API surface |
| `tests/e2e-live` | Playwright | Deployed-stack smoke journeys |
| `tests/unit` | Vitest | Frontend utility and authority helpers |

`tests/run-playwright.sh` is the Playwright wrapper used by local runs. `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` is the master gate runner and forces one Bun worker for database suites.

### 3.2 The zero-tautology rule in practice

The core exhaustive suites are structurally honest about production code:

- `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts` drives real Prisma clients, real schema files and real production services. It says explicitly that it only provisions fixtures and reads metadata.
- `_dbFactory.ts` builds rows from the real `schema.prisma` and live catalog; it does not replace constraints.
- Suite 01 reads `information_schema`, `pg_catalog`, `pg_indexes` and real constraint metadata.
- Suite 02 invokes `LedgerPoster.validateTemplate` and real `buildLedgerTemplate` output.
- Suite 03 invokes the real transform, canonicalisation, signing and Vault code.
- Suite 04 invokes `DynamicRailEngine` through `_engineHarness.ts`, not the live fake-rails HTTP tier.
- Suite 05 drives real authority/session helpers and the real list-query parser.
- Suite 06 uses live PostgreSQL concurrency primitives.
- Suite 07 uses real parsers, KYB sniffers, AML rules and go-live validators.
- Suite 08 uses real SSRF/URL/response-hardening helpers.

The UI and edge tests are weaker:

- `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` `mockApi()` fulfills every `/api/v1/**` call with `{}` or a small fixture. The exhaustive surface tests only assert rendering, layout, direction and theme.
- Auth tests intercept the login endpoint and return a fixture session; they assert the shape of the posted body, not a real login.
- The fake-rails surface test mocks every `/portal-api/**` and only visits `/login`.
- `tests/unit` tests real frontend utility functions, not the full pages.

These are useful regression tests, but they do not satisfy the design's zero-tautology claim for UI behaviour.

### 3.3 Gate progression

`scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh` implements this sequence:

| Gate | Command target | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `T-EX-01` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/01-schema` | Live PostgreSQL required for most tests |
| `T-EX-02` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/02-ledger` | Some tests are pure; checkpoints need PostgreSQL |
| `T-EX-03` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/03-transforms-crypto` | Pure |
| `T-EX-04` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/04-rail-engine` | Pure engine harness |
| `T-EX-05` | core plus all edge backends plus fake rails plus deploy | Mixed Bun suites |
| `T-EX-06` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/06-concurrency` | Live PostgreSQL |
| `T-EX-07` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/07-workflows` | Mostly pure |
| `T-EX-08` | `core-back/test/exhaustive/08-security-edge` | Pure |
| `T-EX-09` | `core-back/test/storage-engine`, `test/backup-admin`, backup daemon | There is no `09-storage-backup` directory |
| `T-EX-09b` | `tests` unit plus exhaustive Playwright | Mocked UI |
| `T-EX-10` | `10-seeder-and-deploy` plus optional cross-service journeys | Journeys skip without `E2E_LIVE=1` |
| Final | `core-back bun test` | Full regression |

The design's numbering differs from the runner: the runner calls the UI matrix `T-EX-09b` and the seeder/deploy suite `T-EX-10`, while the design calls them Suite 10 and Suite 11.

### 3.4 Database provisioning

There is no single test database configuration. The suites use these variables:

| Variable | Default | Used by |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/payment_gateway_monolith_test` | `test/setup.ts`, storage helpers, postgres payment test |
| `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | fallback | Postgres payment test, exhaustive harness fallback |
| `EXHAUSTIVE_DATABASE_URL` | fallback to `POSTGRES_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | Exhaustive harness |
| `STORAGE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` | fallback to `DATABASE_URL` | Storage-engine helpers |
| `STORAGE_TEST_REDIS_URL` | `redis://127.0.0.1:56379` | Cache/velocity and performance |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://127.0.0.1:56379` | Storage performance and production adapters |

The expected local server is PostgreSQL 18 on port 55432 and Redis on 56379, not the default service ports. The test database must already be migrated (`bun run migrate-deploy`) before the DB-backed suites run. `_harness.ts` uses a dedicated Prisma client so it does not share the cached application client. The storage helpers create dedicated schemas or sandboxes with `search_path` so files can run in parallel.

`bun test --parallel=1` is mandatory for the database suites in the runner because they share one database and the invariant hook.

### 3.5 Double-entry invariant

`_harness.ts` exposes `verifyInvariant()` and `assertZeroDrift()`, which wrap the production `InvariantVerifier`. Suite 02 and the storage write-path suites use it after batches. A non-zero drift throws with left/right sides and drift printed.

The invariant hook is not applied to every file that touches the database. The runner enforces one worker, but not a universal `afterEach` hook.

### 3.6 Skipping behaviour

Current named skips:

- `describeDatabase` becomes `describe.skip` when `SELECT 1` fails against the storage database.
- `describeRedis` becomes `describe.skip` when the Redis connection or `PING` fails.
- Storage files register a `test.skip("... requires the live database")` placeholder so a skipped file is still visible.
- `core-back/test/e2e/postgres-payment.test.ts` uses `test.skipIf(!reachable)` for every payment test.
- `write-path.integration.test.ts`, `uow.test.ts`, `ledger-shards.test.ts`, `audit-chain.test.ts`, `outbox-workers.test.ts`, `engine-factory.test.ts` and `performance/*.test.ts` have explicit skips.
- `tests/e2e/exhaustive/full-platform-lifecycle-journeys.spec.ts` skips unless `E2E_LIVE=1`.
- The link-journey test also skips unless `E2E_LINK_KEY` is set.
- `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts` has no skip guard; it fails if the deployed host is unreachable.

No suite currently sets a CI fail-on-skip policy. A run can be green with most DB or live coverage skipped.

### 3.7 Mocked surfaces

| Surface | Mocking approach | Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Admin UI | `mockApi()` intercepts every `/api/v1/**` call | No real permissions, validation or data flow |
| Merchant UI | Same | Same |
| Checkout UI | Route intercepts `/api/v1/pay/**` | No real payment state machine |
| Fake-rails UI | Route intercepts `/portal-api/**` and `/hosted/**` | Only login geometry is tested |
| Login flows | Route intercept returns fixture session | Body-shape assertions only |
| Edge BFF tests | Real Express routers with fake core clients in places | Contract coverage, not live mTLS |
| Engine suite 04 | In-process harness with scripted step results | Deterministic and broad, not live fake-rails |
| Seeder safety | Fake Prisma objects and stubbed handshake | Gate logic only |

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. **A test that asserts only on a stub is not acceptance evidence.** Behaviour claims need a real module or live service.
2. **A skipped DB suite is not a passing DB suite.** Reports must name the skip reason.
3. **The test database is disposable.** Tests must not depend on rows left by another file; use unique references and clean up.
4. **Money invariants are checked after database writes.** Any suite that posts ledger entries must verify zero drift.
5. **Seeded PRNGs must be fixed and named.** A failure must be reproducible from the printed seed.
6. **Live credentials belong in the environment, not in source.** This invariant is currently violated by `tests/e2e-live/live.spec.ts`.
7. **The runner must fail when a required gate fails.** It currently does so for command failures, but not for skips.

## 5. Data / API / config / deployment surface

- Runner: `scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh`.
- Playwright wrapper: `tests/run-playwright.sh`.
- Playwright configs: `tests/playwright.config.ts`, `playwright.exhaustive.config.ts`, `playwright.live.config.ts`.
- Vitest config: `tests/vitest.config.ts`.
- Core setup: `core-back/test/setup.ts`.
- Exhaustive harness: `core-back/test/exhaustive/_harness.ts`, `_dbFactory.ts`.
- Storage helpers: `core-back/test/storage-engine/helpers/db.ts`.
- E2E fixture: `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts`.

## 6. Operational usage

```bash
# Core unit and integration
cd core-back && bun run typecheck && bun test

# Exhaustive gates
./scripts/run-exhaustive-suite.sh

# Playwright mocked UI
cd tests && bun run test

# Deployed-stack live smoke

# Deploy Topology and Configuration

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part owns the deployment input contract: `deploy/deploy.env`, its parser, Zod schema, cross-field validation, topology model and the translation from logical roles to concrete hosts. It defines the node grammar, all configuration groups, precedence rules, topology classification and the validation that runs before any SSH connection.

It does not own the host plan itself (see `deploy.planner`), certificate generation (`deploy.pki`), firewall application (`deploy.firewall`), the pipeline (`deploy.pipeline`) or storage provisioning (`deploy.storage`).

The entrypoint is `deploy/deploy.sh`, which requires Bun and a `deploy/deploy.env`, then executes `bun run deploy/deploy.ts`.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The design requires a flexible 1..N topology:

- compute tiers `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES`, `CHECKOUT_NODES`;
- one PostgreSQL primary, zero or more streaming replicas and optional PgBouncer;
- optional Redis, dedicated audit and log databases, and a backup node;
- any compute or storage role may share a host, but ports must remain distinct and storage roles may not collide with compute listeners;
- configuration is validated before the first SSH connection, so an invalid IP or missing key fails on the operator workstation rather than halfway through production;
- node arrays override the legacy single-host fields;
- the core certificate SAN and firewall allowlists are derived from the same private IPs.

The design names three topology shapes: fully distributed, split/combined hosts, and a single all-in-one staging box. The code additionally supports horizontal compute arrays.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Loading and parsing

`deploy/lib/configSchema.ts` uses a small dotenv parser, not a full dotenv library:

- blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored;
- `KEY=value` is required; lines without `=` are ignored;
- single- or double-quoted values end at the first matching quote, so an inline `#` after the quote is not part of the value;
- unquoted values are truncated at ` #`;
- there is no variable expansion, no `export` handling, no escaped-newline handling and no multi-line value support;
- a duplicate key overwrites the earlier value in the parsed record.

The parsed record is validated with `z.strictObject`. Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored. `loadDeployConfig()` returns either a config plus an empty problem list or a list of Zod issues and cross-field problems.

### 3.2 Node grammar

Every `*_NODES` list, `PG_PRIMARY_NODE`, `PG_REPLICA_NODES`, `REDIS_NODES`, `AUDIT_DB_NODE`, `LOG_DB_NODE` and `BACKUP_NODE` uses:

```text
nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort
```

- `nodeId` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.
- `sshHost` and `privateIp` must be IPv4 addresses. DNS names are not accepted for nodes.
- `sshPort` and `servicePort` must be integers from 1 to 65535.
- Node ids must be unique across every node list.
- A node list rejects duplicate private IPs within that list.
- PostgreSQL primary/replica private IPs must also be globally unique.

The node spec carries only host, SSH port, private IP and service port. SSH user, key path and sudo password still come from the tier's legacy fields (`CORE_SSH_USER`, `CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `CORE_SUDO_PASSWORD`, and so on). Two roles on one SSH endpoint must use the same user, key and sudo password.

### 3.3 Configuration groups

| Group | Keys | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Global | `DEPLOY_MODE`, `DEPLOY_ENV`, `KEEP_RELEASES`, `ROTATE_MTLS_CERTS`, `MTLS_VALIDITY_DAYS`, `LAN_ALLOWED_CIDRS`, `ROLLING_BATCH_SIZE` | Pipeline mode, release retention, certificate rotation and LAN policy. |
| Legacy database | `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH`, `DB_SSH_HOST`, `DB_SSH_PORT`, `DB_SSH_USER`, `DB_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `DB_SUDO_PASSWORD`, `DB_PRIVATE_IP`, `DB_ENGINE`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DATABASE_URL` | Compatibility path for one externally managed PostgreSQL 18 database. |
| Compute node arrays | `CORE_NODES`, `ADMIN_NODES`, `MERCHANT_NODES`, `CHECKOUT_NODES`, `CORE_BACK_URLS` | Horizontal compute tiers and an optional explicit edge upstream list. |
| Core | `CORE_SSH_HOST`, `CORE_SSH_PORT`, `CORE_SSH_USER`, `CORE_SSH_KEY_PATH`, `CORE_SUDO_PASSWORD`, `CORE_PRIVATE_IP`, `CORE_PORT`, `CORE_REMOTE_DIR`, `RUN_PRISMA_SEED` | Core host, listener, release directory and optional seed. |

| Fake Rails | `FAKE_RAILS_ENABLED`, `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOW_IN_PRODUCTION`, `FAKE_RAILS_SSH_*`, `FAKE_RAILS_PRIVATE_IP`, `FAKE_RAILS_BACK_PORT`, `FAKE_RAILS_NGINX_PORT`, `FAKE_RAILS_SSL*`, `FAKE_RAILS_DOMAIN`, `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `FAKE_RAILS_REMOTE_DIR`, `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_CIDRS`, `FAKE_RAILS_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `FAKE_RAILS_ADMIN_*`, `FAKE_RAILS_JWT_SECRET`, `FAKE_RAILS_SEEDER_TOKEN`, `SEED_FAKE_RAILS_BLUEPRINTS` | Optional emulator and tester portal. |

| Test marker | `IS_TEST_SERVER` | Required for the synthetic seed and used as a test-installation declaration. |

### 3.4 Precedence rules

1. **Node arrays over legacy host fields.** `CORE_NODES` overrides `CORE_SSH_HOST`, `CORE_SSH_PORT`, `CORE_PRIVATE_IP` and `CORE_PORT` for planning. The same applies to admin, merchant and checkout. SSH user/key/sudo are still taken from the legacy fields.
2. **PostgreSQL storage fields over legacy database fields.** When any `PG_*` storage field is configured, `PG_DB_NAME`, `PG_DB_USER` and `PG_DB_PASSWORD` are authoritative. Otherwise `DB_*` is used, falling back to `PG_DB_*`.
3. **Derived database URL.** When the PostgreSQL tier is configured and a host exists, `DATABASE_URL` is derived from the PG credentials, the primary private IP and `PGBOUNCER_PORT` when enabled; otherwise the explicit `DATABASE_URL` is used.
4. **Explicit core URL list.** `CORE_BACK_URLS` wins; otherwise `https://<privateIp>:<servicePort>` for every `CORE_NODES` entry; otherwise the legacy `https://<CORE_PRIVATE_IP>:<CORE_PORT>`.
5. **Node service port over configured backend port.** A node's `servicePort` overrides `CORE_PORT`/`ADMIN_BACK_PORT`/`MERCHANT_BACK_PORT`/`CHECKOUT_BACK_PORT` for that node.
6. **CLI over environment.** `--fresh`, `--update`, `--only`, `--nodes`, `--rolling-batch`, `--keep`, `--rotate-certs`, `--skip-build` and `--skip-verify` override the corresponding configuration for one run.
7. **Admin checklist master flag.** `ADMIN_SHOW_CHECKLISTS` wins over the legacy `ADMIN_SHOW_SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_CHECKLIST`; the legacy key is the fallback when the master key is absent.

# Host Planner

## 1. Purpose and scope

The host planner converts a validated `DeployConfig` into a `DeployPlan`:

- unique hosts keyed by `sshHost:sshPort`;
- per-host roles, services, Nginx sites, certificate bundles, firewall rules and deploy order;
- per-tier node plans for core, admin, merchant and checkout;
- the PostgreSQL/Redis/audit/log/backup storage plan;
- the backup plan and topology label.

It owns grouping and unioning only. It does not validate the raw environment (that is `deploy.topology`), generate certificates (`deploy.pki`), apply firewall rules (`deploy.firewall`) or execute the pipeline (`deploy.pipeline`).

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The design requires "smart host deduplication": if two roles share an SSH endpoint, they are one machine. The planner must bootstrap that machine once, merge PM2 services, Nginx vhosts, certificate material and UFW rules, and still keep each horizontal node as its own service identity.

Storage roles are independently scalable. A PostgreSQL primary, replicas, PgBouncer, Redis, audit DB, log DB and backup daemon may be dedicated or co-located. The plan must preserve the intended network policy: the database only accepts core/replica/backup sources, the core only accepts edge sources, and the edge backends bind to loopback.

The rendered topology is intended to be the operator's first confirmation that deduplication and node arrays mean what they intended.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Target collection

`planHosts()` starts from `findSshConflicts()`. Any endpoint shared by roles with different SSH keys or users aborts planning.

`allTargets()` builds a `RoleTarget` for:

1. every compute node from `buildComputeNodes()`, with its service, Nginx sites and firewall rules;
2. legacy database role (only when `DB_MANAGE_VIA_SSH` and the legacy DB path is active);
3. Fake Rails (only when enabled and configured);
4. managed storage nodes from `storageTargets()`.

A compute node is built from the node array when present, otherwise from the legacy single-host fields. The service name is the tier base (`pg-core-back`, `pg-admin-back`, `pg-merchant-back`, `pg-checkout-back`, `pg-fake-rails-back`) for the first node; later nodes get `-<slug(nodeId)>` appended. A node's `servicePort` becomes the service port.

### 3.2 SSH endpoint grouping

The grouping key is `sshHost:sshPort` only. Hostnames, private IPs and role names do not participate. For every target:

- a new host gets the target's service, Nginx sites, certs, firewall and `deployOrder`;
- an existing host appends missing roles, unions certs, merges firewall rules, appends services by unique name, appends Nginx sites by unique site name, and takes the minimum role order.

`ROLE_ORDER` places storage and legacy database first (1), core second (2), Fake Rails third (3), admin fourth (4), merchant fifth (5), checkout sixth (6). Hosts are sorted by `deployOrder` and then by key. This is the order used by `renderTopology` and by compute deployment through the explicit pipeline steps, not a generic host loop.

### 3.3 Service plans

`buildService()` combines the tier's `sourceDir` and `remoteDir` with the node's port and environment:

- core receives `coreEnv()`: database URL, mTLS server material, KMS key, Redis URL, storage environment, Fake Rails and seed flags;
- edge roles receive `edgeEnv()`: core URL list, own client certificate paths, LAN CIDRs for admin, PG-live prefix for merchant, checkout front URL for checkout;
- Fake Rails receives `fakeRailsEnv()`.

Edge environments are built from a base that deliberately excludes `DATABASE_URL`, `KMS_MASTER_KEY` and storage credentials. `NODE_ENV` is forced to `production`.

### 3.4 Nginx plans

`buildNginx()` always produces:

- `admin-lan` on `ADMIN_NGINX_LAN_PORT`, SSL by default, server name `ADMIN_DOMAIN`, static root from the admin release;
- `merchant-public` on HTTP/HTTPS ports, with certbot/custom/self-signed mode;
- `checkout-public` on HTTP/HTTPS ports, with certbot/custom/self-signed mode;
- optional `merchant-lan` when `MERCHANT_LAN_PORT > 0`;
- optional `checkout-lan` when `CHECKOUT_LAN_PORT > 0`;
- optional `fake-rails` when enabled.

Nginx plans are filtered per role and attached to the matching compute host(s). The public merchant/checkout vhosts use the configured domains; the LAN vhosts use the node private IP or `_`. The admin vhost is not attached to a non-admin host.

- `postgres18Provisioner.ts`: PostgreSQL 18 primary, replicas, replication slots, `pg_hba`, PgBouncer, tuning and journal partition cron;

# Storage Engine

## 1. Purpose and scope

The storage engine is the boundary between domain code and PostgreSQL 18, Redis, the dedicated audit database and the dedicated log database. It owns:

- the `StorageEngine` composition object and its ports;
- the transactional unit of work that couples domain writes, `outbox_events` and `audit_outbox`;
- the post-commit WAL flush watermark used by LSN-aware reads;
- primary/replica read routing and replica health tracking;
- Redis cache and sliding-window velocity counters, with an in-memory fallback;
- the dedicated audit hash-chain append adapter and audit query adapter;
- the buffered operational step/access log sink;
- GL account shard arithmetic and shard-aware ledger writes;
- the transactional outbox relay and audit shipper workers;
- the read-model projection for `rm_merchant_daily_stats` and `rm_route_daily_volumes`;
- the mTLS backup-control client used by `core-back` to reach `pg-backup-daemon`;
- the storage health snapshot API.

It does not own the Prisma schema or migration workflow (`core.storage` is paired with `core.data`), the backup daemon implementation (`07-deploy`), the global-search provider catalogue (`core.search`), or domain ledger/attempt decisions.

Dependent systems: `engine/**` through the platform runtime, `api/internal/{admin,merchant,checkout,backups}.ts`, the worker runtime, the global search route, and the storage-engine and backup-admin test suites.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The historical storage blueprint defines a thin, ACID write path for a high-volume switch:

- A payment or ledger write touches the operational row, one `gl_account_shards` balance row, one `outbox_events` row and one `audit_outbox` row in a single transaction.
- The unit of work reports a commit WAL position so a caller can ask for a replica that has replayed at least that position.
- System GL accounts are split into 16 deterministic shards; merchant wallets use a single shard. Shard rows are locked in stable sorted order to avoid deadlocks.
- Outbox events project read models asynchronously so dashboards do not aggregate the ledger on the write path.
- Replica reads are selected by lag and LSN, with primary fallback.
- Redis provides L2 cache and Lua-backed velocity windows; it is never authoritative for money.
- Audit is shipped asynchronously to a dedicated append-only database with a SHA-256 hash chain and immutable rows.
- Operational step/access logs go to a separate log database so logging cannot block a payment.
- Backups are controlled through an mTLS daemon that wraps WAL-G or Barman.

The blueprint's implementation claims must not be repeated as current behavior. The actual code differs in these material ways:

- `ledger.entry_posted` is registered but its handler is a no-op; only `attempt.transitioned` projects read models.
- The two read models are written but not read by dashboards or list endpoints.
- `AuditShipperWorker` marks `audit_outbox.shipped_at`; it never deletes shipped rows.
- Replica routing is used by global search and three merchant list endpoints, not by all dashboards, lists and exports.
- Pagination is offset-based, not keyset-based.
- Access logs record zero database query metrics.
- There is no `gateway_wire_logs` table and no disk spool for the log sink.

# Checkout Edge BFF

## 1. Purpose and scope

`checkout-back` is the public checkout and inbound-webhook edge. It serves anonymous payers and external payment gateways:

- payer link resolution and attempt lifecycle under `/api/v1/pay/*`;
- the checkout status SSE stream;
- browser return handling under `/api/v1/return/*`;
- raw inbound gateway webhooks under `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`.

It owns edge schema validation, the zero-monetary-field assertion, raw webhook capture, header allowlisting, environment translation, client IP propagation, rate limiting, redirect construction and mTLS forwarding to `/internal/checkout/*`. It owns no database, no session, no money resolution and no gateway signature verification.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The checkout edge is deliberately read/execute-only. A payer can select a rail and submit form data, but can never create a link, change a link or supply an amount or currency. `core-back` resolves money from `payment_links` by `linkKey`.

Inbound webhooks are treated as untrusted. The design calls for capturing the raw bytes and headers, forwarding them unchanged to the core inbox, and returning the gateway's configured ack quickly. The core verifies the signature, IP allowlist and replay window. The design's blueprint says the inbox returns the ack in under 10 ms; the as-built core performs verification inline before acking.

The return URL is an untrusted browser hint. Core inspects the attempt, triggers an inquiry where appropriate, and the edge redirects the browser to the checkout status page.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Process and mount order

`checkout-back/index.ts`:

- disables `x-powered-by`;
- sets `trust proxy` to false;
- enables CORS with any origin and no credentials;
- installs request logging;
- serves unauthenticated `GET /health`;
- mounts `/api/v1/inbound` with `inboundRouter` **before** the JSON body parser, so the inbound router can install its own raw parser;
- then installs JSON and URL-encoded parsers (`MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`);
- mounts `/api/v1` with the pay and return routers;
- adds the shared 404 and error handlers.

The listener binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`). The deploy engine writes `127.0.0.1`; Nginx is the public listener.

### 3.2 Middleware and guards

| Layer | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| `payLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), on the pay router. |
| `returnLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, on the return router. |

- Backups are controlled through an mTLS daemon that wraps WAL-G or Barman.

The blueprint's implementation claims must not be repeated as current behavior. The actual code differs in these material ways:

- `ledger.entry_posted` is registered but its handler is a no-op; only `attempt.transitioned` projects read models.
- The two read models are written but not read by dashboards or list endpoints.
- `AuditShipperWorker` marks `audit_outbox.shipped_at`; it never deletes shipped rows.
- Replica routing is used by global search and three merchant list endpoints, not by all dashboards, lists and exports.
- Pagination is offset-based, not keyset-based.
- Access logs record zero database query metrics.
- There is no `gateway_wire_logs` table and no disk spool for the log sink.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Composition root

`core-back/lib/storageEngine/index.ts` builds one `StorageEngine`:

- `createStorageEngine` resolves `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_REPLICA_URLS`, `AUDIT_DATABASE_URL`, `LOG_DATABASE_URL` and Redis from the environment (`index.ts:56-71`).
- It creates the primary Prisma client and one Prisma client per replica URL (`index.ts:72-80`).
- It constructs `PostgresReplicaReadStore` and starts the LSN monitor (`index.ts:82-87`).
- It constructs `PostgresUnitOfWorkAdapter` with an optional post-commit callback (`index.ts:89-92`).
- It selects `RedisCacheAdapter` when a Redis URL exists, otherwise `MemoryCacheAdapter` (`index.ts:94-98`).
- It creates `DedicatedAuditDatabaseDriver` from a dedicated `pg.Pool` and `DedicatedPostgresLogSink` from a separate `pg.Pool` (`index.ts:100-114`).
- It exposes `uow`, `readStore`, `cache`, `auditStore`, `logSink`, `primary`, `health()` and `shutdown()` (`index.ts:116-209`).
- It exports `readThroughReplica` and `readThroughReplicaOrPrimary` helpers (`index.ts:227-268`) and a process-wide singleton (`index.ts:214-225`).

`core-back/index.ts` gets the singleton, installs it into the platform runtime, and installs the log sink into the request logger before listening (`index.ts:255-260`). Shutdown stops the LSN monitor, closes the log sink and cache, disconnects clients and ends both pools (`index.ts:198-207`, `core-back/index.ts:285-291`).

### 3.2 Ports and adapters

`core-back/lib/storageEngine/ports.ts` defines the contracts:

- `UnitOfWorkPort.run(fn, options)` returns `{ data, commitLsn, durationMs }`.
- `StorageTx` exposes `db`, `outbox`, `audit` and `lockGlAccountShardsSorted`.
- `ReadStorePort.execute(consistency, fn, options)` returns `{ data, servedBy, replicaLagMs? }`.
- `CachePort` exposes `get`, `getOrLoad`, `set`, `del`, `incrWindowCounter`, optional `publishInvalidation` and `close`.
- `AuditStorePort` exposes audit query, count, hash-chain verification and detail lookup.

# Checkout Edge BFF

## 1. Purpose and scope

`checkout-back` is the public checkout and inbound-webhook edge. It serves anonymous payers and external payment gateways:

- payer link resolution and attempt lifecycle under `/api/v1/pay/*`;
- the checkout status SSE stream;
- browser return handling under `/api/v1/return/*`;
- raw inbound gateway webhooks under `/api/v1/inbound/:gateway/:env/:pathToken`.

It owns edge schema validation, the zero-monetary-field assertion, raw webhook capture, header allowlisting, environment translation, client IP propagation, rate limiting, redirect construction and mTLS forwarding to `/internal/checkout/*`. It owns no database, no session, no money resolution and no gateway signature verification.

## 2. Design intent (extracted and synthesized from ./design)

The checkout edge is deliberately read/execute-only. A payer can select a rail and submit form data, but can never create a link, change a link or supply an amount or currency. `core-back` resolves money from `payment_links` by `linkKey`.

Inbound webhooks are treated as untrusted. The design calls for capturing the raw bytes and headers, forwarding them unchanged to the core inbox, and returning the gateway's configured ack quickly. The core verifies the signature, IP allowlist and replay window. The design's blueprint says the inbox returns the ack in under 10 ms; the as-built core performs verification inline before acking.

The return URL is an untrusted browser hint. Core inspects the attempt, triggers an inquiry where appropriate, and the edge redirects the browser to the checkout status page.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Process and mount order

`checkout-back/index.ts`:

- disables `x-powered-by`;
- sets `trust proxy` to false;
- enables CORS with any origin and no credentials;
- installs request logging;
- serves unauthenticated `GET /health`;
- mounts `/api/v1/inbound` with `inboundRouter` **before** the JSON body parser, so the inbound router can install its own raw parser;
- then installs JSON and URL-encoded parsers (`MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES`);
- mounts `/api/v1` with the pay and return routers;
- adds the shared 404 and error handlers.

The listener binds to `BIND_HOST` (default `0.0.0.0`). The deploy engine writes `127.0.0.1`; Nginx is the public listener.

### 3.2 Middleware and guards

| Layer | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| `payLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), on the pay router. |
| `returnLimiter` | 60-second window, `PAY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, on the return router. |

# Two-Machine Multi-Topology Matrix

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part owns the executable two-machine lab: SSH/bootstrap, MinIO S3 and SSH vault provisioning, topology config generation for T1–T8, teardown, the 11 verification gates, the stress workload, the self-healing retry loop and the certification report.

It does not own the production deploy engine (`07-deploy`), the storage adapters (`01-core-back/06-storage-engine.md`) or the ledger invariant (`01-core-back/03-ledger.md`).

## 2. Design intent

The historical plan requires eight production topology permutations across `HOST_A` and `HOST_B`:

| ID | Shape |
| :--- | :--- |
| T1 | Single-host multi-node density, co-located PostgreSQL/Redis/audit/log, WAL-G |
| T2 | Compute on A / storage on B, Barman on A |
| T3 | Primary on A, replica + Redis + audit/log on B, WAL-G |
| T4 | Primary on B, local + remote replicas, Redis/audit/log on A, Barman on A |
| T5 | Public checkout/merchant DMZ on B, private core/DB/Redis on A, UFW penetration checks |
| T6 | Symmetric mesh: 4 core, 4 checkout, 4 merchant, 2 admin, 2 replicas, 120k seed |
| T7 | Live scale-out/scale-in under 500 TPS |
| T8 | Chaos: core/replica/Redis/log-DB kills and full primary PITR |

Every topology runs the same 11 gates: provisioning/mTLS/UFW, replica routing and LSN RYOW, Fake Rails/seeder invariants, 500+ TPS checkout/ledger stress, cross-node SSE/POS, concurrent workers, audit immutability/hash chain, log-DB outage, search/pagination, backup/PITR, and chaos/failover.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Bootstrap and lab services

`deploy/test-matrix/hosts.ts`:

- discovers `HOST_A_LAN_IP` with `ip -4 route get 10.209.250.205`;
- creates `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_lab_matrix`, authorizes it on `HOST_A` and `HOST_B` (`salem@10.209.250.205`, password `1234`);
- creates a separate `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_peer` on `HOST_B` and authorizes it on `HOST_A` for Barman/`pg_basebackup`;
- installs/launches MinIO on `HOST_B:9000` with bucket `pg-backups-test`;
- creates the SSH vault directories on both hosts;
- writes `/etc/pg-lab-matrix`, the marker that lets teardown know the host is disposable lab hardware.

### 3.2 Topology generation

`deploy/test-matrix/topologies.ts` builds the eight configs. It uses the real node grammar (`nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`), sets `STORAGE_SHARD_COUNT` to 16 or 32, sets `SYNTHETIC_SEED_PROFILE`, and emits `FAKE_RAILS_NODE` plus a reachable `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` for every topology.

`generateTopologyConfigs.ts` writes `deploy/test-matrix/configs/deploy.T1.env` … `deploy.T8.env` with mode `0600`. `deploy/test/testMatrix.test.ts` validates all eight through the real Zod schema.

### 3.3 Multi-instance deploy support

The matrix depends on the deploy engine supporting several instances of one tier on one host:

- PM2 names are node-suffixed (`pg-core-back-core-1`, `pg-core-back-core-2`);
- each node has `shared/.env.<nodeId>` and its own `.env` symlink;
- each node has `releases/<nodeId>/<timestamp>` and `current-<nodeId>`;
- Nginx renders `upstream` blocks with `least_conn` and `max_fails=2 fail_timeout=3s` over all local and remote nodes;
- edge backends bind the node private IP so a remote Nginx can reach them;
- PostgreSQL roles use independent Debian clusters (`main`, `replica_<nodeId>`, `audit`, `log`) with their own data directory, config, HBA and systemd unit.

### 3.4 Runner and self-healing loop

`runAllTopologiesAndHeal.ts`:

1. bootstraps the lab and writes all eight configs;
2. tears down lab-owned PM2 apps, vhosts, release trees and PostgreSQL clusters;
3. deploys with `deploy/deploy.ts --fresh`;
4. runs all 11 gates in order;
5. on failure, captures PM2 logs and service journals, tears down and retries once;
6. writes `deploy/test-matrix/TOPOLOGY_CERTIFICATION_REPORT.md`.

The runner never stops at the first failed topology; it records the failure and continues to the next configured topology.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. The lab is disposable. Teardown only drops clusters when `/etc/pg-lab-matrix` exists.
2. Secrets stay in generated `0600` config files and are redacted from the report.
3. A topology is certified only when all 11 gates pass.
4. Every gate that writes money must finish with zero double-entry drift and `gl_account_shards == journal_lines`.
5. The audit hash chain is computed by the PostgreSQL trigger under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(994001)`, not by competing Node processes.

## 5. Verification

```bash
cd deploy
bun test ./test/testMatrix.test.ts
bun run test-matrix:bootstrap
bun run test-matrix --topologies=T1,T2
```

Live certification requires `HOST_B` reachable and root/sudo on both hosts. The environment used during implementation could not reach `10.209.250.205`, so only config generation, schema validation and unit tests were executed.

## 6. Known gaps

- Live T1–T8 execution is pending lab availability.
- Gate 4's concurrent webhook/confirm race uses the checkout API but does not yet assert the exact single-ledger-row count through a direct query.
- Gate 10 polls the admin overview for backup completion; the daemon's own `/v1/runs` endpoint is not used directly.
- Gate 11's full primary wipe/PITR restore is orchestration code only; it must be run on the lab.

# Two-Machine Multi-Topology Matrix

## 1. Purpose and scope

This part owns the executable two-machine lab: SSH/bootstrap, MinIO S3 and SSH vault provisioning, topology config generation for T1–T8, teardown, the 11 verification gates, the stress workload, the self-healing retry loop and the certification report.

It does not own the production deploy engine (`07-deploy`), the storage adapters (`01-core-back/06-storage-engine.md`) or the ledger invariant (`01-core-back/03-ledger.md`).

## 2. Design intent

The historical plan requires eight production topology permutations across `HOST_A` and `HOST_B`:

| ID | Shape |
| :--- | :--- |
| T1 | Single-host multi-node density, co-located PostgreSQL/Redis/audit/log, WAL-G |
| T2 | Compute on A / storage on B, Barman on A |
| T3 | Primary on A, replica + Redis + audit/log on B, WAL-G |
| T4 | Primary on B, local + remote replicas, Redis/audit/log on A, Barman on A |
| T5 | Public checkout/merchant DMZ on B, private core/DB/Redis on A, UFW penetration checks |
| T6 | Symmetric mesh: 4 core, 4 checkout, 4 merchant, 2 admin, 2 replicas, 120k seed |
| T7 | Live scale-out/scale-in under 500 TPS |
| T8 | Chaos: core/replica/Redis/log-DB kills and full primary PITR |

Every topology runs the same 11 gates: provisioning/mTLS/UFW, replica routing and LSN RYOW, Fake Rails/seeder invariants, 500+ TPS checkout/ledger stress, cross-node SSE/POS, concurrent workers, audit immutability/hash chain, log-DB outage, search/pagination, backup/PITR, and chaos/failover.

## 3. As-built architecture

### 3.1 Bootstrap and lab services

`deploy/test-matrix/hosts.ts`:

- discovers `HOST_A_LAN_IP` with `ip -4 route get 10.209.250.205`;
- creates `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_lab_matrix`, authorizes it on `HOST_A` and `HOST_B` (`salem@10.209.250.205`, password `1234`);
- creates a separate `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_pg_peer` on `HOST_B` and authorizes it on `HOST_A` for Barman/`pg_basebackup`;
- installs/launches MinIO on `HOST_B:9000` with bucket `pg-backups-test`;
- creates the SSH vault directories on both hosts;
- writes `/etc/pg-lab-matrix`, the marker that lets teardown know the host is disposable lab hardware.

### 3.2 Topology generation

`deploy/test-matrix/topologies.ts` builds the eight configs. It uses the real node grammar (`nodeId@sshHost:sshPort:privateIp:servicePort`), sets `STORAGE_SHARD_COUNT` to 16 or 32, sets `SYNTHETIC_SEED_PROFILE`, and emits `FAKE_RAILS_NODE` plus a reachable `FAKE_RAILS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` for every topology.

`generateTopologyConfigs.ts` writes `deploy/test-matrix/configs/deploy.T1.env` … `deploy.T8.env` with mode `0600`. `deploy/test/testMatrix.test.ts` validates all eight through the real Zod schema.

### 3.3 Multi-instance deploy support

The matrix depends on the deploy engine supporting several instances of one tier on one host:

- PM2 names are node-suffixed (`pg-core-back-core-1`, `pg-core-back-core-2`);
- each node has `shared/.env.<nodeId>` and its own `.env` symlink;
- each node has `releases/<nodeId>/<timestamp>` and `current-<nodeId>`;
- Nginx renders `upstream` blocks with `least_conn` and `max_fails=2 fail_timeout=3s` over all local and remote nodes;
- edge backends bind the node private IP so a remote Nginx can reach them;
- PostgreSQL roles use independent Debian clusters (`main`, `replica_<nodeId>`, `audit`, `log`) with their own data directory, config, HBA and systemd unit.

### 3.4 Runner and self-healing loop

`runAllTopologiesAndHeal.ts`:

1. bootstraps the lab and writes all eight configs;
2. tears down lab-owned PM2 apps, vhosts, release trees and PostgreSQL clusters;
3. deploys with `deploy/deploy.ts --fresh`;
4. runs all 11 gates in order;
5. on failure, captures PM2 logs and service journals, tears down and retries once;
6. writes `deploy/test-matrix/TOPOLOGY_CERTIFICATION_REPORT.md`.

The runner never stops at the first failed topology; it records the failure and continues to the next configured topology.

## 4. Contracts and invariants

1. The lab is disposable. Teardown only drops clusters when `/etc/pg-lab-matrix` exists.
2. Secrets stay in generated `0600` config files and are redacted from the report.
3. A topology is certified only when all 11 gates pass.
4. Every gate that writes money must finish with zero double-entry drift and `gl_account_shards == journal_lines`.
5. The audit hash chain is computed by the PostgreSQL trigger under `pg_advisory_xact_lock(994001)`, not by competing Node processes.

## 5. Verification

```bash
cd deploy
bun test ./test/testMatrix.test.ts
bun run test-matrix:bootstrap
bun run test-matrix --topologies=T1,T2
```

Live certification requires `HOST_B` reachable and root/sudo on both hosts. The environment used during implementation could not reach `10.209.250.205`, so only config generation, schema validation and unit tests were executed.

## 6. Known gaps

- Live T1–T8 execution is pending lab availability.
- Gate 4's concurrent webhook/confirm race uses the checkout API but does not yet assert the exact single-ledger-row count through a direct query.
- Gate 10 polls the admin overview for backup completion; the daemon's own `/v1/runs` endpoint is not used directly.
- Gate 11's full primary wipe/PITR restore is orchestration code only; it must be run on the lab.
EOF

# Two-Machine Topology Matrix

Executable implementation of `design/two-machine-test/two_machine_multi_topology_deployment_and_stress_test_plan.md`.

## Quick start

```bash
cd deploy

| :--- | :--- |

Need confirm admin/merchant builds succeeded; tail didn't show "built". Check exit codes were 0 (tool would show failure?). Likely. Could rerun with grep. Later.

Now review code for serious bugs before final. Key concerns:

1. `deploy/test-matrix/gates.ts` `gate4` hot-link assertion: sets use_count=50, active_locked_count=0, then fires 200. Core link slot logic increments active_locked_count. But after 50 successes, 150 should 409. However if attempts fail due rail unavailable, not 409. Test would fail. Fine, real gate may reveal.
2. `gate5` starts SSE before publishing; `capture` is synchronous and blocks until stream ends. It runs `timeout 8 curl ... | grep -m1 SUCCEEDED`, but publish happens after capture returns, so stream will never get event; it will time out after 8s and then publish. This gate is broken. Need fix: run stream in background on remote, then publish, then wait. Or publish before opening? Then stream misses event. Need use a shell script on remote:
```
( sleep 1; redis-cli publish ... ) & timeout 8 curl -N ... | grep -m1 SUCCEEDED
```
Run entire command on checkout host, but redis-cli may not be installed on checkout host. Could use `nc` to Redis? Better run publish on Redis host via ssh in background locally? We can spawn a child process `spawn` to run `remote.run(redisHost, publish)` after 500ms while `capture` blocks. Since `LabRemote.run` is synchronous spawnSync; use Node `child_process.spawn` or `setTimeout`? The main thread blocked by spawnSync, so setTimeout won't fire. Use shell background on checkout host with `ssh`? Simpler: open SSE on remote in background via `nohup bash -c 'timeout 8 curl ... > /tmp/sse.out' &`, then publish, then wait and read file. Implement:
```
const remote = checkout host
remote.run(checkout, `rm -f /tmp/pg-sse.out; (timeout 8 curl -sS -N URL > /tmp/pg-sse.out 2>&1 || true) &`)
sleep 500ms locally
remote.run(redisHost, publish)
sleep 1000ms
const out = remote.capture(checkout, "cat /tmp/pg-sse.out")
```
But `remote.run` with `&` returns immediately; background process may be killed when shell exits? `nohup` or `setsid`. Use `nohup ... >/tmp/... 2>&1 &`.
Then measure not exact. Could record start/end via file. Simpler gate check output contains SUCCEEDED. Latency not measured. Modify.
Also attempt query uses `SELECT a.id, pl.key` but column names `link_id`? PaymentAttempt model likely `linkId` map `link_id`. Check.
